772d2a8890f92411.speaker: Matthew Foreman
772d2a8890f92411.abstract:
Thematic 3-weeks programme at the Institut Henri Poincaré, Paris, May 18th to June 4th, 2027.
Beware: It was reported to us that scammers are sending to participants fraudulent e-mails about accommodation/fees. Please be particularly cautious about e-mails not coming from the organisers nor from an @ihp.fr address.
REGISTRATION IS FREE, HOWEVER MANDATORY.
Presentation of the programme
In recent years, there have been major advances using techniques from Descriptive Set Theory to show, in a rigorous way, that many classical problems in Dynamical Systems are impossible to solve. In this context, a problem that can be set in a Polish space is said to be impossible to solve if it cannot be settled using inherently countable techniques. These groundbreaking results mostly lie in Ergodic Theory, with further significant advances in Topological and Smooth Dynamical Systems.
One main goal of this program is to further enhance interactions between Descriptive Set Theory and Dynamical Systems. It brings together researchers from different fields to settle some of the most famous problems in dynamics dating to the mid-20th century.
A second main goal is to expand applications of the techniques from Descriptive Set Theory to other areas of mathematics.
Week 1
The program begins with lectures introducing the basic impossibility techniques and lectures explaining fundamental concepts in areas of potential applications.
We plan to have tutorials on:
Impossibility Results
Ergodic Theory
Symbolic Dynamics
Smooth Dynamical Systems
Additionally, there will be Research Talks and Expository Lectures (primarily in Ergodic Theory and Descriptive Set Theory).
Week 2
Research talks in Descriptive Set Theory, Ergodic Theory, Smooth and Symbolic Dynamics, as well as Expository Lectures, including on:
Impossibility Results in Ergodic theory
Complexity Theory
Flexibility and Rigidity
Moreover, we will have Problem and Discussion Sessions.
Week 3
Topical Days (particularly Complex Dynamics with tutorial); Problem Sessions

777bc7e241eb1487.title: Importance Sampling
777bc7e241eb1487.speaker: Simon Coste
777bc7e241eb1487.abstract: Importance sampling is a technique for estimating integrals of the form E[φ(X)], where X has a density g that may be difficult to sample from or otherwise handle. The simplest Monte Carlo method would consist of generating i.i.d. samples X_1,...,X_n from g and averaging the values φ(X_i). By contrast, Importance Sampling (IS) consists of using samples Y_1,...,Y_n from another density, say f, and averaging the reweighted values φ(Y_i) * g(Y_i)/f(Y_i). This works provided that f is positive when g is positive, but there is no free lunch: the price to pay can be high variance and poor accuracy. In this expository talk, I will (1) explain when and how to use IS, with practical examples from chemistry and combinatorics; (2) explain how to measure the accuracy of IS and determine the sample size n needed for an accurate estimation of E[φ(X)], locally for a specific φ; and (3) explain how to measure this accuracy globally using Wasserstein distances, even in infinite dimensions for stochastic diffusions, where "importance sampling" is known under the name of "Girsanov theorem".

7b686fe16a13c1f2.title: De la stabilité aux cascades d'énergie : une transition arithmétique pour l’équation de Schrödinger non linéaire
7b686fe16a13c1f2.speaker: Nicolas Camps
7b686fe16a13c1f2.abstract:
Nous étudions l’équation de Schrödinger non linéaire, un système hamiltonien de dimension infinie, et la possibilité pour l’énergie de petites solutions de migrer vers des fréquences de plus en plus élevées. Nous présentons d’abord le mécanisme de Colliander, Keel, Staffilani, Takaoka et Tao (2010) qui, sur le tore de dimension deux, transfère l’énergie le long d’une chaîne de modes résonants. Sur un guide d’ondes (produit d’une droite et d’un tore carré), Hani, Pausader, Tzvetkov et Visciglia (2015) ont montré que ce mécanisme gouverne la dynamique en temps long, et en ont déduit des solutions dont les normes de Sobolev ne sont pas bornées. Lorsque le tore est irrationnel, les résonances laissent place à des quasi-résonances, dont l’effet dépend de l’arithmétique du rapport des côtés. Pour presque toute valeur de ce rapport, nous montrons que les petites solutions restent petites dans toutes les normes de Sobolev. Pour un ensemble G_\delta dense de valeurs irrationnelles, il existe des solutions arbitrairement petites dont les normes de Sobolev ne sont pas bornées.
Il s’agit d’un travail en préparation avec Gigliola Staffilani et Nikolay Tzvetkov.
7b686fe16a13c1f2.organizer: H. Eliasson, B. Fayad, R. Krikorian, P. Le Calvez

7bdc1c8b6f385022.title: [ANNULÉ] Xenia Flamm, raconte-moi le spectre réel (de variétés de caractères) !
7bdc1c8b6f385022.abstract:
Le spectre réel est un outil de la géométrie algébrique réelle qui permet de compactifier les ensembles semi-algébriques en ajoutant, à l’infini, leurs k-points, pour tout corps k ordonné non-archimédien. J’en présenterai la construction ainsi que les principales propriétés.
Dans une deuxième partie, nous nous intéresserons aux variétés de caractères, c’est-à-dire des espaces de modules de représentations d’un groupe de type fini dans un groupe semi-algébrique G. Ces espaces permettent notamment de décrire de nombreuses structures géométriques sur les variétés. Nous verrons comment le spectre réel permet d’étudier leurs dégénérescences : les points à l’infini peuvent être interprétés comme des représentations à valeurs dans G(k), où k est un corps ordonné non-archimédien. À travers quelques exemples, j’expliquerai en quel sens ces dégénérescences peuvent être vues comme des structures géométriques « non-archimédiennes ».

7be1533a8cdbdf8e.title: Développement asymptotique explicite des E-fonctions hypergéométriques et applications.
7be1533a8cdbdf8e.speaker: Marc Coulomb
7be1533a8cdbdf8e.abstract: La famille des E-fonctions hypergéométriques généralise les fonctions de Bessel, de Kummer, et est liée à de nombreuses fonctions spéciales. Après avoir défini ces notions à l'aide d'un exemple, nous passerons au résultat principal : une formule close et explicite donnant le développement asymptotique des fonctions hypergéométriques dans tout grand secteur angulaire autorisé. De cette formule découlent la sommation explicite de Borel-Laplace des fonctions hypergéométriques divergentes, ainsi que les matrices de Stokes associées. Enfin, nous verrons un exemple d'un tel développement asymptotique faisant intervenir les valeurs de la fonction zêta de Riemann aux entiers.

7d7b9b0a954106bb.title: Homological construction of non-semisimple TQFTs
7d7b9b0a954106bb.speaker: Aleksei Andreev
7d7b9b0a954106bb.abstract: In the 1990s, Lawrence initiated a program to interpret quantum invariants homologically in order to understand their topological nature. Within this framework, twisted homology of configuration spaces of surfaces forms representations of mapping class groups. Recently, De Renzi and Martel showed that, for a specific choice of local system, this construction recovers the projective version of Lyubashenko’s representation for quantum sl_2. Since this representation is part of the non-semisimple Kerler--Lyubashenko TQFT, it is natural to ask whether the homological construction extends to cobordisms. I will answer this question by constructing a homological action of cobordisms via their multi-trajectory spaces and Juhász’s presentation of cobordism categories. As a basic example, I will reformulate Donaldson’s TQFT in these terms, and then sketch how the (projective) Kerler--Lyubashenko TQFT arises as its natural deformation.

7dc634d10a7609b2.title: Les théorèmes de Huber en dimensions 2 et 4
7dc634d10a7609b2.speaker: Paul LAURAIN
7dc634d10a7609b2.abstract: Après avoir rappelé l'énoncé classique du second théorème de Huber, je proposerai une approche fondée sur la méthode du repère mobile. Je présenterai ensuite l'état de l'art concernant les généralisations de ce théorème en dimension 4, en soulignant qu'elles ne permettent pas d'obtenir une généralisation complète et, comment l'approche par repère mobile, nous permet une nouvelle avancée vers un énoncé plus global. Enfin, j'évoquerai quelques applications au cas extrinsèque. Ce travail a été réalisé en collaboration avec Dorian Martino.

7e2553acd62de75e.title: Derived deformation theory of schemes and infinity categories
7e2553acd62de75e.speaker: Samuel Moore
7e2553acd62de75e.abstract: How much about a (derived) scheme does its linear infinity category of quasicoherent sheaves remember? In this talk, I will discuss this question in the setting of deformation theory and make more precise the relationship between deforming schemes and their derived categories. Along the way, I will overview some derived deformation theory, paying special attention to mixed characteristic phenomena. Time permitting, I will discuss some possible extensions and in which ways the results are sharp.

7e64db0a59eb01df.title: Surfaces Browniennes et Explorations Métriques
7e64db0a59eb01df.abstract:
Les surfaces browniennes sont des surfaces aléatoires continues qui apparaissent comme limites de grandes surfaces discrètes choisies au hasard. Elles constituent aujourd’hui des modèles fondamentaux de géométrie aléatoire.
Dans cet exposé, je présenterai ces objets et quelques-unes de leurs propriétés fondamentales. Nous reviendrons sur plusieurs résultats marquants de la théorie, en partant des modèles discrets dont ces surfaces émergent. On verra notamment comment certains processus stochastiques apparaissent naturellement lorsqu’on explore ces surfaces à partir d’un point, et comment ils permettent de mettre en évidence certaines propriétés de Markov spatiales.
Aucun prérequis particulier n’est nécessaire : l’objectif sera surtout de donner une intuition des objets et des méthodes, plutôt que d’entrer dans les détails techniques.

7eae32de1e528464.title: Homotopy reconstruction: how we expanded on the seminal results of Niyogi, Smale, and Weinberger
7eae32de1e528464.speaker: Hana Dal Poz Kouřimská
7eae32de1e528464.abstract:
In this talk I will walk you through how we extended and strengthened the seminal work by Niyogi, Smale, and Weinberger on the learning of the homotopy type from a sample of an underlying space. In their work, Niyogi, Smale, and Weinberger studied samples of \(C^2\) manifolds with positive reach embedded in \(\mathbb{R}^d\). We extend their results in the following ways:
First, we consider both manifolds of positive reach --- a more general setting than \(C^2\) manifolds --- and sets of positive reach embedded in \(\mathbb{R}^d\). The sample P of such a set S does not have to lie directly on it. Instead, we assume that the two one-sided Hausdorff distances --- ε and δ --- between P and S are bounded. We provide explicit --- and tight --- bounds in terms of ε and δ, that guarantee that there exists a parameter r such that the union of balls of radius r centred at the sample P deformation-retracts to S. If time allows we will consider homotopy learning in a significantly more general setting --- we investigate sets of positive reach and submanifolds of positive reach embedded in a Riemannian manifold with bounded sectional curvature. To this end we introduce a new version of the reach in the Riemannian setting inspired by the cut locus. Yet again, we provide tight bounds on ε and δ for both cases (submanifolds as well as sets of positive reach), exhibiting the tightness by an explicit construction.

7f90cfd61645f286.title: Height one phenomena in p-adic Hodge theory
7f90cfd61645f286.speaker: Tasos MOULINOS
7f90cfd61645f286.abstract:
The syntomification of the integers (Z_p^syn) acts as a parameter space for p-adic cohomology theories. By the work of Drinfeld and others, it is known to carry a canonical formal group, and hence a map to the moduli stack of formal groups. Pulling back along this map gives rise to a certain line bundle equipped with a distinguished section "v_1". On the p-completed moduli stack of formal groups, the nonvanishing of v_1 defines the substack parametrizing "height-1" formal groups. Yet the preimage of this locus on Z_p^syn, when computed in p-adic formal stacks, is empty. There is a mismatch here because inverting v_1 on syntomic cohomology gives p-adic étale cohomology, but inverting it on the stack itself before passing to global sections gives nothing.
I will explain how passing to analytic stacks brings this missing locus into view. By realizing the p-completed moduli stack of formal groups as an analytic stack, we construct an algebro-geometric shadow of K(1)-localization. Applied to syntomification, this produces an analytic stack whose dualizable quasi-coherent sheaves recover p-adic Galois representations, and more generally lisse étale sheaves on the generic fiber of a p-adic formal scheme. I will explain how a perfected version of this construction depends only on the generic fiber, providing a geometric counterpart to purity results for K(1)-localized K-theory.
This is joint work in progress with Greg Andreychev.

80313ab580ded52f.title: Murmurations de zéros de fonctions $L$
80313ab580ded52f.speaker: Didier Lesesvre
80313ab580ded52f.abstract: Les murmurations sont un phénomène inattendu récemment découvert : les moyennes de coefficients automorphes présentent des oscillations structurées lorsque les nombres premiers croissent proportionnellement aux conducteurs d'une famille de fonctions $L$. Elles peuvent être interprétées comme des corrélations entre les signes des équations fonctionnelles et les coefficients automorphes, et ou encore comme des phénomènes de transitions dans les statistiques des petits zéros de fonctions $L$. Dans cet exposé, j'introduirai le phénomène des murmurations et les heuristiques qui permettent d'en comprendre les mécaniques, puis je présenterai le cas particulier des fonctions $L$ des carrés symétriques de formes modulaires. L'approche dans ce cas repose de manière centrale sur la formule des traces d'Eichler-Selberg.

Scientific Committee: Mark Kisin (Harvard University), Davesh Maulik (MIT), Carlos Simpson (Université Côte d'Azur).
The Summer School will be held at the Institut des Hautes Études Scientifiques (IHES) from July 5 to 16, 2027. IHES is located in Bures-sur-Yvette, south of Paris (40 minutes by train from Paris) - Access map
This school is open to everybody but intended primarily for young participants, including Ph.D. students and postdoctoral fellows.
Deadline for applications: February 28, 2027
2027 IHES Summer School - Local Systems in Algebraic Geometry
In recent years, there have been several exciting developments in the study of local systems. These include new insights into the topology of Hitchin systems, the theory of rigid local systems, and the rapidly evolving landscape of p-adic non-abelian Hodge theory. These breakthroughs touch upon deep connections between Hodge theory, arithmetic geometry, and representation theory.
The aim of this summer school is to offer young researchers the opportunity to explore these diverse and vibrant areas. Through a series of lecture courses by leading experts, participants will be introduced to foundational ideas in the field, as well as the major questions that guide the development of these areas. In addition, a selection of one-hour research talks will survey recent results and current directions, highlighting connections across different domains.

81f5130d919a8aaf.title: On supercuspidal representations in the l-adic cohomology of some local Shimura varieties
81f5130d919a8aaf.speaker: Yoichi Mieda
81f5130d919a8aaf.abstract: A local Shimura variety is a p-adic analogue of a Shimura variety. Its l-adic cohomology is expected to be related to the local Langlands correspondence. In the Lubin-Tate case, a supercuspidal representation appears only in the middle degree. In the GSp(4) case, a supercuspidal representation appears only in the degrees 3,4, and it appears in the degree 4 if and only if its L-parameter has non-trivial SL(2)-part. In this talk, I will explain my recent results in this direction for more general cases.

825091c772259bd3.title: Global lower resolvent estimate for damped waves
825091c772259bd3.speaker: Arthur Yax
825091c772259bd3.abstract:
In this talk, we will discuss the decay rates of damped waves when the Bardos-Lebeau-Rauch-Taylor Geometric Control Condition (GCC) fails, roughly speaking "there is a geodesic that does not enter the damped region".
Since decay rates are related to resolvent growth (Batty-Duyckaerts), we provide and present a result of global lower resolvent bound, as well as applications of it in various settings.

8342a404054eacb7.title: Lissage par peignes et trivialité locale pour les espaces homogènes au-dessus d’une courbe relative
8342a404054eacb7.speaker: Margot Bruneaux
8342a404054eacb7.abstract:
Soit $R$ un anneau local hensélien, de corps résiduel $\kappa$, soit $C$ une courbe projective lisse sur $R$, à fibres géométriquement connexes, soit $G$ un $C$-groupe réductif dont le tore radical $\operatorname{rad}(G)$ est isotrivial, et soit $E\to C$ un $G$-torseur.
Nous montrons que, si le noyau de l'isogénie centrale
\[
G_{\mathrm{sc}}\times_C \operatorname{rad}(G)\longrightarrow G
\]
est étale sur $C$, ou bien si $\kappa$ est un corps suffisamment grand, alors la trivialité de $E_\kappa\to C_\kappa$ pour la topologie de Zariski implique la trivialité de $E\to C$ pour cette même topologie.
Nous démontrons également une version « moyennée » de ce résultat, en supposant seulement que $\operatorname{rad}(G)$ est isotrivial, ainsi qu'une variante concernant les espaces homogènes projectifs, sans aucune hypothèse restrictive sur $G$.
Ces résultats ont notamment pour conséquences un principe local-global pour les torseurs sur les corps de fonctions de courbes au-dessus d'anneaux de valuation discrète henséliens, renforçant des travaux de Gille--Parimala--Suresh, ainsi qu'une version hensélienne d'un théorème de Drinfeld--Simpson.
Nos démonstrations sont de nature géométrique. Elles reposent sur des compactifications de torseurs et sur une technique de lissage par peignes, dans une version relative et arithmétique que nous développons en détail, en nous appuyant sur les travaux de Kollár et de Graber--Harris--Starr.
En collaboration avec Federico Scavia.

83b6ce1f8bc4646c.title: Dynamique de Aut(F_n) sur G^n, pour G compact et n grand
83b6ce1f8bc4646c.speaker: Florestan Martin-Baillon
83b6ce1f8bc4646c.abstract:
Donnons nous un groupe de Lie compact G et un entier n.
Un n-uplet (g_1, …, g_n) étant donné, on peut changer l’un des g_i en son inverse, ou multiplier l’un des
g_i par g_j (avec j différent de i) : ces opérations élémentaires ne changent pas le sous-groupe de G
engendré par les g_i. Ces opérations engendrent un groupe de difféomorphismes de G^n, et le problème
que nous aborderons est d’étudier la dynamique de ce groupe. Pour n suffisamment grand, nous verrons
qu’il est possible de classer les fermés et les mesures invariants.
83b6ce1f8bc4646c.location_text: Salle B405, bâtiment B, LAGA, Institut Galilée, Université Paris 13

84575c0c51910da8.title: Yugo Takanashi, tell me about the Langlands correspondence!
84575c0c51910da8.abstract:
We will begin by counting solutions of polynomial equations modulo primes and see how, in concrete examples, these counts are encoded in the Fourier coefficients of modular forms. We will then introduce the adelic point of view and Hecke operators, leading from modular forms to automorphic representations of GL_2. This will provide an introduction to the Langlands correspondence for GL_2, relating Hecke eigenvalues to Frobenius traces in two-dimensional Galois representations. We will conclude with a brief discussion of the conjectural picture in higher-dimensional cases.

848c2764cc76482e.title: Mod p de Rham cohomology of Shimura varieties
848c2764cc76482e.speaker: Martin Ortiz
848c2764cc76482e.abstract: The weight part of Serre's conjecture studies the modularity of certain spaces of mod p automorphic forms. In the case of Shimura varieties, this is usually done by considering their etale cohomology, with Serre weights as coefficients. One can also propose a similar conjecture for mod p de Rham cohomology of Shimura varieties, and I conjecture that the two approaches are equivalent. I can prove this generically for G=GL3, and some cases in GSp4. Moreover, for GSp4 this approach produces a generic entailment of Serre weights, which is completely invisible from the etale cohomology perspective.

8680b2f106b96358.title: Cohomological invariants of hermitian pairs over central simple algebras
8680b2f106b96358.speaker: Alexandre Lourdeaux
8680b2f106b96358.speaker_affiliation: Southern University of Science and Technology, Shenzhen, China
8680b2f106b96358.abstract:
In this talk we adapt the Witt theory of hermitian forms over a central simple algebras over fields of characteristic not 2, to hermitian pairs over fields of characteristic 2. Hermitian pairs are hermitian forms with an extra datum that is necessary to describe all simply connected simple groups of type $D_n$ in characteristic 2. In order to define useful and well-behaved cohomological invariants for hermitian pairs, we define them using unramified cohomology attached to the function field of the Severi-Brauer variety associated to the central simple algebra which is the base of our hermitian pairs. We obtain classifying invariants and related them to classical invariants in small degrees.
(This is a joint work with Yong Hu.)

86e7c3606d9ebbed.title: Sard’s theorem in infinite dimension: from real algebraic geometry to sub-Riemannian geometry
86e7c3606d9ebbed.speaker: Antonio Lerario
86e7c3606d9ebbed.abstract:
Sard’s theorem can fail in infinite dimension, even for polynomial maps with finite-dimensional targets. I will explain how quantitative estimates in real algebraic geometry, combined with finite-dimensional approximation, yield Sard criteria in this setting. I will then show how Kupka’s classical counterexample can be realized inside a sub-Riemannian endpoint map. This produces a smooth bracket-generating distribution whose endpoint map has no regular values, disproving the sub-Riemannian Sard conjecture in the smooth category.
Based on joint works with Luca Rizzi and Daniele Tiberio.

879740ae91d3b179.title: Training deep Transformers: mean-field models and convergence analysis
879740ae91d3b179.speaker: Raphael Barboni
879740ae91d3b179.abstract:
Transformers have become the dominant architecture in modern machine learning, yet the theoretical understanding of their training dynamics remains limited, especially for deep architectures with many layers and Attention heads. I will present a rigorous mathematical framework for analyzing gradient-based training of Transformers in the overparameterized regime, where depth, width and context length tend to infinity. This mean-field model features two types of measure representations: token distributions evolving through layers (measures over the token space), and Attention parameters at each layer (measures over the parameter space). Our contributions are twofold: (i) We prove the well-posedness of gradient flow curves in a conditional Wasserstein metric space, establishing a rigorous foundation for gradient-based Transformer training. (ii) We prove convergence of gradient flow towards global minima when the initial training risk is sufficiently low. A key technical contribution is providing necessary and sufficient conditions for injectivity of the Neural Tangent Kernel (NTK) for Attention mechanisms: we show that NTK injectivity is equivalent to linear independence of log-sum-exp functions modulo affine functions, a condition satisfied by diverse token distributions, including discrete distributions, uniform distributions, and Gaussian mixtures.
These results builds on joint works with M. de Hoop, T. Furuya, G. Peyré and F.-X. Vialard.

886374f67d232636.title: Heterotic string/F-theory duality and Borcea-Voisin construction for orbifolds
886374f67d232636.speaker: Gleb Koshevoy
886374f67d232636.abstract:
Calabi-Yau manifolds up to dimension 4 have found application in physics in heterotic string/ F-theory duality, N = 1 string vacua that admit both a heterotic description and a dual F-theory description. We are interested in a heterotic string on a Calabi-Yau orbifold. For a singular Calabi-Yau orbifolds of Fermat type, we consider a variant of the Borcea-Voisin construction of Calabi-Yau manifolds from an elliptic curve and some Calabi-Yau orbifolds.
For this we define Roan pairs of elements of a group and its dual in the Berglund-Hübsch-Krawits setting of the Landau-Ginzburg/Landau-Ginzburg mirror symmetry, and efficiently compute Hodge numbers of Calabi-Yau manifolds. For orbifolds of Fermat type, our formulas for Hodge numbers resemble the Batyrev-Borisov for orbifolds of toric hypersurfaces, but are different and give different sets of monomials for deformations.
The talk is based on joint work with Alexander Belavin and Maxim Malyutin.
886374f67d232636.department: Analyse Algébrique; Topologie et Géométrie Algébriques
886374f67d232636.organizer: Penka Georgieva, Elba Garcia-Failde, Ilia Itenberg, Alessandro Chiodo

892203e7a7e511fe.title: Nonrelativistic Conformal Collider Physics of Multiparticle Point Production
892203e7a7e511fe.speaker: Dam Thanh Son
892203e7a7e511fe.abstract:
Motivated by nuclear experiments where a few neutrons are produced by a local source, we develop a formalism of "nonrelativistic conformal collider physics." We define detector operators in the nonrelativistic conformal field theory describing fermions at unitarity. We reduce the problem of computing the momentum distribution and correlation between final particles produced by a local source ("point-produced") to the computation of correlation functions involving the detector operators. The general formalism is applied to the point production of three unitary fermions, where we find the momentum and angular distribution of final particles, and point production of a large number of fermions. We discuss a nonrelativistic version of celestial holography, which maps the asymptotic out-state to a quantum wave function in the so-called "oscillator frame." Based on arXiv:2608.18202 with Cyuan-Han Chang, Subham Dutta Chowdhury, and Ian Moult.

8af0db1291c997b3.title: Bijections bourgeonnantes pour cartes biparties et applications au modèle d’Ising
8af0db1291c997b3.speaker: Marie Albenque
8af0db1291c997b3.abstract:
Dans les 30 dernières années, beaucoup de bijections entre cartes planaires et arbres décorés ont été développées, et elles sont souvent cruciales pour l’analyse asymptotique de cartes plantaires aléatoires.
Dans cet exposé, je présentai un petit panorama des bijections bourgeonnantes et notamment une nouvelle bijection entre cartes biparties et des arbres bourgeonnants, qui généralisent des travaux antérieurs de Bousquet-Mélou et Schaeffer. Cela nous permet notamment d’obtenir de nouveaux résultats énumératifs pour des cartes décorées par un modèle d’Ising.
Travail en collaboration avec Laurent Ménard et Nicolas Tokka.

8b58ebbb6185cf66.title: Estimations précisées pour des opérateurs paraboliques
8b58ebbb6185cf66.speaker: Khalid Baadi
8b58ebbb6185cf66.abstract:
Cette thèse vise à obtenir des estimations affinées pour des opérateurs paraboliques selon deux perspectives différentes : les solutions fondamentales et les problèmes de Cauchy, avec un accent particulier sur les solutions des équations paraboliques, et les transformées de Riesz paraboliques, avec un accent particulier sur les propriétés analytiques de ces opérateurs.
Dans la première partie, nous établissons une théorie complète et universelle du caractère bien posé des problèmes de Cauchy paraboliques et de la construction de solutions fondamentales. Notre théorie va au-delà du cadre de Lions et repose sur une méthode variationnelle. Nous appliquons ensuite cette théorie aux équations paraboliques dégénérées, en fournissant une nouvelle preuve constructive des bornes d’Aronson. Enfin, nous ajoutons des termes d’ordre inférieur non bornés appartenant à des espaces de Lebesgue mixtes, voire de Lorentz, sous-critiques. Cette extension est rendue possible par l’identification et la démonstration de plongements de Sobolev adaptés et optimaux pour les laplaciens dégénérés.
Dans la seconde partie, nous déterminons l’intervalle optimal des $p\in(1,2)$ pour lequel les transformées de Riesz paraboliques à coefficients non réguliers sont bornées sur $\mathrm{L}^p$, en extrapolant à partir du cas $p=2$, qui correspond à l’estimation de Kato pour la racine carrée parabolique récemment établie. Nous considérons également le cas de parties elliptiques dégénérées. Nous commençons par élucider la décroissance spatio-temporelle limitée dans les estimations hors diagonale pour le gradient parabolique de la famille de résolvantes. Nous développons les techniques adaptées et recourons ensuite à un argument d’itération afin d’extrapoler la bornitude à l’intervalle approprié.

8c608e98e501a176.title: Beyond crystalline cohomology, rigid cohomology
8c608e98e501a176.speaker: Thomas Serafini
8c608e98e501a176.abstract: Crystalline cohomology is not a "good" cohomology for non-proper varieties - for instance, the crystalline H1 of the affine line is not finite-dimensional. Following ideas from Monsky and Washnitzer, Berthelot defined rigid cohomology on general varieties in characteristic p > 0, which provides the "right" extension of crystalline cohomology to arbitrary varieties. The central idea is that of overconvergence, i.e. considering analytic functions that converge not on a p-adic lifting of the variety, but rather on a neighborhood of it. Following and detailing the example of the affine line, we will build to the definition of rigid cohomology and explain its relation to p-adic differential equations.

8caedad483f08113.title: Uncertainty and unique continuation for dispersive PDEs at two time points
8caedad483f08113.speaker: Diego Fiorletta
8caedad483f08113.abstract:
Imposing too strong simultaneous decay or localization constraints on a function and its Fourier transform causes the function to vanish identically (Uncertainty Principle). The same applies to a solution to some dispersive evolutionary PDE if similar constraints are imposed on its profile at two different time points.
In the first part of the talk, I will introduce a manifestation of the Uncertainty Principle, the Benedicks-Amrein-Berthier Theorem. The $L^2$ norm on $\mathbb{R}^n$ of a function is controlled by the sum of the $L^2$ norms of the function and its Fourier transform observed outside sets of finite Lebesgue measure (Amrein-Berthier). In particular, no non-zero function supported on a set of finite Lebesgue measure can have a Fourier transform with the same property (Benedicks).
In the second part I will show how the above statements translate into qualitative and even quantitative unique continuation results when the Fourier transform is replaced by the propagator, evaluated at a non-zero time T, associated to some dispersive PDE, in particular considering linear and non-linear instances of the Schr\"odinger equation.

8cf2a51d13cfb6c4.title: 14e séminaire ITZYKSON - Dualité markovienne : méthodes algébriques et applications
8cf2a51d13cfb6c4.abstract:
14e séminaire ITZYKSON : Dualité markovienne : méthodes algébriques et applications
Le 14e séminaire Itzykson est organisé par Jean-René Chazottes (CPHT), Guillaume Dubach (CMLS), Ruben Minasian (IPhT) et Julio Parra-Martinez (IHES).
Depuis bientôt une quinzaine d’années l’axe math-physique de la FMJH organise un séminaire Itzykson tous les ans à l’IHES. Il s’agit d’une journée consacrée à un thème de physique mathématique, avec un cours et deux ou trois exposés spécialisés (en français ou en anglais selon le choix des orateurs).
Le prochain séminaire Itzykson portera sur la dualité markovienne, et ses liens avec les algèbres de Lie et les systèmes de particules en interaction. Ces sujets sont reliés par une même idée directrice : l'approche algébrique de la dualité, qui permet de construire et d'analyser des processus markoviens exactement solubles. Le séminaire donnera des perspectives algébriques, probabilistes et physiques sur des résultats récents, notamment au sujet des symétries des générateurs markoviens, des interprétations trajectorielles en génétique des populations, et des fluctuations macroscopiques hors d'équilibre.
Les cours et exposés de cette journée seront présentés par :
Cristian Giardinà (Università di Modena e Reggio Emilia)
Noemi Kurt (Goethe-Universität Frankfurt)
Frank Redig (TU Delft)
L’inscription est gratuite mais nécessaire et sera possible jusqu'au 23 novembre 2026. Un buffet-déjeuner sera offert aux participants qui s'y seront inscrits. Le séminaire sera filmé et diffusé en différé sur la chaîne YouTube de l'IHES.

8cfff265b2847517.title: Rigorous identification of dynamics from data
8cfff265b2847517.speaker: Konstantin Mischaikow
8cfff265b2847517.abstract:
It is well established that there is no algorithm that given countable data can identify up to conjugacy the global dynamics of nonlinear system. Thus, if we wish to systematically and rigorously understand data driven dynamics we need a courser characterization of dynamics that still capable capturing essential features, e.g., fixed points, periodic orbits, chaotic dynamics, bifurcations, etc.
With this in mind I will focus on two topics.
1. I will describe a combinatorial/algebraic topological approach to dynamics based on ideas of Conley and show that at this level dynamics can be learned given enough data and enough computing power. In addition, I will show that for low dimensional examples this approach is computationally tractable and requires relatively little data.
2. I will show how using encoders and latent dynamics this approach can give rigorous results about high dimensional systems. I will present examples that show that experimental results are much more promising than theory suggests.

Recent trends at the interface between information theory, probability, statistics and high-dimensional geometry raise new questions on the role and importance of entropy in the understanding of both asymptotic and finite range phenomena, in particular towards discrete structures and applications to areas such as quantum information, percolation and random matrices. Recent fruitful developments warrant imminent blossom of new ideas and results in this area in the near future.
Another central theme at the interface of High-Dimensional Probability and Convexity is the study of isoperimetric properties of log-concave measures (including isoperimetric-type questions related to convex bodies). This is not a mere curiosity: convexity and isoperimetry play an important role in the study of concentration of measure phenomena which is crucial for harnessing various high-dimensional effects in Probability as well as several applied fields.
The scope of the semester includes developing further connections between Information Theory and Convexity, in all of the different directions described above. The semester will aim to strengthen these powerful interdisciplinary methods, aiming towards challenging issues and applications, including the isoperimetry questions for log-concave measures, and super-concentration properties of models from random matrix theory and statistical mechanics.
The semester’s objective is to foster cross-fertilization between probability, analysis, information theory and convex geometry (continuous and discrete). By organizing two thematic pre-schools, we will ensure active participation by junior researchers, which should have a lasting effect on their careers, as well as influence the routes along which these research areas will be developed in the future. Our two workshops will further provide opportunities for many re- searchers from across the globe to interact and collaborate. We believe that close interactions between these disciplines are a necessary condition to address many mathematical challenges raised in the last decades, and that the timing is optimal to bring together all these powerful ideas which have been recently developed in several communities. Therefore, our proposed semester program will have a strong and lasting impact on High-Dimensional Probability, Convexity and Analysis as a whole.

A Siegel domain is a finite-volume subset of a symmetric space whose translates under the action of the relevant arithmetic group cover the entire space. In this talk, we consider an analogue for the p-adic period spaces introduced by Rapoport and Zink. We give a partial criterion for the existence of a Siegel domain and discuss its expected applications.

8de6607c53900f8d.title: Torus actions on compactified braid varieties and polytopality of subword complexes
8de6607c53900f8d.speaker: Mikhail Gorsky
8de6607c53900f8d.abstract:
Every cluster variety admits a faithful regular group action scaling all cluster variables. Given a partial compactification of a cluster variety, a natural question is whether this action extends to a regular action on the compactification. I will explain that, in the case of braid varieties for simple Lie groups, the answer is affirmative for brick compactifications. If the braid variety is an open Richardson variety in the flag variety, the same result holds for the corresponding closed Richardson variety. In the latter case, the faithfully acting group is a torus of rank the Kazhdan-Lusztig d-invariant. The same result holds for projected Richardson varieties. I will also explain that, in general, a braid variety is a torus if and only if each of its brick compactifications is a toric variety with respect to this extended action, if and only if the polar dual of the moment polytope for this action realizes the corresponding subword complex. The braid words satisfying this property turn out to be precisely the double root free words of V. Pilaud and C. Stump. This provides a novel approach to the longstanding open question of the polytopality of spherical subword complexes asked by A. Knutson and E. Miller in 2004, and in particular gives infinite families of subword complexes admitting polytopal realizations in dimension higher than the rank of the corresponding Coxeter group. The talk is based on joint work with Lara Bossinger and José Simental, arXiv:2609.12414.
This talk will take place in hybrid mode at the Institut Henri Poincaré.

Operator algebras are self-adjoint subalgebras of the bounded operators on a Hilbert space and divide into two main classes: C∗-algebras and von Neumann algebras, according to whether one demands that they are closed in the norm topology or the weak operator topology. When one first meets these algebras, they might look quite similar, but they have different natures as exemplified by the commutative case: via the Gelfand transform, abelian C∗-algebras are algebras of continuous functions vanishing at infinity on a locally compact Hausdorff space, while abelian von Neumann algebras are essentially bounded measurable functions on a measure space. These flavours persist in general. Topological concepts such as dimension and invariants such as K-theory pervade the study of C∗-algebras, while measure-theoretic style methods are often used to study von Neumann algebras.
The long thematic program OA will focus on operator algebras and its still evolving interactions with ergodic theory, topological dynamics, discrete subgroups of semisimple Lie groups, analytic, ergodic and geometric group theory, quantum information theory and random matrices.

8f10de0ff45c5eb1.title: Un degré de différentiabilité peut tout changer
8f10de0ff45c5eb1.speaker: Hélène Eynard-Bontemps
8f10de0ff45c5eb1.abstract:
Par lisse, certains entendent de classe $C^1$, d’autres $C^\infty$, alors que pour l’analyse élémentaire, la mécanique Newtonienne ou les questions de courbure, $C^2$ semble plus naturel… Les mathématiques regorgent d’exemples de problèmes ou de techniques qui sont extrêmement sensibles à la régularité dans laquelle on travaille, souvent pour des raisons profondes et intéressantes. J’illustrerai cette affirmation à l’aide d’exemples tirés de la dynamique unidimensionnelle (qui s’intéresse aux difféomorphismes de l’intervalle et du cercle) mais aux origines bien géométriques : le célèbre théorème de Denjoy et le bijou moins connu qu’est le lemme de Nancy Kopell.

8f822d7a3777c5a9.title: Moduli of vector bundles: from K3 surfaces to higher dimensional irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifolds of higher dimension.
8f822d7a3777c5a9.speaker: Kieran O'Grady
8f822d7a3777c5a9.abstract: After a quick review of the main results on moduli spaces of semistable sheaves on K3 surfaces we will recall a fundamental theorem of Verbitsky. The latter result opens the way to an extension to higher dimensional IHSM's of one key result valid for K3 surfaces, provided we consider vector bundles with certain characteristic classes. Lastly we will illustrate this principle by stating a recent result of ours on moduli spaces of stable vector bundles on IHSM's of Type K3^[2] (deformations of the Hilbert square of a K3 surface). 8fe97fd51029ffcd.title: A Dieudonné theory for analytic p-divisible groups
8fe97fd51029ffcd.speaker: Lucas Gerth
8fe97fd51029ffcd.abstract: We prove a classification of families of analytic p-divisible groups on adic spaces S over Qp in terms of Hodge–Tate triples on S, generalizing a theorem of Fargues. From this, for S a perfectoid space, we construct an analytic Dieudonné theory with values in mixed characteristic shtukas. As applications, we obtain moduli descriptions of local Shimura varieties of EL and PEL type. We also explain how to derive generalizations of the fundamental exact sequence of Colmez--Dospinescu--Nizio? on smooth Stein spaces.

903ed044580a6eb8.title: Tsen-Lang-like properties for quadratic forms over valued fields and function fields
903ed044580a6eb8.speaker: Nicolas Daans
903ed044580a6eb8.abstract:
In the 1930s, Artin conjectured that, for every natural number $d$ and every prime $p$, every form of degree $d$ in $d^2+1$ variables over the field of $p$-adic numbers $\mathbb{Q}_p$ has a non-trivial zero. In the terminology of Tsen-Lang theory, Artin conjectured that $\mathbb{Q}_p$ is a $C_2$-field. We now know that this conjecture is false in general: for example, there exists a form of degree 4 in 18 variables over $\mathbb{Q}_2$ with no non-trivial zero. The conjecture is true for quadratic forms, by an elementary application of Hensel's lemma. More generally, the behaviour of quadratic forms over henselian valued fields can often be understood quite well in terms of the value group and residue field. On the other hand, in contrast to the types of properties studied in Tsen-Lang theory, it is not at all clear how information about quadratic forms over a field $K$ can be used to understand quadratic forms over function fields over $K$. In this talk, we will discuss questions, results, and open problems concerning invariants of quadratic forms over fields and their behaviour under valuations and field extensions.
The talk will be based in part on joint work with K. J. Becher and V. Mehmeti.
903ed044580a6eb8.organizer: S. Anscombe, V. Bagayoko, H. Fournier

905168b43bf26504.title: Lagrangian Klein bottles in S^2 x S^2
905168b43bf26504.speaker: Nikolas Adaloglou
905168b43bf26504.abstract:
The study of Lagrangian submanifolds is a central theme in symplectic geometry. In this talk, after a brief introduction on the basics of symplectic geometry, we are going to study Lagrangian submanifolds in \(S^2\times S^2\), equipped with standard symplectic forms. Our goal is to understand which symplectic forms on \(S^2\times S^2\) carry Lagrangian Klein bottles. We will focus mainly on constructing the Klein bottles, using certain techniques from the theory of Lagrangian torus fibrations. This theory effectively reduces many constructive problems into problems of classical affine geometry of the plane.
Afterwards, I will explain how to obstruct the existence of some Lagrangian Klein bottles, using pseudoholomorphic curve techniques.
Together, the obstructive part and the constructive part completely determine which symplectic forms in \(S^2\times S^2\) carry a Lagrangian Klein bottle.

925a4c8748c5b99e.speaker_affiliation: Rényi Institute, Budapest, et EPFL, Lausanne
925a4c8748c5b99e.abstract:
What makes the chromatic number of a graph large?
There have been many attempts to answer this question. The
most natural approach is to look for unavoidable substructures in
graphs of large chromatic number. In 1943, Hadwiger made the
conjecture that every graph of chromatic number r can be
transformed into a complete graph of r vertices by a series of
edge contractions and vertex and edge deletions. This is one of
the most important unsolved problems in graph theory. After giving
a somewhat biased survey of the problem, I plan to report on some
related recent results, joint with Fox and Suk.

92c76a615e013520.title: Points critiques stationnaires pour un modèle champ de phase en mécanique de la rupture
92c76a615e013520.speaker: Martin Rakovsky
92c76a615e013520.abstract: Cette thèse est consacrée à la fonctionnelle de Mumford-Shah, utilisée pour modéliser les fissures fragiles dans un matériau élastique, et plus particulièrement à son approximation par la fonctionnelle d'Ambrosio--Tortorelli. Nous nous intéressons notamment à l'analyse asymptotique des points critiques de la fonctionnelle d'Ambrosio--Tortorelli, afin d'étendre aux points critiques la convergence des minimiseurs globaux obtenue par $Gamma$-convergence. Nous commençons par présenter les fonctionnelles de Mumford--Shah et d'Ambrosio--Tortorelli et le principe de l'approximation champ de phase. Ensuite, en dimension $1$, nous établissons la convergence des points critiques dans le cas où l'on rajoute à la fonctionnelle d'Ambrosio--Tortorelli une condition d'obstacle. En dimension quelconque, la convergence des points critiques est connue sous l'hypothèse supplémentaire que l'énergie d'Ambrosio--Tortorelli converge. En dimension $2$, nous montrons ce résultat en ne supposant qu'une partie de la convergence de l'énergie. Enfin, nous étudions le système parabolique associé aux équations vérifiées par les points critiques d'Ambrosio--Tortorelli. Nous établissons l'existence, les conditions d'unicité et la régularité des solutions de ce système, et obtenons en particulier leur régularité maximale en toute dimension.

9308b264c7e8a5bc.title: Algebraic Theory of Indefinite Theta Functions
9308b264c7e8a5bc.speaker: Kenz Kallal
9308b264c7e8a5bc.abstract:
Séminaire de géométrie arithmétique
Jacobi's theta function $\Theta(q) := 1 + 2q + 2q^4 + 2q^9 + \cdots $, and more generally the theta functions associated to positive-definite quadratic forms, have the property that they are modular forms of half-integral weight. The usual proof of this fact is completely analytic in nature, using the Poisson summation formula. However, $\Theta$ is also related to diffusion of heat on a uniform circle-shaped material: it is a restriction of the fundamental solution to the heat equation on a circle. By algebraically characterizing the heat equation as a specific flat connection on a certain bundle on a modular curve, we produce a completely algebraic technique for proving modularity of theta functions. More specifically, we produce a refinement of the algebraic theory of theta functions due to Moret-Bailly, Faltings--Chai, and Candelori. As a consequence of the algebraic nature of our theory and the fact that it applies to indefinite quadratic forms / non-ample line bundles (which the prior algebraic theory does not), we also generalize the Kudla--Millson analytic theory of theta functions for indefinite quadratic forms to the case of torsion coefficients. This is joint work with Akshay Venkatesh.

9318d88da2514dc2.abstract:
Recent breakthroughs have shown that AI can now prove theorems. At the same time, many of the deepest open questions about AI are, at heart, questions of mathematics and physics: high-dimensional geometry, non-convex optimisation, the statistical mechanics of learning. AI is becoming both a tool for and a subject of research in our fields, and a working knowledge of it is fast becoming essential for every young researcher.
This one-week school, funded by Qube Research & Technologies, will introduce the fundamental concepts of modern AI. It is designed for PhD students and early-career researchers in mathematics and theoretical physics with no prior specialisation in AI. The programme combines lectures with hands-on lab sessions.

934cdfe8c21f0d30.title: Kinetic theory: from long-range interactions to turbulence and quantum simulators, Paris
934cdfe8c21f0d30.abstract:
This is a thematic trimester programme with short courses, seminars and workshops on Kinetic theory: from long-range interactions to turbulence and quantum simulators.
January 18 to April 9, 2027 at the Institut Henri Poincaré, Paris
REGISTRATION IS MANDATORY AND FREE
IMPORTANT WARNING: Scam / Phishing / SMiShing! Note that ill-intentioned people may be trying to contact some of participants by email or phone to get money and personal details, by pretending to be part of the staff of the conference center. IHP and the organizers will NEVER contact you by phone on this issue and will NEVER ask you to pay for accommodation/ board / possible registration fee in advance.
Deadline for financial support request has been extended to: June 30th, 2026.
Summary
The program centers on the development of a unified understanding of kinetic theory in systems with long‑range interactions, with a particular emphasis on the quantum regime. Long‑range interacting quantum systems—realized experimentally in cold atoms, trapped ions, and polar molecules—exhibit rich dynamical behavior such as metastability, collisionless dynamics, anomalous transport, critical scaling, and turbulence‑like phenomena. These effects are often linked to the Vlasov equation, the collisionless kinetic equation that emerges in the thermodynamic limit. While Vlasov theory is conceptually well established in classical plasma physics, its systematic extension to quantum many‑body systems remains incomplete.
A key scientific motivation of the program is that different communities—mathematical physics, quantum many‑body theory, and AMO physics—address similar non‑equilibrium long‑range phenomena using different methods, preventing the emergence of a unified framework. The program aims to bridge these approaches and clarify conceptual connections between classical and quantum kinetic theories.
The scientific agenda spans several interconnected themes. One major theme is the analysis of classical transport, Vlasov dynamics, and their differences from Boltzmann kinetic theory, including how turbulence, chaos, and long‑range correlations emerge in classical systems. Another theme concerns the quantum generalizations of Vlasov theory, focusing on rigorous derivations and effective equations for quantum gases, including mean‑field and Gross–Pitaevskii limits, and the treatment of finite‑size effects in quantum simulators.
The program will explore non‑equilibrium many‑body dynamics in quantum systems, including quantum turbulence, cascade processes, ergodicity breaking, and anomalous scaling. A related line of inquiry concerns the dynamics of quantum correlations and entanglement, the onset of quantum chaos, and the characterization of universal quasi‑static dynamics in isolated systems. Another scientific direction is the study of effective theories in quantum matter, connecting renormalisation‑group methods with kinetic descriptions and identifying the regimes where classical scaling concepts can illuminate quantum behavior.
On the mathematical side, the program emphasizes rigorous derivations of macroscopic equations from microscopic many‑body dynamics, particularly in long‑range systems, and the formulation of effective transport equations, scaling limits, and mean‑field theories. Renormalisation‑group tools are highlighted both in their rigorous and approximate forms, with the aim of connecting microscopic models to emergent large‑scale behavior in many‑body systems.
Finally, the proposal identifies a scientific need to synthesize current insights into a coherent and predictive quantum kinetic theory for long‑range interactions, and to outline a roadmap of open problems invol

Lectures of the Introductory School
Gross-Pitaevskii equation from Quantum Dynamics
Serena Cenatiempo
While the theory of quantum mechanics describes interactions between the fundamental constituents of matter at microscopic scales, these interactions can lead to fascinating effects at the macroscopic level. Understanding the emergence of these phases from the microscopic description of quantum systems is a fundamental yet highly challenging mathematical problem. In this course, we will explore this challenge in the case of the interacting Bose gas, a system whose low-temperature phases exhibit the so-called Bose-Einstein condensation phenomenon, a phase of matter in which particles remain confined purely due to quantum effects. In particular, we will discuss how the non-linear Hartree and Gross-Pitaevskii equations arise as effective descriptions for the dynamics of a large number of particles exhibiting condensation, in relevant scaling regimes. Time permitting, we will also discuss how quantum fluctuations around the condensate can be accurately described by the so-called Bogoliubov theory.
Renormalization Group for Long-Range Interactions: From the Central Limit Theorem to the O(N) Model
Nicolò Defenu
These lectures introduce the renormalization group (RG) through the lens of long-range interactions, starting from the simplest setting where the method can be carried out exactly. We first formulate the central limit theorem as an RG problem. Summing and rescaling independent random variables defines a flow in the space of probability distributions, whose fixed point for any finite-variance distribution is the Gaussian. This shows how universality emerges, since all microscopic details other than the variance are irrelevant. Relaxing the finite-variance condition reveals a broader family of fixed points, the Lévy stable distributions. For these, the exponent α of the power-law tail alone selects the fixed point, and the Gaussian is recovered for all α ≥ 2. The fixed point therefore follows from the tail, but the converse does not hold, since the Gaussian basin of attraction contains distributions with arbitrary rapidly decaying tails. We then carry these ideas over to interacting field theories by considering the O(N) model with a long-range kinetic term proportional to q^σ. In the large-N limit the theory is solvable, and the competition between the analytic q^2 and the non-analytic q^σ terms produces a threshold σ* separating long-range and short-range universality, in direct analogy with the single-variable problem. Finally, a calculation at order 1/N shows how the anomalous dimension of the short-range fixed point shifts the boundary to σ* = 2 − η_SR. It also explains why the non-analytic term is not renormalized, which fixes η_LR = 2 − σ throughout the long-range regime.

9474e939c66d1996.speaker: Gregorio Baldi
9474e939c66d1996.abstract: In this joint work with J. Lam, we discuss explicit examples of non-integral variations of Q-Hodge structures. Our approach leverages Fenchel--Nielsen-type parameterizations, due to Kabaya and Maskit, of the Teichmüller component of relative character varieties. Additionally, we discuss various Diophantine results concerning the O_{K,S}-integral points of such character varieties, and give a new proof of Beauville's classical theorem on families of elliptic curves. If time permits, pathological behaviors of the Hodge locus of non-integral QVHS will also be presented.

948f8b866a315159.title: Constructions de flots d’Anosov sur des 3-variétés hyperboliques
948f8b866a315159.speaker: François Béguin
948f8b866a315159.abstract: Un flot sur une 3-variété est dit d'Anosov s’il existe, en tout point, une direction contractée et une direction dilatée par ce flot. La dynamique des flots d’Anosov en dimension 3 est intimement reliée à la topologie des variétés portant ces flots. Une des grandes problématique du domaine est de déterminer quelles 3-variétés — notamment quelles 3-variétés hyperboliques — portent des flots d’Anosov. La plupart ? Presqu’aucune ? Je présenterai deux résultats, obtenus avec C. Bonatti, B. Ma et B. Yu, qui apportent des éléments de réponses à ces questions.

957bd11bbe483012.title: Conférence de Stéphanie Debette, « Santé cérébrale, défi sociétal du 21ème siècle »
957bd11bbe483012.abstract:
« Santé cérébrale, défi sociétal du 21ème siècle »
La santé cérébrale est un enjeu majeur du XXIᵉ siècle, qui dépasse le seul domaine médical pour toucher aux dimensions sociétales, économiques et stratégiques. Plus d'une personne sur trois sera concernée par une maladie cérébrale au cours de sa vie. Ces maladies sont la première cause de handicap et la deuxième cause de décès dans le monde. Le vieillissement de la population augmente le poids des pathologies liées à l'âge, et les troubles de santé mentale progressent chez les jeunes.
La présentation se concentrera sur les maladies vasculaires cérébrales, particulièrement fréquentes et graves. Parmi elles, la maladie des petits vaisseaux cérébraux est la plus répandue. On peut la repérer tôt en imagerie.
Nous évoquerons les progrès récents dans la compréhension de ses mécanismes biologiques et dans l’analyse d'images cérébrales par intelligence artificielle
Cette conférence hybride sera suivie d'un moment convivial.

95db7503a93ba418.title: Defects in skein theory
95db7503a93ba418.speaker: Juan Ramón Gómez García
95db7503a93ba418.abstract:
Skein theory forms a once-extended categorified TQFT that assigns skein algebras to surfaces and skein modules to 3-manifolds.
These algebras and modules are defined in terms of generators of topological flavor, namely a certain class of graphs embedded in the 3-manifold,
modulo the relations induced by evaluating (locally) these graphs in an underlying ribbon category. In this talk I will explain how this picture
can be extended to stratified manifolds with strata of codimension 1 and 2 (called defects). Using the appropriate algebraic structures,
we can define evaluation functors around defects, yielding notions of stratified skein modules and algebras. Examples of these structures
are provided by the formalism of parabolic restriction. As an application, we use an interpolating version of parabolic defects to construct
a categorification of the Turaev coproduct in the HOMFLY skein algebra.

965960f6ccbd08e9.title: The Doubly Conformal Dispersion Relation
965960f6ccbd08e9.speaker: Balt van Rees
965960f6ccbd08e9.abstract:
We provide a simple derivation of the conformal dispersion relation of Carmi and Caron-Huot which reconstructs a CFT four-point function from its double discontinuity. We exhibit a hidden conformal symmetry which explains the appearance of the "magic variable" x as a simple cross-ratio, built from four physical cross-ratios. We also introduce a regulator in the double discontinuity operation and then prove that one subtraction suffices for all integrals to converge.

96ebc0808993dd3e.title: Ruben Haalebos - Portfolio Decarbonization under Incomplete Carbon and Transition Information
96ebc0808993dd3e.abstract: We study dynamic portfolio decarbonization under incomplete information about firms' carbon intensities and the underlying transition state. The investor maximizes expected utility of terminal wealth net of a penalty on perceived cumulative financed emissions. Asset returns and carbon intensities depend on a stochastic transition factor, while the investor may need to infer the current transition state, its long-run mean and firms' carbon intensities from market observations and periodic noisy disclosures. The optimal strategy combines a Merton-type component with climate-dependent expected-return adjustments, a direct carbon intensity penalty and intertemporal hedging demands associated with stochastic carbon intensities and learning. In a numerical application, incomplete information has limited effects on welfare and target satisfaction when prior beliefs are well specified. By contrast, biased beliefs generate welfare losses in either direction but asymmetric environmental consequences: optimistic and pessimistic beliefs induce opposite portfolio tilts and therefore affect the probability of exceeding the cumulative emissions target differently.

970c7dbfcd1f9463.title: Colloquium : "Nielsen meets Weil"
970c7dbfcd1f9463.speaker: Maxim Kontsevich
970c7dbfcd1f9463.abstract: A hundred years ago Jacob Nielsen proposed a lower bound on the number of fixed points of a self-map, utilizing the action on the fundamental group. The natural bookkeeping device is the Reidemeister trace, a linear combination of twisted conjugacy classes. I will review the classical theory and propose an analogue for varieties over finite fields, in the spirit of the rationality part of the Weil conjectures, where the self-map is replaced by the Frobenius automorphism. The resulting conjecture can be checked in non-trivial examples.

9817b8cf32f5e5d2.title: On the undecidability of the QWEP for C*-algebras
9817b8cf32f5e5d2.speaker: Isaac Goldring
9817b8cf32f5e5d2.abstract: In his landmark 1993 paper, Kirchberg introduced a property of C*-algebras called the QWEP, which stands for “quotient of the weak expectation property”. As the name suggests, the property is defined by the fact that the algebra is a quotient of a C*-algebra with the weak expectation property, which was a property introduced by Lance years earlier in connection with the theory of tensor products of C*-algebras. While at first glance this seems to be a strange property, Kirchberg showed that whether or not every C*-algebra has the QWEP is equivalent to the famous Connes Embedding Problem (CEP) from von Neumann algebra theory. The CEP remained open for nearly 50 years until its recent refutation in 2020 via a result in quantum complexity theory (as well as the equivalence with Kirchberg’s QWEP conjecture). Several years ago, I showed that the QWEP is an axiomatizable property of C*-algebras. In this talk, I will present joint work with Aruseelan and Hart where we show that the QWEP does not have an effective axiomatization and, in fact, there can be no effectively axiomatizable satisfiable theory of C*-algebras all of whose models have the QWEP (modulo some nontrivially conditions). The proofs uses the connection with the quantum complexity results mentioned above as well as other techniques from C*-algebra theory. No prior knowledge of continuous logic, operator algebras, or quantum complexity will be assumed.

How to get to IHES
This workshop will bring together experts in string theory and quantum field theory to discuss recent advances in these fields, and also to foster collaboration between the Korean and French theoretical and mathematical physics communities.
Key topics will include conformal field theory, generalized symmetries and topological quantum field theory, scattering amplitudes, quantum gravity/holography, black-hole physics.
The event will mark the second edition of a new biennial series, alternating between the Korea Institute for Advanced Study (KIAS) and institutions in the Saclay region, near Paris, and it will feature speakers both from Saclay and Korea, as well as worldwide experts in these areas.

9a45aa9c03af67e7.title: On the Wasserstein Geodesic Principal Component Analysis of probability measures
9a45aa9c03af67e7.speaker: Alice Le Brigant
9a45aa9c03af67e7.abstract:
The GdT OT-PDE-ML is a research seminar organized by the ParMA team. It brings together researchers to discuss recent theoretical and numerical developments at the crossroads of Optimal Transport theory, Partial Differential Equations and Machine Learning.
Abstract: In this talk we discuss how to perform Principal Component Analysis (PCA) of a dataset whose elements are probability distributions, compared using the Wasserstein distance. The goal is to identify geodesic curves in the space of probability measures that best capture the modes of variation of the underlying dataset. To achieve this, we leverage the Riemannian interpretation of the Wasserstein metric. We first address the case of a collection of centered Gaussian distributions, and show how to lift the computations in the space of invertible linear maps using Bures-Wasserstein geometry. For the more general setting of absolutely continuous probability measures, we use Otto-Wasserstein geometry and neural networks to parameterize geodesics in Wasserstein space. Finally, we compare to classical tangent PCA through various examples and provide illustrations on real-world datasets.

9baffe2d745b97da.title: Development of new post hoc methods for structured data
9baffe2d745b97da.speaker: Romain Périer
9baffe2d745b97da.abstract: Cette soutenance présentera certaines de mes contributions à la théorie des tests multiples. Je présenterai notamment de nouvelles méthodologies pour contrôler les fausses découvertes grâce à des bornes de confiance et des procédures de contrôle du False Discovery Rate (FDR). Ces procédures assurent un recouvrement post hoc, ce qui signifie qu'elles préservent les garanties statistiques même après l'intervention du praticien --- comme le p-hacking ou le HARKing --- et offrent une plus grande flexibilité en lui permettant de sélectionner l'ensemble de rejets de manière adaptative. De plus, ces méthodes exploitent également la structure des données ; elles vont au-delà de l'hypothèse i.i.d. traditionnelle en prenant en compte l'hétérogénéité des données afin d'améliorer la puissance statistique.

9cf62b913497ab87.title: Fomin-Kirillov algebras
9cf62b913497ab87.speaker: Leandro Vendramin
9cf62b913497ab87.abstract:
Fomin-Kirillov algebras EnE_nEn​ are quadratic algebras introduced by Fomin and Kirillov in the late 1990s to study the combinatorics of Schubert polynomials. They contain a commutative subalgebra isomorphic to the cohomology ring of the flag manifold, and they are related to Nichols algebras over the symmetric group. It has been known for some time that Fomin-Kirillov algebras EnE_nEn​ are finite-dimensional for n≤5n\leq 5n≤5, but whether this holds for n>5n>5n>5 has remained open since the algebras were introduced. In this talk, I will review basic properties of Fomin-Kirillov algebras and present joint work with Andruskiewitsch, Angiono, Heckenberger, Lentner, and Reiher, in which we prove that Fomin-Kirillov algebras EnE_nEn​ are infinite-dimensional for all n>5n>5n>5.
This talk will take place on Zoom only.

9f79361b0f0772b7.title: De la modélisation aux problèmes inverses : une méthodologie pour les systèmes dynamiques en biomédecine.
9f79361b0f0772b7.speaker: Pierre Monmarché
9f79361b0f0772b7.abstract:
Oratrice : Annabelle Collin (Université de Nantes)
Résumé : Les systèmes dynamiques constituent un cadre naturel pour décrire l'évolution temporelle et spatiale de nombreux phénomènes rencontrés en biologie, et en médecine. Qu'ils soient formulés sous la forme d'équations différentielles ordinaires (EDO) ou d'équations aux dérivées partielles (EDP), ces modèles permettent de formaliser des mécanismes biologiques, physiologiques ou épidémiologiques et d'étudier leur dynamique.
Dans cet exposé, nous présenterons les principales étapes d'une démarche de modélisation mathématique appliquée à des problématiques biomédicales : construction et formalisation du modèle, étude de ses propriétés théoriques, approximation numérique, puis confrontation du modèle aux données à travers la résolution de problèmes inverses. Une attention particulière sera portée à l'estimation de paramètres et d'états non directement observables, ainsi qu'aux difficultés associées à l'identifiabilité, aux incertitudes et au caractère potentiellement bruité ou incomplet des observations.
Nous nous intéresserons plus particulièrement aux approches séquentielles, qui permettent de mettre à jour progressivement l'estimation de l'état du système et de ses paramètres au fur et à mesure de l'acquisition de nouvelles données.
Cette démarche sera illustrée sur un exemple volontairement simple, permettant de mettre en évidence les principales étapes méthodologiques tout en montrant comment des modèles relativement parcimonieux peuvent déjà conduire à des résultats quantitatifs pertinents et exploitables dans un contexte de santé publique.
Retransmission : https://www.ihp.fr/fr/live-0

a0e4a946883cae1d.title: FAMED triangulations will live forever
a0e4a946883cae1d.speaker: Antonin GUILLOUX
a0e4a946883cae1d.abstract:
I will present a joint work with Fathi Ben Aribi and Ka Ho Wong around volume conjectures. Roughly, a volume conjecture describes a link between the semiclassical limit of a quantum invariant of a triangulated hyperbolic knot complement and the hyperbolic geometry of its complement. There are several flavors and we will focus of a version by Andersen and Kashaev.
Recently, arguments by Fathi and Ka Ho reduce essentially this conjecture to a combinatorial property of the triangulation, called FAMED. I will explain this condition and how to extensively test this condition, and a path toward a proof of the volume conjecture.

a160eee0f090d283.title: Around the Pearcey Process
a160eee0f090d283.speaker:
Thomas Chouteau
Pierre Lazag
a160eee0f090d283.abstract:
I. Pierre Lazag (Université Catholique de Louvain-la-Neuve) - "An introduction to the Pearcey point process and number rigidity"
The Pearcey point process is a universal determinantal point process appearing in the scaling limit of a random integrable model near a cusp singularity of its limit shape. In this talk, I will introduce the Pearcey point process and describe how it arises in models such as non-intersecting Brownian motions and random skew-plane partitions. If time permits, I will discuss its analytic and probabilistic properties such as number rigidity.
II. Thomas Chouteau (Université de São Paulo) - "Multiplicative Statistics of the Pearcey Process and the Boussinesq Hierarchy"
The Pearcey process is a universal point process that arises in the study of various integrable models. In this talk, we investigate its multiplicative statistics through three distinct representations of deformed Pearcey kernels: an IIKS integrable representation, a finite-temperature representation, and a representation for a conditionally thinned process. These three frameworks provide complementary viewpoints to analyze multiplicative statistics and yield several new results. From an integrable systems perspective, we show that the logarithmic derivative of the multiplicative statistics with respect to one of the deformation parameters solves the first two equations of the Boussinesq hierarchy, and we determine the associated initial conditions. Finally, we connect these multiplicative statistics to a pair of auxiliary functions satisfying a coupled system of integro-differential equations.
a160eee0f090d283.organizer: Jérémie Bouttier, Marco Mazzola, Sofia Tarricone

a30b364eaa318fa2.title: ProofTree: Structured Representations for Human-Centred Mathematical Exploration
a30b364eaa318fa2.speaker: Carl Jontza
a30b364eaa318fa2.abstract:
If formal proofs become abundant, how can we help people find mathematics they care about and explore it in ways that are understandable and engaging? I will present ongoing work on ProofTree, investigating a persistent, versioned graph of goals, assumptions, and alternative arguments as an intermediate representation connecting human-readable reasoning with formal proofs. The aim is to support discovery, understanding, and human guidance at levels of abstraction suited to a person’s background, interests, and objectives.
A case study from Lean-based proof hierarchies, involving confusion between an induction hypothesis and a proof obligation, will motivate technical questions about preserving logical scope, revising arguments, and maintaining links to checked proofs. I will discuss what records of exploration should preserve for subsequent reuse, and outline an evaluation agenda that considers mathematical relevance, understanding, and user experience alongside proof completion and human and computational cost.

a329e1844f0ce445.title: Reprojections des pavages par le Spectre et motifs hexagonaux
a329e1844f0ce445.speaker: Arnaud Chéritat
a329e1844f0ce445.abstract: L'une des monotuiles apériodiques découvertes en 2023 par Smith et al. est appelée spectre. On peut associer naturellement aux pavages par le spectre un relevé à $\mathbb{R}^4$ du graphe des arêtes du pavage. On peut faire de même avec un autre graphe, issu d'une décoration particulière de la tuile. En reprojetant ces graphes vers le plan selon différentes directions, on observe des motifs intéressants. J'ai effectué une analyse détaillée de l'un d'entre eux.

a54947280dbc198b.title: Régulateur cyclosyntomique des corps de nombres ~~ Transfer principles and the Kato–Kuzumaki conjecture
a54947280dbc198b.speaker: Quentin Gazda, Felipe Gambardella
a54947280dbc198b.abstract:
Felipe Gambardella (Orsay), 2-3pm
Transfer principles and the Kato–Kuzumaki conjecture.
Seeking a Diophantine characterisation of cohomological dimension of fields, Kato and Kuzumaki introduced the C_i^q property for every pair of non-negative integers i and q. These properties are inspired by Lang’s notion of a C_i field and Bloch-Kato’s conjecture relating Milnor K-theory with Galois cohomology. An interesting property of C_i fields is that they satisfy a transfer principle with respect to equicharacteristic complete discrete valuations – i.e. if a field k is C_i, then the field of Laurent series k((t)) is C_{i+1}. However, for the C_i^q property, no such transfer result is known to hold and the situation is more subtle than the one of C_i fields. For instance, the optimistic statement “k((t)) satisfies C_{i+1}^q whenever k satisfies C_i^q ” is false. This talk reports on joint work with Konstantinos Kartas. I will present a transfer principle for C_i fields with respect to non-discrete valuations. This principle has as a corollary a transfer principle for a variant of the Kato-Kuzumaki properties. Moreover, this is enough to establish the Kato-Kuzumaki conjecture for several fields of arithmetic interest such as the perfection of Fp((t_1)) . . . ((t_n)) or C(x_1, . . . , x_n)((t_1)) . . . ((t_m)) and to establish a strengthening of the C_1^1 property for Q_p introduced by Wittenberg.
Quentin Gazda (IMJ-PRG), 3.30-4.30pm
Régulateur cyclosyntomique des corps de nombres
Dans cet exposé, nous présenterons un travail en commun avec Tess Bouis où nous construisons une version q-déformée du régulateur de Dirichlet p-adique des corps de nombres. De manière surprenante, notre construction ne nécessite ni la complétion en p, ni que p soit premier. Nous interpréterons ce régulateur à travers la notion de q-Gauges, objets globaux ayant vocation à interpoler les structures de Hodge p-adiques en chaque p.

a5b13a77b85fcc84.title: Zeta Values as Moments: A Random Matrix Theory
a5b13a77b85fcc84.speaker: Hartmut Monien
a5b13a77b85fcc84.abstract: The values of the Riemann zeta-function $\zeta\left(\alpha+\beta n\right)$ with $\alpha>1$, $\beta>0$ and $n$ a positive integer can be viewed as moments of a probability distribution. In my talk I will construct the corresponding random matrix model and determine its asymptotic spectral curve, which exhibits an unusual feature, the complete asymptotics of its partition function and uniform approximations to its correlation functions using a discrete version of Riemann-Hilbert problem with Airy and Bessel asymptotics. This relates a problem in number theory to ideas of Vershik and Okounkov in the representation theory of the symmetric group.

a6590d9b3aadaf36.title: Constructing actions with Fraïssé limits
a6590d9b3aadaf36.speaker: Paolo Boldrini
a6590d9b3aadaf36.abstract: Given an action of a countable group on the Cantor space, clopen subsets can be compared by cutting and moving through the action or by evaluating them on invariant measures. Dynamical comparison asserts that the measure-theoretic notion controls the dynamical one. Since its first appearance, dynamical comparison has been verified for a wide variety of actions. In this talk, I will survey some recent positive results in this direction and present the construction of the first examples of topologically free minimal actions that fail dynamical comparison, obtained in a joint work with Akshara Prasad. The construction is based on an algebraic invariant known as the type semigroup and involves Fraïssé limits of Boolean algebras equipped with monoid-valued measures.

a7356c5a669739dc.title: Horizon flux-balance laws in the multiscale perturbation
a7356c5a669739dc.speaker: Ali M. Seraj
a7356c5a669739dc.speaker_affiliation: Institute for Research in Fundamental Sciences (IPM), Tehran
a7356c5a669739dc.abstract:
Séminaire Amplitudes et Gravitation sur l'Yvette (IHES/IPhT)
I study the evolution of the event horizon in a “two-timescale” perturbative expansion around a stationary black hole. This leads to strong constraints on the “coarse-grained” horizon dynamics. At leading order, the horizon exhibits an “adiabatic rigidity”: the leading corrections to its angular velocity and inaffinity remain uniform on each horizon cut, while evolving on the slow timescale. We then provide a systematic procedure for transforming a perturbative bulk solution, given for example in Lorenz gauge, to an ingoing Newman--Unti gauge adapted to the horizon, allowing the perturbed horizon geometry to be extracted directly from the metric. Finally, we formulate “horizon conservation laws” associated with horizon symmetries, including energy, dynamical entropy, and angular momentum. We expand the charges through second order and their fluxes through third order in perturbation theory, providing a framework for future applications to horizon absorption and backreaction in extreme mass-ratio inspirals.

a7b2d95119407252.title: Comptage exact de courbes sur le tore épointé
a7b2d95119407252.speaker: Mingkun Liu
a7b2d95119407252.abstract: Le théorème des géodésiques premières affirme que, sur une surface hyperbolique de genre g avec n pointes, le nombre de géodésiques fermées primitives de longueur au plus L est asymptotique à $e^L/L$. Mirzakhani a montré dans sa thèse que, si on ne compte que celles qui ne s'intersectent pas, la croissance devient polynomiale, d'ordre $L^{6g-6+2n}$. Dans cet exposé, on se concentre sur le cas du tore épointé, et on compte les courbes selon leur longueur de mot plutôt que leur longueur hyperbolique. On verra que, dans ce cadre, il est possible d'obtenir des formules exactes. Il s'agit d'un travail en commun avec Filippo Baroni et David Fisac.
