rec.title: Amplitudes for Superradiant Scattering
rec.speaker: Panagiotis Marinellis
rec.speaker_affiliation: Center for Fundamental Physics, ShanghaiTech University, Shangai
rec.abstract:
Séminaire Amplitudes et Gravitation sur l'Yvette (IHES/IPhT)
Superradiance allows incident radiation to extract energy from a rotating or charged body. In this talk, I will present a QFT description of this phenomenon using on-shell scattering amplitudes. Working at wavelengths much larger than the size of the target, we describe its internal transitions through mass-changing amplitudes and spectral functions. I will explain how electrostatic and rotational energy shifts enter these transitions, and how the competition between absorption and stimulated emission produces amplification. We first derive the absorption and emission probabilities in this effective description, then take their classical limit to match to black hole observables. A charged scalar model provides a concrete illustration through matching to the low frequency Reissner–Nordström absorption cross section, before extending the discussion to rotational superradiance and matching the Kerr black hole’s response function. I will conclude by showing the connection to classical observables in the KMOC framework and the consistency with the black hole area law.

rec.title: Reentrant Algebraic Order at High Temperature
rec.speaker: Joan Elias Miró
rec.abstract:
Increasing temperature typically drives systems from order to disorder. This familiar expectation can fail, however, when a system is coupled to a critical sector, a phenomenon often discussed in the context of symmetry non-restoration. In this talk, I will present a UV-complete model with a global U(1) symmetry in d = 2 + 1 dimensions that exhibits a Berezinskii-Kosterlitz-Thouless (BKT) ordered phase at arbitrarily high temperatures. A careful separation of scales yields a two-dimensional Euclidean effective field theory whose construction remains perturbatively controlled even when its soft modes become strongly coupled. We determine the BKT phase boundary by carefully matching this theory to existing lattice Monte Carlo results. The high-temperature phase supports gapless static modes and algebraically decaying correlations even as $T \to \infty$. I will end by discussing spin lattice realizations of the model.

rec.title: Kneser Graphs: Variations on a Theme
rec.speaker: Matej Stehlik
rec.abstract:
Kneser graphs are a classical family of graphs that play a central role in graph colouring. In 1978, Lovasz determined their chromatic number using topological methods. Schrijver later strengthened this result by identifying vertex-critical induced subgraphs of Kneser graphs, now known as Schrijver graphs.
The talk will survey several recent developments involving these graph families, including constructions of edge-critical subgraphs of Schrijver graphs, a common generalisation of Kneser and Schrijver graphs, and a new family of vertex-critical graphs for which the standard topological lower bounds on the chromatic number are not tight.
The talk is based on joint work with Carmen Arana, Penny Haxell, and Tomas Kaiser.

rec.title: Grid Minors in planar graphs
rec.speaker: Eileen Robinson
rec.abstract:
In 1984, Robertson and Seymour showed that the treewidth of a planar graph with no t × t grid as minor is bounded by a function g(t). Together with Thomas, they later proved that g(t) can be taken to be linear. The current best known bound, due to Gu and Tamaki (2012), is g(t) ≤ 9/2 t − 11/2. In this talk, I will show an improved bound of g(t) ≤ 4t + O(1), which is within a factor 2 of optimal.
This talk is based on joint work with Wouter Cames van Batenburg, Quentin Claus, Gwenaël Joret, Robin Petit and Jean-Florent Raymond.

rec.title: Combinatorial tools for posets topology and simplicial complexes
rec.speaker: Lucas Pouillart
rec.abstract: Topological theory of posets originates from a simple observation : the Möbius function of an interval of a poset P can be interpreted as the Euler characteristic of a simplicial complex. It turned out that in a lot of cases, these complexes hold a lot more information on P and that a lot of interesting examples satisfy the (homotopy) Cohen-Macaulay property, which gives both nice topological and algebraic properties. A lot of techniques were developed by combinatorialists to prove the Cohen-Macaulay property and give interpretations of algebraic and topological problems for posets as enumeration problems, and I will present some of them in this talk.

rec.title: Informative Trains: A Memory-Efficient Journey to a Self-Stabilizing Leader Election Algorithm in Anonymous Graphs
rec.speaker: Sylvain Gay
rec.abstract:
We study the self-stabilizing leader election problem in anonymous n-nodes networks. Achieving self-stabilization with low space memory complexity is particularly challenging, and designing space-optimal leader election algorithms remains an open problem for general graphs. In deterministic settings, it is known that Ω(log log n) bits of memory per node are necessary [Blin et al., Disc. Math. & Theor. Comput. Sci., 2023], while in probabilistic settings the same lower bound holds for some values of n, but only for an unfair scheduler [Beauquier et al., PODC 1999]. Several deterministic and probabilistic protocols have been proposed in models ranging from the state model to the population protocols. However, to the best of our knowledge, existing solutions either require Ω(log n) bits of memory per node for general worst-case graphs, or achieve low state complexity only under restricted network topologies such as rings, trees, or bounded-degree graphs.
In this paper, we present a probabilistic self-stabilizing leader election algorithm for arbitrary anonymous networks that uses O(log log n) bits of memory per node. Our algorithm operates in the state model under a synchronous scheduler and assumes knowledge of a global parameter N = Θ(log n). We show that, under our protocol, the system converges almost surely to a stable configuration with a unique leader and stabilizes within O(poly(n)) rounds with high probability.
Our algorithm is inspired by the uniform constant-state leader election protocol in [Vacus and Ziccardi, PODC 2025] for the beeping model (without self-stabilization). A novel component of our approach is the introduction of an information train mechanism that propagates O(log n)-bit information across the network while requiring only O(loglog n) local memory per node. We believe this mechanism may be of independent interest for the design of space-efficient self-stabilizing distributed algorithms.

rec.title: From linear logic proof-nets to signed digraphs
rec.speaker: Raffaele Di Donna
rec.abstract: I will present some recent results from my doctoral research on linear logic proof-nets, using a purely graph-theoretic language. The general idea is to study the relationship between the structural, geometric properties of linear logic proofs and their logical features, with particular emphasis on the role of connectivity. After a brief introduction to proof-nets and the Danos-Regnier correctness criterion, I will present my contributions and show that one of them is a special case of a more general result about signed directed multigraphs. The result provides a sufficient condition for the existence of a directed cycle consisting exclusively of arcs of a given sign, based on restrictions involving paths, signs and forbidden patterns.

rec.title: Introduction aux "enhanced categories"
rec.speaker: Sylvain Douteau
rec.abstract: Dans cette exposé, j'exposerai dans les grandes lignes la notion de "enhanced categories" introduite par Kaledin. Celle-ci est très inspirée de la théorie des dérivateurs, et vise à remplacer à la fois le formalisme 1-catégorique des catégories modèles et les raisonnements homotopiques des infinies catégories

rec.title: Les polygraphes réguliers et leur théorème de recollement homotopique
rec.speaker: Clémence Chanavat
rec.abstract:
Je commencerai par présenter deux (ou trois) manières de régulariser les polygraphes, que j'appellerai méthode-Hadzihasanovic, méthode-Steiner et, si le temps le permet, méthode-Henry.
J'expliquerai pourquoi la méthode-Hadzihasanovic ne produit pas toujours des polygraphes, à moins que l'on impose aux ∞-catégories strictes des lois d'échange supplémentaires, dictées par des égalités de topologie combinatoire.
Je terminerai par un théorème de recollement, issu de mes derniers travaux, qui assure que certains de ces polygraphes sont librement générés en un sens homotopique, ce qui signifie que ce sont aussi des polygraphes dans la théorie des (∞, n)-catégories.

rec.title: Combinatoire des mots, combinatoire énumérative et combinatoire algébrique autour de la forme normale alternante des tresses
rec.speaker: June Roupin
rec.abstract:
Les tresses sont des objets topologiques qui possèdent de très bonnes propriétés combinatoires, et peuvent en particulier être représentées et étudiées comme des classes d’équivalence de mots sur l'alphabet des transpositions. Un concept naturel dans ce contexte est la notion de forme normale : le choix d’un représentant unique pour chaque tresse. La forme normale alternante, dont l’étude a initialement été motivée par ses liens avec l’ordre standard des tresses, associe à chaque tresse sur n fils une séquence unique de tresses sur n-1 fils, appelés des blocs, permettant de définir récursivement un unique représentant.
Dans cet exposé, je vais présenter quelques propriétés combinatoires et algébriques importante de la forme normale alternante, notamment la régularité et l'automaticité du langage associé. Je vais ensuite aborder plusieurs applications de ces résultats couvrant divers domaines de combinatoires : énumération des tresses ; bon ordre totale sur le monoïde de tresse ; généralisations aux monoïdes d'Artin-Tits.

rec.title: Set-defined graph classes: χ-boundedness meets tropical algebra
rec.speaker: Tomáš Hons
rec.abstract: We study set-defined graph classes: hereditary classes whose vertices are assigned fixed-length numerical tuples, with adjacency determined solely by equality patterns among coordinates. These classes arise in structural graph theory, communication complexity, logic, and adjacency labeling schemes. We ask when they are χ-bounded. We prove a decomposition theorem which allows us to prove that all set-defined classes are fractionally χ-bounded. For classes consisting of all graphs realizable by a fixed Boolean rule on equality patterns, we prove a strong dichotomy: every such class is either polynomially χ-bounded or contains the class of D-dimensional shift graphs for some D. We provide an algorithm that, given a Boolean-function description of a full set-defined class, decides χ-boundedness of the class by reducing the problem to feasibility of tropical linear programs, and its correctness follows from a duality with winning strategies in mean-payoff games. Interestingly, this connection between χ-boundedness and tropical algebra also works in the other direction. This is a joint work with Sarosh Adenwalla, Samuel Braunfeld, John Sylvester, and Viktor Zamaraev.

rec.title: Well-typed program generation, with prenex polymorphism
rec.speaker: Gabriel Scherer
rec.abstract:
Fuzzing” is a popular testing approach where we throw random inputs at a program and check that it respects some expected properties on all inputs. Fuzzing a metaprogram such as a compiler requires producing random input programs. To exercise interesting behaviors of the compiler, we want our input programs to be well-formed in a strong sense, in particular to be well-typed. Generating random well-typed program is difficult when the type-system is powerful, there is a whole scientific literature on the topic, see for example [Testing an Optimising Compiler by Generating Random Lambda Terms, Pałka, 2012].
Most existing generators integrate a large part of the implementation of a type-checker, “inverted” to assist in top-down random term generation by efficiently discarding choices that result in ill-typed programs. Scaling this approach to a full language would result in implementing two sophisticated type-checkers, once in the compiler and once in the program generator. This is one type-checker too many!
We present preliminary work on reusing the constraint-based type inference approach [The Essence of ML-based type inference, Pottier and Rémy, 2004] to write a single type-checker that can be used for both purposes: to check types of user-provided programs, and to efficiently guide a random program generator. This only requires a fairly simple modification to constraint generators: parametrizing them over a search monad. We have succesfully implemented a generator of simply-typed terms in this style, and are in the process (almost done) of scaling it to Hindley-Milner type inference.
(Relevant previous work is [Making Random Judgments: Automatically Generating Well-Typed Terms from the Definition of a Type-System, Fetscher, Claessen, Pałka, Hughes, Findler]. They start from Redex, a Racket DSL to implement simple type systems, and derive a random program generator. The limitation of this approach is that Redex only works with fairly simple type systems, in particular we do not expect it to scale to ML-style type inference with polymorphism, which is the part that hand-crafted generators also struggle on.)
Note: I gave a Formath talk on a preliminary version of this work in March 2024. At the time my prototype only supported the simply-typed lambda-calculus. The extension to Hindley-Milner is follow-up joint work with my 2025 intern Hugo Barreiro. I will also discuss optimizations to the search monad that are necessary to effectively generate terms of larger size.

rec.title: Remarques autour de la formule U^X = ∑_A:U X^A
rec.speaker: Mathieu Anel
rec.abstract: Cette formule classique de théorie des types est remarquable en ce qu’elle égalise des constructions contravariante et covariante en X. Pour l'étudier, je vais me placer dans la catégorie des algèbres sous la monade polynomiale associée à la famille universelle de types U’—>U. Cette catégorie est additive et monoïdale et on peut y relire la formule en terme de dualité et de formes quadratiques. Cela permet une caractérisation précise des paires (U,X) pour lesquelles la formule est vraie.

rec.title: ProofTree: Structured Representations for Human-Centred Mathematical Exploration
rec.speaker: Carl Jontza
rec.abstract:
If formal proofs become abundant, how can we help people find mathematics they care about and explore it in ways that are understandable and engaging? I will present ongoing work on ProofTree, investigating a persistent, versioned graph of goals, assumptions, and alternative arguments as an intermediate representation connecting human-readable reasoning with formal proofs. The aim is to support discovery, understanding, and human guidance at levels of abstraction suited to a person’s background, interests, and objectives.
A case study from Lean-based proof hierarchies, involving confusion between an induction hypothesis and a proof obligation, will motivate technical questions about preserving logical scope, revising arguments, and maintaining links to checked proofs. I will discuss what records of exploration should preserve for subsequent reuse, and outline an evaluation agenda that considers mathematical relevance, understanding, and user experience alongside proof completion and human and computational cost.

rec.title: Verso Blueprint: Reimagining Blueprints for the AI Era
rec.speaker: Emilio Gallego Arias
rec.abstract:
Large-scale formalization projects have long needed tools to
coordinate contributions, track dependencies, and connect mathematical
exposition with formal proofs. A key example is Lean
Blueprint. Introduced in 2020 for the sphere eversion project, Lean
Blueprint extends plasTeX to provide a shared map of statements,
dependencies, Lean declarations, and progress. Lean Blueprint's model
has been quite influential and has helped shape how mathematicians and
formalizers work together on large-scale formalization projects.
This talk presents recent work on Verso Blueprint, a Lean-native
implementation of the Lean Blueprint concept built on Verso, Lean's
official markup language. Designed for close integration with Lean,
Verso Blueprint maintains a three-layer database linking source
material, informal statements, and their formalized counterparts. The
database is populated from Verso documents, analysis of Lean
declarations, and other user-provided data. Interactive HTML views
provide navigation and previews, connecting mathematical exposition
with the formal development. We have now largely reached our original
goal, with functionality comparable to Lean Blueprint or Lean
Architect.
But matching that functionality is no longer enough: this is an
extraordinary moment for formalisation. The practice is radically
chaining even as we build its tools.
When we began this project, our central use case was for humans to
write detailed statements and dependencies to guide
formalization. Today, coding agents are increasingly writing and
interacting with the blueprints themselves in an autonomous
fashion. Blueprints are taking on the reverse role: not just guiding
the construction of formal proofs, but making AI-generated proofs
intelligible to humans. At the same time, dependency tracking and
organizational information remain essential for coordinating
large-scale autoformalization. For example, Prove2Me, a theorem
database with dependency tracking, played a key coordination role in
the recent Fermat's Last Theorem auto-formalization milestone.
What comes next for blueprints in this extraordinary moment? We are
redesigning Verso Blueprint around the idea of "programmatic
blueprints": human-readable, machine-actionable objects synchronized
with formal developments. Our ambition is for blueprints to become a
*foundational harness for AI-assisted formalization*, maintaining the
shared state of a project and coordinating what happens next across
mathematicians, formalizers, code repository workflows, and agents.

rec.title: Compilation of pattern-matching by small inversion
rec.speaker: W. Ait Moussa
rec.abstract:
Dependent inductive data types are an essential part of type theory based proof-assistant, where they close the gap between theorem proving and functional programming. Their meaning and computational behavior are given by dependent recursors, but those are tedious and unintuitive to work with in a dependent setting. Today, the established practice in dependent settings is to have an expressive high-level dependent pattern matching construct with the same logical power as recursors but which is more natural to work with.
This talk will be split into three parts. First, I will go over the history and established theory of dependent-pattern matching and its correspondence to recursors. Then I will present an alternative translation of the non-recursive part of pattern matching to recursors using small-inversion. Finally, I will present an implementation for Rocq of the latter, written by Thierry Martinez a few years back ; in addition to its value as a basis for a specification for this translation, of particular interest is its extensive use of Ocaml's GADTs in order to formalize a notion of intrinsically well-formed Rocq terms.

rec.title: Dynamics of singularity surfaces for the compressible viscous fluids.
rec.speaker: Marcel Zodji
rec.speaker_affiliation: Laboratoire de Mathématiques et Modélisation d'Évry
rec.abstract:
The motion of a compressible viscous fluid is described by the Navier-Stokes system.
It is a system of hyperbolic-parabolic mixed-type PDEs. In this talk, we will study
the so-called density patch problem: \emph{If we are given a density that is initially "regular"
on both sides of a hypersurface across which it is discontinuous, will this structure
be preserved over time?}
An important quantity in the mathematical analysis of this system is the so-called effective flux,
which was discovered by Hoff and Smoller (1985). More precisely, the mathematical properties
of this quantity play a crucial role in the study of the propagation of oscillations in
compressible fluids [Serre, 1991], in the construction of weak solutions [P-L Lions, 1996] or the
propagation of discontinuity surfaces [Hoff, 2002], to cite just a few examples.
In the case of density-dependent viscosities, the behavior of the effective flux degenerates,
which renders the analysis more subtle.

rec.title: Multi-scale modeling and analysis of signal processing in neurons
rec.speaker: Claire Guerrier
rec.abstract: In this talk, I will present models for signal propagation in neurons, ranging from the macro- to the micro-scale, with various applications to neuronal signalling. The first application concerns myelin plasticity, and the influence of neuronal myelin geometry on signal transmission. We investigate the evolution of the maximum of a signal in a damped heat equation on x>0, with a Dirichlet boundary condition representing the signal, which models signal transmission in a myelinated internode. We derive an expression of the solution, and derive the Dirichlet-to-Neumann operator at x=0. We then investigate the max. At a more refined scale, to investigate signal summation in the neuronal dendritic tree, we consider the Poisson-Nernst Planck system of equations representing ionic electrodiffusion in an electrolyte. This system expresses a sharp boundary layer of the size of the Debye length at the boundary, where the extra-charges accumulates. In particular, we derive an asymptotic approximation of the solution at steady state, in the regime of small Debye length.

rec.title: Mosquito borne disease outbreak : Climate change impact to Physics Informed Neural Network use
rec.speaker: Aniket Banerjee
rec.abstract:
Dengue, Zika and chikungunya are expanding across new
territories as their vector, the tiger mosquito _Aedes albopictus_,
tracks a warming climate. Forecasting where and when outbreaks will
occur requires models that are both mechanistically faithful to mosquito
ecology and disciplined by real observational data — yet the
biological parameters that govern transmission, such as the biting rate,
the extrinsic incubation period and mosquito survival, are precisely the
ones we cannot measure directly in the field.
In this talk, I present a national -scale furcating framework that
couples a mechanistic _Aedes albopictus_ population model, in the spirit
of the Arbocarto approach, to a vector-to-human transmission layer, and
the use of Neural Network use to predict diffusion pattern in
epidemiological systems. I will explain the modelling choices behind the
population and transmission layers, the structure of the inverse
problem, and how PINNs let a mechanistic model "speak" to messy,
heterogeneous data.

rec.title: Impact de la sélection sur la transmission du génome dans une population biparentale
rec.speaker: Camille Coron
rec.abstract: Nous considérons une population d’individus modélisée par un modèle de Moran biparental, et nous nous intéressons à la contribution asymptotique des ancêtres au génome de l’ensemble de la population. En particulier, nous étudions l’impact de la sélection de viabilité sur cette grandeur. Sous l’hypothèse que la population contient initialement une fraction positive d’individus favorisés, nous caractérisons cette quantité asymptotique de génome comme la valeur limite d’un système dynamique. Sous l’hypothèse d’une sélection infinie, nous caractérisons la dynamique complète de la quantité de génome transmise par un seul mutant initial ; en particulier, nous montrons que la loi de la quantité asymptotique de génome transmise par ce mutant est la solution d’une équation de point fixe en loi.

rec.title: Lissage par peignes et trivialité locale pour les espaces homogènes au-dessus d’une courbe relative
rec.speaker: Margot Bruneaux
rec.abstract:
Soit $R$ un anneau local hensélien, de corps résiduel $\kappa$, soit $C$ une courbe projective lisse sur $R$, à fibres géométriquement connexes, soit $G$ un $C$-groupe réductif dont le tore radical $\operatorname{rad}(G)$ est isotrivial, et soit $E\to C$ un $G$-torseur.
Nous montrons que, si le noyau de l'isogénie centrale
\[
G_{\mathrm{sc}}\times_C \operatorname{rad}(G)\longrightarrow G
\]
est étale sur $C$, ou bien si $\kappa$ est un corps suffisamment grand, alors la trivialité de $E_\kappa\to C_\kappa$ pour la topologie de Zariski implique la trivialité de $E\to C$ pour cette même topologie.
Nous démontrons également une version « moyennée » de ce résultat, en supposant seulement que $\operatorname{rad}(G)$ est isotrivial, ainsi qu'une variante concernant les espaces homogènes projectifs, sans aucune hypothèse restrictive sur $G$.
Ces résultats ont notamment pour conséquences un principe local-global pour les torseurs sur les corps de fonctions de courbes au-dessus d'anneaux de valuation discrète henséliens, renforçant des travaux de Gille--Parimala--Suresh, ainsi qu'une version hensélienne d'un théorème de Drinfeld--Simpson.
Nos démonstrations sont de nature géométrique. Elles reposent sur des compactifications de torseurs et sur une technique de lissage par peignes, dans une version relative et arithmétique que nous développons en détail, en nous appuyant sur les travaux de Kollár et de Graber--Harris--Starr.
En collaboration avec Federico Scavia.

rec.speaker: Alexis Bouthier
rec.abstract:
Si G est réductif sur un corps, un théorème de Raghunathan-Ramanathan énonce que
tout G-torseur sur la droite affine, trivial sur la clôture séparable, est trivial.
Le cas non-réductif avait été écarté d'emblée par les auteurs comme "rather complicated".
On montre qu'un tel énoncé vaut pour tout k-groupe lisse (et même pas lisse du tout).
On discutera également d'autres extensions et généralisations à l'étude des G-torseurs sur des espaces affines.

rec.title: Mod p de Rham cohomology of Shimura varieties
rec.speaker: Martin Ortiz
rec.abstract: The weight part of Serre's conjecture studies the modularity of certain spaces of mod p automorphic forms. In the case of Shimura varieties, this is usually done by considering their etale cohomology, with Serre weights as coefficients. One can also propose a similar conjecture for mod p de Rham cohomology of Shimura varieties, and I conjecture that the two approaches are equivalent. I can prove this generically for G=GL3, and some cases in GSp4. Moreover, for GSp4 this approach produces a generic entailment of Serre weights, which is completely invisible from the etale cohomology perspective.

On verra qu'en remplaçant les hypersurfaces de petit degré par des espaces homogènes il est possible d'obtenir des caractérisations de nature diophantienne de la dimension cohomologique. Il s'agit de travaux en commun avec Giancarlo Lucchini Arteche.

rec.abstract: We prove a classification of families of analytic p-divisible groups on adic spaces S over Qp in terms of Hodge–Tate triples on S, generalizing a theorem of Fargues. As applications, we obtain moduli descriptions of local Shimura varieties of EL and PEL type. We also explain how to derive generalizations of the fundamental exact sequence of Colmez--Dospinescu--Nizio? on smooth Stein spaces.

rec.title: Le principe d'incertitude fort sur les groupes abéliens finis
rec.speaker: Emma Weschler
rec.abstract:
En mécanique quantique, le principe d'incertitude d'Heisenberg stipule qu'on ne peut connaître simultanément avec précision la position et la vitesse d'une particule. Cette célèbre inégalité relie en réalité une fonction et sa transformée de Fourier.
En 1989, motivés par des applications en traitement du signal, Donoho et Stark donnent un nouveau principe d'incertitude, non plus pour des fonctions définies sur les réels mais sur un groupe abélien fini. Ce dernier a ensuite été significativement amélioré : en 2006, Tao prouve ce qu'on peut appeler un principe d'incertitude fort pour des fonctions définies sur Z/pZ, où p est premier.
Plus récemment, en 2021, Garcia, Karaali et Katz généralisent ce principe aux corps finis, pour des fonctions vérifiant une certaine condition de symétrie qu'on détaillera.
Dans cet exposé, on présentera une généralisation du principe d'incertitude fort pour des groupes abéliens finis quelconques et nous verrons ce que donne l'étude de ce dernier sur les groupes cycliques.

rec.title: Numerical semigroups, conjectures, algorithms, and applications.
rec.speaker: Maria Bras-Amorós
rec.abstract:
A numerical semigroup is a subset of N containing zero, with finite complement, and such it is closed under addition. We will introduce the main results on the topic, the connection with algebraic geometry, and the construction of different trees for their classification by different parameters.
Some open conjectures will be presented relating the parameters of a numerical semigroup as well as concerning their growth with respect to the maximum gap, i.e. the Frobenius number, and with respect to the number of gaps, i.e., the genus. We will expose the partial known results and the state of the art of the algorithms for counting semigroups. >
We will finally get a glimpse into the role that numerical semigroups have in the area of error-correcting codes and in music theory.

rec.title: Biased random walk on dynamical percolation
rec.speaker: Nina Gantert
rec.abstract:
As an example for a random walk in random environment, we
study biased random walk for dynamical percolation on the
d-dimensional lattice. We establish a law
of large numbers and an invariance principle for this random walk
using regeneration times.
Moreover, we verify that the Einstein relation holds, and we
investigate the speed of the walk
as a function of the bias. While for d = 1 the speed is
increasing, we show that in general this
fails in dimension d ? 2. As our main result, we establish two
regimes of parameters, separated
by a critical curve, such that the speed is either eventually
strictly increasing or eventually
strictly decreasing. This is in sharp contrast to the biased
random walk on a static supercritical
percolation cluster, where the speed is known to be eventually
zero.
Based on joint work with Sebastian Andres, Dominik Schmid and
Perla Sousi.

rec.title: Percolation de premier passage brochette
rec.speaker: Maxime Marivain
rec.abstract:
Nous étudions un nouveau modèle de percolation de premier passage, appelé percolation de premier passage brochette, dans lequel les temps de passage associés aux arêtes situées sur une même droite sont égaux. Nous établissons tout d'abord un théorème de convergence point à point, où la constante de temps est identifiée. En particulier, nous étudions le cas où cette constante de temps est nulle et mettons en évidence l'existence d'une grande variété de comportements possibles.
Nous démontrons ensuite un théorème de forme, montrant que la forme limite est le diamant L^1. Nous étendons ensuite l'analyse en établissant un théorème de convergence point à point dans le cadre où les temps de passage peuvent prendre la valeur infinie. Enfin, nous nous intéressons à la déviation transversale maximale des géodésiques par rapport à la ligne droite. Nous démontrons l'existence de géodésiques sous des hypothèses faibles et déterminons l'ordre de grandeur de leur déviation par rapport à la ligne droite en fonction du comportement de la distribution des temps de passage au voisinage de son infimum.

rec.title: À propos de la tessellation de Poisson-Delaunay : quelques techniques classiques et de nouveaux résultats de loi
rec.speaker: Cecilia d'Errico
rec.abstract:
Dans cet exposé, nous présentons la tessellation de Delaunay issue d’un processus ponctuel de Poisson homogène sur Rd. Dans une première partie, nous parlerons de la cellule typique et montrerons comment obtenir sa loi à l’aide d’une technique 'combo'
classique : la formule de Mecke + changement de variable de Blaschke-Petkantschin. Dans la deuxième partie, nous étudions le volume de cette cellule : nous voyons comment obtenir ses moments, puis nous résolvons le problème des moments pour déterminer la loi
du volume de la cellule typique. Enfin, nous présenterons d’autres résultats de loi de fonctionnelles de la cellule typique que nous avons obtenus en étendant ces techniques.

rec.title: Delocalisation of the disordered long-range discrete Gaussian chain
rec.speaker: Corentin Faipeur
rec.abstract:
The long-range discrete Gaussian chain (DGC) is a 1D height function model with $1/r^\alpha$ interactions between pairs of sites at distance $r$. The DGC is known to delocalise at every temperature when $\alpha>2$ (i.e. the typical height at the origin diverges when the size of the system goes to infinity), to localise when $1<\alpha<2$, and to present a localisation/delocalisation phase transition at $\alpha=2$.
In this talk, we will consider a disordered version of the long-range DGC, obtained by adding an external random field. We will show that this disordered model becomes delocalised at all temperatures for all $\alpha>3/2$, and provide quantitative estimates of this delocalisation phenomenon. If time permits, I will also present a central limit theorem for the height at the origin. Joint work with Christopher Chalhoub, Paul Dario and Arnaud Le Ny.
rec.location_text: Salle B405, bâtiment B, LAGA, Institut Galilée, Université Paris 13
rec.series_name: Séminaire de l'équipe Probabilités et Statistique

rec.title: [mini-cours] Combinatorics and Geometry: Crossing paths—in the age of AI. (Part 1)
rec.speaker: János Pach
rec.speaker_affiliation: Rényi Institute, Budapest, et EPFL, Lausanne
rec.abstract:
Crossing numbers: Dead or alive. The crossing
number of a graph G, denoted by cr(G), is the smallest number of
edge crossings in any drawing of G in the plane. Clearly, cr(G)=0
if and only if G is planar. Garey and Johnson proved that
determining cr(G) is an NP-complete problem. Over the past forty
years, crossing numbers have proven to play a vital role in
various fields, including discrete and computational geometry,
number theory, and circuit layout (such as providing lower bounds
on the chip area required for a graph's physical layout). Yet,
many of the foundational questions that inspired research in this
area remain open, and new mysteries continue to emerge. Quo
vadis?
rec.location_text: Salle B107
rec.series_name: Séminaire de l'équipe Probabilités et Statistique

rec.title: [mini-cours] Combinatorics and Geometry: Crossing paths—in the age of AI. (Part 2)
rec.speaker: János Pach
rec.speaker_affiliation: Rényi Institute, Budapest, et EPFL, Lausanne
rec.abstract:
What makes the chromatic number of a graph large?
There have been many attempts to answer this question. The
most natural approach is to look for unavoidable substructures in
graphs of large chromatic number. In 1943, Hadwiger made the
conjecture that every graph of chromatic number r can be
transformed into a complete graph of r vertices by a series of
edge contractions and vertex and edge deletions. This is one of
the most important unsolved problems in graph theory. After giving
a somewhat biased survey of the problem, I plan to report on some
related recent results, joint with Fox and Suk.
rec.location_text: Salle B107
rec.series_name: Séminaire de l'équipe Probabilités et Statistique

rec.title: Catalan sums, infinite noodle and 1/Pi
rec.speaker: Paul Thévenin
rec.abstract:
We investigate a family of infinite sums of products of Catalan numbers, indexed by trees.
These sums naturally appear in the study of the infinite noodle, which is an infinite random discrete planar graph.
This infinite noodle is the limit, in a local sense, of large uniformly random meandric systems,
which are configurations of non-crossing loops in the plane.
In particular, we show that our sums are all polynomials in 1/Pi with rational coefficients, and provide an algorithm to compute them.
This is joint work with Alin Bostan and Valentin Féray.
rec.location_text: Salle B405, bâtiment B, LAGA, Institut Galilée, Université Paris 13
rec.series_name: Séminaire de l'équipe Probabilités et Statistique

rec.title: Empirical distribution of ancestral lineages in populations with density-dependent interactions
rec.speaker: Madeleine Kubasch
rec.abstract: We study a density-dependent Markov jump process describing a population where each individual is characterized by a type, and reproduces at rates depending both on its type and on the population type distribution. We are interested in the empirical distribution of ancestral lineages in the population process. First, we exhibit a time-inhomogeneous Markov process, which allows to capture the behavior of a sampled lineage in the population process. This is achieved through a many-to-one formula, which relates the expected value of a functional evaluated over the lineages in the population process to the expectation of the functional evaluated along this time-inhomogeneous process. This provides a direct interpretation of the underlying survivorship bias. Second, we consider the large population regime, when the population size grows to infinity. Under classical assumptions, the population type distribution converges to a deterministic limit. Here, we focus on the empirical distribution of ancestral lineages in this large population limit, for which we establish a many-to-one formula. Using coupling arguments, we further quantify the approximation error which arises when sampling in this large population approximation instead of the finite-size population process.

rec.series_name: Séminaire de l'équipe Probabilités et Statistique

rec.title: La fonction de support du polytope poissonien en grande dimension
rec.speaker: Benjamin Dadoun
rec.abstract:
Dans cet exposé, on considère l'enveloppe convexe des points d'un processus ponctuel de Poisson dans la boule unité euclidienne, lorsque la dimension tend vers l'infini, et nous étudions plus précisément la fonction de support de ce polytope poissonnien.
Nous en identifierons d'abord les différents régimes asymptotiques, selon l'intensité du nombre de points échantillonnés, et nous les comparerons à ceux obtenus par Bonnet?Kabluchko?Turchi (RSA, 2020) pour le volume moyen occupé.
Nous présenterons ensuite des résultats de convergence en loi pour une certaine renormalisation de la fonction de support, en faisant (si le temps le permet) le lien avec un problème de recouvrement résolu par Janson (Acta Math., 1986).
Il s'agit d'un travail avec Pierre Calka (LMRS, Université de Rouen Normandie).
rec.location_text: Salle B405, bâtiment B, LAGA, Institut Galilée, Université Paris 13
rec.series_name: Séminaire de l'équipe Probabilités et Statistique

rec.title: Noise sensitivity and directed polymers
rec.speaker: Anna Donadini
rec.abstract:
Noise sensitivity for functionals of independent random variables, introduced by Benjamini, Kalai and Schramm in 1999 in the context of Boolean functions, describes the phenomenon where a small perturbation of the underlying randomness leads to an asymptotically independent outcome.
In this talk, we extend classical noise sensitivity criteria beyond the Boolean setting and derive quantitative estimates with optimal rates. We then consider the model of directed polymers in random environments, and apply our results to the regime in which the partition function converges to a universal limit known as the Stochastic Heat Flow, which we show to be independent of the white noise arising from the scaling limit of the disorder.

rec.title: L'intégrale de Wick
rec.speaker: Carlo Bellingeri
rec.abstract:
Dans cet exposé j'introduireai l’intégrale de Wick, une nouvelle notion d’intégrale stochastique fondée sur le produit de Wick de variables aléatoires, pour une classe de processus stochastiques qui ne sont pas nécessairement gaussiens. Cette intégrale est définie pour des intégrandes polynomiaux et est centrée. Dans le cas du mouvement brownien fractionnaire, l’intégrale de Wick coïncide avec l’opérateur de divergence du calcul de Malliavin. Nous établissons une formule de correction reliant l’intégrale de Wick à l’intégrale de Young, ainsi qu’une formule d’Itô. Ces deux formules comportent une infinité de termes correctifs, exprimés sous forme d’intégrales par rapport aux fonctions cumulantes du processus, et se réduisent à des identités classiques dans le cas gaussien. Ces résultats sont obtenus en développant d’abord des formules de diagrammes pour les polynômes d’Appell. Notre théorie s’applique à divers processus à valeurs dans des chaos de Wiener d’ordre borné, notamment au processus de Rosenblatt. Des extensions au cadre des chemins rugueux seront également présentées.
Travail en collaboration avec Emilio Ferrucci (SISSA).

rec.title: Height one phenomena in p-adic Hodge theory
rec.speaker: Tasos MOULINOS
rec.abstract:
The syntomification of the integers (Z_p^syn) acts as a parameter space for p-adic cohomology theories. By the work of Drinfeld and others, it is known to carry a canonical formal group, and hence a map to the moduli stack of formal groups. Pulling back along this map gives rise to a certain line bundle equipped with a distinguished section "v_1". On the p-completed moduli stack of formal groups, the nonvanishing of v_1 defines the substack parametrizing "height-1" formal groups. Yet the preimage of this locus on Z_p^syn, when computed in p-adic formal stacks, is empty. There is a mismatch here because inverting v_1 on syntomic cohomology gives p-adic étale cohomology, but inverting it on the stack itself before passing to global sections gives nothing.
I will explain how passing to analytic stacks brings this missing locus into view. By realizing the p-completed moduli stack of formal groups as an analytic stack, we construct an algebro-geometric shadow of K(1)-localization. Applied to syntomification, this produces an analytic stack whose dualizable quasi-coherent sheaves recover p-adic Galois representations, and more generally lisse étale sheaves on the generic fiber of a p-adic formal scheme. I will explain how a perfected version of this construction depends only on the generic fiber, providing a geometric counterpart to purity results for K(1)-localized K-theory.
This is joint work in progress with Greg Andreychev.
rec.location_text: Salle B405, bâtiment B, LAGA, Institut Galilée, Université Paris 13

rec.title: On the Hasse principle in twist families
rec.speaker: Adam MORGAN
rec.abstract: I will discuss joint work with Alex Bartel in which we study the frequency of failures of the Hasse principle in quadratic twist families of torsors under an abelian variety. The main technical ingredient is a result on the distribution of 2-Selmer groups in certain families of twists defined by Frobenian conditions.
rec.location_text: Séminaire commun AGA/TA

rec.title: Minimal model for localization of topological Fukaya categories of surfaces
rec.speaker: Pierre BODIN
rec.abstract:
In the first half of this talk, I will present the construction of the topological Fukaya category of a graded marked surface, as introduced by Haiden, Katzarkov, Kontsevich, and present some of its main properties.
In the second half, I will present a minimal model for the localization of this category at a spherical object corresponding to a simple closed curve on the surface. This new description will then be used to describe the indecomposable objects of the localization in terms of graded curves on the singular surface obtained by collapsing the simple closed curve to a point.
rec.location_text: Salle B405, bâtiment B, LAGA, Institut Galilée, Université Paris 13

rec.title: Localization in Equivariant Hermitian K-Theory
rec.speaker: Guillaume BRESSAN
rec.abstract:
Algebraic K-theory is a major invariant in algebraic geometry that consists in studying vector bundles on a scheme. To compute K-theory groups, there exist a number of fundamental theorems such as the localization theorem which relates the K-theory of a scheme X to that of an open subscheme U through a fiber sequence of spectra. This theorem also exists in variants of K-theory such as 1) hermitian K-theory, which studies vector bundles equipped with a quadratic form and 2) equivariant K-theory, which studies G-equivariant vector bundles where G is a group acting on X. However, no such theorem existed until now for equivariant hermitian K-theory, which combines these two variants. In this talk, we present such a theorem when X is non-singular. We will mainly discuss derived infinity-categories,
infinity-toposes and algebraic stacks.

rec.title: Dynamique de Aut(F_n) sur G^n, pour G compact et n grand
rec.speaker: Serge Cantat
rec.abstract:
Donnons nous un groupe de Lie compact G et un entier n.
Un n-uplet (g_1, …, g_n) étant donné, on peut changer l’un des g_i en son inverse, ou multiplier l’un des
g_i par g_j (avec j différent de i) : ces opérations élémentaires ne changent pas le sous-groupe de G
engendré par les g_i. Ces opérations engendrent un groupe de difféomorphismes de G^n, et le problème
que nous aborderons est d’étudier la dynamique de ce groupe. Pour n suffisamment grand, nous verrons
qu’il est possible de classer les fermés et les mesures invariants.
rec.location_text: Salle B405, bâtiment B, LAGA, Institut Galilée, Université Paris 13

rec.title: Characterizing totally geodesic manifolds in negative curvature
rec.speaker: David Fisher
rec.abstract: The talk centers around the question of what invariant sets for Anosov flows and diffeomorphisms can look like. It is known that closed invariant sets can be arbitrarily bad and for example be fractals of arbitrary Hausdorff dimension. An old and interesting question, first raised by Hirsch in 1968 is what closed invariant submanifolds can look like. There are many surprising rigidity results in this direction, some quite old, and recently Rose Eliott Smith and I proved a new one, giving a dynamical characterization of totally geodesic submanifolds in negative curvature. I will explain the theorem and both the classical motivation and some more contemporary motivation. If time permits I will give some hints about the proof and particularly how it uses very old results from Smale and Mane.

rec.title: Constructions de flots d’Anosov sur des 3-variétés hyperboliques
rec.speaker: François Béguin
rec.abstract: Un flot sur une 3-variété est dit d'Anosov s’il existe, en tout point, une direction contractée et une direction dilatée par ce flot. La dynamique des flots d’Anosov en dimension 3 est intimement reliée à la topologie des variétés portant ces flots. Une des grandes problématique du domaine est de déterminer quelles 3-variétés — notamment quelles 3-variétés hyperboliques — portent des flots d’Anosov. La plupart ? Presqu’aucune ? Je présenterai deux résultats, obtenus avec C. Bonatti, B. Ma et B. Yu, qui apportent des éléments de réponses à ces questions.

rec.title: Non-algebraic Anosov flows in higher dimensions
rec.speaker: Danyu Zhang
rec.abstract: Anosov flows are prototypical examples of hyperbolic dynamics that preserve invariant uniformly contracting and expanding distributions. We recall the classification of algebraic Anosov flows by Per Tomter and currently known examples of non-algebraic Anosov flows. We give a construction of non-algebraic Anosov flows in higher dimensions that fibres over the recent Fenley—Mann—Potrie example of dimension 4, which relies on arithmetic Kleinian groups acting on torus.

changes.old_value:
Dans cette thèse, nous présenterons des asympotiques d'états cohérents propagés par une équation de Schrödinger associée à un Hamiltonien donné. Ces résultats étendent ceux obtenus par Combescure et Robert, dans lesquels un état cohérent propagé est approché dans la limite $h\to 0$ par des paquets gaussiens déformés dits états cohérents comprimés. Cette description reste valide pour des temps $t$ pouvant tendre vers l'infini quand $h\to 0$, dans le régime $|t|\leq |\log h|/(6\lambda_0)$ où $\lambda_0$ est l'exposant de Lyapunov maximal de la dynamique classique. L'échec de cette approximation au temps $|\log h|/(6\lambda_0)$ est relié à la flexion des paquets d'ondes évolués : une fois étalés à l'échelle $h^{1/3}$, les états comprimés ne founissent plus une description appropriée. Pour obtenir une représentation valide jusqu'à des temps $|t|\leq C|\log h|$ avec un plus grand $C$ (par exemple jusqu'au temps d'Ehrenfest $|\log h|/(2\lambda_0)$ où un étalement à des échelles macroscopiques est autorisé), on ajoute des hypothèses sur le flot $\Phi_t$ associé à la dynamique classique, imposant des contraintes sur les directions d'élongation. La description obtenue met en évidence que les états propagés ne doivent plus être considérés comme microlocalisés en un point mais plutôt le long d'une sous-variété isotrope (correspondant à des directions instables).
Ces résultats seront ensuite appliqués à l'étude de l'équation des ondes amorties sur une variété Anosov, on expliquera comment une telle asymptotique d'états cohérents propagés peut être utilisée pour obtenir des estimées de propagateurs, permettant d'obtenir un trou spectral et des estimées de résolvante pour l'opérateur associé, et ainsi de montrer la décroissance exponentielle de l'énergie des solutions.

imj-107.name: Séminaire IMJ-PRG PhD preprint seminar
imj-107.organizers: Théo Pinet et Juan Ramón Gómez García
imj-107.description:
Séminaire permettant aux doctorants et étudiants de Master de l'IMJ-PRG (de toutes les équipes) de se familiariser avec les résultats apparaissant dans les récentes prépublications de leurs collègues. L'objectif des présentations est d'expliquer de manière accessible, à l'aide d'exemples et/ou de cas particuliers plus simples, les résultats principaux d'une prépublication donnée. Le séminaire est à distinguer du Séminaire des thésards par sa volonté de se concentrer sur les résultats de recherche propres aux étudiants de l'IMJ-PRG (et non pas aux résultats généraux et définitions abstraites du domaine de recherche sous-jacent).
Aura typiquement lieu les mercredis de 17h00 à 18h30-19h00.

imj-53.name: Phd Seminar - Séminaire des doctorant.e.s
imj-53.organizers: Salim Alloun, Pedro Alves, Baptiste Dugué, Brian Flanagan, Ivory Fronteau, Kostyantyn Krutoy
imj-53.description:
Le séminaire des doctorant.e.s est l'occasion pour les doctorant.e.s de présenter des résultats et des problématiques dignes d'intérêt devant un public de non-spécialistes. L'ambiance y est informelle ; poser des questions naïves est encouragé, et les questions moins naïves sont bienvenues dans la mesure où elles n'entravent pas le bon déroulement de l'exposé.
Chaque jeudi à 18h, en alternance entre Jussieu et Sophie Germain.
The PhD seminar is an opportnuity for PhD students to present results and topics worthy of interest in front of a non-specialist audience. The mood is informal ; asking naive questions is highly encouraged and less naive questions are also welcomed, as long as they don't intefere with the smoothness of the talk.
Every Thursday at 6pm, alternating between Jussieu and Sophie Germain.

imj-91.name: Séminaire Arithmetic Geometry Preprint Seminar
imj-91.department: Formes Automorphes; Théorie des Nombres; Topologie et Géométrie Algébriques
imj-91.organizers: Yves André, Javier Fresán, Wiesława Nizioł
imj-91.description: Souvent, il nous arrive de vouloir étudier en détail une prépublication qui nous intéresse particulièrement, peut-être décisive pour notre travail, mais d’autres tâches renvoient ce voeu aux calendes. Le but de ce séminaire est de nous inciter à réaliser ce voeu, en faisant aussi profiter tour à tour les collègues géomètres arithméticiens des efforts investis dans cette lecture. Il s’agira donc d’exposer, en deux heures, une prépublication significative d’autrui de son choix, devant un public varié de géomètres arithméticiens.

imj-93.name: Groupe de travail Algèbre de Hecke, Catégorie de Soergel et 2-catégories monoidales tressées
imj-93.description:
L'objectif de ce groupe de travail est de comprendre le théorème principal de l'article :
Catharina Stroppel: Categorification: tangle invariants and TQFTs, Proceedings of the ICM 2022. arXiv:2207.05139
Références :
Ben Elias, Mikhail Khovanov: Diagrammatics for Soergel categories, Int. J. Math. Math. Sci. 2010, Art. ID 978635, 58 pp. DOI:10.1155/2010/978635
Ben Elias, Shotaro Makisumi, Ulrich Thiel, Geordie Williamson: Introduction to Soergel Bimodules, Springer, ISBN: 978-3-030-48825-3, DOI:10.1007/978-3-030-48826-0
Christian Kassel, Vladimir Turaev: Braid Groups, Springer, ISBN: 978-0-387-33841-5 DOI:10.1007/978-0-387-68548-9
⚠️ à partir de janvier 2023, la date et l'heure du groupe de travail risque de changer.

imj-95.name: Groupe de travail Knot Online Seminar
imj-95.organizers: Groupe de travail Louis-Adrien Robert et Emmanuel Wagner
imj-95.description:
[K-OS] KNOT ONLINE SEMINAR
[K-OS] is an online research seminar which focuses on knot theory and low-dimensional topology. Talks will be delivered by authors of recent arXiv articles that made a breakthrough in our field. It happens the 3rd Thursday of months Thursdays from 16:00 to 17:00 (CET/CEST Berlin, Brussels, Madrid, Paris, Rome, Vienna, Warsaw, Zurich) on Zoom.
It is organized by Alexandra Kjuchukova, Lukas Lewark, Louis-Hadrien Robert and Emmanuel Wagner. It benefits from logistical support from the CNRS, the university of Paris and the university of Regensburg.

imj-96.name: Groupe de travail Preuve de la conjecture de Bogomolov-Fu-Tschinkel par J. Poineau
imj-96.description:
Voici le calendrier du groupe de travail sur la preuve de la conjecture de Bogomolov-Fu-Tschinkel par J. Poineau :
0) 24/01 Introduction générale : Conjecture de Bogomolov-Fu-Tschinkel et morphismes de Lattès, stratégie de la preuve
1) 31/01 Analytification de Berkovich sur un corps valué complet et sur un anneau de Banach
2) 07/02 Théorie du (pluri)potentiel global sur les espaces de Berkovich : métriques FS, CPSH (continue psh), métrique d'équilibre d'un système dynamique polarisé (thèse de Pille-Schneider); sur un corps: mesures de MA de métriques CPSH, estimée de Chern-Levine-Nirenberg (Boucksom-Eriksson?)
3) 07/03 Continuité des mesures canoniques (Haar ou Dirac au point de Gauss) sur P^1 [I, Thm 6.8] et des mesures d'équilibre (via Chern-Levine-Nirenberg)
4) 21/03 Hauteurs, énergie mutuelle des mesures et continuité [II et Favre--Riviera-Letelier]
5) 04/04 Cas des Lattès : minoration centrale (énergie mutuelle d'intervalles en valuation triviale) et globale [II, section 6]
6) 18/04 Minoration globale de l'énergie mutuelle et fin de la preuve [II, sections 7-8]
Les séances auront lieu de 10h à 12h en salle 15.25.502 à Jussieu sauf pour le 24/1 qui aura lieu en salle 15.16.413.

m2fonda-gt-combi.name: GT M2 — Combinatoire et entropie
m2fonda-gt-combi.description: Entropy methods in additive combinatorics (Green–Manners–Tao, Hochman), Jan.–Feb. 2026.

m2fonda-gt-dag.name: GT M2 — Géométrie dérivée (DAG Jussieu working group)
m2fonda-gt-dag.description: Goal: postnikov towers of connective E∞-rings are square-zero extensions (Lurie, Higher Algebra 7.4.1.28). Weekly programme started 2 Oct 2025 (∞-categories, stable ∞-categories, E∞-rings, cotangent complex).

m2fonda-gt-dgt.name: GT M2 — Géométrie différentielle non lisse et applications
m2fonda-gt-dgt.description: Optimal transport, metric measure spaces, CD/RCD conditions and stability under lower Ricci bounds (Jan. 2026).

m2fonda-gt-groups.name: GT M2 — Groupes et courbure
m2fonda-gt-groups.description: Curvature and fundamental groups (Bonnet, Cartan–Hadamard, Preissmann, Milnor), then hyperbolic groups (Oct. 2025).

m2fonda-gt-hyper.name: GT M2 — Géométrie hyperkählérienne
m2fonda-gt-hyper.description: Holonomy and Berger's classification, Calabi–Yau, variations of Hodge structure, period map and global Torelli (Oct. 2025).

m2fonda-gt-k.name: GT M2 — K-théorie (groupe de lecture)
m2fonda-gt-k.description: Algebraic K-theory following Srinivas: K0, K1, K2, then higher K-groups via the plus and Q constructions (Oct. 2025).

m2fonda-gt-langlands.name: GT M2 — Langlands p-adique en dimension deux
m2fonda-gt-langlands.recurrence: Tuesdays 16:40–18:40, Jussieu 15-16-101 (as stated in the PDF of 4 Nov. 2025)
m2fonda-gt-langlands.description: p-adic Langlands for GL2(Qp): (φ,Γ)-modules, Fontaine rings, following Astérisque 319/330/331.

m2fonda-gt-mmp.name: GT M2 — Programme minimal
m2fonda-gt-mmp.description: Minimal model program; call for speakers (2025–26).

m2fonda-gt-rh.name: GT M2 — Correspondance de Riemann-Hilbert
m2fonda-gt-rh.description: Flat connections, local systems and representations of π1; Gauss–Manin connection; then regular singularities or D-modules (Nov. 2025).

m2fonda-gt-shen.name: Sujet proposé — Faisceaux cohérents et super-connexions
m2fonda-gt-shen.description: Topic proposed by Shu Shen (not yet organised): coherent sheaves, derived categories, antiholomorphic superconnections and Block's equivalence (Bismut–Shen–Wei).

m2fonda-gt-vss.name: GT M2 — Sexual and gender-based violence and discrimination working group
m2fonda-gt-vss.description: Student working group of the M2, 2025–2026 (presentation PDF updated 2025-12-16). Sessions are arranged among the participants and not published with dates.

paris-apres-midi-topologie.name: Après-midi de topologie (Paris)
paris-apres-midi-topologie.description: Afternoons of several topology talks announced in the LAGA topology seminar listing, e.g. « Après-midi parisienne de topologie » (8 Jan 2026, LAGA) and « Après-midi topologie algébrique » (26 Mar 2026, Sophie Germain). Dates are irregular: no recurrence is claimed. Announcements also circulate on the sem-top.paris mailing list.

arxiv:2609.08635.title: Finite-size Entanglement Certification via Third-Order Local Randomized Measurements
arxiv:2609.08635.summary: Certifying entanglement in high-dimensional systems usually requires full state tomography, whose cost grows rapidly with the system dimension. Local randomized measurements offer a scalable alternative, but existing tests based on second-order correlations access only limited information about the state. Here, we derive a finite-size entanglement certificate that extends local randomized measurements to third order.
arxiv:2609.08635.authors: Giovanni Scala, Corrado Cosimo Mattiacci, Dorota Pietryka, Gniewomir Sarbicki

arxiv:2610.41904.title: Lax-idempotent monads in homotopy theory
arxiv:2610.41904.summary: We extend the theory of lax-idempotent monads to the setting of $(\infty,2)$-categories. In particular, we prove an analogue of Kock and Z\"oberlein's characterization of the category of algebras over a lax-idempotent monad. We then apply this theory to many examples that arise naturally in homotopy theory.

arxiv:2611.14090.title: Equivariant Quantisation of Hypertoric Varieties via Symplectic Cuts
arxiv:2611.14090.summary: We study the equivariant geometric quantisation of a non-compact hypertoric orbifold of complex dimension $2n$ by compact symplectic cuts. When the defining arrangement has a non-empty bounded base region and the fixed lift is integral, we prove that, at every positive regular integral level $d$, the space of sections on the cut is the sum of the fibre-rotation weight spaces of weight at most $d$ in the original quantisation. The higher cohomology of the cut pre-quantum line orbibundle vanishes, so its equivariant index is the character of its actual section space.

arxiv:2611.16156.title: Many more odd zeta values are irrational
arxiv:2611.16156.summary: We prove that for any sufficiently large odd integer $s$, there exist at least \[ 2.78 \, \sqrt{\frac{s \log\log s}{\log s}} \] irrational values among $\zeta(3), \zeta(5), \dots, \zeta(s)$, where $\zeta$ is the Riemann zeta function. This improves on the best known estimate by a constant factor times $\sqrt{ \log\log s}$. The proof combines the elimination technique and an arithmetic lemma of Fischler--Sprang--Zudilin, the hypergeometric constructions of Lai--Yu, and the Hankel determinant method that appeared in the proof that $\zeta(5)$ is irrational posted by Fauzan on September 17, 2026.
arxiv:2611.16156.authors: St\'ephane Fischler, Li Lai, Johannes Sprang, Wadim Zudilin

arxiv:2611.16685.title: Fluctuations of Local Patterns in Non-Periodic Uniquely Ergodic Systems
arxiv:2611.16685.summary: We study various families of non-periodic configurations of symbols assigned to vertices of regular graphs. We restrict ourselves to such systems where considered configurations support a uniquely ergodic measure. Symbols can be interpreted as particles and we are concerned with configurations which minimize the interaction energy of particles, the so-called ground-state configurations.

arxiv:2611.17357.title: Log-concavity of rank and crank statistics for integer partitions
arxiv:2611.17357.summary: Let $M(m,n)$ and $N(m,n)$ denote the numbers of partitions of $n$ with crank $m$ and rank $m$, respectively. Ji and Zang [Adv. Math. 2021] conjectured that $M(m,n)$ is log-concave in $m$ for $n\ge72$ and $|m|\le n-72$, and that $N(m,n)$ is log-concave in $m$ for $n\ge73$ and $|m|\le n-73$.

arxiv:2611.17358.title: Automatic $n$-dimensional recurrences over finite $p$-groups with negative predecessor coordinates
arxiv:2611.17358.summary: We study $n$-dimensional recurrences on $\mathbb{N}^n$ over finite $p$-groups. The rules are ordered products of group endomorphisms, with a $p$-automatic additional sequence and compatible $p$-automatic boundary data. For finite, nonempty, lexicographically positive predecessor sets, we prove automaticity whenever at most one coordinate contains entries of both signs.

arxiv:2611.17360.title: Positive Dual Certificates for Real Separated Subset Sums: Chamber Optimality of the Conway-Guy and Bohman Sets, and Exact Values up to Eight
arxiv:2611.17360.summary: Let $f_R(n)$ be the least possible largest element of a set of $n$ positive reals whose $2^n$ subset sums are pairwise at least 1 apart, and let $f_Z(n) \ge f_R(n)$ be the corresponding integer quantity of the Erd\H{o}s distinct subset sums problem. Fixing the signs of all signed relations $\varepsilon\cdot x$, $\varepsilon \in \{-1,0,1\}^n$, decomposes the real problem into polyhedral chambers, on each of which it is a linear program. We prove that for every $n$ the Conway-Guy set is the unique optimum of its chamber.

arxiv:2611.17378.title: A $19/5$ lower bound for the four-dimensional Erd\H{o}s box problem
arxiv:2611.17378.summary: For every power $q\ge2$ of~$2$, we construct a box-free subset of $[q^5]^4$ with $q^{19}$ points, improving the lower-bound exponent in the four-dimensional Erd\H{o}s box problem from $15/4$ to $19/5$. In fact, $[q^5]^4$ partitions into $q$ isomorphic box-free sets. The proof uses a finite-field rectangle lemma and orthogonality in a four-dimensional bilinear space.

arxiv:2611.17379.title: Region Coloring of Spatial Graphs using Knot-theoretic Ternary Quasigroups
arxiv:2611.17379.summary: We construct coloring conditions around vertices for region colorings of unoriented spatial graph diagrams by knot-theoretic ternary quasigroups. These conditions require cyclic products of left and right operators around each vertex to be the identity. We prove that the resulting coloring sets are preserved under the generalized Reidemeister moves and relate our construction to the palette framework.

arxiv:2611.17386.title: TSP instances that require exponentially many subtour elimination constraints
arxiv:2611.17386.summary: We construct pathological TSP instances that require exponentially many subtour elimination constraints (SECs) in the sense that, if a smaller collection of SECs is imposed, then the Dantzig-Fulkerson-Johnson model returns a disconnected solution costing less than an optimal tour. For asymmetric instances on $n$ vertices, we prove a growth rate of \(\Omega(\phi^n)\), where \(\phi\approx 1.618\) is the golden ratio. A node-splitting reduction gives metric instances with \(\Omega(\phi^{n/2})\) growth.

arxiv:2611.17397.title: Admissibility-Preserving Control for Block Strict-Feedback Systems Under Time-Varying Asymmetric Actuator and State Constraints
arxiv:2611.17397.summary: This paper addresses the tracking control of block strict-feedback nonlinear systems subject to time-varying asymmetric actuator and full state constraints. To that end, we develop a time-varying Admissibility-Preserving Control (APC) framework, in which the Admissibility-Preserving Input Realization (APIR) generates the plant input through a dynamic realization. The APIR guarantees input admissibility under the moving actuator set whenever each actuator bound contracts slower than the decay rate of the realization, and a closed-form lower bound on its gain is derived.
arxiv:2611.17397.authors: Saurabh Kumar, Lohitvel Gopikannan, Shashi Ranjan Kumar, Abhinav Sinha

arxiv:2611.17403.title: Graded unitarity constraints on simply-laced affine Kac--Moody algebras
arxiv:2611.17403.summary: We investigate constraints imposed by four-dimensional unitarity (recently formalised as graded unitarity) on possible simply-laced affine Kac--Moody vertex algebras arising from four dimensions via the SCFT/VOA correspondence. Under the assumption that the $\mathfrak{R}$-filtration is weight-based with respect to the currents and the Casimir operators, with appropriately shifted $R$-charge assignments for the latter, we demonstrate that all values of the level other than a discrete set are incompatible with four-dimensional unitarity. This set includes all the boundary admissible affine vertex algebras, those corresponding to rank-one Kodaira SCFTs, as well as certain non-admissible…

arxiv:2611.17419.title: Sasakian Hodge Numbers of Calabi-Yau Links
arxiv:2611.17419.summary: The link of an isolated weighted homogeneous hypersurface singularity whose degree equals the sum of its weights is a Sasakian manifold that admits a contact Calabi-Yau structure, and its Sasakian Hodge numbers are dimensions of graded pieces of the Milnor algebra of the defining polynomial. In earlier work these numbers were computed with Gr\"obner bases for the $7$-dimensional links of $7549$ of the $7555$ weighted Calabi-Yau threefold links, and two conjectures were raised from the data. The first asserts that polynomials with the same weights have Milnor algebras whose relevant graded pieces have equal dimensions; the second asserts that the Sasakian Hodge number $h^{2,1}_S$ of the link…
arxiv:2611.17419.authors: Edward Hirst, Henrique N. S\'a Earp, Tom\'as S. R. Silva

arxiv:2611.17443.title: $A_1^{(1)}$-Grounded partitions at levels $1$ and $2$, Part II: affine crystal structure
arxiv:2611.17443.summary: Grounded partitions are coloured partitions with difference conditions, introduced by Dousse and Konan, that are in bijection with the paths of the Kyoto path model of Kang, Kashiwara, Misra, Miwa, Nakashima and Nakayashiki. We describe the affine crystal structure on the grounded partitions arising from the level $1$ and level $2$ perfect crystals of type $A_1^{(1)}$. At level $1$, grounded partitions are naturally identified with $2$-restricted partitions, and the affine crystal structure is given by Kleshchev's modular branching rule for symmetric groups in characteristic $2$.

arxiv:2611.17465.title: Dimension bounds for higher Bruhat orders
arxiv:2611.17465.summary: We study the Dushnik-Miller dimension of higher Bruhat orders. For the inclusion order $B_{\mathrm{inc}}(n,k)$, with $k$ fixed, we prove that the order of dimension growth is $n^k$, by exhibiting standard examples for the lower bound and explicit systems of coordinates for the upper bound. A recent Tur\'an-system construction of Gao, Kuang, Pikhurko and Wang gives an upper coefficient within a factor smaller than $4$ of the lower coefficient.

arxiv:2611.17476.title: Ozone groups and fixed rings of double Ore extensions
arxiv:2611.17476.summary: We determine centers of two families of four-dimensional double Ore extensions without torsion assumptions, restricting to $f\ne0$ in $\mathcal O$. On the PI locus of $\mathcal K$, we classify the ozone groups and obtain normal commutative fixed rings of generic degree two over the center, including a nonmonogenic example. For an odd-torsion subfamily of $\mathcal O$, independent odd orders $n\geq1,m>1$ yield ozone group $C_n^2\times C_2^2$, PI degree $2nm$ and fixed-algebra PI degree $m$, with unchanged center.

arxiv:2611.17485.title: Quantum Fundamental Groups of Spaces with Finite-Sheeted Universal Covers
arxiv:2611.17485.summary: Discrete quantum groups have attracted much interest, but there was a lack of natural examples until Voigt constructed quantum permutations of finite and infinite sets in arXiv:2208.01310. In this paper, we construct the quantum fundamental groups that contain the classical fundamental groups as subgroups. This is a new class of natural examples of discrete quantum groups arising from symmetries of covering spaces in topology.
arxiv:2611.17485.authors: Shuzhou Wang, Zhenhua Wang, Matthew Zediker

arxiv:2611.17489.title: Isolation of $k$-cliques in uniform hypergraphs
arxiv:2611.17489.summary: A copy of a hypergraph $F$ is called an $F$-copy. For any integers $k$ and $r$ with $2 \leq r \leq k$, let $K_k^r$ denote the complete $r$-uniform hypergraph whose vertex set is $[k] = \{1, 2, \dots, k\}$ (that is, the edges of $K_k^r$ are the $r$-element subsets of $[k]$). Given an $r$-uniform $m$-edge hypergraph $H$, the $K_k^r$-isolation number of $H$, denoted by $\iota(H, K_k^r)$, is the size of a smallest subset $D$ of the vertex set of $H$ such that the closed neighbourhood $N[D]$ of $D$ intersects the vertex sets of the $K_k^r$-copies contained by $H$ (equivalently, $H-N[D]$ contains no $K_k^r$-copy).

arxiv:2611.17494.title: New Congruences for Simultaneously $l$-Regular and $t$-Distinct Partition in $k$-Colors
arxiv:2611.17494.summary: Let $RD_{\ell,t}^k(n)$ enumerates the number of $k$-colored simultaneously $l$-regular and $t$-distinct partitions. In this article, we establish some new infinite families of congruences modulo prime $p$, $p\geq5$ and modulo powers of 5 for $RD_{\ell,t}^k(n)$. For instance, for each $n\geq0$, $0\leq\alpha\leq{2k-2}$ and $k\geq1$, \begin{align*} \sum_{n=0}^{\infty}RD_{(5^{2k-1},5^{2k-1})}^2\big(5^{2k+\alpha-1}n+\frac{9\cdot5^{2k+\alpha-1}-2\cdot5^{2k-1}+1}{12}\big)q^n\equiv& 0\pmod{5^{k+\left[\frac{\alpha}{2}\right]}} \end{align*}
arxiv:2611.17494.authors: Anjelin Mariya Johnson, S. N. Fathima

arxiv:2611.17496.title: Wasserstein geometry of analytic cycle spaces
arxiv:2611.17496.summary: We use optimal transport to define an intrinsic distance on connected components of the Barlet space of analytic cycles on a compact K\"ahler manifold, by associating to each cycle its normalized volume measure. We prove that any two cycles in the same connected component can be joined by a deformation of finite Wasserstein length, and that the resulting metric is complete and geodesic. On the locus of smooth reduced cycles at regular parameter points, Wasserstein lengths and energies coincide with those of the normalized Weil--Petersson metric.
arxiv:2611.17496.authors: Fabio Cavalletti, Lorenzo Cecchi, Antonio Lerario

arxiv:2611.17510.title: Cartan Dynamics and Limit Sets on Flag Manifolds
arxiv:2611.17510.summary: The classical convergence principle describes the collapse of the Riemann sphere under divergent sequences of M\"obius transformations. We develop its counterpart for arbitrary real semisimple Lie groups acting on flag manifolds, and use it to study limit sets and domains of discontinuity of discrete subgroups. The key is to let the source move: the destination of $x$ under $(g_m)$ is the set of all limits of $g_mx_m$ with $x_m\to x$.
arxiv:2611.17510.authors: \'Angel Cano, Marlon M. L\'opez-Flores, Jos\'e Seade, Andrew Shaw

arxiv:2611.17525.title: Generalized Power Graph of a Group
arxiv:2611.17525.summary: In this paper, we introduce a new class of graphs, called generalized power graphs, and investigate some of their key properties, such as completeness, connectivity, and planarity.

arxiv:2611.17536.title: A new tautological relation on $\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{2,14}$ in cohomology
arxiv:2611.17536.summary: We construct a relation $\mathsf{Q}$ in the cohomological tautological ring $\mathsf{RH}^*(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{2,14})$ which lies outside the space of $3$-spin relations. $\mathsf{Q}$ is a simple linear combination of pure boundary strata classes of codimension 9 supported on the divisor $\Delta_0 \subset \overline{\mathcal{M}}_{2,14}$ of irreducible nodal curves, and transforms according to the irreducible representation of $\Sigma_{14}$ associated to the partition $(2^7)$. The result shows that the set of $3$-spin relations cannot be complete in cohomology.
arxiv:2611.17536.authors: Samir Canning, Bochao Kong, Rahul Pandharipande, Dan Petersen, Aaron Pixton, Johannes Schmitt

arxiv:2611.17542.title: On the Hofer-Zehnder conjecture for Reeb flows without symmetry
arxiv:2611.17542.summary: This paper continues our investigation of the Hofer-Zehnder conjecture for dynamically convex, non-degenerate Reeb pseudo-rotations of $S^{2n-1}$. The main result of the paper is that, for $n\geq 3$, such a flow has at most $n-3$ alternating prime closed orbits and hence at most $2n-3$ prime closed orbits in total. In particular, the flow on $S^5$ has exactly three prime closed orbits, all of which are non-alternating and elliptic.
arxiv:2611.17542.authors: Erman Cineli, Viktor L. Ginzburg, Basak Z. Gurel

arxiv:2611.17557.title: Freeness of crossed modules, augmented quandles, and augmented racks
arxiv:2611.17557.summary: We study freeness of crossed modules, augmented quandles, and augmented racks. We show that the associated quandle functor and the associated crossed module functor are left adjoint to the natural forgetful functors. For a map $f\colon S\to G$, we define the free augmented rack $R_f\to G$ and the free augmented quandle $Q_f\to G$.

arxiv:2611.17567.title: A proof of the Jamneshan-Tao conjecture by embedding nilspaces in nilmanifolds
arxiv:2611.17567.summary: We prove that every compact finite-rank nilspace admits a continuous injective morphism into a toral nilspace of the same step, and hence into a connected filtered nilmanifold. Combining this embedding theorem with the general nilspace inverse theorem, we establish the Jamneshan-Tao conjecture and extend its conclusion to second-countable compact abelian groups. This yields an inverse theorem for Gowers norms on all such groups, in which the correlating functions factor through morphisms into nilmanifolds.
arxiv:2611.17567.authors: Pablo Candela, Diego Gonz\'alez-S\'anchez, Bal\'azs Szegedy

arxiv:2611.17584.title: The Ulam sequence grows subexponentially
arxiv:2611.17584.summary: We prove that the $n$-th element of the Ulam sequence, a somewhat mysterious recursively-defined sequence of positive integers, has size $e^{O(\sqrt{n})}$; previous upper bounds were exponential in $n$. Our argument uses an additive-combinatorial lemma, possibly of independent interest, about covering finite difference sets with multiplicatively short intervals. The proofs are due to ChatGPT.

arxiv:2611.17624.title: The Gaps Between the $\Delta$-Unknotting Number and Its Lower Bounds
arxiv:2611.17624.summary: Let $u^{\Delta}(K)$ denote the $\Delta$-unknotting number of a knot $K$, and let $a_2(K)$ denote the second coefficient of the Conway polynomial. It is known that $u^{\Delta}(K)\geq |a_2(K)|$. We define the $\Delta$-gap of $K$ by $G^{\Delta}(K):=u^{\Delta}(K)-|a_2(K)|$.

arxiv:2611.17633.title: Complete Center Classification of a Quintic $\mathbb Z_2$-Equivariant System via Rational Descent and Ramification
arxiv:2611.17633.summary: We develop a new structural method to completely classify the elementary centers of a ten-parameter quintic $\mathbb Z_2$-equivariant system. The method overcomes the computational bottleneck of direct focus-quantity elimination by combining a Li\'enard reduction, a necessary-and-sufficient analytic involution criterion, and rational descent with residue and ramification analysis. We obtain forty-two explicit original-parameter conditions covering the entire center locus, including all degenerate and boundary cases.
arxiv:2611.17633.authors: Feng Li, Meilan Cai, Chaochao Sun

arxiv:2611.17647.title: Vector bundles on spin K\"ahler surfaces and the multi-spinor Seiberg-Witten equations
arxiv:2611.17647.summary: We compute new lower bounds on the second Chern class of a vector bundle $\mathscr{E}$ on a spin K\"ahler surface $X$ that satisfies $c_1(\mathscr{E}) = 0$ and $H^2(\text{End}_0\mathscr{E}) = 0.$ When $X$ is a regular elliptic surface and $\mathscr{E}$ has rank 2, our bound is sharp. Our technique is to use Furuta's finite-dimensional approximation on the multi-spinor Seiberg-Witten equations, together with their algebro-geometric interpretation by the second named author. We also use these techniques to prove an existence theorem for singular Fueter sections and multi-spinor Seiberg-Witten solutions that holds for every Riemannian metric on a large class of 4-manifolds.

arxiv:2611.17657.title: Schreier Sets And the Product of Fibonacci And Catalan Numbers
arxiv:2611.17657.summary: First, we introduce strictly super-Schreier sets, which provide a new combinatorial interpretation of products of Fibonacci and Catalan numbers. Second, we show that the numbers of sets in higher-order Schreier families do not satisfy any linear recurrence relation, thus answering a question in the existing literature.
arxiv:2611.17657.authors: Kevin Beanland, Hung Viet Chu, Carrie E. Finch-Smith

arxiv:2611.17677.title: Folding of cluster algebras
arxiv:2611.17677.summary: We develop a general framework for folding cluster algebras from simply-laced Cartan data equipped with admissible finite-group actions. For arbitrary finite sequences, we establish folding of root data, compatible pairs, $\bfi$-box seeds, and their individual cluster variables, without reducedness, finite-type, or acyclicity assumptions. In the reduced case, the folding is realized through quantum unipotent coordinate algebras and is compatible with dual PBW generators.

arxiv:2611.17678.title: Nonexistence of a quasi-symmetric $2$-$(33,15,35)$ design
arxiv:2611.17678.summary: It is shown that there exists no quasi-symmetric $2$-$(33,15,35)$ design with intersection numbers $6$ and $9$. This is proved by considering the ternary code generated by the incidence vectors of the blocks and its dual code.

arxiv:2611.17685.title: Semistable 1-Motives: Monodromy, Explicit Periods, and Local Duality
arxiv:2611.17685.summary: Let $K/\mathbf Q_p$ be unramified, with $p>2$. For a $1$-motive with constant lattice, split torus, and good abelian quotient, we compute the semistable extension complex from toric valuations and formal-group logarithms. A canonical monodromy boundary exists for every semistable representation; it detects splitting over crystalline periods and the increase in monodromy rank.

arxiv:2611.17702.title: General linear groups in tangent categories
arxiv:2611.17702.summary: General linear groups are well-studied Lie groups that encode the linear symmetries of a finitely-dimensional linear space. In differential geometry, they are an important ingredient of various constructions, including fibre bundles and the frame bundle of a principal bundle. They also appear in algebraic geometry as affine group schemes.
