arxiv:2611.17719.title: The non-stationary $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$ affine Laumon function and its difference equation
arxiv:2611.17719.summary: We present an explicit $q$-Givental type formula for the $\widehat{\mathfrak{gl}}_N$ non-stationary affine relativistic Toda or affine Laumon function introduced by Shiraishi. We prove the conjecture of [J. Shiraishi, Affine screening operators, affine Laumon spaces and conjectures concerning non-stationary Ruijsenaars functions.

arxiv:2611.17732.title: Rigidity for pivotal braided r-categories of moderate growth and applications to vertex operator algebras
arxiv:2611.17732.summary: Let $\mathcal{C}$ be an abelian pivotal braided r-category with simple unit object $\mathbf{1}$ over any field. We present a ChatGPT-generated proof, prompted by Bin Gui, that any object $X$ in $\mathcal{C}$ of moderate growth, in the sense that $\dim\mathrm{End}(X^{\otimes n})<n!$ for some $n\in\mathbb{Z}_{\geq 1}$, is rigid. The proof crucially uses ideas from the recent proof of Etingof and Penneys that $X$ is rigid if it is also non-negligible, that is, $X\otimes Y$ contains $\mathbf{1}$ as a direct summand for some object $Y$.

arxiv:2611.17734.title: Global generation of coinvariant vector bundles on $\overline{\mathrm{M}}_{0,n}$
arxiv:2611.17734.summary: Using fusion closed-ness and strong generation properties, we identify collections of modules over vertex operator algebras (VOAs) whose induced vector bundles of coinvariants on the moduli space $\overline{\mathrm M}_{0,n}$ of stable $n$-pointed curves of genus zero are globally generated. These results specialize to \cite{Fak12} for affine VOAs at positive integer levels, and of \cite{DG23} for strongly rational VOAs that are generated in degree 1. To illustrate the results, and to show that fusion-closedness is essential, we give numerous examples, including Lattice VOAs, Simple Current Extensions of Affine VOAs, and various tensor products.

arxiv:2611.17748.title: Exponential Double and Multiple Riordan Arrays as Fiber Products
arxiv:2611.17748.summary: A double Riordan array has nonzero entries only in positions $(n,k)$ with $n+k$ even, and its even and odd parts are Riordan arrays with the same multiplier function. We develop this observation systematically, with the emphasis on exponential double and exponential multiple Riordan arrays. Using generalized Riordan arrays with respect to a sequence $(c_n)$, we show that the double Riordan group, the exponential double Riordan group, the multiple Riordan group, and the exponential multiple Riordan group are fiber products of (generalized) Riordan groups over the Lagrange group.

arxiv:2611.17764.title: Rational lines on pairs of quadrics and cubic hypersurfaces
arxiv:2611.17764.summary: We study rational lines on smooth intersections of two quadrics and on smooth cubic hypersurfaces over number fields. For an intersection of two quadrics in $n$ variables, we prove the Hasse principle and weak approximation for the variety of lines when $n\geq 11$, and more generally for the variety of $r$-planes when $n\geq 3r+8$. In this range an $r$-plane exists over the ground field if and only if one exists over every real completion.
arxiv:2611.17764.authors: Tim Browning, Stephanie Chan, Nick Rome

arxiv:2611.17782.title: Exceptional sequences of line bundles on $\mathrm{Fl}(1,\ell;\ell+1)$
arxiv:2611.17782.summary: Let $X_\ell=\mathrm{Fl}(1,\ell;\ell+1)\subset\mathbb{P}^\ell\times(\mathbb{P}^\ell)^\vee$ be the incidence variety of points and hyperplanes in $\mathbb{P}^\ell$. We prove that for every $\ell\ge 3$, every exceptional sequence of line bundles on $X_\ell$ of maximal length $\ell(\ell+1)=\operatorname{rk} K_0(X_\ell)$ is full. Together with the case $\ell=2$, due to Altmann, Hochenegger and Witt, this shows that for all $\ell\ge2$ an exceptional sequence of line bundles on $X_\ell$ is full if and only if it has maximal length.

arxiv:2611.17799.title: Localization for Lipschitz monotone quasi-periodic operators with power-law hopping
arxiv:2611.17799.summary: We prove spectral and dynamical localization for quasi-periodic operators on $\mathbb Z^d$ with Lipschitz monotone potentials and power-law hopping. For sufficiently small coupling, localization holds at every allowed phase whenever the hopping decay exponent $r$ exceeds the Diophantine exponent $\tau$. The proof is based on multiscale analysis with exponentially growing scales.
arxiv:2611.17799.authors: Hongyi Cao, Yunfeng Shi, Peizhen Wang

arxiv:2611.17812.title: Closed formulas for the permanents of structured matrices
arxiv:2611.17812.summary: We give finite formulas for permanents of structured matrices and prove polynomial bounds for their evaluation. Over any field, the permanent of a matrix of bounded rank-width can be computed from the matrix alone, answering a question of Lyaudet. In characteristic $p>0$, the bound is $p^{O(k)}n^{O(1)}$, where $k$ is the rank-width.

arxiv:2611.17813.title: An accelerated multiobjective gradient flow with implicit Hessian-driven damping
arxiv:2611.17813.summary: In this paper, we propose an accelerated multiobjective gradient flow with implicit Hessian-driven damping for unconstrained convex multiobjective optimization problems in a real Hilbert space. The continuous flow is formulated as a system of two first-order equations involving only a single multiobjective projection operator and suitable time-scaling factors. Formally, it can also be expressed as a second-order system with explicit multiobjective Hessian-driven damping, which corresponds to the usual Hessian-driven damping introduced by Alvarez et al. [J.

arxiv:2611.17839.title: Weighted Euler transforms, real-rootedness, and $\gamma$-positivity
arxiv:2611.17839.summary: For $a>0$ and a polynomial $F$ of degree $m$, let $H_{a,F}$ denote the weighted Euler numerator of $F$, defined as the numerator of the generating function $\sum_{k\ge0}(a)_kF(k)x^k/k!$ with denominator $(1-x)^{a+m}$. For every $a>0$, we show the following preservation result: if the numerators $H_{a,F}$ and $H_{a,G}$ have only real nonpositive zeros, then the same holds for $H_{a,FG}$. The proof relies on an explicit multiplication formula in falling-factorial coordinates and a characterization of multiplier sequences for generalized Laguerre bases due to Br\"and\'en and Ottergren.

arxiv:2611.17841.title: Inequalities for intersection numbers from Hodge-Riemann relations
arxiv:2611.17841.summary: We derived inequalities for intersection numbers of nef classes inside algebras satisfying the K\"ahler package, using Hodge-Riemann relations up to degree two. As an application, we construct certain strictly Lorentzian polynomials and show that they cannot be realized as the volume polynomial of nef classes inside such an algebra.

arxiv:2611.17844.title: A Helly theorem for the Bruhat-Tits building
arxiv:2611.17844.summary: Let $K$ be a discretely valued field with valuation ring $\mathcal{O}$. We show that a finite family of $\mathcal{O}$-lattices in $K^m$ is adapted to a common basis if any subfamily of at most $m+1$ $\mathcal{O}$-lattices is. In other words, in the Bruhat-Tits building of $\operatorname{GL}(m)$, a finite family of simplices lies in a common apartment if and only if any subfamily of at most $m+1$ simplices does.
arxiv:2611.17844.authors: Rudrendra Kashyap, Kiumars Kaveh, Christopher Manon, Boris Tsvelikhovskiy

arxiv:2611.17847.title: Projective surfaces with infinite fundamental group and trivial profinite completion
arxiv:2611.17847.summary: For every nontrivial finite abelian group \(A\) of odd order, we construct a smooth complex projective surface with infinite topological fundamental group and trivial \'{e}tale fundamental group. The isomorphism types of its finite subgroups are precisely those of the subgroups of \(A\). The surface is Kobayashi hyperbolic and has Stein universal cover.

arxiv:2611.17855.title: On configurations that are nearly generalised polygons
arxiv:2611.17855.summary: Payne (1972) introduced nearly generalised $n$-gons as $(s+1)$-regular bipartite graphs of girth $2n$ with small excess over the Moore bound. Biggs and Ito (1980) proved nonexistence of such graphs if $s > 1$ and $n > 3$, leaving open the existence of regular antipodal planes. We revisit this problem from several equivalent viewpoints.
arxiv:2611.17855.authors: Sam Adriaensen, John Bamberg, Jason Williford

arxiv:2611.17885.title: Goodman-type lower bounds for graph homomorphism densities
arxiv:2611.17885.summary: For a finite graph $H$ with $v(H)$ vertices, chromatic number $\chi(H)$, and chromatic polynomial $P_H$, define $\Phi_H(p)=(1-p)^{v(H)}P_H((1-p)^{-1})$. This polynomial interpolates the homomorphism densities of $H$ in balanced complete multipartite graphons. We study the lower bound $t(H,W)\ge\Phi_H(p)$ on the homomorphism density of $H$ in graphons $W$ of edge density $p>1-1/(\chi(H)-1)$, which generalises Goodman's triangle bound.

arxiv:2611.17893.title: Fano-Enriques threefolds of Fano index $>1$
arxiv:2611.17893.summary: We study $\mathbb{Q}$-Fano threefolds of Fano index greater than $1$ whose Weil divisor class group has nontrivial torsion. We give a complete list of their possible numerical types: there are $176$ of them, which refine to $182$ possible graded Hilbert series. At least $40$ numerical types are realised: $27$ by quotients of weighted complete intersections by cyclic groups, twelve by quotients of threefolds of codimension $4$ or $5$ and one by a quotient of the del Pezzo threefold of degree $5$.

arxiv:2611.17901.title: Chow Stability of Polarized K3 Surfaces with ADE singularities
arxiv:2611.17901.summary: The asymptotic Chow stability of smooth polarized K3 surfaces is known through the existence of Ricci-flat metrics and Donaldson's theorem. We give a purely algebraic proof and extend the result to polarized K3 surfaces with at worst ADE singularities. The proof gives a uniform effective bound for the exponent, depending only on the degree of the polarization.

arxiv:2611.17989.title: The Exact Stabilization Time of Self-Stabilizing Coloring: Mean, Variance, and Distribution
arxiv:2611.17989.summary: The worst-case stabilization time of a self-stabilizing algorithm usually says little about its typical behavior beyond the order of magnitude. This paper revisits the classical self-stabilizing $Delta+1$ coloring algorithm with vertices activated at random, one at a time (the random central daemon). Considering the number of color changes as a random variable, we study its mean, variance and, on several families of graphs, its exact distribution.
arxiv:2611.17989.authors: {\'E}lie de Panafieu (NPA), Fabien Mathieu (NPA), Maria Gradinariu Potop-Butucaru (NPA), S{\'e}bastien Tixeuil (NPA, IUF)

arxiv:2611.17999.title: Additive cubes are avoidable over $\{0,1,2,3\}$, $\{0,1,4\}$ and $\{0,2,5\}$
arxiv:2611.17999.summary: We prove that additive cubes are avoidable over the alphabet $\{0,1,2,3\}$, thereby solving a long-standing question initiated by Pirillo and Varricchio in 1994. By extending the reduction and spectral machinery of Cassaigne, Currie, Schaeffer, and Shallit (2014), we prove that the search for additive cubes in such morphic images reduces to a finite graph traversal. We exhibit eight explicit morphisms from $\{0,1,3,4\}^*$ to $\{0,1,2,3\}^*$ of length 3 whose images on the Cassaigne \textit{et al.} infinite word contain no additive cubes.

arxiv:2611.18040.title: Hidden Quantum Markov Processes: Mealy Formulation and Observable Reduction
arxiv:2611.18040.summary: We formulate hidden quantum Markov processes in a Mealy architecture using a single completely positive unital transition expectation coupling the present hidden system, the emitted output, and the next hidden system. Together with a boundary state, it generates a quasi-local, finitely correlated hidden--output state; for the commutative generator associated with a classical Mealy kernel, this state is the full joint law of the classical Mealy model. Moore realizations correspond to transition expectations that factor on the prescribed hidden algebra.

arxiv:2611.18047.title: Twisted Fourier-Mukai partners of genus 1 curves
arxiv:2611.18047.summary: We study twisted derived equivalence between genus 1 curves over an arbitrarly perfect field.
arxiv:2611.18047.authors: Tanya Kaushal Srivastava, Sofia Tirabassi, Na\"ia Vivares

arxiv:2611.18058.title: Perfect Matching Complexes of $3\times 2n$ Grid Graph
arxiv:2611.18058.summary: The perfect matching complex of a simple graph $G$ is an abstract simplicial complex whose facets (maximal faces) are precisely the perfect matchings of $G$. In this article, we study the topology of the perfect matching complex of the $3\times 2n$ grid graph and show that it is homotopy equivalent to a wedge of $f_{n-1}$ copies of $(n-1)$-dimensional spheres, where $f_{k}$ denotes the $k$-th Fibonacci number. This proves a particular case of the conjecture given by Chandrakar and Singh for perfect matching complex of grid graphs.
arxiv:2611.18058.authors: Himanshu Chandrakar, Trung Chau, Shuchita Goyal, Rahul Karki, B. Subhash

arxiv:2611.18059.title: Compatible zero-sum partitions of finite Abelian groups and their applications
arxiv:2611.18059.summary: Let $(\Gamma,+)$ be a finite Abelian group and let $g\in\Gamma\setminus\{0\}$. A partition of $\Gamma$ is called $g$-compatible if no part contains both $x$ and $x+g$. For a prescribed involution $h$ and odd $r\ge3$, we prove that $\Gamma$ admits an $h$-compatible partition into zero-sum $r$-element sets if and only if $r$ divides $|\Gamma|$ and $\Gamma$ has at least three involutions.

arxiv:2611.18076.title: Upper bounds for the number of spanning forests of a graph
arxiv:2611.18076.summary: Let $G$ be a simple graph on $n$ vertices, and let $F(G)$ denote the number of spanning forests of $G$. Bencs and Csikv\'ari proved that every $r$-regular graph $G$ with $r\ge 2$ satisfies $F(G)\le r^n$. Motivated by this result, they conjectured that if $G$ has minimum degree at least $3$, then $F(G)\leq \prod_{i=1}^n d_i$, where $(d_1, d_2, \dots, d_n)$ is the degree sequence of $G$.
arxiv:2611.18076.authors: Tingzeng Wu, Shuxin Lu, Xiangshuai Dong

arxiv:2611.18083.title: Separability defects in artificial satellite theory: intermediaries, zonal harmonics and secular separatrices
arxiv:2611.18083.summary: A five-input Poisson-bracket operator, which reproduces the Levi-Civita separability expressions and is cubic in the Hamiltonian, is used as a diagnostic of artificial satellite theory, in a modified polar-nodal chart regular at prograde equatorial orbits. For the general intermediary proposed by the author in 2020, covering those of Sterne, Garfinkel, Brouwer, Aksnes, Cid and Lahulla and Deprit, the linearised defects vanish if and only if the integrability ansatz holds, the condition for additive first-order Hamilton-Jacobi separation in polar-nodal variables. Second-order defects follow in closed form, and the coupling with the nodal pair comes from the dependence on the physical…

arxiv:2611.18087.title: On the convergence of the False Nearest Neighbours algorithm
arxiv:2611.18087.summary: The False Nearest Neighbours (FNN) algorithm is one of the most widely used methods for choosing the embedding dimension, i.e. the number $k$ of delay coordinates, in the time-delay reconstruction of a dynamical system from an observed scalar time series. We prove rigorous results on the behaviour of this algorithm for long time series. We consider a smooth dynamical system on a compact manifold $M$ and an invariant probability measure $\mu$.

arxiv:2611.18102.title: Singularly embedded solitons and Stokes phenomenon in the fifth order KdV equation
arxiv:2611.18102.summary: We study embedded solitons (ES) in a fifth-order Korteweg-de Vries (KdV) equation near a reversible Hamiltonian saddle-centre bifurcation. The solitons correspond to homoclinic orbits to an equilibrium whose linearisation has a pair of real and a pair of purely imaginary eigenvalues. Existence of symmetric homoclinic near the bifurcation is a codimension-one phenomenon governed by a parameter-dependent Stokes constant associated with an inner equation.
arxiv:2611.18102.authors: Roberto Barrio, Vassili Gelfreich, J. Tom\'as L\'azaro, Juan Ramon Pacha

arxiv:2611.18134.title: On the Construction of New Families of Distance Equienergetic Graphs
arxiv:2611.18134.summary: For a graph $G$ with vertex set $V(G)=\{v_{i}:1\leq i \leq p\}$ and edge set $E(G)=\{e_{j}:1\leq j \leq q\},$ its subdivision graph $S_G$ is generalized to $S_{G}(n,m),$ by replacing each vertex $v_{i}$ with $n$ vertices and each edge-vertex $e_{j}$ with $m$ vertices, with each copy having the same neighbors as the vertex it replaces. Building on this construction, we define the generalized subdivision vertex join $S_{G_{1}}(n,m)\dot{\vee} G_{2}$ and the generalized subdivision edge join $S_{G}(n,m)\veebar G_{2},$ which extend the known subdivision vertex and subdivision edge join of graphs. In this paper, we determine the distance spectrum of $S_{G_{1}}(n,n)\dot{\vee} G_{2}$ and…

arxiv:2611.18167.title: Equidistribution of Gross lattices of supersingular elliptic curves
arxiv:2611.18167.summary: For a prime $p$, we consider two important families of integral quadratic lattices associated to isomorphism classes of supersingular elliptic curves over $\overline{\mathbb{F}_{p}}$, the lattices of endomorphisms of trace zero, and the Gross lattices of endomorphisms. We prove effective equidistribution of the shapes of these lattices as $p\to\infty$ through primes, in the arithmetic locally symmetric space of unimodular lattices up to isometry. As an application, we obtain, as $p\to\infty$, the asymptotic distribution of successive minima of these lattices.

arxiv:2611.18193.title: Graphs attaining Haemers' toughness bound
arxiv:2611.18193.summary: Haemers \cite{Haemers2020} conjectured that every connected noncomplete graph $G$ satisfies $t(G)\geqslant\mu_2/(\mu_n-\delta)$, where $t(G)$ is the toughness of $G$, $\mu_2$ and $\mu_n$ are its algebraic connectivity and Laplacian spectral radius, and $\delta$ is its minimum degree. Greaves and Zhu \cite{GreavesZhu2026} recently proved this conjecture, leaving the equality case open. We characterize all graphs attaining equality: a graph attains equality if and only if its complement has a complete component whose order is at least the Laplacian spectral radius of every other component.

arxiv:2611.18194.title: The M\"obius function of factorizations with a simple prime factor
arxiv:2611.18194.summary: The poset of factorizations of a positive integer $n$ (ordered by refinement) is known to have a very irregular M\"obius function. We prove that this function becomes completely explicit whenever $n$ is divisible by a prime $q$ to the first power only ($q^2 \nmid n$). Specifically, between a factorization with $k$ factors and $n$ itself, the M\"obius function is given by $(-1)^{k-1}$ multiplied by the number of ways to order the factors that are not divisible by $q$.

arxiv:2611.18195.title: Stability theorems for $\varepsilon$-simplicial sets
arxiv:2611.18195.summary: We establish stability results for internal homs of $\varepsilon$-simplicial sets, a framework motivated by nerves of Frobenius monoids in the category of relations. Rotations are modelled through edge witnesses and horn-filling conditions, without requiring unique fillers. For $\varepsilon$-fibrant objects $X$ and $Y$, we prove that the internal hom $\mathrm{Fun}(X,Y)$ satisfies the $\varepsilon$-coherence conditions and admits fillers for all $\varepsilon$-horns of dimension at least two.

arxiv:2611.18198.title: Infinite Index Identities for Argyres-Douglas Theories and Graded Vector Space Isomorphisms for VOAs
arxiv:2611.18198.summary: Supersymmetric indices provide stringent tests of dualities between superconformal field theories (SCFTs). We establish infinite families of Schur-index identities among four-dimensional $\mathcal N=2$ Argyres-Douglas (AD) theories, with the logarithms of their fugacities related linearly. These identities connect theories with markedly different physical properties without requiring infrared duality, while still implying simple relations among their central charges and flavor levels.

arxiv:2611.18212.title: Frobenius and perfection in framed motives
arxiv:2611.18212.summary: We develop explicit Frobenius and perfection arguments for framed motives over imperfect fields. In positive characteristic, power framing homotopies and local framed transfers make relative Frobenius invertible after inverting the characteristic. Descent through successive Frobenius twists then gives a proof of strict homotopy invariance for homotopy invariant quasi-stable additive framed presheaves and identifies the canonical comparison with the perfect closure as a stable Nisnevich local equivalence of framed motives.

arxiv:2611.18218.title: The Chabauty--Kim dimension inequality via noncommutative Iwasawa theory
arxiv:2611.18218.summary: We establish Kim's conjectural dimension inequality for smooth projective geometrically connected curves $C/\mathbb{Q}$ of genus at least two with a rational basepoint. For every odd prime $p$ of good reduction, we prove that $$\mathrm{dim} H_f^1(G_{\mathbb{Q},\Sigma},U_n^\mathrm{\'et}) < \mathrm{dim}(U_n^{\mathrm{dR}}/F^0)$$ for all sufficiently large $n$, where $U_n^\mathrm{\'et}$ and $U_n^\mathrm{dR}$ are the $n$'th lower central series truncations of the $\mathbb{Q}_p$-pro-unipotent geometric \'etale, and de Rham fundamental groups of $C$, and $\Sigma$ is any finite set of places containing $p$, $\infty$, and the primes of bad reduction. Inspired by Coates and Kim's work on curves with…

arxiv:2611.18222.title: Motivic Invariants of Automorphisms and the Plane Cremona Group
arxiv:2611.18222.summary: Recent work of Campbell and Zakharevich studies the $K$-theory spectrum of varieties. In previous work, the second author constructs a derived version of the $\mathbb{A}^1$-Euler characteristic, giving a map out of this spectrum. We analyse the morphism that the derived $\mathbb{A}^1$-Euler characteristic induces out of $K_1(\mathrm{Var}_k)$.
arxiv:2611.18222.authors: Ran Azouri, Anubhav Nanavaty, Jesse Pajwani

arxiv:2611.18231.title: Periodic orbits of quadratic polynomials of periods six and seven
arxiv:2611.18231.summary: The dynamics of quadratic polynomials is commonly studied by using the family of maps f_{c}(x) = x^{2} + c, where c include C. In this paper we form equations of periodic orbits of periods six and seven on a new (u,v)-plane and consider also the corresponding equations on the (x,y)-plane. The new (u,v)-model produces equations for the periods six and seven with significantly lower degree than the ones obtained by the previous models which enables us to find their solutions.

arxiv:2611.18237.title: Link invariants in nilpotent group gauge theories
arxiv:2611.18237.summary: We consider 3-dimensional topological gauge theories with nilpotent gauge groups, both finite, that is Dijkgraaf-Witten theories, and continuous, that is Chern-Simons theories. Abelian topological quantum field theories are exactly those which do not detect the Borromean rings, and nilpotent gauge groups provide the natural next steps beyond the abelian case. We show that the untwisted Dijkgraaf-Witten theory with gauge group $G$ detects Brunnian links with up to $n+1$ components, but no Brunnian links with more components, if and only if $G$ is $n$-step nilpotent.
arxiv:2611.18237.authors: Thomas Nicosanti, Pavel Putrov, Johann Quenta-Raygada

arxiv:2611.18258.title: Equivariant resolution of singularities for $T$-varieties in positive characteristic
arxiv:2611.18258.summary: Let the ground field be algebraically closed of positive characteristic. We prove that every variety endowed with an algebraic torus action whose general orbits have codimension at most three admits an equivariant resolution of singularities. The proof combines the description of such varieties in terms of proper polyhedral divisors and divisorial fans, the existence of log resolutions in dimension at most three, and the resolution of toroidal embeddings established by Kempf, Knudsen, Mumford and Saint-Donat.

arxiv:2611.18289.title: Transforming local positivity: from minimal valuations to irrational Seshadri constants
arxiv:2611.18289.summary: We explain how a valuative Nagata type statement proposed by Dumnicki, Harbourne, K\"uronya, Ro\'e and Szemberg on a polarised surface $(S, H)$ implies maximality (and hence often irrationality) of Seshadri constants on simple cyclic covers. As sample applications we show that very general degree two K3 surfaces and very general hypersurfaces in $\mathbb P^3$ of degree $6$, $8$ or $d\geq 10$ have irrational Seshadri constant at a very general point, unless $d$ is a square.

arxiv:2611.18296.title: From Butson Hadamard switching to graph switching and back
arxiv:2611.18296.summary: Switching is a local operation that preserves specified properties of a combinatorial object. It has been used to derive constructions of inequivalent Hadamard matrices and nonisomorphic cospectral graphs. In this paper we investigate the relation between these constructions for real and Butson Hadamard matrices.
arxiv:2611.18296.authors: Aida Abiad, Ronan Egan, Stef Mohnen

arxiv:2611.18317.title: Non-abelian Hodge correspondence for semistable parabolic connections on curves in positive characteristic
arxiv:2611.18317.summary: Let $C$ be a smooth projective curve over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic $p>0$. We establish a non-abelian Hodge correspondence between semistable parabolic connections on $C$ and semistable parabolic Higgs bundles on its Frobenius twist $C'$, allowing arbitrary prescribed residue eigenvalues, parabolic weights and filtration types. The relationship between the parabolic weights and residue eigenvalues on the two sides is encoded in a table analogous to Simpson's table.

arxiv:2611.18320.title: All coupling Anderson localization in the quantum kicked rotor model
arxiv:2611.18320.summary: In this paper, we study $$\mathscr{H}=\lambda \Delta +\tan\pi(\theta+n^2\alpha)\delta_{n,n'},\ n\in\Bbb Z$$ and prove its Anderson localization for all $\lambda >0$ and Lebesgue almost every (a.e.) $(\alpha, \theta)\in\Bbb T^2$. This conforms in the full measure sense the main assumption of Fishman-Grempel-Prange [{\it Phys. Rev.

arxiv:2611.18344.title: Enumeration of Cospectral Graphs with Respect to the Average Flow Matrix
arxiv:2611.18344.summary: A graph is said to be determined by the spectrum of a graph-associated matrix if no nonisomorphic graph shares the same spectrum with it. In this paper, we introduce the average flow matrix of a connected graph and study its spectral properties. We investigate its effectiveness in distinguishing graphs by carrying out a computational enumeration of connected graphs having a cospectral mate with respect to this matrix up to order 10.

arxiv:2611.18353.title: Cover times of random recursive trees and linear preferential attachment trees
arxiv:2611.18353.summary: We study the cover times of uniform random recursive trees and linear preferential attachment trees, including the negative-parameter models corresponding to random $d$-ary increasing trees. We prove explicit limits in probability and expectation when the cover times are rescaled by $n (\log n)^2$. In particular, for the uniform random recursive tree the cover time is close to $e n (\log n)^2$ with high probability.
arxiv:2611.18353.authors: Omer Angel, Christina Goldschmidt, Peleg Michaeli

arxiv:2611.18357.title: The Moduli of Canonical Threefolds of Minimum Volume
arxiv:2611.18357.summary: We determine the moduli space of complex projective canonical threefolds of volume $1/420$. It consists of an irreducible rational component of dimension $33$ and two isolated points, represented by the explicitly constructed rigid threefolds Vega and Altair.
arxiv:2611.18357.authors: Pinxian Bie, Peien Du, Zhengjie Yu

arxiv:2611.18358.title: Quadratic APN Functions of $\mathbb{F}_2^{10}$ with a Self-Equivalence of Prime Order
arxiv:2611.18358.summary: Almost perfect nonlinear (APN) functions of $\mathbb{F}_2^n$ have the lowest possible differential uniformity. The only known APN permutation in even dimension, in dimension six, is equivalent to a quadratic APN function with a nontrivial linear self-equivalence; no APN permutation is known for even $n \geq 8$. In a published collection of about 3.8 million quadratic APN classes of dimension eight, at most 0.34% have a nontrivial linear self-equivalence.

arxiv:2611.18374.title: The $\operatorname{Proj}$ construction for pro-graded Huber pairs
arxiv:2611.18374.summary: Inspired by the theory of pro-graded adic rings developed recently by Ishizuka and Yoshikawa, we introduce and study the notions of a pro-graded Huber ring and a pro-graded Huber pair \begin{equation*}((\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{A}_{\textrm{gr}}), \mathcal{A}^{+}),\end{equation*}which capture the intuition of a complete Huber ring (or Huber pair) equipped with a dense graded subring. Using these notions, we define and study an analog \begin{equation*}\operatorname{Proj}(\mathcal{A}, \mathcal{A}_{\textrm{gr}}, \mathcal{A}^{+})\end{equation*}of the $\operatorname{Proj}$ construction from algebraic geometry in the realm of adic spaces, without restricting our attention to adic spaces satisfying…

arxiv:2611.18384.title: From Diagonal Coloring to Proper Vertex Labelings Distinguishing Adjacent Facial Sums
arxiv:2611.18384.summary: In this paper we study proper vertex labelings of 3-connected plane graphs that give distinct boundary-vertex sums to faces sharing an edge. Let $\lambda(G)$ be the least $k$ for which labels from $\{0,\ldots,k\}$ suffice, and let $\laml(G)$ be its arbitrary-real-list counterpart. Our two main results are an eight-element list theorem for fullerenes and the universal bound $\lambda(G)\le708587$ for all 3-connected plane graphs.

arxiv:2611.18391.title: Color Refinement Distinguishes Connected Rooted Outerplanar Graphs
arxiv:2611.18391.summary: Color refinement, also known as the $1$-dimensional Weisfeiler-Leman algorithm ($1$-WL), is a classical near-linear-time heuristic for graph isomorphism, which also captures the expressive power of message-passing graph neural networks. A long line of work asks on which graph classes $1$-WL, or its higher-dimensional variant $k$-WL, identifies every graph; the least such $k$ is the WL-dimension of the class. Planar graphs have WL-dimension at most $3$ (Kiefer, Ponomarenko and Schweitzer, 2019), and whether $2$-WL already distinguishes all planar graphs is a central open problem.
arxiv:2611.18391.authors: Louann Coste (DI-ENS), M{\'o}nika Csik{\'o}s (IRIF), Laurent Viennot (DI-ENS, ARGO)

arxiv:2611.18432.title: A quotient formula for the Behrend function
arxiv:2611.18432.summary: The Behrend function is essential in enumerative geometry. However, computing it, even in zero dimension, has been a highly subtle and mysterious matter since its introduction in the 2000s. We present a quotient formula for the Behrend function of any closed $r$-dimensional affine scheme $X^r \subset \mathbb{A}^N$, evaluated at a singular point, where $0\leq r \leq N-1$.

arxiv:2611.18461.title: An Obstruction to Realizing Aspherical $3$-Manifold Groups via Torus Surgery
arxiv:2611.18461.summary: Let $Y$ be a closed, connected, oriented, aspherical $3$-manifold with fundamental group $\pi = \pi_1(Y)$ and positive first Betti number $\beta_1(Y) > 0$, and let $X_0 = Y \times S^1$. We prove that no torus surgery on $X_0$ along a torus-fibered $T^2$-knot $T \subseteq X_0$ can yield a $4$-manifold $X = X_{0; T, f}$ with fundamental group $\pi$. The obstruction combines the vanishing of the Euler characteristic of $X$ with a classifying-map argument showing that the unimodular intersection form on $H^2(X; \mathbb{Z})$ must admit an isotropic subgroup of rank $\beta_1(\pi)$, forcing $\chi(X) \geq 2$.

arxiv:2611.18474.title: Efficient Reconfiguration of Independent Transversals
arxiv:2611.18474.summary: We study the reconfiguration of independent transversals in graphs with a prescribed vertex partition. Given a graph $G$ with a vertex partition $\mathcal{V}=(V_1,\ldots,V_m)$, an independent transversal is an independent set containing exactly one vertex from each part $V_i$ of $\mathcal{V}$. The reconfiguration problem concerns transforming one independent transversal into another through a sequence of local changes, while preserving the independent transversal property at every step.

arxiv:2611.18483.title: Rigidity of the moving particle lemma for the interchange process
arxiv:2611.18483.summary: Let $G=(V,c)$ be a finite connected weighted graph. We establish the exact conditions for attaining equality in the moving particle lemma for the interchange process on $G$ subject to a unit voltage drop across two terminal vertices $x\neq y \in V$. First, equality can occur only in irreducible representations indexed by partitions with at most two rows.

arxiv:2611.18495.title: Cohen Macaulayness and Buchsbaumness of Cartesian Products of Paths and Cycles
arxiv:2611.18495.summary: We study the independence complexes of Cartesian products of paths and cycles. Let G(m,n) denote the Cartesian product of the path P_m and the cycle C_n, and let Delta(m,n) denote its independence complex. We determine the well-covered graphs in this family and use reduced homology to study their Cohen-Macaulay and Buchsbaum properties.

arxiv:2611.18518.title: Polytopal realization of double root free subword complexes
arxiv:2611.18518.summary: We give a convex geometric sufficient condition for a convex polytope to realize a spherical subword complex. Using this criterion, we first prove that each root independent spherical subword complex is polytopal, for any Coxeter group. Then we prove the polytopality of double root free subword complexes, for any Coxeter groups.

arxiv:2611.18555.title: Towards invertibility of derived categories of sheaf-theoretic line operators
arxiv:2611.18555.summary: We investigate when the braided monoidal $\infty$-categories of sheaf-theoretic line operators of $3$-dimensional topological quantum field theories are invertible in the higher Morita category, so that they determine invertible $4$-dimensional anomaly theories. We consider a zoo of different examples which are inherently derived. First, enhancing Ben-Zvi--Francis--Nadler, we show that a symmetric monoidal category of quasi-coherent sheaves $\mathrm{QC}(X)$ is invertible only if $X$ is a point, and convolution categories on loop stacks are Morita trivial whenever the stack satisfies descent along its diagonal, e.g. for classifying stacks.

arxiv:2611.18560.title: On the pure part of the cohomology of character varieties
arxiv:2611.18560.summary: We prove the purity conjecture of Hausel and Rodriguez-Villegas relating the graded dimension of the pure part of the cohomology of the twisted character variety $M^B(r,d)$ of $GL(r)$ of genus $g$ with the cohomology of a suitable quiver variety associated to the quiver $S_g$ with one vertex and $g$ loops. In particular, this provides an explicit formula for the pure part of the mixed Hodge polynomial of $M^B(r,d)$ in terms of the Kac polynomial $A_{S_g,r}(q)$. Our approach is based on the $P=W$ theorem to transfer the purity conjecture into a statement about the perverse filtration on the cohomology of th stack of Higgs bundles on a genus $g$ curve.

arxiv:2611.18633.title: Minimum cores in lattice graphs: zonotope structure and quartic growth
arxiv:2611.18633.summary: A core of a graph is a nonempty vertex set in which every member has at least as many neighbours inside the set as outside. We study the minimum size $c_{m,n}$ of a finite core in the graph on $\Z^m$ joining points at sup-norm distance at most $n$. The local majority condition imposes a global geometric constraint: the convex hull of every core has an explicit lattice zonotope $H_n^{(m)}$ as a Minkowski summand.

arxiv:2611.18684.title: Delaunay Combinatorics of the Moduli and Teichm\"uller Space of Closed Genus-Two Riemann Surfaces
arxiv:2611.18684.summary: Every closed Riemann surface of genus two is hyperelliptic, so it is determined by six branch points on the sphere, which become cone points of angle pi in the quotient orbifold metric. The Delaunay decomposition of these cone points, dual to the Voronoi diagram of the Weierstrass points, gives a trivalent graph with eight vertices, twelve edges and six faces. We classify these graphs.

arxiv:2611.18709.title: Generalized particle systems: a locality-factorized metamodel for self-propelled particles and agent-based models
arxiv:2611.18709.summary: We propose a single formal object, the generalized particle system (GPS), under which self-propelled particle systems (SPPS) and agent-based models (ABMs) are instances of one construction. A GPS is a typed finite population, a per-particle state space with arbitrary internal structure, a global environment, a neighbourhood map that may depend on the configuration, and type-indexed local rules; these assemble into a generator whose iteration is a monoid action, i.e. an autonomous dynamical system. Update schedules and stochastic rules are added at the same generality, so sequential and noisy models (the original Primordial Particle System, Vicsek) are covered, not approximated.

arxiv:2611.18719.title: Triadic and assortative structure of absorbing states in the Axelrod model
arxiv:2611.18719.summary: We study the Axelrod model of cultural dissemination, viewed as a finite-state Markov chain on an arbitrary finite graph, and classify its absorbing states. An absorbing configuration splits the edges into interior edges, whose endpoints share their whole culture, and boundary edges, whose endpoints share nothing. A partition of the vertices into connected blocks is the domain partition of some absorbing configuration exactly when its quotient graph is properly $q$-colourable.

arxiv:2611.18745.title: Rank-One Sutured Instanton Homology Detects Homology Products
arxiv:2611.18745.summary: We prove that a balanced sutured manifold $(M,\gamma)$ satisfying $\dim_{\mathbb C} SHI(M,\gamma)=1$ is an integral homology product; that is, $H_*(M,R_-(\gamma);\mathbb Z)=H_*(M,R_+(\gamma);\mathbb Z)=0$. Consequently, for every taut balanced sutured manifold $(M,\gamma)$, $SHI(M,\gamma)\cong\mathbb C$ if and only if $(M,\gamma)$ is a product sutured manifold. The proof uses the enhanced Euler characteristic of $SHI$ and a specialization formula for sutured torsion.

arxiv:2611.18752.title: Lower semicontinuity of dimension for quasi-Bernoulli measures under conformal projections
arxiv:2611.18752.summary: We study the dependence of the Hausdorff dimension of projected quasi-Bernoulli measures on a conformal iterated function system on the real line. For every fixed quasi-Bernoulli probability measure on the symbolic space, we prove that the dimension of its push-forward under the coding map is lower semicontinuous in the $C^{1+\theta}$ topology, without any separation assumption or shift-invariance requirement on the symbolic measure. The proof combines bounded distortion and finite-scale entropy estimates with uniform control of the entropy dimension over measures whose densities are bounded above and below.

arxiv:2611.18762.title: Field algebras associated with non-symmetric lattices
arxiv:2611.18762.summary: Field algebras, introduced by Bakalov and Kac, generalize vertex algebras by replacing locality with a weaker associativity-type axiom. We develop the structure theory of field algebras with a view toward geometric examples in which a natural bilinear form fails to be symmetric. We prove a reconstruction theorem for field algebras, producing a field algebra structure from a generating family of fields.

arxiv:2611.18776.title: Determinants of amphichiral knots of braid index at most three
arxiv:2611.18776.summary: We show that an odd number n is the determinant of an amphichiral knot of braid index at most three if and only if both n and n + 4 are sums of two squares. The proof rests on the known description of amphichiral knots of braid index three as closures of alternating 3-braid words with a rotation or reflection symmetry (Birman--Menasco, Stoimenov, Jung). Determinant formulas for closed 3-braids are also known (e.g. through the reduced Burau representation at t = -1); what is added here is their evaluation on the two symmetric families, which gives the condition on n + 4, and an explicit construction for the converse.

arxiv:2611.18787.title: The cop number of the flower snarks, and the generalized Petersen graphs with cop number two
arxiv:2611.18787.summary: We study two questions of Morris, Runte and Skelton (Australas. J. Combin. 83 (2022)) on the game of Cops and Robbers.

arxiv:2611.18788.title: Self-adjoint boundary conditions for equation-free multiscale modelling
arxiv:2611.18788.summary: Equation-free modelling is a computation multiscale modelling scheme for the simulation of complex dynamical systems. Efficient computations are achieved by solving the given microscale model in small, well-separated `patches' spread across the space-time domain, with each patch providing a data point for the macroscale simulation. Patch coupling bridges the unsimulated space between patches and supports the macroscale dynamics.

arxiv:2611.18817.title: Invariant measures with uniform projection on surfaces and billiards
arxiv:2611.18817.summary: In this paper, we study probability measures on the unit tangent bundle which are invariant under the geodesic flow and whose projection to the base manifold is the normalized Riemannian volume. We show that the Liouville measure is the only such measure on a complete oriented surface of finite area with ergodic geodesic flow. In particular, this resolves a conjecture of Katok--Knieper--Weiss in dimension two.

arxiv:2611.18852.title: A toric construction of the spectral Tate curve
arxiv:2611.18852.summary: We develop toric geometry spectral algebraic geometry. In particular, we lift toric varieties to flat schemes over the sphere spectrum. Furthermore, we prove several rigidity and strictness results allowing us to define and produce strict group actions of flat algebraic tori.

arxiv:2611.18853.title: Quasi-product and multiplicative Markov measures Radon-Nikodym problem, random walks: the free group case
arxiv:2611.18853.summary: The purpose of this paper is a conceptual clarification of the role of a special class of measures on topological Markov chains - multiplicative Markov measures - in the context of random walks. It is achieved by combining the interpretation of multiplicative Markov measures on the boundary of a free group as the unique solutions of the Radon - Nikodym problem for product cocycles of the boundary action and the fact that the Radon - Nikodym cocycle of the harmonic measure of a nearest neighbour random walk on a free group is a product one.

arxiv:2611.18875.title: The conductors of fibered Burnside rings
arxiv:2611.18875.summary: We give an explicit formula for the conductors of the primitive idempotents of fibered Burnside algebras of finite rank. This formula generalizes previous results for Burnside rings, monomial representation rings, and cyclic fibers, removing the coprimality condition required in the latter case. We also derive some consequences for cyclic fiber groups and $p$-groups.

arxiv:2611.18907.title: The Walsh spectrum of the Dobbertin APN function
arxiv:2611.18907.summary: APN functions yield the best resistance to differential attacks when used as a building block of a block cipher. APN functions induced by monomials over finite fields have received particular interest both for their simplicity and their unique properties. A key property of APN functions is their linearity, which has been determined for all known APN monomials outside of the Dobbertin APN monomials.

arxiv:2611.18917.title: History independence and base-dominant rigidity for polynomial skew products
arxiv:2611.18917.summary: We study history independence of fast directions and its relation to the Binder--DeMarco dimension formula for regular polynomial skew products of degree $d\ge2$. Assuming uniform expansion on the support of the measure of maximal entropy and a base Lyapunov exponent larger than the vertical exponent, we prove that history independence is equivalent to conjugacy to a polynomial product by an affine shear map. Under history independence, the measure of maximal entropy satisfies the Binder--DeMarco dimension formula.

arxiv:2611.18921.title: Odd-degree cycles and rationality of Peskine sixfolds of discriminant 24
arxiv:2611.18921.summary: Benedetti and Faenzi conjectured that, for a general trivector $\sigma\in\mathcal D^{1,6,10}$, the Peskine sixfold $X_1^\sigma$ is rational if the Brauer class $\beta$ on the associated K3 surface vanishes. We prove this implication for every $\sigma$ in a nonempty Zariski open subset $U\subset\mathcal D^{1,6,10}$. When $\beta=0$, we construct a line on the generic fiber of the Peskine fibration after a cubic field extension and use odd-degree descent to obtain a line over the original function field.

arxiv:2611.18940.title: Proper implies improper for the chromatic symmetric function
arxiv:2611.18940.summary: Stanley's question of whether the chromatic symmetric function distinguishes trees has been unanswered for over thirty years. It has now been checked for trees with at most 29 vertices, and for several classes of trees. There is the perception that answering the question might be easier for the class of ``proper'' trees, i.e. trees where every vertex is either a leaf or adjacent to a leaf.

arxiv:2611.18959.title: Rigidity for Families of Abelian Varieties over $\mathcal{M}_{g,n}$
arxiv:2611.18959.summary: We provide a new proof of Farb's theorem on the global rigidity of the period map $\mathcal{M}_{g,n} \to \mathcal{A}_g$. We extend this classification to essentially include the period map for $\mathcal{M}_{2,n}$. We also provide a classification of holomorphic maps $\mathcal{M}_g \to \mathcal{A}_{h}$ for $h \leq 2g-1$.

arxiv:2611.18966.title: Decompositions of the diagonal of complete intersections in products of projective spaces
arxiv:2611.18966.summary: We study rationality of very general complete intersections in products of projective spaces. By constructing specific reference varieties and apply specialization method in the form of relative torsion orders, we extend the quintic constructions by Hotchkiss and the quartic constructions by B\"ohning, Graf von Bothmer, Pirutka and Zhang to very general complete intersections in products in every characteristic. In particular, we prove that very general quartic hypersurfaces of positive dimension admit no decomposition of the diagonal in every characteristic.

arxiv:2611.18973.title: On stretched Kostka polynomials
arxiv:2611.18973.summary: Stretched Kostka polynomials are defined by $f_{\lambda,\mu}(N) := K_{N\lambda,N\mu}$, where $K_{\lambda,\mu}$ denotes the corresponding Kostka number. In 2004, King-Tollu-Toumazet conjectured that, for every integer $k$, there are only finitely many polynomials $f_{\lambda,\mu}(N)$ such that $f_{\lambda,\mu}(1)=k$. For $k=3$, KTT also conjectured that there are exactly two such polynomials.
arxiv:2611.18973.authors: Alexey Garber, Igor Pak, Zachary Slonim

arxiv:2611.18989.title: Rank Functions of Flag Matroids with Applications to Order-Neutral Submodular Valuations
arxiv:2611.18989.summary: We provide a rank function axiomatization for flag matroids and show that it is cryptomorphic to the definition of flag matroids as a sequence of matroid quotients. Afterwards, we present some applications of flag matroid rank functions by providing solutions to selected problems. In particular, we discuss connections between flag matroids and submodular valuations in computational economics by showing that rank functions of flag matroids of length $k$ are precisely the same as $\{0, 1, \dots, k\}$-order-neutral submodular valuations.

arxiv:2611.18993.title: Zero area of quartic Fibonacci Julia sets
arxiv:2611.18993.summary: We give a computer-assisted proof that the Julia set of the degree-four Fibonacci renormalization 2-periodic point has zero planar Lebesgue measure. As a corollary, the degree four Fibonacci polynomial $z^4+c_{\mathrm{Fib}}$ has zero measure Julia set.

arxiv:2611.19010.title: Equivariant intersection cohomology of some $4$-dimensional locally standard $T$-pseudomanifolds
arxiv:2611.19010.summary: Locally standard $T$-pseudomanifolds are singular analogues of quasitoric manifolds. In this paper, we study a certain class of four-dimensional locally standard $T^2$-pseudomanifolds over convex polygons. We establish an Orlik-Raymond type classification and study their ordinary and equivariant cohomology, as well as their intersection and equivariant intersection cohomology.

arxiv:2611.19024.title: Spherical functions of the quantum symmetric pair of type FII
arxiv:2611.19024.summary: We prove Schl\"osser's conjecture relating quantum FII spherical functions to Askey--Wilson polynomials for equal left and right coideal parameters and determine the corresponding radial operator. An explicit transport formula gives the shifted restrictions for arbitrary nonzero parameters.

arxiv:2611.19133.title: Psyquandle Fares
arxiv:2611.19133.summary: We introduce a new infinite family of invariants of singular knot and links and of pseudoknots by extending the biquandle fares construction to the case of psyquandles. We give the axioms explicitly for four cases of fare-based invariants: 1-fares, signed crooked 2-fares, signed through 2-fares and signed complete 2-fares. We provide examples of each type, illustrating the method of computation and collecting some results for toy examples using small-cardinality psyquandles and abelian coefficient groups.

arxiv:2611.19137.title: Intervals in affine Bruhat order
arxiv:2611.19137.summary: Let $(W,S)$ be an irreducible affine Coxeter system. We study Bruhat intervals in $W$ via the well-known characterization of Bruhat order in terms of galleries. We start by using folded galleries to formulate an analogous order on the coweight lattice, which we call Iwahori order.
arxiv:2611.19137.authors: Elizabeth Mili\'cevi\'c, Petra Schwer, Anne Thomas

arxiv:2611.19164.title: The length of the longest path in random acyclic orientations of a complete multipartite graph
arxiv:2611.19164.summary: We study the distribution of the length of the longest path in a uniformly random acyclic orientation of a complete multipartite graph. We derive an explicit analytic expression for the probability generating function of the longest path length, and, for an arbitrary fixed number of parts of equal size, we apply analytic combinatorics in several variables to obtain asymptotics (as the part size tends toward infinity) for its mean longest path length.
arxiv:2611.19164.authors: Aiden Corcoran, Erik Lundberg, Elisabeth Rodriguez

arxiv:2611.19217.title: Legendrian surgery on the unit cotangent bundle of the Klein bottle and infinitely many Stein fillings
arxiv:2611.19217.summary: We show that a single Legendrian surgery on the canonical contact structure of the unit cotangent bundle $ST^*K$ of the Klein bottle $K$ produces a planar contact $3$--manifold $(Y,\xi)$ with infinitely many pairwise non-homeomorphic Stein fillings. The fillings are obtained from the disk cotangent bundle $DT^*K$ by attaching a single Weinstein $2$--handle along the images of one Legendrian knot under the powers of a contactomorphism of $(ST^*K,\xi_{\mathrm{can}})$, no positive power of which extends over $DT^*K$. The construction takes place in a planar open book of $(ST^*K,\xi_{\mathrm{can}})$, and $(Y,\xi)$ is contactomorphic to Baykur's recent example of a planar contact $3$--manifold…

arxiv:2611.19219.title: Stabilizing Parabolic Vector Bundles
arxiv:2611.19219.summary: For an irreducible parabolic flat vector bundle of rank $r < 2\sqrt{g}$ on a genus $g$ curve, we prove that an analytically general isomonodromic deformation is stable. This refines Landesman-Litt's semistability result for bundles of rank $< 2\sqrt{g+1}$. The proof applies the non-generically globally generated (non-GGG) lemma to establish infinitesimal obstructions to extending destabilizing subbundles of semistable bundles.

arxiv:2611.19221.title: A Note on the Cosupport of Balmer-Favi Idempotents
arxiv:2611.19221.summary: Let $g_x$ be the Balmer-Favi idempotent at a point $x$ of the spectrum of a rigidly-compactly generated tensor triangulated category. We study the equality $\operatorname{Cosupp}(g_x)=\operatorname{gen}(x)$ by expressing $g_x$ as a local dual. We prove the equality for the derived category of a Noetherian scheme and for the stable module category of a finite group scheme over a field of positive characteristic.

arxiv:2611.19224.title: Quadratic Embedding Constants of Block Graphs and Characterization of Cactus-like Graphs
arxiv:2611.19224.summary: A (finite or infinite) connected graph is called \textit{cactus-like} if every pair of distinct maximal cliques has at most one vertex in common and its clique graph is a tree. Equivalently, a cactus-like graph is a block graph whose clique graph is a tree. We prove that a finite connected graph $G$ with at least two vertices is cactus-like if and only if its quadratic embedding constant satisfies $\mathrm{QEC}(G)<-1/2$.

arxiv:2611.19243.title: Veech dichotomy for specific covering surface over Veech surface
arxiv:2611.19243.summary: It is known that Veech dichotomy, which states that minimal directions are uniquely ergodic, holds for Veech surface and covering surface branched at a single non-periodic connection point of Veech surface. We give a sufficient condition for Veech dichotomy holds for a finite translation cover of a Veech surface, and applies it on branched cover of square-tiled surfaces to construct examples that satisfy Veech dichotomy but aren't Veech surfaces.

arxiv:2611.19256.title: Independent Sets in $C_4$-Free Planar Graphs: Sharp Claw-Free Bounds and Structural Reductions
arxiv:2611.19256.summary: For every claw-free $C_4$-free planar graph, we prove the sharp weighted bound $\alpha_w(G)\ge (10/31)\sum_v w(v)$, equivalently $\chi_f(G)\le31/10$. The proof uses a line-graph representation and the matching polytope; the exceptional small roots are excluded analytically by planar duality and degree-four neighborhood analysis in triangulations. We also prove that, in every $2$-connected $C_4$-free graph of minimum degree at least four, an independent selection of claw centers leaves a compatible subgraph of noncenters with fractional chromatic number at most three; planarity is not required.

arxiv:2611.19281.title: Hadwiger-Debrunner numbers from rainbow Tur\'an numbers and beyond
arxiv:2611.19281.summary: The Hadwiger-Debrunner number $\operatorname{HD}_d(p,q)$ is defined as the maximum piercing number over all finite families of compact convex sets in $\mathbb R^d$ in which among every $p$ sets, some $q$ have non-empty intersection. We develop three complementary constructions that improve lower bounds for Hadwiger-Debrunner numbers. For any fixed $q>d\ge 2$, a randomly sparsified family of hyperplanes, analyzed using hypergraph containers, yields $\operatorname{HD}_d(p,q)\ge p^{(d+q-2)/(q-1)+o(1)}$ as $p\rightarrow\infty$.
arxiv:2611.19281.authors: Wenchong Chen, Gennian Ge, Yang Shu

arxiv:2611.19310.title: Homotopy Classification of Pointed Self-Maps of $\mathbb{RP}^3\#\mathbb{RP}^3$
arxiv:2611.19310.summary: We classify pointed self-maps of $M=\mathbb{RP}^{3}\#\mathbb{RP}^{3}$ up to pointed homotopy. Using the universal cover $S^2\times\mathbb R$, we reduce the problem to paths in the sphere mapping space with even or odd endpoint conditions. The evaluation fibration, Whitehead products, and a double-coset calculation determine the resulting secondary invariants.

arxiv:2611.19312.title: The Common-Color Spectrum of Endpoint Set-Coloring Ramsey Numbers
arxiv:2611.19312.summary: The set-coloring Ramsey number $R(n;r,s,t)$ is the least $N$ such that every assignment of an $s$-element subset of $[r]=\{1,\ldots,r\}$ to each edge of $K_N$ contains a $K_n$ whose edge labels have at least $t$ common colors. Motivated by the work of Erd\H{o}s and Szemer\'edi on $R(n;r,r-1,1)$, we write $R(n;r,r-1,t)=\exp\bigl(nf_{r,n}(t)\bigr)$ and study $f(t):=f_{r,n}(t)$ as $t$ ranges from $1$ to $r-1$. For fixed integers $r\ge2$ and $1\le t<r$, we prove that, as $n\to\infty$, \( \frac12\log\frac{r}{r-t}+o(1) \le f(t) \le \frac{r}{r-t}\log\frac{r}{r-t} +C+O_{r,t}\!\left(\frac{\log n}{n}\right), \) where $C>0$ is an absolute constant.
arxiv:2611.19312.authors: Guantao Chen, Qiong Fan, Chunxiang Wang

arxiv:2611.19326.title: On the multiplicity of the Laplacian eigenvalue 1 of a graph
arxiv:2611.19326.summary: A connected graph $G$ with $n\ge 2$ vertices and $\varepsilon$ edges is called a \emph{$k$-cyclic graph} if $k=\varepsilon-n+1$. The Laplacian matrix is defined as $L(G)=D(G)-A(G)$, where $D(G)$ is the diagonal matrix of vertex degrees and $A(G)$ is the adjacency matrix of $G$. Let $m_{G}(1)$ be the multiplicity of the Laplacian eigenvalue $1$ of $G$.
arxiv:2611.19326.authors: Fei Wen, Kai Wang, Tao Wang

arxiv:2611.19346.title: Motivic Borel-Moore Homology is Borel-Moore Motivic Homology
arxiv:2611.19346.summary: This paper studies the higher Chow groups of arbitrary finite type separated schemes using motivic homotopy theory, serving as a Borel-Moore counterpart to the $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant motivic cohomology of Bachmann-Elmanto-Morrow. We construct a filtration on the G-theory spectrum of a finite type separated scheme $X$, inducing an Atiyah-Hirzebruch style spectral sequence whose associated graded pieces are a complex computing the higher Chow groups of $X$. We prove that this complex is representable in the stable motivic homotopy category, and is a module over the $\mathbb{A}^1$-motivic complex, giving rise to an action of $\mathbb{A}^1$-invariant motivic cohomology on the Bloch-Levine…

arxiv:2611.19361.title: Distance-$2$ isolation of connected graphs
arxiv:2611.19361.summary: If $\mathcal{F}$ is a set of graphs and $F$ is a copy of a graph in $\mathcal{F}$, then we call $F$ an $\mathcal{F}$-graph. Let $G$ be a connected $n$-vertex graph. For a subset $D$ of the vertex set $V(G)$, let $N^2[D]$ denote the second closed neighbourhood of $D$.

arxiv:2611.19371.title: Bumpless pipe dreams for involutions and shifted plane partitions
arxiv:2611.19371.summary: This article studies a triangular variant of bumpless pipe dreams for involutions in the symmetric group. We prove that a natural weight generating function for these objects recovers all involution Schubert polynomials. For vexillary involutions, we derive a $K$-theoretic extension of this result that gives a new formula for orthogonal Grothendieck polynomials.
arxiv:2611.19371.authors: Eric Marberg, Alejandro H. Morales, Tianyi Yu

arxiv:2611.19378.title: Lower bounds for the Kolmogorov widths of global attractors of dissipative systems
arxiv:2611.19378.summary: We introduce the notion of a strengthening set in a Hilbert space and prove an exponential lower bound for its Kolmogorov widths. For compact sets containing the origin, the strengthening property is equivalent to the existence of such a bound. As an application, we obtain an exact formula for the widths of the global attractor of a diagonal dissipative system.

arxiv:2611.19407.title: Horrocks-Mumford sheaves on toric varieties
arxiv:2611.19407.summary: Previous work of the authors introduced the class of Horrocks-Mumford sheaves over normal algebraic k-varieties, the most prominent example being the classical Horrocks-Mumford bundle on projective four-space. For a smooth semiprojective toric variety, we derive an explicit description of these sheaves in terms of finitely generated graded modules over the Cox ring which we use for an algorithmic treatment. In particular, we discuss some explicit examples, their indecomposability and local freeness.
arxiv:2611.19407.authors: Klaus Altmann, Andreas Hochenegger, Frederik Witt

arxiv:2611.19411.title: Representability of Galois extensions
arxiv:2611.19411.summary: We study faithful Galois extensions in a presentably symmetric monoidal $\infty$-category $\mathscr{C}$ by a dualizable $\mathbb{E}_1$-group $G$. We prove that these extensions correspond to colimit-preserving symmetric monoidal functors from $\mathrm{An}^{\mathrm{B}G}$ to $\mathscr{C}$. Under suitable assumptions, we use this correspondence to construct a Galois pro-anima that classifies Galois extensions in $\mathscr{C}$.

arxiv:2611.19433.title: Existence of alternating Hamiltonian paths on specific bicolored point sets
arxiv:2611.19433.summary: Consider a bicolored point set $P$ in general position in the plane consisting of $n$ blue and $n$ red points. We show that if $P$ can be partitioned into bicolored pairs $(a_i,b_i)$ such that, for every $i$, $a_i$ and $b_i$ have different colors and the sets $P\setminus \{a_i\}$ and $P \setminus \{b_i\}$ have the same order type, then there exists a noncrossing alternating Hamiltonian path on $P$. We also investigate the case when $P$ lies on the circle, and every interval along the circle contains at most $c$ more points of one color than of the other.

arxiv:2611.19434.title: Ramsey goodness of large generalized fans
arxiv:2611.19434.summary: Given graphs $G$ and $H$, the Ramsey number $r(G,H)$ is the smallest integer $N$ such that any red-blue edge coloring of $K_N$ contains a red copy of $G$ or a blue copy of $H$. If $H$ is connected, Burr's lower bound gives $r(G,H)\geq (\chi(G)-1)(|V(H)|-1)+s(G)$, where $s(G)$ is the minimum size of a color class over all proper $\chi(G)$-colorings of $G$. The graph $H$ is called $G$-good if equality holds in this bound.

arxiv:2611.19437.title: On $z_{2M}(21,4)$: the Hole Extensions of the Chen--Chen Configuration Are Reducible, and the Extremal Configurations of $z_2(21,4)$ Are Not Unique
arxiv:2611.19437.summary: The second order extended Zarankiewicz number $z_{2M}(m,n)$ of Qi and Yu allows a secondary half of a $2$-edge to be shared, while the $1$-edge graph stays $C_4$-free and extremal and $1$-edges and main halves stay exclusive. Whether $z_{2M}(21,4)=55$ is open. Since deleting a $2$-edge removes exactly one displayed square, $z_{2M}(21,4)=55$ if and only if there is no irreducible admissible configuration with exactly $56$ displayed squares, and by the cell count of Qi and Yu and the heredity of irreducibility such a configuration without empty cells is an extremal $55$-square configuration of $z_2(21,4)$ plus one $2$-edge at its hole.
arxiv:2611.19437.authors: Carles Mar\'in, Liqun Qi, Gaohang Yu

arxiv:2611.19443.title: Powers of projective lines inside full flag varieties
arxiv:2611.19443.summary: Up to now, symplectic foliations of Poisson varieties have been primarily studied from a set theoretic perspective by describing their symplectic leaves individually as orbit closures. In the direction of obtaining algebro-geometric characterizations, for the standard Poisson structure $\pi$ on the full flag variety $G/B_+$ of a complex semisimple algebraic group $G$, we prove that the irreducible components of the reduced part of the 0-degeneracy locus of $(G/B_+, \pi)$ are precisely the inclusion-maximal $T$-stable complete Poisson submanifolds of $(G/B_+, \pi)$ that are isomorphic to powers of $\mathbb{P}^1$. This characterization is based on a theorem that explicitly classifies the…

arxiv:2611.19450.title: Counting real meromorphic differentials on $\mathbb{CP}^1$
arxiv:2611.19450.summary: The counting problem for meromorphic differentials on $\mathbb{CP}^1$ with fixed orders of zeros and poles and vanishing residues at some specific poles, up to the action of $\mathrm{PGL}_2(\mathbb{C})$ and the multiplication by a nonzero constant, was completely solved before by several authors. In all the cases when there are finitely many such meromorphic differentials, an explicit formula for their number was found and also, in the case of residueless meromorphic differentials with two zeros, a link to the WDVV equations and the KP hierarchy was established. We consider a real analog of these counting problems by requiring that a meromorphic differential is preserved by a real structure…

arxiv:2611.19459.title: An $(\infty,1)$-category of conically smooth stratified bordisms
arxiv:2611.19459.summary: To study derived defect topological quantum field theories, we construct an $(\infty,1)$-category of stratified bordisms and sketch its $(\infty,d)$-dimensional analogue. In the first chapters we develop a method for constructing symmetric monoidal $(\infty,1)$-categories, inspired by Segal spaces but better suited to geometric inputs, which we call interval Segal spaces. Using this framework, we construct the $(\infty,1)$-category of $d$-dimensional smooth manifolds via smooth $\infty$-sheaves thereof, in an attempt to address fibrancy issues present in prior work on this subject.

arxiv:2611.19467.title: Link Spectra of Lorenz-like Templates and the Horseshoe
arxiv:2611.19467.summary: We give a complete classification of the inclusion relations between the link spectrum of the horseshoe template $L(0,1)$ and those of the nonnegative Lorenz-like templates $L(0,a)$. For a template $T$, its link spectrum $\mathscr L(T)$ consists of the link types carried by $T$, allowing parallel strands along its strips. For integers $a\geq0$, the spectra of $L(0,a)$ and $L(0,1)$ are comparable under inclusion if and only if $a\notin\{0,2\}$.

arxiv:2611.19473.title: A Proof of The Twin-Star Hypothesis in Dimension Five
arxiv:2611.19473.summary: It was recently shown that the question of whether the determinant-like map \(\det^{S^2}\) is unique up to multiplication by a scalar is equivalent to a combinatorial conjecture regarding cycle-free \(d\)-partitions of the complete graph \(K_{2d}\), known as the twin-star hypothesis. This hypothesis asserts that every cycle-free \(d\)-partition of \(K_{2d}\) is weakly equivalent to one that contains a component isomorphic to the twin-star graph \(TS_d\). This hypothesis was previously established for \(d\le4\).

arxiv:2611.19478.title: Generic finiteness of rotating relative equilibria in the planar $N$-vortex problem
arxiv:2611.19478.summary: For every $N\ge2$, we prove that Zariski-generic nonzero real circulations, with any prescribed signs, admit at most $N^{2N}$ labeled, collision-free rotating relative equilibria modulo translations, rotations in $SO(2)$, and positive scaling. The excluded parameters lie in an explicit finite union of quadratic hypersurfaces. The proof combines a logarithmic-residue obstruction to positive-dimensional complex solution sets with B\'ezout degree bounds.

arxiv:2611.19490.title: Fixed-space indices and symmetry breaking in variational problems
arxiv:2611.19490.summary: We establish a quantitative criterion for variational bifurcation with prescribed exact stabilizers under finite group actions. Combining scalar spectral flow on fixed spaces with overgroup nullities, we bound the number of bifurcation parameters when the restricted singular set is finite. The theorem allows strongly indefinite Fredholm Hessians and singular ambient endpoints, without parameter differentiability or regular crossings.
arxiv:2611.19490.authors: Daniele Garrisi, Alessandro Portaluri, Li Wu

arxiv:2611.19496.title: Maximality of the Do\v{s}en--Petri\'c Boolean Category
arxiv:2611.19496.summary: We prove that the zero-identity Boolean category of Do\v{s}en and Petri\'c, freely generated by a nonempty set of propositional variables, is maximal. Adjoining any equation between parallel morphisms that does not follow from the defining equations, and closing under the operations on morphisms and uniform formula substitution, collapses this category to a preorder. This disproves their conjecture that the category is not maximal.

arxiv:2611.19506.title: Quantum periods and threefold flips
arxiv:2611.19506.summary: We study regularized quantum periods under birational contractions involving threefold flips. Let $g:X \dashrightarrow X'$ be a birational map between Fano threefolds with terminal quotient singularities which contracts exactly one prime divisor $E$ and extracts no divisor. We prove that $$ \lim_{r \rightarrow +\infty}\widehat{G}_{X,rE}(t) =\widehat{G}_{X'}(t).
arxiv:2611.19506.authors: Yang He, Artan Sheshmani, Shing-Tung Yau

arxiv:2611.19508.title: An asymptotic resolution of the Gao--Thangadurai conjecture on the Harborth constant
arxiv:2611.19508.summary: The Harborth constant $\mathsf g(G)$ of a finite abelian group $G$ of exponent $n$ is the least integer $k$ such that every subset of $G$ of size at least $k$ contains $n$ elements whose sum is zero. Let $C_n$ be a cyclic group of order $n$. Gao and Thangadurai \cite{gt} in 2004 conjectured that $\mathsf g(C_n\oplus C_n)=2n+(-1)^n$ for all integers $n\ge3$.

arxiv:2611.19516.title: Denoising-Induced Recovery of Effective Dynamics
arxiv:2611.19516.summary: Recovering dynamical equations from data is a central problem in nonlinear science. In practice, measurements are corrupted by noise and often contain fast oscillations that are not part of the slow dynamics of interest. For this reason, data are typically pre-processed before model recovery or classsification.

arxiv:2611.19543.title: Large caps in $\mathbb{F}_3^9$ and $\mathbb{F}_3^{11}$
arxiv:2611.19543.summary: We construct sets of $1104$ points in $\mathbb{F}_3^9$ and $5744$ points in $\mathbb{F}_3^{11}$, each containing no three distinct collinear points. A reflection lift sends the Calderbank--Fishburn $236$-cap to a cap with three parallel layers of sizes $512,80,512$; both outer layers are linearly equivalent to the FunSearch $512$-cap. A coordinate substitution in Hill's $112$-cap uses replacement sets of sizes $80,32,32$ for the three values of one scalar coordinate.

arxiv:2611.19571.title: Orbital graph structure of alternating full groups and simple torsion amenable groups of exponential growth
arxiv:2611.19571.summary: We develop a framework for constructing simple alternating full groups A(G, X), associated with finite fragmentations of minimal expansive dihedral Cantor actions, with controlled orbital-graph codings and purely non-Hausdorff singularities. We also prove that positive entropy of a naturally labeled admissible orbital line forces exponential word growth of the acting group. As an application, we construct continuum many pairwise abstractly nonisomorphic, finitely generated, infinite, simple, torsion, amenable groups of exponential word growth.

arxiv:2611.19580.title: Log Hodge-de Rham degeneration beyond the toroidal case
arxiv:2611.19580.summary: Let $\phi\colon X \to S$ be a flat and proper one-parameter degeneration of algebraic varieties with a single degenerate fiber $X_0$. If $\phi\colon (X|X_0) \to (S|0)$ is log smooth and saturated, the log Hodge-de Rham spectral sequence is known to degenerate at the page $E_1$. Adding to that some further well-known related properties, we say that the log de Rham complex $\Omega^{\bullet,\mathrm{log}}_{X/S}$ is cohomologically flat as a filtered complex, short cffc.

arxiv:2611.19583.title: Finite-summability in the noncommutative geometry of crossed products
arxiv:2611.19583.summary: We study finite-summability of unbounded representatives of $K$-homology classes for crossed-product $C^*$-algebras associated with actions on compact spaces. Using Kasparov's Dirac--dual-Dirac method, we isolate geometric conditions on the $\gamma$-element under which elements of $K$-homology can be transferred to a crossed product associated with a proper action and represented by finitely summable unbounded cycles defined from Dirac-type operators with an unbounded potential. We relate finite-summability of these operators to integrability properties of the potential by spectral estimates for Schr\"odinger operators on manifolds of bounded geometry.
arxiv:2611.19583.authors: Robin J. Deeley, Magnus Goffeng, Levi Lorenzo

arxiv:2611.19594.title: A New Record for the Katz-Tao Sum-Difference Exponent
arxiv:2611.19594.summary: We prove the record bound $C_{3b}\le 209357544569848128/114631769327023765=1.8263483657186\ldots$ for the Katz-Tao sum-difference exponent, valid in every abelian group without $2$-torsion. Using only Shannon inequalities, conditional copies and Katz-Tao's original directions, whose classical single-grid argument gives $11/6$, we break $11/6$, obtaining $2762/1509$ and $152/83$. For every abelian group we prove the universal bound $C_{\mathrm{all}}=10304335425987192362/5641833174538280329=1.8264161855212\ldots$, which is below the previous record for the real Katz-Tao constant.

arxiv:2611.19599.title: The Dedekind-MacNeille Completion as a Functor
arxiv:2611.19599.summary: We study the Dedekind-MacNeille completion through representable functors on the wide subcategory $\mathbf{Pos}_{\mathrm{cl}}$ of posets and lower cut-continuous (closed) maps. On this category the completion is contravariantly functorial and naturally isomorphic to $\mathrm{Hom}_{\mathbf{Pos}_{\mathrm{cl}}}(-,[1])^{\mathrm{op}}$, via $A\mapsto\chi_A$ and its inverse $f\mapsto f^{-1}(\{0\})$. The naturality of this identification makes the Yoneda lemma applicable: uniqueness of the representing object and the endomorphism monoid of the completion follow formally.

arxiv:2611.19600.title: The Deepest Pairs of Points Are Not as Deep as Conjectured
arxiv:2611.19600.summary: Given any finite set of points in $\mathbb{R}^2$, Neumann-Lara and Urrutia \cite{NLUr88} proved in 1988 that there is always a pair such that every circle through the two points encloses a positive fraction of all points. While Edelsbrunner et al.\ \cite{EHSS89} showed that the fraction is at least $\sfrac{1}{2} - \sfrac{1}{\sqrt{12}} = 0.211\ldots$, Urrutia \cite{Urr02} conjectured that the constant $\sfrac{1}{4} = 0.25$ in the upper bound proved by Hayward, Rappaport and Wenger \cite{HRW89} is best possible. We disprove this conjecture by lowering the constant to $\sfrac{3}{14} = 0.214\ldots$.
arxiv:2611.19600.authors: Herbert Edelsbrunner, Alexey Garber, Morteza Saghafian, Emo Welzl

arxiv:2611.19606.title: The $E_6$-Grassmannian, its minuscule Coxeter matroids, and the lines on a cubic surface
arxiv:2611.19606.summary: We study the minuscule Coxeter matroids of type $E_6$, whose ground set is the set of 27 lines on a smooth cubic surface. We characterize them by a tritangent exchange property and classify them into 230 orbits under the Weyl group. Every nonempty matroidal stratum of the $E_6$-Grassmannian is an open subscheme of a torus, and all orbits but one are realizable over every infinite field.

arxiv:2611.19615.title: The $J$-Homomorphism From Localising The Cobordism Hypothesis
arxiv:2611.19615.summary: Lurie's cobordism hypothesis classifies fully extended framed topological field theories valued in a symmetric monoidal $(\infty,n)$-category $\mathcal{C}$ with duals by the $\infty$-groupoid $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{fd}}$ of fully dualisable objects. This classification results in an $O(n)$-action on $\mathcal{C}^{\mathrm{fd}}$, where $O(n)$ acts on the framed bordism category by change of framing. Lurie observed that for a connective spectrum, this action is ``a version of the classical $J$-homomorphism.'' We make this identification explicit: with respect to the right action of $O(n)$ on framings, the $O(n)$-action on the localisation $L(\mathrm{Bord}_n^{\mathrm{fr}}) \simeq S$ is precisely…

arxiv:2611.19620.title: Braid monodromy and the Cartwright--Steger surface
arxiv:2611.19620.summary: Building on the Livne-like construction of Cartwright, Koziarz and Yeung, we construct a closed smooth 4-manifold with a map to the two-sphere whose generic fiber has genus 109 and whose four exceptional fibers are determined by explicit braid and permutation data. A pencil of four-pointed spheres realizes the same global braid monodromy and makes the covering holomorphic. We show that the contraction of its thirty-six exceptional curves is the Cartwright-Steger surface, hence our smooth construction gives a topological description of this complex surface.

arxiv:2611.19627.title: A Recursive Construction of Perfect and Odd Perfect Sequences of Unbounded Length over the Unit Quaternions
arxiv:2611.19627.summary: We give a recursive construction, with closed-form index functions, of perfect and odd perfect periodic autocorrelation sequences over the eight simple unit quaternions $\Qe=\{\pm1,\pm i,\pm j,\pm k\}$ in every length $2^n$. The sequences are built, as in the recursive perfect array construction of Blake, from \emph{twisted periodic extensions}: a short sequence continued with period $M$ up to a right factor $u\in\Qe$. Over roots of unity the twists cannot be regenerated by a one-dimensional recursion, consistently with Mow's conjecture; over $\Qe$ we show that no single sequence of length $M\not\equiv0\pmod 4$ carries a twist $\pm i,\pm j$ or $\pm k$ either, but that \emph{pairs} of…

arxiv:2611.19632.title: Ramsey Numbers of Most Even-Linked Double Stars
arxiv:2611.19632.summary: For $n \geq m$, the linked double star $S_c(n, m)$ is the graph formed by taking two disjoint stars $K_{1, n}$ and $K_{1, m}$ and linking their centers with a path on $c$ vertices. In this paper, we investigate the Ramsey numbers of even-linked double stars, that is, where $c = 2p$ for some $p \in \mathbb{N}$. Determining the Ramsey numbers of the $p = 1$ case (classical double stars) is a longstanding open question; the $p = 2$ case was resolved by Burr and Erd\H{o}s in 1976, and Liu and Chen made progress for general even-linked double stars in 2026.
arxiv:2611.19632.authors: Chaitanya Karamchedu, Mithra Karamchedu, Maria Klawe, Andr\'es R. Vindas-Mel\'endez

arxiv:2611.19635.title: Constructive and computational methods for extremal and near-extremal box colorings
arxiv:2611.19635.summary: We investigate extremal and near-extremal 2-colorings of three-dimensional grids without monochromatic axis-parallel boxes. Our approach focuses on the parameter $\rho(a,b)$, defined to be the minimum number of monochromatic rectangles in a 2-coloring of an $a\times b$ grid. We determine $\rho(a,b)$ for several small grids and use these values to obtain upper bounds on the number of layers that can be stacked to form an $a\times b\times c$ grid without creating a monochromatic box.

arxiv:2611.19639.title: State-space symmetry in Boolean network ensembles
arxiv:2611.19639.summary: Studies of evolving Boolean network systems have found that Boolean functions cluster into equivalence classes with a characteristic frequency distribution - a pattern governed by the Zyklenzeiger symmetry group - but the dynamical origin of this symmetry has remained unexplained. Here we show that it is a consequence of a fundamental symmetry of Boolean network dynamics itself. A Boolean network consists of nodes that update according to Boolean functions of their regulatory inputs; its global dynamics is encoded in a state-space network.

arxiv:2611.19641.title: A Quantitative Kuratowski Theorem
arxiv:2611.19641.summary: Suppose that a graph $G$ contains exactly $k$ different subdivisions of a $K_5$ or $K_{3,3}$. We prove that in this case the crossing number of $G$ is at most $\binom{3k+7}{2}$ (and, when $k\le 2$, it is at most $k$).
