arxiv:2611.19659.title: Associahedra are 8-colourable
arxiv:2611.19659.summary: Determining the chromatic number of associahedra is a long-standing open problem. Tan [arXiv:2611.05323] recently proved that associahedra are 12-colourable, which is the first constant upper bound. This paper adapts Tan's argument to show that associahedra are 8-colourable.

arxiv:2611.19665.title: Real zeros of Durfee polynomials: Proof of the Canfield--Corteel--Savage conjecture
arxiv:2611.19665.summary: We prove the conjecture of Canfield, Corteel, and Savage that for every positive integer $n$, the Durfee polynomial $D_n(x)=\sum_{d=1}^{\lfloor\sqrt n\rfloor}p(n,d)x^d$ counting partitions of $n$ by the side length of their Durfee square has only real zeros. More precisely, $D_n$ has a simple zero at the origin and exactly $\lfloor\sqrt n\rfloor-1$ simple negative zeros. Consequently, for every $n\ge1$, the sequence $p(n,1),\ldots,p(n,\lfloor\sqrt n\rfloor)$ is strictly log-concave and unimodal.

arxiv:2611.19668.title: Enumerating Solutions to Type (2,3) Composition Identities of Finite Endofunctions
arxiv:2611.19668.summary: We enumerate ordered pairs $(f,g)$ of endofunctions on a finite labeled set $X$ satisfying a composition identity of type $(2,3)$, with two factors on one side and three on the other. For all sixteen forms up to exchanging $f$ and $g$, we derive formulas involving finite sums and generating functions. The arguments use images and fibers, homomorphisms between functional digraphs, and isomorphism types of iterates.

arxiv:2611.19673.title: Bi-Lipschitz right-left equivalence of finite plane-to-plane germs
arxiv:2611.19673.summary: We show that the bi-Lipschitz right-left equivalence of finite holomorphic map germs $(\mathbb{C}^2,0)\to(\mathbb{C}^2,0)$ admits continuous moduli, already among finitely determined polynomial germs of corank one and degree five. The moduli come from a new invariant of finite germs: for two tangent branches of the critical set whose images are tangent, the limit of the ratio of the norms of the images of nearby points is preserved by bi-Lipschitz right-left equivalence. For germs $(F,H)$ with quasihomogeneous components the invariant is computed from the height functions of $F$ and $H$: it is given by the moduli of the values of the height function of the component of lower weighted degree…

arxiv:2611.19675.title: Equivariant homomorphisms and Mordell--Weil groups of twists of Albanese varieties of cyclic multiple planes
arxiv:2611.19675.summary: Let $X'\to X$ be a Galois cover of smooth projective varieties over a field $k$ with group $G$, and let $G$ act on an abelian variety $A$ over $k$. We prove an exact sequence relating the Mordell--Weil group of the twist of $A$ by $k(X')/k(X)$ to the group of $G$-equivariant homomorphisms from the Albanese variety of $X'$ to $A$; the remaining obstruction is killed by $|G|$. This corrects structure theorems in two earlier papers of the author and in a corrigendum to the first, where the equivariance condition was omitted.

arxiv:2611.19678.title: $\ell^p$-Busemann space and the coarse Novikov conjecture
arxiv:2611.19678.summary: We introduce the notion of an \(\ell^p\)-Busemann space, which is a complete Busemann convex geodesic metric space whose tangent cones admit uniformly controlled homogeneous bi-Lipschitz embeddings into \(\ell^p\)-spaces. An \(\ell^p\)-Busemann space is called admissible if it contains dense sequences of closed convex subsets isometric to certain Finsler manifolds. We then prove that the rational coarse Novikov conjecture holds for proper metric spaces with bounded geometry that admit coarse embeddings into admissible \(\ell^p\)-Busemann spaces.

arxiv:2611.19691.title: The structure of varieties with nef anticanonical divisor in positive characteristic
arxiv:2611.19691.summary: Let $X$ be a regular projective variety with nef anticanonical divisor over an algebraically closed field of characteristic $p>0$, and let $f:X\to A$ be a surjective morphism to an abelian variety. We prove that there exists an isogeny $A' \to A$ such that, the base change $f': X\times_AA' \to A'$ admits a Zariski locally trivial structure. If moreover $-K_X\equiv D$ for some semiample $\mathbb Q$-divisor $D$, then $-K_X\sim_{\mathbb Q}D$, and there exists an isogeny $A' \to A$ such that, the base change $ X\times_AA' \cong X_0\times A'$ where $X_0$ is the fiber over the identity $0\in A'$.

arxiv:2611.19704.title: The automorphism group of the super Jordan plane
arxiv:2611.19704.summary: We complete the description of the automorphism group of the super Jordan plane $\mathcal B$ over a field of characteristic zero, extending the classification of super-automorphisms obtained by N. Andruskiewitsch and F. Dumas in \cite{AD}.
arxiv:2611.19704.authors: W. de Araujo, D. Bagio, R. Baltazar, A. Santana, R. Vinciguerra

arxiv:2611.19711.title: On Semi-interval and Para-interval Graphs
arxiv:2611.19711.summary: Bau and Johnson introduced semi-interval graphs and asked whether one of the two extremal sets can always be replaced by a single vertex. A negative answer to this question is given by a tree which has no such representation. It is also shown that a finite connected graph with at least two vertices is a semi-interval graph if and only if it is bipartite.
arxiv:2611.19711.authors: Chenxi Lv, Yiming Lei, Chunlei Xu

arxiv:2611.19750.title: Asymptotic Order of the Minimum Number of Graph-Saturating Edges
arxiv:2611.19750.summary: Given an $H$-free graph $G$, a non-edge $e$ of $G$ is called $H$-saturating if $G+e$ contains a copy of $H$. The function $f_H(n,m)$ denotes the minimum number of $H$-saturating non-edges over all $n$-vertex $H$-free graphs with exactly $m$ edges. In this paper, we give a complete classification of the asymptotic behavior of $f_H(n,\operatorname{ex}(n,R)+1)$ for any fixed graph $H$ satisfying $\chi(H)>\chi$ and $\chi(H-e)>\chi$ for every $e\in E(H)$, where $\chi\ge 2$ and $R$ is an arbitrary fixed edge-critical graph with $\chi(R)=\chi+1$.

arxiv:2611.19759.title: Isolated Singularities Not Resolved by Iterated Nash Blowups
arxiv:2611.19759.summary: Castillo, Duarte, Leyton-\'Alvarez, and Liendo asked whether iterating ordinary Nash blowups in characteristic zero or normalized Nash blowups in arbitrary characteristic can fail to resolve isolated singularities arXiv:2511.17862. We answer this question affirmatively with two constructions of isolated singularities, one nonnormal and one normal, both giving counterexamples to normalized Nash iteration in every characteristic.

arxiv:2611.19797.title: Stability of the tangent bundle on del Pezzo surfaces
arxiv:2611.19797.summary: In this article, we study the Bridgeland stability of the tangent bundle on del Pezzo surfaces. We obtain a complete description of the region where the tangent bundle is (un)stable with respect to the standard Bridgeland stability conditions associated to the anticanonical polarization.
arxiv:2611.19797.authors: Tristan Collins, Jason Lo, Yun Shi, Shing-Tung Yau

arxiv:2611.19805.title: Word complexity cutoffs for mixing properties of subshifts
arxiv:2611.19805.summary: Investigating word complexity cutoffs for partial and light mixing in subshifts, we construct partially mixing rank-one subshifts whose word complexity functions $p(q)$ satisfy $ \liminf_{q\to\infty}\frac{p(q)}q<2+\epsilon $ for any prescribed $\epsilon>0$ and, conversely, we prove that every lightly mixing rank-one subshift satisfies $ \liminf_{q\to\infty}\frac{p(q)}q>2, $ establishing $2$ as the optimal limiting threshold in the rank-one setting. More quantitatively, we show that every $\alpha$-partially mixing rank-one subshift satisfies $ \liminf_{q\to\infty}\frac{p(q)}q\geq 2+\frac{\alpha}{(1+\alpha)}. $ Our constructions are a combination of staircase and Chacon-like rank-one stages;…

arxiv:2611.19809.title: No complete set of mutually unbiased bases in C^6 without Fourier vanishing
arxiv:2611.19809.summary: A recent exact certificate shows that C^6 admits no seven mutually unbiased bases, hence at most five (OpenAI, 2026). That argument has two parts. The first proves the Fourier-vanishing conjecture of Matolcsi, Ruzsa and Weiner for every complex Hadamard matrix of order six other than Tao's cubic matrix, and excludes the cubic matrix separately.
arxiv:2611.19809.authors: Jinze Yang, Yile Liu, Yangyang Li, Xiu-Hao Deng

arxiv:2611.19813.title: Cyclic Hasse diagrams of manifolds and noncommutative path cohomology
arxiv:2611.19813.summary: Let $M$ be a connected oriented closed manifold of dimension $d\geq 2$, equipped with a regular CW structure, and let $P$ be its face poset. We consider the cyclic Hasse diagram $G_P^{\mathrm{cyc}}$, obtained from the directed Hasse diagram $G_P$ by adding an arrow from each maximal cell to every $0$-cell of $M$. Over an arbitrary field $\mathbb K$, we completely describe the path cohomology algebra $PH^*(G_P^{\mathrm{cyc}})$ in terms of the $\mathbb K$-Betti numbers of $M$.

arxiv:2611.19816.title: An improved lower bound for piercing the chessboard by lines
arxiv:2611.19816.summary: Let $p_n$ be the least number of lines meeting the interior of every cell of an $n\times n$ board. We prove that $\liminf_{n\to\infty}p_n/n\ge0.7520517>\frac34$. The previous bound was $0.7$.

arxiv:2611.19824.title: The Erd\H{o}s similarity problem for polynomials and analytic maps
arxiv:2611.19824.summary: In this paper, we study the Erd\H{o}s similarity problem by replacing affine copies with images of polynomial maps or analytic maps. This is inspired by a connection between a partial converse of Szemer\'edi's theorem and the Erd\H{o}s similarity problem and its variants, as well as a version of polynomial Szemer\'edi's theorem by Bergelson and Leibman. In particular, we strengthen several known results in the literature.

arxiv:2611.19834.title: Asymptotics of the three-color Hadwiger-Ramsey numbers
arxiv:2611.19834.summary: The Hadwiger-Ramsey number $R_h(k;\ell)$ is defined as the smallest integer $n$ such that for any edge coloring of a complete graph on $n$ vertices in $\ell$ colors at least one of the color classes induces a graph with a $K_k$ minor. We show that $R_h(k;3) = \left(\beta^{-1} + o(1)\right)k \sqrt{\ln k}$, where $\beta^{-1} = 2/\sqrt{-\ln(10-4\sqrt6)} = 1.58149\ldots$. This resolves the first open case of a problem by Axenovich and Steiner, who determined the asymptotic behavior of $R_h(k;2)$ and asked about the asymptotics of $R_h(k;\ell)$ for $\ell \geq 3$.

arxiv:2611.19835.title: Saturation and Semi-Saturation Numbers of Joins with Complete Graphs
arxiv:2611.19835.summary: For a nonempty family $\mathcal F$ of graphs, a graph is $\mathcal F$-semi-saturated if adding any missing edge creates a copy of some member of $\mathcal F$ containing the added edge, and is $\mathcal F$-saturated if it is also $\mathcal F$-free. The minimum numbers of edges in such graphs of order $n$ are denoted by $\operatorname{ssat}(n,\mathcal F)$ and $\operatorname{sat}(n,\mathcal F)$, respectively. We study these parameters for families of graphs obtained by taking the join of a fixed complete graph with each member of a given graph family.
arxiv:2611.19835.authors: Changqing Xu, Yan Yang, Junxue Zhang

arxiv:2611.19842.title: Splitting of separatrices in generalized standard maps
arxiv:2611.19842.summary: We consider generalized standard maps, that is, maps $F_h:(x,y) \mapsto (x+y+f(x;h),y+f(x;h))$ under quite general assumptions. These maps are area preserving. In particular, the Chirikov standard map, the area preserving H\'enon map and the case $f(x;h)= \varepsilon(x-x^n)$, $n\ge 2$, where $\varepsilon = 4 \sinh^2(h/2)$ satisfy our hypotheses.
arxiv:2611.19842.authors: Inmaculada Baldom\'a, D\'idac Gil-Rams, Pau Mart\'in

arxiv:2611.19846.title: Borel $(2n+1)$-coloring for bounded degree function graphs
arxiv:2611.19846.summary: Let $G=(X,E)$ be a Borel graph generated by $n$-many bounded-to-one Borel functions. We show that $G$ admits a Borel proper $(2n+1)$-coloring, which answers a problem of Kechris, Solecki and Todor\v{c}evi\'{c}.

arxiv:2611.19855.title: Scaling Fourier Inequalities for Locally Compact Quantum Groups
arxiv:2611.19855.summary: In this paper, we study Fourier and convolution inequalities on locally compact quantum groups in the presence of the scaling group. For $1\le p\le 2$, we investigate a family of scaling Fourier transforms and the associated norms $H_{p,\theta}(\mathbb G)$, and we show that $H_{p,\theta}(\mathbb G)<1$ for the real quantum $az+b$ group and $0<\theta<1$, $1<p<2$. We also investigate scaling convolution for locally compact quantum groups and, by extending the ordinary convolution, obtain the corresponding scaling Young inequality in four different regions.

arxiv:2611.19866.title: Uniquely balanced polyhedral complexes are highly connected
arxiv:2611.19866.summary: We establish higher connectivity of polyhedral complexes admitting a unique positive balanced top cycle. Our main result shows that, after quotienting by common lineality, every skeleton satisfies the corresponding higher connectivity property. The proof bounds the number of connected components surviving facet deletions by the dimension of the top-cycle space using homological and linear-algebraic arguments.

arxiv:2611.19870.title: Toward an Admissibility Theory of Aharonov--Bohm Arbitrage
arxiv:2611.19870.summary: This note develops a provisional admissibility framework for Aharonov-Bohm type arbitrage. Starting from a categorical filtration $F:\mathcal T_{\mathrm{mic}}^{\mathrm{op}}\to \mathsf{Prob}$ and its distortion on microscopic histories, we ask when a favorable closed microscopic loop can be realized as an executable relative ordinal arbitrage over an open macro-time interval. The history endofunctor $\mathsf{Hist}$ retains the staged decomposition of economic activities, while the twisted-arrow category $\operatorname{Tw}(\mathsf{Hist}(\mathcal T_{\mathrm{mic}}))$ represents a microscopic loop as an arrow between distinct histories.

arxiv:2611.19873.title: Uniqueness of limit cycle{s} in a class of classical trinomial Li\'enard systems
arxiv:2611.19873.summary: This paper studies the number of limit cycles of the polynomial Li\'enard system $\dot x=y-F(x)$, $\dot y=-x$, where $F(x)=a_1x^{2N}+a_2x^{2m+1}+x^{2n+1}$, with integers \(N,m,n\) satisfying $2\le N\le m<n$, $a_1\ne0$ and $a_2\neq 0$. It is proved that this system has exactly one limit cycle and that every periodic orbit is hyperbolic and attracting for $a_2<0$; this system has no limit cycles for $a_2>0$. The uniqueness proof compares the widths and relative midpoints of the two scalar arcs obtained in potential coordinates.
arxiv:2611.19873.authors: Hebai Chen, Yuhuan Lu, Qian Wang Rui Zhang

arxiv:2611.19874.title: A Negative Answer to a Variant of the Lins-de Melo-Pugh Conjecture
arxiv:2611.19874.summary: We study the polynomial Li\'enard system $$\dot x=y-(a_1x^{2m+1}+a_2x^{2n+1}+x^{2N}),\qquad \dot y=-x,$$ where $0\leq m< n<N$ are integers and $a_1a_2<0$. The supremum of the numbers of limit cycles in this family is at least two for every integer $N\geq3$ and at least three for $N=5$. These results disprove Conjectures 1.5 and 1.6 of Cen et al. [Sci.
arxiv:2611.19874.authors: Hebai Chen, Jie Jin, Zhijie Li, Jueliang Zhou

arxiv:2611.19880.title: Instability of non-minimal critical points of Newton's equation with real analytic potentials
arxiv:2611.19880.summary: We prove that any non-minimal critical point of a real analytic potential on a finite-dimensional Euclidean space possesses a nonconstant zero-energy Newton trajectory that converges to the equilibrium as \(t\to+\infty\). By time reversibility, this yields forward Lyapunov instability. We do not assume the critical point is isolated.

arxiv:2611.19881.title: Weighted bisections of triangle-free subcubic graphs
arxiv:2611.19881.summary: We prove a conjecture of Gerke, Gutin, Yeo, and Zhou: for every finite triangle-free subcubic graph other than the claw and every nonnegative edge weighting, there is a bisection whose weight is at least $11/15$ of the total edge weight. This bound is best possible, as shown by the Petersen graph. The proof uses matching-based local distributions, weighted induction, and convex separation to establish the edgewise cut guarantees while maintaining global balance.

arxiv:2611.19895.title: Diagonal and Fine Tower Dimensions for Minimal Circle Homeomorphisms and Product Actions
arxiv:2611.19895.summary: We study minimal circle homeomorphisms and their products with Cantor systems, and show that these actions have diagonal dimension at most two and fine tower dimension at least two. Consequently, diagonal dimension, fine tower dimension, and tower dimension are all equal to two for minimal circle homeomorphisms. We also obtain a strict separation between tower dimension and fine tower dimension on a one-dimensional space.

arxiv:2611.19898.title: Minimal sets of countable group actions on regular curves
arxiv:2611.19898.summary: We study minimal sets of countable groups acting by homeomorphisms on regular curves. If the ambient action has a finite orbit, every infinite minimal set is an equicontinuous Cantor system. If there is no finite orbit, the minimal set is unique and remains minimal for every finite-index subgroup.
arxiv:2611.19898.authors: Enhui Shi, Suhua Wang, Yifei Yu

arxiv:2611.19908.title: The maximum length of a Hamiltonian path in the grid graph $P_m \times P_n$
arxiv:2611.19908.summary: Label the $mn$ vertices of the grid graph $P_m \times P_n$ bijectively by $1, \dots, mn$ and read the labels in increasing order; this produces a Hamiltonian path whose length in the Manhattan metric is denoted $M(P_m \times P_n)$. McNeil conjectured, on the basis of computer evidence, that $M(P_n \times P_n) = n^3 - 3$ for even $n$ and $n^3 - n - 1$ for odd $n$. Fried recently determined $M(P_m \times P_n)$ up to an additive error of one.

arxiv:2611.19936.title: Far-field prediction of algebraic curves via generalized asymptotes
arxiv:2611.19936.summary: The asymptotic behavior of algebraic curves is classically described by means of linear asymptotes. However, many infinite branches exhibit a non-linear behavior that cannot be represented accurately by straight lines. In this paper we propose a computational framework for far-field prediction of algebraic curves based on generalized asymptotes.

arxiv:2611.19943.title: Character variety of the punctured sphere and the determinantal variety
arxiv:2611.19943.summary: We show that the SL(2;C) character variety of the n-punctured sphere is described via the determinantal variety defined by an n x n symmetric matrix of rank at most 4 whose entries are the traces of simple closed curves on the surface. This result generalizes the Fricke-Klein-Vogt relations to arbitrary n, and we determine the structure of the kernel of the associated matrix.

arxiv:2611.19973.title: Fano blowups of Grassmannians along sub-Grassmannians
arxiv:2611.19973.summary: Let $\tilde X$ be the successive blowup of the Grassmannian $\operatorname{Gr}(d,n+1)$ with $n\ge3$, in arbitrary characteristic, along sub-Grassmannians of codimension $r_1,\dotsc,r_s\ge2$ that meet transversely. We prove that, if $d\ne2$, then $\tilde X$ is Fano if and only if $\sum_i(r_i-1)\le n$, and we give a similar criterion for $d=2$. As applications, we prove that the successive blowup of $\mathbb{P}^4$ along $s$ planes that meet transversely is Fano if and only if $s\le4$.

arxiv:2611.19977.title: Variants of Expansivity, Shadowing and Spectral Decomposition
arxiv:2611.19977.summary: In this paper, we first distinguish a very recently introduced notion of mean asymptotic expansivity from asymptotic expansivity. Then, we extend the spectral decomposition theorem due to Smale to bi-mean asymptotically expansive homeomorphisms with the shadowing property. We also extend a measurable spectral decomposition theorem due to Shin to shadowable measures for bi-mean asymptotically expansive homeomorphisms.
arxiv:2611.19977.authors: Pramod Kumar Das, Manoj B. Prajapati

arxiv:2611.20015.title: Submatrices of character tables and centers of ordinary and queer q-Schur superalgebras
arxiv:2611.20015.summary: We obtain bases of the centers of the ordinary $q$-Schur superalgebra $\mathcal{S}_q(m|n,r)$ and the queer $q$-Schur superalgebra $\mathcal{Q}_q(n,r)$ in terms of Casimir elements of the Hecke algebra $\mathcal{H}_r$ and the Hecke-Clifford algebra $\mathcal{H}_r^c$, respectively. The key step is to find an invertible submatrix of the character table of $\mathcal{H}_r$ or $\mathcal{H}_r^c$ whose column index set is the support of the corresponding $q$-tensor module appearing in Schur-Weyl duality: for $\mathcal{H}_r$ this is the set $H_{m,n}(r)$ of $(m|n)$-hook partitions of $r$, while for $\mathcal{H}_r^c$ this is the set $\mathrm{SP}_n(r)$ of strict partitions of $r$ of length $\leq n$.…

arxiv:2611.20018.title: Projective Models of Genus 21 K3 Surfaces
arxiv:2611.20018.summary: We construct projective models for general primitively polarized K3 surfaces $(S,h)$ of genus $21$ (degree $h^2=40$) inside the 12-dimensional fine quiver moduli space $X = N(3;3,4)$ parameterizing stable representations of the $3$-Kronecker quiver with dimension vector $(3,4)$. As a corollary, we show that the corresponding moduli space $\mathscr{M}_{21}$ is unirational and prove O'Grady's generalized Franchetta conjecture for genus $21$. Then we investigate the geometry of $(S,h)$ through its Fourier--Mukai partner $S' = M_{S}(4,h,5)$ and construct an explicit isomorphism $f : S^{[2]} \xrightarrow{\sim} S'^{[2]}$ together with a common closed embedding into the projectivization…

arxiv:2611.20037.title: Fundamental groups of closed four-manifolds with positive biorthogonal curvature
arxiv:2611.20037.summary: In this paper, we prove that a group is the fundamental group of a closed, connected, oriented smooth four-manifold admitting a metric of positive biorthogonal curvature if and only if it is finitely presented. This answers a question of Bettiol. The manifold can be chosen to be stably parallelizable, hence spin with vanishing signature, and with Euler characteristic $2(1-p+q)$, where $p$ and $q$ are the numbers of generators and of nontrivial relators in a given finite presentation.

arxiv:2611.20040.title: Simple abelian varieties with prescribed endomorphism ratio
arxiv:2611.20040.summary: Let $A$ be a simple abelian variety over an algebraically closed field, and set $m(A)=2\dim A/[\operatorname{End}^0(A):\mathbb Q]$. We prove that, for every prime $p$ and every positive rational number $\mu$, there exist simple abelian varieties of characteristic $p$ with endomorphism ratio $\mu$, both of $p$-rank zero and of positive $p$-rank. In particular, we answer a question of Oort in a stronger form.

arxiv:2611.20048.title: Representability of Intertwining Operators for Weak Modules of Vertex Operator Algebras
arxiv:2611.20048.summary: Let $V$ be a vertex operator algebra. For every weak $V$-module $W$, we construct a weak $V \otimes V$-module $\mathcal{R}(W)$ representing the bifunctor $\mathcal{I}\binom{W}{-\;-}$ of intertwining operator spaces, in the sense that there exists a natural isomorphism \[ \mathcal{I}\binom{W}{-\;-} \cong \Hom_{V\otimes V} \ab\big(-\otimes -, \; \mathcal{R}(W)). \] As applications of this natural isomorphism, we first establish a Yoneda-type lemma for spaces of intertwining operators, and then identify the unique largest locally restricted submodule $\mathcal{R}_{\lr}(V^\prime)$ of $\mathcal{R}(V^\prime)$ with the coend of the bifunctor $-\otimes-^\prime$: \[ \mathcal{R}_{\lr}(V^\prime) \cong…

arxiv:2611.20055.title: Minimal Models for Free Quasi-Invariant and Stationary Actions
arxiv:2611.20055.summary: In this paper, we generalize the fact that essentially free p.m.p. actions of a countably infinite group admit a minimal model, proved by Weiss and Zucker. We prove that minimal models exist for every essentially free non singular action. Furthermore, as in the p.m.p. case, we prove that all essentially free $\mu$-stationary actions (with respect to a fixed generating probability measure $\mu$) admit a common minimal model.

arxiv:2611.20056.title: Matrix Star-Triangle Relations
arxiv:2611.20056.summary: We propose a matrix generalization of the star--triangle relations and identify solutions underlying the $\mathfrak{sl}_n$ chiral Potts models.

arxiv:2611.20074.title: Property A and the identification of the maximal and reduced uniform Roe algebras
arxiv:2611.20074.summary: Let $X$ be a discrete metric space of bounded geometry. We prove that $X$ has property A if and only if the canonical map $$\lambda:C^*_{u,max}(X)\to C^*_u(X)$$ is an isomorphism.

arxiv:2611.20077.title: Deligne pairing isomorphisms for projective duals and higher-rank associated hypersurfaces
arxiv:2611.20077.summary: Given a family \pi:X\to S of complex projective varieties, polarised by a (sufficiently) relatively very ample L, we give an isomorphism between a Deligne pairing involving higher relative cotangent Chern classes, and the relative projective dual line X^\vee(L). As a consequence, we obtain explicit Deligne pairing isomorphisms for all of the higher associated hypersurfaces of Gelfand--Kapranov--Zelevinsky, including mixed polarisations, as well as higher-rank versions of such hypersurfaces involving sufficiently positive vector bundles.

arxiv:2611.20086.title: Structure of gaps and generalized Wilf's conjecture
arxiv:2611.20086.summary: In this article, we study the gaps, the maximal gaps, and the pseudo-Frobenius elements of generalized numerical semigroups of minimum embedding dimension. For these semigroups, we give an explicit description of the set of gaps, explicit formulas for the genus and the number of maximal gaps, and an explicit description of the set of pseudo-Frobenius elements in terms of the blocks of consecutive gaps of an associated numerical semigroup. In particular, we obtain an explicit formula for the type.
arxiv:2611.20086.authors: Om Prakash Bhardwaj, Carmelo Cisto, Priyavrat Deshpande

arxiv:2611.20093.title: On Win's Conjecture for Edge-Disjoint Perfect Matchings
arxiv:2611.20093.summary: In 1982, Win conjectured that, for every even integer $n$ and every integer $k$ $1\le k\le n-2$, any graph $G$ of order $n$ satisfying $d_G(x)+d_G(y)\ge n+k-2$ for every pair of nonadjacent vertices $x,y$ contains $k$ pairwise edge-disjoint perfect matchings. In this paper, we prove a stronger result for all sufficiently large even $n$. More precisely, we show that under the same degree-sum condition, $G$ contains $\lfloor k/2\rfloor$ pairwise edge-disjoint Hamilton cycles, together with an additional perfect matching when $k$ is odd, all pairwise edge-disjoint.
arxiv:2611.20093.authors: Yufei Chang, Yangyang Cheng, Zhilan Wang, Shuo Wei

arxiv:2611.20104.title: Stability of Carath\'eodory Outer Measures Generated by Spatial Gauges
arxiv:2611.20104.summary: We study outer measures generated by covering costs that depend on both the diameter and the location of a covering set. After establishing the metric and Borel-regularity properties of this construction, we investigate its stability under perturbations of the spatial gauge. For power gauges, we prove a uniform logarithmic criterion: if the exponent perturbation multiplied by $\log(1/r)$ converges uniformly to $\lambda$, then the induced measure is multiplied by $e^{-\lambda}$.
arxiv:2611.20104.authors: Ren\'e Erlin Castillo, H\'ector Camilo Chaparro

arxiv:2611.20105.title: Embedding of Barnes-Wall lattices into Cayley-Dickson algebras
arxiv:2611.20105.summary: The family of Barnes-Wall lattices includes the balanced Barnes-Wall lattice $M_n$ over $\mathbb{Z}[\sqrt{2}]$ and two ordinary Barnes-Wall lattices $L_n$ and $L'_n$ over $\mathbb{Z}$, which are geometrically equivalent to each other. Embedding of these lattices into the Cayley-Dickson algebras of an appropriate dimension is considered. It is shown that for all $n \geq 2$ the lattices $M_n$ and $L_n$ are closed under multiplication and are generated by the sets of pairwise products of their elements.

arxiv:2611.20113.title: The dual of separated metric compact Hausdorff spaces is an infinitary variety of algebras
arxiv:2611.20113.summary: A metric compact Hausdorff space is a Lawvere metric space equipped with a compatible compact Hausdorff topology (which does not need to be the induced topology). These spaces maintain many important features of compact metric spaces, but the resulting category is much better behaved. We prove that the category of separated metric compact Hausdorff spaces is dually equivalent to a variety of infinitary algebras.

arxiv:2611.20136.title: An isolated complex Hadamard matrix with nonzero defect
arxiv:2611.20136.summary: We exhibit a complex Hadamard matrix of nonzero defect which is isolated among complex Hadamard matrices, up to Hadamard equivalence. This counterexample is realized by a Butson-type Hadamard matrix of size $13$, with entries roots of order $6$ of unity. In the language of commuting squares, this shows that the span condition, previously introduced by the second author as a sufficient condition for isolation, is not a necessary condition for isolation.

arxiv:2611.20138.title: Planar PArcK is PSPACE-complete
arxiv:2611.20138.summary: Partizan Arc Kayles, or PArcK, is a partizan combinatorial game on edge colored graphs, and is a generalization of the game Domineering. Previously, PArcK was shown to be PSPACE-complete on bipartite graphs. In this paper we show that PArcK is PSPACE-complete even when restricted to planar graphs of degree at most three by a reduction from Generalized Hex.

arxiv:2611.20167.title: Maximal Independent Sets in Set Systems
arxiv:2611.20167.summary: We prove a general theorem on the existence of small maximal independent sets in set systems satisfying natural local density conditions. For an antichain whose degrees are uniform and whose small sets lie in few blocks and whose links overlap little, we show that there is a maximal independent set whose size is asymptotically given by an explicit expression in the degrees, as the degrees grow. The proof comes with a polynomial-time algorithm that finds such a set.

arxiv:2611.20173.title: The $k$-th Milnor and Tjurina numbers: conjectures and a bifurcation formula for pairs
arxiv:2611.20173.summary: We study the higher-order Milnor and Tjurina numbers of isolated hypersurface singularities and extend these invariants to pairs of plane holomorphic germs. We first show that a conjectured upper bound of Hussain, Yau and Zuo on the ratio between the higher-order Milnor and Tjurina numbers of isolated hypersurface singularities in three-dimensional complex space does not hold: it fails already for the simplest singularity, a non-degenerate quadratic one, and the ratio tends to infinity as the order grows. We then prove that a conjecture of Shi, Yau and Zuo on semiquasihomogeneous singularities holds for plane curves, for every order and over formal power series, and show that it fails in…
arxiv:2611.20173.authors: Arturo Fern\'andez-P\'erez, Evelia R. Garc\'{i}a Barroso, Marcela Ribeiro, Nancy Saravia-Molina

arxiv:2611.20182.title: Unirationality of Meromorphic Differential Strata
arxiv:2611.20182.summary: We prove that all components of the meromorphic differential strata are unirational in genus $2\le g\le 5$ and with relatively low number of poles. In particular, it follows that the moduli space of pointed even spin curves $\mathcal{S}_{5;1}^+=\mathcal{S}_5^+\times_{\mathcal{M}_5}\mathcal{M}_{5,1}$ is unirational.

arxiv:2611.20184.title: Two categorifications of the Kekul\'e relations
arxiv:2611.20184.summary: We give new relations in the kernel of the foam evaluation. As a consequence we obtain categorifications of all the Kelul\'e relations introduced by Morrison. Along the way, we discover an equivalent set of relations for which we provide categorifications as well.
arxiv:2611.20184.authors: Jernej Grlj, Ziyi Lei, Emmanuel Wagner

arxiv:2611.20197.title: Integral zero-sum incidence identities and Davenport constants in rank three
arxiv:2611.20197.summary: We study the Davenport constant of finite abelian groups through signed identities among zero-sum subsequences. An integral incidence identity of degree $t$ for a sequence assigns integer weights to its nonempty zero-sum subsequences so that the weights add up to one, while those of the subsequences containing any given nonempty set of at most $t$ terms add up to zero. Over a finite abelian $p$-group $H$, the zero-sum subsequences of a sequence of any length have an indicator polynomial of degree at most $D(H)-1$, and this gives a transfer principle: if, for each $t\ge0$, every sequence of $L(t)$ terms over $Q$ admits such an identity of degree $t$, then $D(Q\oplus H)\le L(D(H)-1)$ for…
arxiv:2611.20197.authors: Claudiu G. Pop, George C. Rad, George C. \c{T}urca\c{s}

arxiv:2611.20205.title: Independent set reconfiguration is hard at treewidth four
arxiv:2611.20205.summary: Independent Set Reconfiguration asks whether one of two given independent sets of equal size can be transformed into the other by moving one token at a time while keeping the occupied vertices independent. In token sliding, a token moves along an edge. In token jumping, it may move to any unoccupied vertex.
arxiv:2611.20205.authors: Hussein Abbas, Haydar Hamieh, Amer E. Mouawad, Ali Slim

arxiv:2611.20221.title: Lengths and Counting of Palindromic Prefixes of Standard Sturmian Words
arxiv:2611.20221.summary: Every standard Sturmian word $c_\mathbf{d}$ is determined by a directive sequence $\mathbf{d}=(d_i)_{i\ge 1}$ of positive integers, and its palindromic prefixes are obtained by iterated palindromic closure. We describe the lengths of these prefixes by the numbers $j\,\ell_{i-1}+\ell_{i-2}-2$, where $\ell_n$ is the length of the $n$-th standard word and $1\le j\le d_i$, and we show that each nonzero length is attained by exactly one pair $(i,j)\neq(1,1)$. For a purely periodic directive sequence of period $k$ we then prove that the number $\pi_\mathbf{d}(N)$ of nonempty palindromic prefixes of length at most $N$ satisfies \[…

arxiv:2611.20237.title: Positivity of simplicial volume of convex projective manifolds
arxiv:2611.20237.summary: Let $\Omega$ be an irreducible properly convex projective domain admitting a discrete cocompact group action of projective automorphisms. We prove that the Holmes--Thompson volumes of projective simplices with vertices in $\Omega$ are uniformly bounded. As a consequence, we prove that a closed properly convex projective manifold of dimension at least two has positive simplicial volume if and only if it is irreducible.

arxiv:2611.20240.title: A Proof of Stein's Equidissection Conjecture
arxiv:2611.20240.summary: In 1970 Monsky showed that a square cannot be dissected into an odd number of equal-area triangles. His proof used an ingenious colouring of the plane based on a 2-adic valuation on $\mathbb{R}$ together with Sperner's lemma. Subsequent work established similar results for regular polygons, centrally symmetric polygons, and polyominoes.

arxiv:2611.20256.title: Continuous-Time Stochastic Contraction Induced by Common White Noise
arxiv:2611.20256.summary: This paper studies contraction properties of stochastic dynamical systems governed by It\^o stochastic differential equations. We consider two trajectories driven by a common noise process and measure their separation using Finsler distances, which encompass Riemannian and norm-induced distances. Two notions of contraction are then investigated: $L^p$-contraction, defined by exponential decay of the $L^p$-norm (or the $p$-th moment) of the distance, and almost sure contraction, defined by exponential decay of the distance along almost every sample path.
arxiv:2611.20256.authors: Sunghyun Koo, Jin Gyu Lee, Hyungbo Shim

arxiv:2611.20270.title: Ramsey sets are canonically Ramsey
arxiv:2611.20270.summary: A set $A$ of points is called Ramsey if, for each $r$, every $r$-coloring of a sufficiently high-dimensional Euclidean space contains a monochromatic congruent copy of $A$. We show that for each Ramsey set $A$, every $r$-coloring of a sufficiently high-dimensional Euclidean space, regardless of the number of colors used, contains a monochromatic or a rainbow congruent copy of $A$. This answers a question raised in virtually every paper on the topic.

arxiv:2611.20276.title: Medicaid Quality Disparities: Domain-Specific Performance Analysis and Approaches for State-Level Improvement
arxiv:2611.20276.summary: Medicaid covers nearly 78 million people, yet care quality varies across states, programs, and clinical domains. Using the 2024 CMS Child and Adult Core Sets (9,781 usable state-measure observations from 11,100 records), this study combined descriptive statistics, benchmark-gap analysis, correlation, and OLS regression to find where shortfalls cluster. Disparities were strongly domain-specific.

arxiv:2611.20282.title: Canonical metrics on punctured spheres, II: compactified moduli spaces of black holes
arxiv:2611.20282.summary: Let $g_{\mathfrak{p}_{\ell}}$ denote the canonical scalar-flat metric on $S^n\setminus \mathfrak{p}_{\ell}$ introduced in Part~I, which for $n=3$ corresponds to the Brill--Lindquist initial data for $\ell$ black holes, and let $\eta\in H_{\ell}$ be its associated mass matrix. In this paper, we investigate the asymptotic behavior of the metrics and the mass matrix $\eta$ as subsets of punctures collide. Such collisions cause every mass to diverge; if a cluster $A$ of black holes collapses at a relative scale $t$, the mass matrix satisfies $\eta=E(A)\ln(1/t)+O(1)$, diverging along an explicit ray $E(A)\in H_{\ell}$.

arxiv:2611.20286.title: Maximum likelihood degrees of 3D polytopes built from polygons of ML degree one
arxiv:2611.20286.summary: We construct 3D polytopes that admit a scaling with maximum likelihood (ML) degree one by using codimension zero toric fiber products of lower-dimensional polytopes and classify all the 3D polytopes that can be constructed in this way. We also study a family of 3D polytopes whose faces admit ML degree one scalings. We give a tight lower bound for the ML degree of these polytopes with a square base and we show that every value between this bound and the normalized volume of the polytope can be attained.
arxiv:2611.20286.authors: Eliana Duarte, Federico Lazzeri, Bowen Li, Ludovico Piazza, Bernhard Reinke, Nico Wolf

arxiv:2611.20287.title: Structural properties of semi-cutting sets
arxiv:2611.20287.summary: Let $G=(V,E)$ be a finite simple undirected graph, let $T\subseteq V$, and let $F\subseteq E$. We call $F$ semi-cutting for $T$ if $d_{G}(u,w)<d_{G\setminus F}(u,w)$ for every two distinct terminals $u,w\in T$. We prove the sharp bound $|F|\ge |T|-1$.
arxiv:2611.20287.authors: Bart{\l}omiej Bosek, Oriol Serra, Llu\'is Vena

arxiv:2611.20303.title: On dynamical and parameter spaces for the Maximally Generalized McMullen family of rational maps
arxiv:2611.20303.summary: We explore the maximally generalized McMullen family of rational maps $F_{n,d,c,a}(z) = z^n + a/z^d + c$, for $n,d\in \mathbb{Z},$ with $n,d\geq 3$, $a\in \mathbb{C}^*$ and $c\in \mathbb{C}$. In the dynamical plane, we establish annular regions containing the Julia sets, and show that the geometric limits of both the Julia and filled Julia sets as $n,d\to \infty$ are contained in the unit circle. In parameter space, for any fixed $a\in \mathbb{C}^*$, we examine the boundedness locus in the $c$-plane.
arxiv:2611.20303.authors: Suzanne Boyd, Jillian Cervantes, Rachel Foster, Olivia Hwang, Sebastian Marcano, Molly Roughan

arxiv:2611.20304.title: A notion of pseudo-morphisms with applications to the study of polynomial maps and of link-homotopy groups of 2-string link
arxiv:2611.20304.summary: We introduce a notion of pseudo-morphism for groups, which extends the notion of group morphism from a group to a ring. We show that pseudo-morphisms from a group $G$ to an integral domain $R$ form a filtred Hopf algebra which can be seen as an efficient notion of dual for $G$. We also show that pseudo-morphisms are closely related to the notion of polynomial maps in the sense of Eilenberg-MacLane/Passi, the two notions even coinciding when $G$ is finitely generated and $R$ is a field.

arxiv:2611.20308.title: Stability conditions on Lazarsfeld-Mukai bundles over abelian surfaces
arxiv:2611.20308.summary: We study the stability of Lazarsfeld-Mukai bundles associated with smooth curves over abelian surfaces. When the general curve in $|L|$ have Clifford dimension one and maximal gonality, for $\rho \gg 0$ we show that every component of the relative Brill-Noether loci \(W^1_d(|L|)\) dominating the linear system parametrizes generically \(\mu_L\)-stable rank-two Lazarsfeld-Mukai bundles. We also apply Bayer-Li wall-crossing to higher-rank bundles: if \(\operatorname{NS}(S)=\mathbb Z\cdot L\), \(A\) is a globally generated complete linear series of degree \(d\) on a smooth curve \(C\in|L|\), \(h^0(C,A)=r+1\) with \(r>2\), and \(d\ne g-1\), then the associated bundle \(E_{C,A}\) is…

arxiv:2611.20344.title: Up or down at every integer: Collatz-type maps of arbitrary sets and the up-down graph
arxiv:2611.20344.summary: For a set $S$ of positive integers let $T_S$ send $x$ to $\lceil 3x/2\rceil$ if $x\in S$ and to $\lceil x/2\rceil$ otherwise. The odd numbers give the Collatz map, the even numbers give it again after a shift by one, and $S=\mathbb{N}$ gives Mahler's map $x\mapsto\lceil 3x/2\rceil$. All these maps are subgraphs of the up-down graph $G$, in which every $x$ has the edges $x\to\lceil x/2\rceil$ and $x\to\lceil 3x/2\rceil$, and so are the families of maps in which the direction is forced at some numbers and free at the others.

arxiv:2611.20346.title: Canonical activation patterns and ReLU pattern varieties
arxiv:2611.20346.summary: A ReLU pattern variety records the polynomial relations among the coefficients of the affine maps associated with a prescribed set of activation patterns of a ReLU network. We study how the combinatorics of the canonical set of activation patterns of an unbiased ReLU network is reflected in the geometry of its pattern variety. In particular, we introduce the notion of pattern stability and characterize pattern stability and combinatorial stability for shallow networks.
arxiv:2611.20346.authors: Bella Finkel, Yaoying Fu, Chenxi Wu

arxiv:2611.20350.title: Relative involutions and inverses in monoidal dualities and slice constructions
arxiv:2611.20350.summary: Our goal in this paper is to work towards developing a framework for characterizing dualities of weak categorical structures. It is often the case that duality involutions are characterized by relations which are more general than $f^2=1$. Moreover, it is also true that many dualities cannot be expressed using involutions alone.

arxiv:2611.20353.title: Finite generation of the second homology group of the genus three Torelli group
arxiv:2611.20353.summary: We prove that the group $H_2(\mathcal{I}_3;\mathbb{Z})$ is finitely generated, where $\mathcal{I}_3$ is the Torelli subgroup of the mapping class group of a closed genus-three surface $\Sigma_3$. A key role in the proof is played by establishing the following property: for each symplectic transvection $t_x\in\mathrm{Sp}_{6}(\mathbb{Z})$, we have $$ \bigl(t^{120}_x-1\bigr)^{57}\bigl(t_x^{24}-1\bigr)(t_x-1)^6H_2(\mathcal{I}_3;\mathbb{Z})=0. $$ The proof is based on the study of the spectral sequences associated with the action of $\mathcal{I}_3$ on the Bestvina-Bux-Margalit complex of minimizing cycles and with the actions on certain auxiliary complexes of the stabilizers of two- and…

arxiv:2611.20373.title: Nazarov-Sklyanin Lax operators at higher rank
arxiv:2611.20373.summary: We construct a rank-$m$ Nazarov-Sklyanin Lax operator for generalized Macdonald functions. The operator acts on the horizontal Fock module of quantum toroidal $\mathfrak{gl}_1$, extended by an auxiliary polynomial space with $m$ components. A geometric realization is given by the tensor product with the dual tautological line on the equivariant $K$-theory of a Hecke correspondence studied by Negut.

arxiv:2611.20374.title: Goldman's Ergodicity Conjecture and Branched Developing Maps
arxiv:2611.20374.summary: We prove that every representation $\rho:\pi_1(\Sigma_g)\rightarrow\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathrm{R})$ which sends every simple closed curve to a hyperbolic element admits a branched developing map. As a corollary, the mapping class group action on the Euler class zero component of the $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathrm{R})$-character variety of a genus $g$ surface is ergodic if $g\geq3$. (The action is not ergodic if $g=2$.) Moreover, almost every representation of nonzero Euler class admits a branched developing map.

arxiv:2611.20383.title: The unitary group $U_3(4)$ as a Galois group over $\mathbb{Q}$
arxiv:2611.20383.summary: We prove that the simple unitary group $U_3(4)=\operatorname{PSU}_3(\mathbb{F}_4)$, of order $62400$, is the Galois group of a regular extension of $\mathbb{Q}(t)$, and hence of infinitely many extensions of $\mathbb{Q}$. The extension has four branch points, with inertia groups of orders $2$, $2$, $3$, $3$, and it is the only extension with these properties up to a rational change of the coordinate $t$. We give an explicit polynomial of degree $65$ for it.

arxiv:2611.20395.title: Lifting the local logarithmic Cartier transform modulo $p^n$
arxiv:2611.20395.summary: Let $p$ be a prime number and $n\ge 1$ an integer. We construct a local logarithmic Cartier transform modulo $p^n$, following an approach by Shiho. More precisely, consider the ring $W$ of Witt vectors of a perfect field of characteristic $p$.

arxiv:2611.20408.title: Equilateral-triangle-free sets in finite planes
arxiv:2611.20408.summary: For a prime $p>3$, let $F(p)$ be the largest cardinality of a subset of $\mathbb F_p^2$ containing no equilateral triangle with nonzero squared side length. Alex Iosevich asked for the exact value of $F(p)$. By constructing such subsets of $\mathbb F_p^2$ from cap sets in $\mathbb F_3^n$, we obtain the uniform lower bounds \[ F(p)\gg \begin{cases} p^{2\gamma}, & p\equiv 11\pmod{12},\\ p^{1+\gamma}, & p\equiv 1\pmod{12}.
arxiv:2611.20408.authors: Daewoong Cheong, Thang Pham, Le Quang-Ham

arxiv:2611.20413.title: An Implementation of the 3-Dimensional Extended Persistent Homology Transform
arxiv:2611.20413.summary: The Extended Persistent Homology Transform (XPHT) describes a shape through the extended persistence diagrams of its directional height functions. We present an algorithm for computing a finite directional sample of the three-dimensional XPHT from a triangulated boundary. Our main construction determines essential first-homology pairings by combining an ordered tree-cotree decomposition with evaluation-dual cocycles.

arxiv:2611.20424.title: Quasi-F-split heights and derived Morita invariance
arxiv:2611.20424.summary: In this paper, we study quasi-F-splitting from the viewpoint of non-commutative algebraic geometry. Let k be a perfect field of characteristic p. For a proper dg-category over k with a Serre functor, we define quasi-F^e-split heights for e\geq 1 by using finite topological restriction homology with coefficients in a shift of the Serre functor.

arxiv:2611.20450.title: Physics-informed neural network for model-based global computation of the asymptotic phase of limit-cycle oscillators
arxiv:2611.20450.summary: The asymptotic phase is the central object of phase reduction theory for limit-cycle oscillators. It is a scalar coordinate defined throughout the basin of attraction of a limit cycle that advances at a constant natural frequency along every trajectory. Computing the phase from a given mathematical model requires solving a first-order partial differential equation (PDE) over the entire basin, which is challenging due to high computation costs and complex boundary conditions.

arxiv:2611.20463.title: M\"obius Invertibility of Rank Invariants
arxiv:2611.20463.summary: One of the best known invariants of multi-parameter persistent homology is the rank invariant, which is subsumed by the generalized rank invariant (GRI), obtained by naturally extending its domain. M\"obius inversion of the GRI not only provides a compact encoding of this invariant but is also useful for clarifying its relationship with other invariants of multi-parameter persistent homology. However, M\"obius inversion of the GRI has been defined only under suitable finiteness conditions on its domain and support.
arxiv:2611.20463.authors: Nathaniel Clause, Woojin Kim, Facundo M\'{e}moli

arxiv:2611.20486.title: Inverse Problem for Super-linearization with Single Observable and Diagonalizable Principal Submatrix
arxiv:2611.20486.summary: Super-linearization is, roughly speaking, embedding an $n$-dimensional nonlinear dynamical system into an $(n + m)$-dimensional linear system. We introduce and address, in this paper, the inverse problem: given a linear system $\dot x= M x$, what type of dynamical systems can be super-linearized to it? We focus on the special case where the dimension reduction is one (i.e., $m = 1$) and the leading $n$-by-$n$ principal submatrix of $M$ is diagonalizable, and provide a solution to the problem.

arxiv:2611.20504.title: A proof of a conjecture on bipartite correspondence packing
arxiv:2611.20504.summary: A correspondence cover assigns a set of possible colors to each vertex of a graph. For each edge, a matching between the two endpoint color sets specifies the forbidden color pairs. A correspondence coloring selects one color at each vertex so that no forbidden pair is selected.

arxiv:2611.20539.title: Graph Intersections and Hypergraph Discrepancy
arxiv:2611.20539.summary: Let $G$ and $H$ be graphs on $n$ vertices with $e(G)=p\binom{n}{2}$ and $e(H)=q\binom{n}{2}$, where $p,q\in(0,1)$ are fixed. Bollob\'as and Scott studied intersections of two graphs under random relabelling and asked for the minimum $L^2$ norm of the deviation of their intersection size from its expected value. We answer this question by proving that, for graphs of order $n$ with fixed edge densities $p,q\in(0,1)$, the minimum is \begin{equation*} \left(\sqrt{\frac{p(1-p)q(1-q)}{2}\cdot\frac{1-\sqrt R}{1+\sqrt R}}\right)n+o(n), \end{equation*} where $R=\max\{p,1-p,q,1-q\}$.

arxiv:2611.20547.title: Klein four slices of the representation suspensions of $H\underline{\mathbb{F}_2}$
arxiv:2611.20547.summary: We study the regular slice filtration of representation spheres $S^V\wedge H\underline{M}$. For every finite group $G$, we locate all slices in an explicit interval $[n(V),k(V)]$ and show that both endpoints occur. We introduce a \emph{defect vector} to measure a slice's failure.

arxiv:2611.20554.title: $L$-systems on the large Witt design
arxiv:2611.20554.summary: Let $L=\{0,1,2,3,4,8\}$, associated with the large Witt design $S(5,8,24)$, and let $m(n,24,L)$ be the maximum size of a family of $24$-element subsets of an $n$-element set whose distinct members have intersection sizes in $L$. We prove that there are positive constants $c,C,n_0$ such that, for every $n\geq n_0$, \[ cn^{316/63}\leq m(n,24,L)\leq Cn^{169/29}. \] We also obtain similar results for the systems associated with $S(4,7,23)$, $S(3,6,22)$, and $S(3,4,14)$.

arxiv:2611.20586.title: $G$-Hilbert schemes of canonical abelian quotient threefolds
arxiv:2611.20586.summary: Ishida and Iwashita showed that the canonical abelian quotient singularities of dimension three that are not Gorenstein fall into four families. For the two families that have not been treated before, we extend a method of K\k{e}dzierski and compute the toric charts of the $G$-Hilbert scheme explicitly. As a result, we show that the $G$-Hilbert scheme has at worst conifold singularities.

arxiv:2611.20615.title: Hyperbolic string vertices as geometric chains
arxiv:2611.20615.summary: For 0<L<=2arcsinh(1), the hyperbolic string vertices of Costello and Zwiebach consist of the bordered hyperbolic surfaces with geodesic boundary of length L whose interior simple closed geodesics have length at least L. We show that the corresponding regions in moduli space are compact oriented orbifolds with corners whose boundaries are, including orientations and automorphism groups, the spaces of twisted sewings. Hence their generating chain satisfies the master equation without the bracket term exactly in a complex of geometric chains.

arxiv:2611.20620.title: Cycles on the universal moduli of rank 2 bundles over the hyperelliptic locus
arxiv:2611.20620.summary: We establish a strong Franchetta property for the universal moduli stack of rank two vector bundles over smooth hyperelliptic curves and identify the image of the Chow ring in the cohomology of a fiber via restriction and the cycle class map as precisely the monodromy invariant cohomology classes. More precisely, for every genus $g\geq 2$, degree $d$, and hyperelliptic curve $C$ of genus $g$, we show that the restriction and the cycle class map identifies the Chow ring of the universal moduli stack with the subring of $H^* (Bun_{2,d}(C),\mathbb Q)$ generated by twisted $\kappa$-classes, which coincides with $H^{*}(Bun_{2,d}(C), \mathbb Q)^{\pi_1(\mathcal H_g,[C])}$. We use this viewpoint to…

arxiv:2611.20638.title: Convergence rate of periodic homogenization for convex Hamilton--Jacobi equations with super critical viscosity
arxiv:2611.20638.summary: This paper is devoted to studying the convergence rate in periodic homogenization of the viscous Hamilton--Jacobi equation (with supercritical viscosity index $\sigma>1$) \[ \partial_t u_\varepsilon+H(x/\varepsilon,\partial_xu_\varepsilon)=\varepsilon^\sigma\Delta u_\varepsilon,\quad (x,t)\in\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}_+,\ \] subject to a given initial datum. For Tonelli Hamiltonians $H$, the solution $u_\varepsilon$ is proved to converge to a certain $u:\mathbb{R}^n\times\mathbb{R}\rightarrow\mathbb{R}$ (solving the effective problem) in the optimal rate $O(\varepsilon^{\min\{\sigma-1,1\}})$. We also obtain a rate for the case of non-convex Hamiltonians and discussed its optimality…
arxiv:2611.20638.authors: Gengyu Liu, Zibo Wang, Jianlu Zhang

arxiv:2611.20639.title: A study guide for Bourgain's 2003 sum-product theorem and 2010 discretized projection theorem
arxiv:2611.20639.summary: These notes present Bourgain's proofs of the discretized sum-product theorem and its applications. The discussion emphasizes the construction of trees with multiscale porosity from small additive doubling, using either quantitative Freiman theorrem or the Pl\"unnecke-Ruzsa inequality, and the amplification of these structures by multiplication. Additive combinatorial tools connect the resulting growth estimates to discretized sum-product problem.

arxiv:2611.20659.title: Polynomial twisted periods and affine vertex algebras
arxiv:2611.20659.summary: We prove the conjecture of Kang, Lawrie, and Song that Zhu's $C_2$-algebra of a simply-laced boundary admissible affine vertex algebra is isomorphic to the Jacobian ring of an invariant potential obtained by lifting a polynomial twisted period from a Cartan subalgebra via the Chevalley isomorphism. We further identify the $C_2$-algebras of the corresponding Drinfeld-Sokolov reductions with the Jacobian rings of the restrictions of this potential to Slodowy slices. We also extend the Jacobian presentation to non-simply-laced principal boundary admissible affine vertex algebras, where the restriction of the potential to the Cartan subalgebra satisfies a Dunkl-singularity equation with…

arxiv:2611.20667.title: Near-synchronous multiphoton quantum interference
arxiv:2611.20667.summary: Nonclassical multiphoton interference is an important resource for optical quantum information processing, and its output statistics depend on the distinguishability of the input photons. In this paper, using time delay as a tunable parameter, we theoretically analyze the interference behavior of independent pure-state single photons with identical Gaussian spectral envelopes under near-synchronous conditions. Using the immanant representation of the single-photon internal-state overlap matrix to express the weights of the exchange-symmetry components, we determine the leading asymptotic behavior and approximation error of each weight, and characterize the weight suppression laws when…

arxiv:2611.20668.title: Local limit theorems and counting for transverse subgroups
arxiv:2611.20668.summary: Transverse subgroups form a special class of discrete subgroups of connected semisimple real algebraic groups that includes all discrete subgroups of rank-one Lie groups, as well as Anosov and relatively Anosov subgroups. We study the joint distribution of partial Cartan projections and the two associated Cartan flags for Zariski dense $\theta$-transverse subgroups. Assuming local mixing of the associated Bowen-Margulis-Sullivan measure, we prove two local limit theorems and deduce counting asymptotics in Euclidean balls and tubes, together with equidistribution of the Cartan flags.
arxiv:2611.20668.authors: Sam Edwards, Minju Lee, Hee Oh

arxiv:2611.20681.title: Haar local mixing for transverse subgroups
arxiv:2611.20681.summary: Transverse subgroups form a special class of discrete subgroups of connected semisimple real algebraic groups that includes all discrete subgroups of rank-one Lie groups, as well as Anosov and relatively Anosov subgroups. For torsion-free Zariski dense $\theta$-transverse subgroups, we establish Haar local mixing for the partial Weyl chamber action under a Bowen-Margulis-Sullivan (BMS) local mixing hypothesis. The proof is based on a transfer principle using the domains of discontinuity introduced by Delarue-Monclair-Sanders and extended to transverse subgroups by Guedes Bonthonneau-Lefeuvre-Weich.
arxiv:2611.20681.authors: Sam Edwards, Minju Lee, Hee Oh

arxiv:2611.20707.title: State-Dependent Saving and Heavy-Tailed Shocks in a Stochastic Solow Growth Model via a Logistic L\'evy Framework
arxiv:2611.20707.summary: This work develops a stochastic Solow growth model in which the aggregate saving rate is state dependent and evolves on a faster time scale than capital. The saving target follows a mean-reverting process driven by symmetric $\alpha$-stable L\'evy noise, while the saving control adjusts toward this target and capital accumulates according to a Solow equation. After scaling, the model is a three-dimensional stochastic dynamical system with multiplicative heavy-tailed noise and a logistic saving function.

arxiv:2611.20774.title: Flat and very flat pro-quasi-coherent pro-sheaves on ind-schemes
arxiv:2611.20774.summary: This is a paper about homological algebra of flat pro-quasi-coherent pro-sheaves. We recall and collect various techniques such as accessibility and deconstructibility, and adopt them to ind-schemes under various assumptions. We also discuss the foundations of the notion of an ind-scheme.

arxiv:2611.20776.title: Extensions of $q$-supercongruences arising from a quadratic summation of Gasper and Rahman
arxiv:2611.20776.summary: In this paper, inspired by recent work of Guo and Zhao, and of Guo and Zudilin, we establish two parametric extensions of their $q$-supercongruences using Gasper and Rahman's quadratic summation, the Chinese remainder theorem, and the creative microscoping method. These extensions yield two one-parameter generalizations of the $q$-supercongruences considered by Guo and Zhao and by Guo and Zudilin.

arxiv:2611.20777.title: Treewidth and Separation Number: An Optimal Linear Bound
arxiv:2611.20777.summary: The \emph{separation number} $\sn(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the smallest integer $a$ such that every subgraph $H$ of $G$ admits a separation $(A,B)$ of {\em order} $|A\cap B|\le a$ whose two sides $A\setminus B$ and $B\setminus A$ each contain at most $2|V(H)|/3$ vertices. Dvo\v{r}\'ak and Norin proved that $\tw(G)\le 15\sn(G)$ for every nonempty graph $G$. We improve the constant to its optimal value: every nonempty graph satisfies $\tw(G)\le 4\sn(G)-2$.

arxiv:2611.20784.title: On homogeneous hypertournaments
arxiv:2611.20784.summary: Sullivan recently constructed continuum many countable homogeneous $n$-hypertournaments for every $n\ge3$ by forbidding configurations he calls pair-cancelling. We show that, for every family $\mathcal F$ of pair-cancelling $n$-hypertournaments, the class of all linearly ordered finite $\mathcal F$-free $n$-hypertournaments is Ramsey and has the ordering property. In particular, freely ordered $\mathbf{H}_4$-free $3$-hypertournaments are Ramsey, answering a question of Cherlin, Hubi\v{c}ka, Ne\v{s}et\v{r}il, and the author from 2021.

arxiv:2611.20790.title: Relationship between generic Hecke algebra modules and $0$-Hecke algebra modules
arxiv:2611.20790.summary: Let $H_{R,a}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$ be the Hecke algebra over a principal ideal domain $R$ with parameter $a\in R$. The representation theories of $H_{\mathbb{C}(v^{1/2});v}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$ and $H_{\mathbb{C};0}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$ differ substantially and have largely been studied independently. In this paper, we relate the categories of finitely generated modules of these two algebras through specialization functors from the category of finitely generated $H_{\mathbb{C}[v^{1/2}];v}(\mathfrak{S}_n)$-modules.
arxiv:2611.20790.authors: Young-Hun Kim, So-Yeon Lee, Young-Tak Oh

arxiv:2611.20804.title: A Recursive Construction of Perfect Arrays of Every Shape $2^{a_1}\times\cdots\times2^{a_d}$ over the Unit Quaternions
arxiv:2611.20804.summary: We extend the recursive construction of perfect and odd perfect sequences over the simple unit quaternions $\Qe=\{\pm1,\pm i,\pm j,\pm k\}$ of Blake to arrays of any dimension. The three operations of that construction act on one direction of an array at a time, and are valid whenever the array is periodic in the remaining directions. Starting from a perfect array $P$ of shape $M_2\times\cdots\times M_d$ they give perfect arrays of shape $2^a\times M_2\times\cdots\times M_d$ for every $a\ge0$, with explicit index functions and with the array orthogonality property for the divisor $2$ in the lifted direction; from $a=5$ on these arrays are, in general, Kronecker products of a sequence with…

arxiv:2611.20816.title: Criterion for Glasner property and IC-Rigidity for actions on homogeneous space
arxiv:2611.20816.summary: Let $G$ be a semi-group acting continuously on a compact metric space $X$. The action $G\curvearrowright X$ is called Glasner if for every infinite set $A\subseteq X$ and every $\varepsilon>0$, there exists $g\in G$ such that $gA$ is $\varepsilon$-dense in $X$. Let $\mathcal{K}(X)$ denote the space of nonempty compact subsets of $X$.

arxiv:2611.20820.title: Collapsibility of Vietoris--Rips complexes of hypercube graphs in codimension two
arxiv:2611.20820.summary: Shukla conjectured that the collapsibility number of the Vietoris-Rips complex $\mathrm{VR}(I_n;r)$ of the $n$-dimensional hypercube graph at scale $r$ equals $2^r$ for all $n\ge r+1$. We prove the conjecture for $n=r+2$ and every $r$, which gives the first known cases with $r\ge 4$ beyond the cross-polytope case $n=r+1$. Writing $\mathrm{VR}(I_n;r)$ as the independence complex of the graph $H_{n,r}$ that joins two points when their Hamming distance exceeds $r$, we construct a cover of $H_{r+2,r}$ by $2^r$ co-chordal subgraphs.

arxiv:2611.20829.title: On the volume of amoebas of complete intersections
arxiv:2611.20829.summary: We study the $2k$-dimensional volume of the amoeba of a smooth complete intersection $V$ of dimension $k$ in $(\C^*)^n$, $n\ge2k$, with Newton polytopes $\Delta_1,\dots,\Delta_{n-k}$. For $n=2k$ we prove $\Vol(\A(V))\ge\mathcal M(V)/\MV(\Delta_1,\dots,\Delta_k,-\Delta_1,\dots,-\Delta_k)$, where $\mathcal M(V)$ is the coamoeba volume counted with multiplicity, and we show $\mathcal M(V)\ge\pi^{2k}$ for plane curves ($k=1$, $n=2$) whose Newton polygon is not centrally symmetric, for nondegenerate varieties with odd $\MV(\Delta_1,\dots,\Delta_k,\Delta_1,\dots,\Delta_k)$, and for smooth towers of curve fibrations. We determine the equality case for curves and towers, and prove that $k$-planes…

arxiv:2611.20832.title: Creation Sequences for Numerical Semigroups and Exact Counts of Semigroup Partitions
arxiv:2611.20832.summary: A numerical semigroup is a subset of the non-negative integers that contains $0$, is closed under addition and has finite complement. A threshold graph is built by adding vertices one at a time, each new vertex being isolated or dominating, and the record of these choices is its \emph{creation sequence}. Reading the creation sequence as a lattice path gives an integer partition and, through the Keith--Nath correspondence, a numerical set in which the dominating vertices are the elements and the isolated vertices are the gaps.

arxiv:2611.20843.title: Characterization of Cubic Graphs with Exactly Two Lonely Edges
arxiv:2611.20843.summary: Perfect matchings are fundamental to understanding structural connectivity in cubic graphs, with "lonely edges" (edges in exactly one perfect matching) forming a critical underexplored class. Goedgebeur et al. (J.

arxiv:2611.20847.title: The G\"ottsche conjecture and the G\"ottsche--Yau--Zaslow formula
arxiv:2611.20847.summary: The aim of these notes is to give an account, intended for the non-specialist, of the two proofs of the G\"ottsche conjecture given, respectively, first by Tzeng, and shortly after by Kool, Shende and Thomas. Given a smooth, complex, projective surface $S$ and a positive integer $\delta$, the G\"ottsche conjecture predicts that if $L$ is a sufficiently positive line bundle on $S$, then the number of $\delta$-nodal curves in a general $\delta$-dimensional linear subsystem $\Lambda\subset |L|$ is given by a universal polynomial of degree $\delta$ in the four numbers $L^2$, $L K_S$, $K_S^2$, and $c_2(S)$. Besides, the G\"ottsche--Yau--Zaslow formula expresses the generating function of the…

arxiv:2611.20862.title: Unconditionally Positive Nonstandard Finite Difference Schemes for $p$-Laplacian Reaction--Diffusion Equations
arxiv:2611.20862.summary: We propose a conservative, semi-implicit nonstandard finite difference scheme for the reaction--diffusion equation $u_t=\lambda(|u_x|^{p-2}u_x)_x+f(u)$, $p>1$, where, as is customary, the $p$-Laplacian is regularized by a parameter $\eps>0$. The scheme combines a denominator function, a lagged diffusion coefficient, and a nonlocal treatment of the loss part of the reaction. For every time step and mesh size we prove that the scheme is well posed and positive, that it preserves an invariant region $[0,K]$ whenever the reaction admits one, and that it reproduces every constant equilibrium exactly.
arxiv:2611.20862.authors: Achraf Zinihi, Matthias Ehrhardt, Moulay Rchid Sidi Ammi

arxiv:2611.20923.title: Linear Algebra over Bands
arxiv:2611.20923.summary: We introduce Eckmann-Hilton operators on bands, which allow for a suite of matroidal constructions, in particular, matroid unions and matroid stable intersections. This enables the construction of general linear monoids over bands. Geometrically, we show that matroid stable intersection extends the transverse intersection of linear spaces over fields and the stable intersection of tropical linear spaces, lending new insight into intersection theory on bands.

arxiv:2611.20947.title: List colouring of circular-arc graphs
arxiv:2611.20947.summary: A circular-arc graph takes a set of nonempty closed arcs on a circle as its vertex set, and two vertices are adjacent when their corresponding arcs intersect on the circle. We show the chromatic number of any circular-arc graph equals its list chromatic number. Our methodology is an application of Schauz's coefficient formula within the Alon-Tarsi and Combinatorial Nullstellensatz framework.

arxiv:2611.20960.title: Triples in matroid circuits
arxiv:2611.20960.summary: We prove that, if $X$ is a four-element independent set in a vertically $5$-connected representable matroid $M$, then either there is a circuit of $M$ that contains at least three elements of $X$, or there is a representation $A$ of $M$ such that each column of $A$ has at most two non-zero elements and each of the columns indexed by $X$ has exactly one non-zero element. We also prove a version of this result without the connectivity assumptions.
arxiv:2611.20960.authors: Jim Geelen, Bert Gerards, Geoff Whittle

arxiv:2611.20962.title: Discriminants and resultants of orthogonal polynomials
arxiv:2611.20962.summary: The concept of a linked pair of two sequences of polynomials, one of which is orthogonal, is introduced. Such a pair always has a resultant that factors. Two methods for producing such linked pairs are given: one for general orthogonal polynomials and the other for any polynomial in the Askey scheme.
arxiv:2611.20962.authors: Mourad E. H. Ismail, Jihyeug Jang, Jang Soo Kim, Dennis Stanton

arxiv:2611.20966.title: Finite-order exponential mixing does not imply the central limit theorem for unique equilibrium states
arxiv:2611.20966.summary: Let $M$ be a compact smooth manifold of dimension at least three, $\varphi:M\to\mathbb R$ be continuous, and $R\ge2$ be an integer. We construct a $\mathcal C^\infty$ diffeomorphism $T:M\to M$ and an observable $f\in\mathcal C^\infty(M,\mathbb R)$ such that $(T,\varphi)$ has a unique equilibrium state $\mu$ and $\mu(f)=0$. The system $(T,\mu)$ is exponentially mixing of order $R$ but not of order $R+1$ for H\"older observables, and $n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=0}^{n-1}f\circ T^i$ does not satisfy the central limit theorem.

arxiv:2611.20974.title: Projective planes with abelian collineation groups of type (F) are Desarguesian
arxiv:2611.20974.summary: We use prime ideal factorization and residue class fields of cyclotomic integer rings to prove that every abelian direct product difference set is classical. This implies that every projective plane of order $n$ with an abelian collineation group of order $n(n-1)$ is Desarguesian, proving a conjecture of Jungnickel and de Resmini. As a consequence, we obtain the classification of circular Costas maps and of Costas polynomials conjectured by Muratovic-Ribic, Pott, Thomson and Wang and by Torres and Rubio.

arxiv:2611.21008.title: The Odd Shift is not sofic in dimensions $d \ge 3$
arxiv:2611.21008.summary: In this paper, we prove that the Odd Shift $S_{odd}$ is not sofic for dimensions $d \ge 3$. Our proof uses lower bounds from communication complexity, specifically the result of Raz and Spieker on the nondeterministic communication complexity for the connectivity problem. We also prove that $S_{odd}$ is not sofic for dimension $d=2$ under the assumption we call Mute Ocean.

arxiv:2611.21010.title: The Singular LeBrun Transform: Complex Conformal and Contact Geometry
arxiv:2611.21010.summary: A holomorphic conformal structure is rigid in the presence of rational curves: a complex conformal manifold that is not conformally flat contains no immersed rational null geodesic. So a natural compactification of such a manifold, on which its null geodesics close up, must degenerate along the boundary. We study this phenomenon for the complex conformal manifold that LeBrun attached to a complex contact manifold $Z$ in inverting Salamon's twistor construction: the space $M_{\mathbb{C}}$ of balanced conics of $Z$ transverse to the contact distribution, with its holomorphic Riemannian metric of holonomy contained in $\mathrm{Sp}(n,\mathbb{C})\mathrm{Sp}(1,\mathbb{C})$.

arxiv:2611.21071.title: Centralizers in Catalan Monoids
arxiv:2611.21071.summary: Fix a chain $X_n=\{1<\cdots<n\}$, where $n$ is a positive integer. The Catalan monoid $\mathcal{C}_n$ consists of all decreasing and order-preserving transformations of $X_n$, with function composition as the operation. For $\beta\in\mathcal{C}_n$, its centralizer is $C(\beta)=\{\alpha\in\mathcal{C}_n:\alpha\beta=\beta\alpha\}$.

arxiv:2611.21074.title: Gorenstein toric Fano $d$-varieties have Picard ranks at most $2d$
arxiv:2611.21074.summary: We show that the Picard rank of $d$-dimensional Gorenstein toric Fano varieties is at most $2d$. This generalizes Batyrev's conjecture of Picard ranks for smooth toric Fano varieties, which was proved by Casagrande for all $\mathbb{Q}$-factorial Gorenstein toric Fano varieties. The convex-geometric proof is a generalization of Casagrande's proof and Eikelberg's theory of non-$\mathbb{Q}$-factorial toric Picard groups, with key ideas from work of Debarre, {\O}bro, Fujita and the first author.

arxiv:2611.21108.title: Equivariant geometry of quadrics blown-up along a twisted quartic
arxiv:2611.21108.summary: We prove that $G$-Fano threefolds which are given by the blow-up of a smooth quadric along a twisted quartic curve are $G$-birationally superrigid if and only if $G$ is isomorphic to $\mathfrak{A}_5\times\mathbb{Z}_2$. We also prove that the action of $G$ is linearisable if and only if $G$ does not contain a subgroup isomorphic to $\mathbb{Z}_2^3$.

arxiv:2611.21118.title: Intersection theory and Chern classes on normal varieties II
arxiv:2611.21118.summary: We prove a uniform bound linear in the rank for the local correction terms in the Riemann--Roch formula for reflexive sheaves on normal surfaces over algebraically closed fields of arbitrary characteristic. We also establish the usual tensor and symmetric-power formulas for second Chern characters and prove Wahl's asymptotic Riemann--Roch conjecture and its higher-rank generalization. These results yield second Chern classes of reflexive sheaves on arbitrary normal projective varieties, compatible with pullback by finite surjective morphisms.

arxiv:2611.21121.title: N\'eron Functions on Jacobians of Odd-Degree Hyperelliptic Curves
arxiv:2611.21121.summary: We express N\'eron functions on Jacobians of odd-degree hyperelliptic curves of arbitrary genus in terms of admissible pairings, using the pullback of the theta divisor via a generalized Abel--Jacobi morphism. Over non-archimedean local fields, we relate N\'eron functions to local N\'eron pairings on the curve and, moreover, deduce a comparison between unramified $p$-adic N\'eron functions and unramified local Coleman--Gross height functions. Furthermore, we decompose the N\'eron function into an intersection term $I$ and a Green function term $T$, and compute $T$ for specific semistable reduction types.

arxiv:2611.21133.title: Polynomial growth and dynamic asymptotic dimension
arxiv:2611.21133.summary: We show that principal ample groupoids with local polynomial growth of degree at most $s$ have dynamic asymptotic dimension at most $\lfloor s\rfloor$. As a consequence, $\sigma$-compact principal ample groupoids with local polynomial growth have slow dynamic asymptotic dimension growth.

arxiv:2611.21153.title: Orbifold Morse Handles I. Morse Indices and Isomorphism Classes of Ordered Handles
arxiv:2611.21153.summary: We classify the Morse indices and ordered handles arising from nondegenerate critical points of smooth functions on effective orientable four-dimensional orbifolds. Let $\rho\colon G\to\mathrm{SO}(4)$ be a faithful representation of a finite group. Let $V\subset\mathbb R^4$ be the negative eigenspace of a nondegenerate Hessian that is invariant under $\rho(G)$.

arxiv:2611.21173.title: Elliptic Gromov-Witten Invariants of Instanton Moduli
arxiv:2611.21173.summary: We calculate the genus $1$ Gromov-Witten invariants with one tautological divisor insertion of the moduli space $\mathcal{M}(r,n)$ of rank-$r$, $c_2=n$ torsion-free sheaves on $\mathbb{P}^2$ framed along the infinity divisor. As rational functions of the framing parameters, we determine the polar parts of these invariants by exploring the equivariant geometry of the Gieseker-Uhlenbeck map $\mathcal{M}(r,n)\to\mathcal{M}_0(r,n)$. We determine the polynomial part of these invariants by relating their large framing limits to the results \cite{ILPT} for the rank $1$ case, namely $\mathrm{Hilb}^n(\mathbb{C}^2)$.

arxiv:2611.21187.title: A Polynomial Time Algorithm for Finding a Minimum 5-Partition of a Submodular Function
arxiv:2611.21187.summary: Given a real-valued submodular function on a finite ground set, the minimum $k$-partition problem asks for a partition into $k$ nonempty parts minimizing the sum of their function values. We give a polynomial-time algorithm for $k=5$. The idea follows directly from the previous $k=4$ result, where there is precisely one obstruction for generalizing it to $k=5$.
arxiv:2611.21187.authors: Yuhao Liu, Ke Shi, Chao Xu

arxiv:2611.21188.title: No complete set of mutually unbiased bases in dimension ten contains the Fourier pair or three product bases
arxiv:2611.21188.summary: With computer-assisted proofs that $\mathbb{C}^6$ admits at most three mutually unbiased bases (MUBs) now available, $\mathbb{C}^{10}$ is the smallest dimension in which it is unknown whether a complete set of $d+1=11$ MUBs exists; only three MUBs are known. We prove that every triple of mutually unbiased product bases of $\mathbb{C}^2\otimes\mathbb{C}^5$ is strongly unextendible: no vector is unbiased to all three bases. Consequently no set of four MUBs in dimension ten, and in particular no complete set, contains three product bases.
arxiv:2611.21188.authors: Jinze Yang, Yile Liu, Yangyang Li, Xiu-Hao Deng

arxiv:2611.21191.title: Symmetric Chemical Reaction Networks: Realizations and Steady States
arxiv:2611.21191.summary: We investigate symmetric chemical reaction networks and their steady states. From classical equivariant dynamical systems and network theory it is known that the mass- action ODE of any symmetric chemical reaction network is equivariant. For symmetries that permute the species, we prove that any equivariant mass-action ODE is realized by a symmetric chemical reaction network and construct a sparsest such realization.
arxiv:2611.21191.authors: Sebastian Debus, Kurt Klement Gottwald, Nils Gubela

arxiv:2611.21192.title: Borel--Serre Callias Classes and Cuspidal Localization
arxiv:2611.21192.summary: We construct equivariant Callias classes on the Borel--Serre space of a Hilbert modular group and prove a Kasparov product formula. For torsion-free normal congruence subgroups and twists by powers $m_j\geq2$ of the holomorphic cotangent line bundles, we identify the image of the maximal higher index in the representation ring of the finite quotient with the equivariant index of the cuspidal Dolbeault operator on total forms. The comparison uses a Fredholm homotopy that separates an invertible noncuspidal block.

arxiv:2611.21197.title: Counterexamples to Green's Conjecture via E_6-covers
arxiv:2611.21197.summary: We show that curves of genus 10 which are W(E_6)-covers of the projective line provide counterexamples to Green's Conjecture on syzygies of canonical curves. This leads to a 9-dimensional family of explicit counterexamples to Green's Conjecture. We also show that the same curves provide counterexamples to the Green-Lazarsfeld Secant Conjecture.
arxiv:2611.21197.authors: Marian Aprodu, Gavril Farkas, Jinhyung Park

arxiv:2611.21205.title: Cyclic homology of Sheaf Categories
arxiv:2611.21205.summary: In this note, we explain the circle action on the Hochschild homology of categories of sheaves and their admissible subcategories in terms of the six-functor formalism using factorization homology, including (quasi-)coherent sheaves on derived stacks, sheaves on manifolds with prescribed microsupports, and Tamarkin categories with prescribed microsupports.
