We also explain the Gysin sequence for $C_\ell$ and $S^1$-(co)invariants and the K\"unneth sequence for $S^1$-(co)invariants of the Hochschild homology relative to any complex-oriented symmetric monoidal category.

arxiv:2611.21210.title: Full-Cover and Non-Overlapping Uni-domination in Graphs: Bounds and Complexity
arxiv:2611.21210.summary: A vertex is uni-dominated by a set $S \subseteq V(G)$ if exactly one vertex of $S$ lies in its closed neighborhood, and the uni-domination number $\mathrm{ud}^*(G)$ is the largest number of vertices a single set can uni-dominate. The graphs admitting an efficient dominating set are those with $\mathrm{ud}^*(G) = n$. Hedetniemi and Rall asked for the largest constant $c$ with $\mathrm{ud}^*(T) \geq c \cdot n$ for every tree $T$ of order $n$.
arxiv:2611.21210.authors: Florent Foucaud, Yan Gerard, Christian Laforest, Le Vu Pham

arxiv:2611.21212.title: Explicit cohomological transfer for Morita equivalent Lie groupoids
arxiv:2611.21212.summary: It is well known that Morita equivalent Lie groupoids have isomorphic differentiable cohomology. At the cochain level, however, explicitly transporting a cocycle from one groupoid to a Morita equivalent one is less straightforward. We provide explicit formulas for such cohomological transfers in arbitrary degree.

arxiv:2611.21213.title: A necessary regularity condition for finite-time stopping of the string with dry friction
arxiv:2611.21213.summary: We consider the one-dimensional wave equation with dry (Coulomb) friction, u\_{tt} -u\_{xx} + Sgn(u\_t )= 0, with Dirichlet boundary conditions. Whether every finite-energy solution stops in finite time has been open since 1978. We show that stopping in finite time is impossible whenever the initial slope or the initial velocity is unbounded: the space W 1,$\infty$ x L $\infty$ for (u, u t ) is invariant under the flow in both time directions, while stopped states are Lipschitz.

arxiv:2611.21220.title: Capacities from the Chiu-Tamarkin complex II: Product formula and toric domains
arxiv:2611.21220.summary: In this article, we continue our study of equivariant symplectic capacities of open sets in a cotangent bundle defined via the Chiu-Tamarkin complex constructed from the microlocal theory of sheaves. The paper consists of two parts: 1) We develop the theory of $S^1$-equivariant Chiu-Tamarkin complex over complex-oriented ring spectra. 2) Applications of the theory to symplectic capacities: We show that a product formula for the capacities, whose Ekeland-Hofer capacities version is folklore since 1988, is not true via an (uncountable family of) counterexample(s). The counterexample (family) is the product of a concave toric domain of dimension $6$ ($2n\geq 6$) and a $2$-dimensional disk.

arxiv:2611.21256.title: Odd faces as a parameter for maximum independent set in embedded graphs
arxiv:2611.21256.summary: We give a polynomial-time algorithm for finding a maximum weight independent set in a graph embedded in a surface of bounded genus and with a bounded number of vertex-disjoint odd faces. In particular, we obtain an algorithm for graphs with an even-faced embedding in a torus and for planar graphs with a bounded number of odd faces, answering a question of Thomass\'e (2018) and a question of Choi, Gorsky, Kim, McFarland, and Wiederrecht (2025) respectively. We reduce the original problem to finding a minimum cost non-negative integer circulation with homology constraints in the dual of a certain double cover of the original graph.
arxiv:2611.21256.authors: Samuel Fiorini, Stefan Kober, Caleb McFarland

arxiv:2611.21297.title: Stability manifolds and resolutions of singularities
arxiv:2611.21297.summary: In this article, we study descent and lifting of Bridgeland stability conditions along Verdier quotients. We give a torsion-pair criterion for lifting every stability condition on the quotient to a weak stability condition with a prescribed heart on the null category. When this criterion holds for every heart on the null category, the space of weak stability conditions with this massless subcategory is homeomorphic to the product of the stability space of the quotient and the discrete set of hearts of bounded $t$-structures on the null category.

arxiv:2611.21333.title: Non-factorisable Yangian Lax matrices through oscillators
arxiv:2611.21333.summary: We construct oscillator realisations of Yangian Lax operators in type $A$, with particular interest in non-factorisable operators associated with prime snake modules. Our construction applies to finite-dimensional skew representations of $Y(\mathfrak{gl}_n)$. We prove that these representations are generated by the tensor vacuum in suitably ordered tensor products of oscillator representations.

arxiv:2611.21345.title: Arithmetic Universality and Integer Decomposition in Disjunctions of Three Staircase Simplices
arxiv:2611.21345.summary: The staircase simplices $\{x\in[0,1]^d:x_{\sigma(1)}\le\cdots\le x_{\sigma(d)}\}$, $\sigma\in S_d\,$, are the $d!$ unimodular cells of the staircase triangulation of the unit cube. The disjunctive hull (Cayley polytope) of a selection $P_0, \ldots, P_n$ of them has the integer decomposition property (IDP) if, for all integers $\lambda_i\ge0$, every lattice point of $\sum_i\lambda_i P_i$ is a sum of vertices, $\lambda_i$ of them from $P_i$. For two simplices, IDP always holds.

arxiv:2611.21385.title: \(A_{\alpha}\)-Wronskian Vertices of Paths and Controllability of Path-Rooted Products
arxiv:2611.21385.summary: For a graph \(G\) with adjacency and degree matrices \(A(G)\) and \(D(G)\), set \(A_{\alpha}(G)=\alpha D(G)+(1-\alpha)A(G)\) for \(0\leq\alpha<1\). Using Chebyshev polynomials and a theorem of Conway and Jones, we classify the \(A_{\alpha}\)-Wronskian vertices of every path \(P_n\), \(n\geq2\) (equivalently, the standard basis vectors cyclic for \(A_{\alpha}(P_n)\)). The central vertex of an odd-order path is never Wronskian; for every other vertex, we determine an explicit finite set of algebraic exceptional parameters.

arxiv:2611.21416.title: Polynomial bounds for quasiplanar graphs
arxiv:2611.21416.summary: A graph $G$ is $k$-quasiplanar if it can be drawn in the plane without $k$ pairwise crossing edges. It was a longstanding conjecture that $n$-vertex $k$-quasiplanar graphs have $O_k(n)$ edges. This was recently resolved by Sadhu and, independently, by Pach, Tardos, and Zeng, based on a theorem in topology proven by Beeker and Lazarovich.
arxiv:2611.21416.authors: Aleksa Milojevi\'c, Patryk Morawski, Benny Sudakov, Istvan Tomon

arxiv:2611.21418.title: Sumsets modulo ideals: Baire category and descriptive complexity
arxiv:2611.21418.summary: Given an ideal $\mathcal I$ on the nonnegative integers, we study the family $\Sigma(\mathcal I)$ of all sets for which every $\mathcal{I}$-small modification is not a nontrivial sumset $A+B$. We prove that $\Sigma(\mathcal I)$ is comeager whenever $\mathcal{I}$ is an Erd\H{o}s--Ulam ideal generated by a nonincreasing sequence of positive weights. This answers an open question for the ideal $\mathcal{Z}$ of asymptotic density zero sets in [Proc.

arxiv:2611.21420.title: Siphon faces in slow-fast mass-action networks
arxiv:2611.21420.summary: When the species of a siphon in a mass-action network, however many, are fast and their invariant face loses transverse stability along the slow flow, trajectories follow the face past this loss before leaving it. We study three consequences. (i) If the transverse Metzler linearisation is irreducible, the entry-exit relation with its Perron root gives the exit.

arxiv:2611.21435.title: Perfect 3-colorings of the generalized Petersen graphs GP(n,2)
arxiv:2611.21435.summary: We enumerate the parameter matrices of all perfect 3-colorings of the generalized Petersen graphs GP(n,2), n >= 5. We show that there are only five matrices that can be the parameter matrix of such a coloring. Two of them occur if and only if 5 | n, two occur if and only if 3 | n, and the remaining one occurs if and only if 10 | n.

arxiv:2611.21437.title: P = W conjectures for varieties with nilpotent fundamental group
arxiv:2611.21437.summary: We prove the cohomological and the geometric $P=W$ conjectures for the moduli spaces of $G$-Higgs bundles and $G$-local systems on any smooth complex projective variety $X$ with nilpotent fundamental group, and any connected complex reductive group $G$. To the best of our knowledge, our results provide the first instances of $P=W$ conjectures beyond curves and abelian varieties. Finally, we provide examples of our theorem for classical groups: as a byproduct of this analysis we investigate when symplectic resolutions of the corresponding character varieties exist.
arxiv:2611.21437.authors: Barbara Bolognese, Camilla Felisetti, Andreas Gross, Alex K\"uronya, GyeongHyeon Nam, Martin Ulirsch

arxiv:2611.21451.title: Counting Matrices of Prescribed Jordan Type in Incidence Algebras
arxiv:2611.21451.summary: We count nilpotent matrices in the incidence algebra of a finite poset over a finite field that belong to a prescribed conjugacy class for the adjoint action of the general linear group. We prove that these counts depend only on the comparability graph of the poset. We introduce shuffle-prefix posets, a class containing all finite interval orders, and give explicit formulas for their nilpotent Jordan counts.
arxiv:2611.21451.authors: Keivan Mallahi-Karai, Samrith Ram, Hadi Salmasian

arxiv:2611.21484.title: Ice and mirrors
arxiv:2611.21484.summary: Given a mirror pair of smooth affine principal upper cluster varieties admitting reddening sequences, we show that homological mirror symmetry for principal cluster varieties -- assumed compatible with certain cluster structures -- descends under freezing. This allows us to induct on the following class. A skew-symmetrizable matrix is peelable if, by mutations and removing sinks or sources, it can be reduced to the empty matrix; it is sub-peelable if it is a principal submatrix of a peelable matrix.

arxiv:2611.21492.title: Expansion in powers of simple groups of Lie type
arxiv:2611.21492.summary: We prove an expansion theorem for direct powers of all nonabelian finite simple groups $G$ other than the alternating groups and the Suzuki groups ${}^2B_2(q)$. If $G^m$ is generated by $d\ge2$ elements, then $G^m$ has a symmetric generating multiset of at most $Cd$ elements and normalized spectral gap at least $C^{-1}d^{-\log_2 3}$, for an absolute constant $C>0$. In particular, this answers a question of Sabatini on $\mathrm{PSL}_2(\mathbb{F}_p)^p$.

arxiv:2611.21499.title: Cantor Julia sets of positive area in non-autonomous dynamics
arxiv:2611.21499.summary: For every $a>0$, we prove the existence of a sequence of polynomials with rational coefficients whose non-autonomous iteration produces a Julia set of planar area $a$. We also construct a sequence of rational maps with rational coefficients whose Julia set has the same prescribed area. No individual map in this rational sequence is M\"obius-conjugate to a polynomial, and no choice of M\"obius coordinates at successive phases turns it into a polynomial sequence.

arxiv:2611.21506.title: Generic splitting types and Terao's conjecture for seventeen and eighteen lines
arxiv:2611.21506.summary: We prove that the generic splitting type of the logarithmic bundle of an arrangement of at most eighteen lines in the complex projective plane is determined by the intersection lattice. In particular, Terao's freeness conjecture holds for seventeen and eighteen lines. For any number of lines, it holds for free arrangements whose smaller exponent is at most eight.

arxiv:2611.21516.title: Crossing Numbers of Complete Graphs: the independent odd crossing number
arxiv:2611.21516.summary: We show that the Harary--Hill bound on the crossing number of complete graphs as well as the Zarankiewwicz bound on the crossing number of complete bipartite graphs, both recently established by OpenAI, also hold for the independent odd crossing number. This implies that the same bounds hold for several other crossing number variants such as the (independent) algebraic crossing number and the (independent) pair crossing number.

arxiv:2611.21540.title: The Sum of Leaf Weights in the Minimum Spanning Tree of the Complete Graph
arxiv:2611.21540.summary: Let $G_n$ be a random weighted complete graph on $n$ vertices, where edges have i.i.d. $\text{Unif}(0,1)$ weights. Let $T_n$ be the Minimum Spanning Tree (MST) of $G_n$.
arxiv:2611.21540.authors: Julia Gaudio, Phawin Prongpaophan, Mikl\'os Z. R\'acz

arxiv:2611.21555.title: Regular subgroups of wreath products and Cayley Cartesian products
arxiv:2611.21555.summary: The Cartesian product of Cayley graphs is again a Cayley graph. For connected graphs, the converse question reduces to Cartesian powers of Cartesian-prime graphs, and consequently to the study of regular subgroups of wreath products in the product action. We prove that, for a transitive permutation group $G$ of degree $2p$ or $4p$, where $p$ is prime, $G\wr S_2$ contains a regular subgroup if and only if $G$ does, and construct counterexamples of degree $8p$ for every prime $p\equiv3\pmod4$.
arxiv:2611.21555.authors: Zhaochen Ding, Ted Dobson, Ademir Hujdurovi\'{c}, Yakun Wang

arxiv:2611.21556.title: Random compositions of quasiperiodic cocycles
arxiv:2611.21556.summary: We consider the multiplicative process given by random compositions of linear cocycles over toral translations. Under appropriate generic assumptions, we establish effective large deviations estimates as well as the H\"older continuity of the associated Lyapunov exponent of the process. These properties in particular show the regularizing effect of randomness on quasiperiodic dynamics.
arxiv:2611.21556.authors: Ao Cai, Pedro Duarte, Silvius Klein

arxiv:2611.21567.title: Peak state transfer in trees and the cost of distance
arxiv:2611.21567.summary: There is peak state transfer between vertices $u$ and $v$ in a graph $G$ if there exists a time $t$ for which $|(\mathrm{e}^{\mathrm i t M})_{u,v}|$ saturates the triangle inequality imposed by its spectral decomposition and $M$ is either the adjacency or Laplacian matrix. We show that peak state transfer at distance $d$ requires $\frac{d^3}{24}(1 + o(1))$ edges in the adjacency case, $\Omega(d^2)$ edges in the Laplacian case, and that the leading coefficient in the former is tight. We find a family of graphs with Laplacian peak state transfer at distance $d$ and $\Theta(d^5)$ edges, showing that peak state transfer is achievable in a polynomial graph size.

arxiv:2611.21569.title: Heavy-Light Wall Crossings and Motivic Asymptotics of Moduli Spaces of Curves. Part II: Tameness of Motivic Measures
arxiv:2611.21569.summary: This paper is concerned with the study of the fixed-genus asymptotics of motivic measures of moduli spaces of stable pointed curves and their minimal all-light Hassett compactifications as the number of markings tends to infinity. A motivic wall-crossing argument gives a universal change of variables between the two generating series, depending only on the value of the Lefschetz class. For an arbitrary motivic measure, we use stabilization graphs and support patterns to express the all-light series in terms of universal chain factors and finite residual quotient families.

arxiv:2611.21574.title: Counterexamples to Grad's conjecture of any knot type
arxiv:2611.21574.summary: We construct smooth magnetohydrostatic counterexamples to Grad's conjecture in toroidal domains of arbitrary knot type. The magnetic field is nonvanishing, and nested pressure tori fill the domain outside a nondegenerate magnetic axis. The equilibria have trivial Euclidean symmetry group and occur in smooth families of inequivalent configurations.
arxiv:2611.21574.authors: Alberto Enciso, Javier Pe\~nafiel-Tom\'as, Daniel Peralta-Salas

arxiv:2611.21576.title: Quantum Cohomology and irrationality of K\"uchle fourfolds
arxiv:2611.21576.summary: We prove that very general K\"uchle fourfolds of types (c1), (c6), (b8), and (b11) are irrational. The key ingredients are a new rationality criterion, based on the theory of Hodge atoms due to Katzarkov--Kontsevich--Pantev--Yu and its integral extension by Gu\'er\'e, and a computation of the action of quantum multiplication on the vanishing cohomology of these fourfolds, which uses a version of the Quantum Lefschetz Hyperplane Principle. Quantum multiplication acts as a scalar on the vanishing cohomology, and we give an enumerative interpretation of this scalar.

arxiv:2611.21599.title: Hyperlyve: Parallelized Enumeration and Exact Lyapunov Stability Certification for Deep ReLU Networks
arxiv:2611.21599.summary: We introduce Hyperlyve (Hyperplane Partitioned Lyapunov Verification and Enumeration), a framework for proving the asymptotic stability of nonlinear dynamical systems, including those with neural network controllers. Hyperlyve learns and formally certifies continuous piecewise-affine (CPA) neural Lyapunov functions within a counterexample-guided inductive synthesis (CEGIS) loop. Hyperlyve's key innovation is a parallel algorithm that enumerates the hyperplane arrangement formed by the ReLU activations of deep networks and certifies that Lyapunov conditions hold within each polyhedral region.
arxiv:2611.21599.authors: Brian Yarbrough, Jesse Wayment, Jingbo Wang, Philip E. Par\'{e}, Shreyas Sundaram

arxiv:2611.21654.title: Quantum $K$-theoretic Whitney relation for Lagrangian Grassmannian
arxiv:2611.21654.summary: We give a quantum $K$-theoretic analogue of the Whitney relation for the torus-equivariant $K$-ring of the Lagrangian Grassmannian. As a consequence, we give a presentation of the torus-equivariant quantum $K$-ring of the Lagrangian Grassmannian. The strategy for obtaining such relations is to use the quantum $K$-theoretic Whitney relation for the full-flag manifold in type $C$ established by the author and Kato's pushforward map from the quantum $K$-ring of the full-flag manifold to that of the partial flag manifold.

arxiv:2611.21656.title: Cycles of Arbitrary Period in Multidimensional Heterogeneous Hegselmann-Krause Dynamics
arxiv:2611.21656.summary: We study periodic behavior in heterogeneous Hegselmann-Krause opinion dynamics with multidimensional opinions and norm-defined confidence neighborhoods. We prove that, for every dimension $d\ge3$, every $\ell_q$ norm with $q\in[1,\infty]\setminus\{2\}$, and every integer $m\ge2$, a system of five agents admits a periodic trajectory of minimal period $m$; moreover, different periods can coexist for fixed confidence radii. Four agents remain stationary, while the fifth moves along a line segment contained in their convex hull.

arxiv:2611.21657.title: Counting formulas and refined generating functions for inversion-sequence Classes 152 and 207
arxiv:2611.21657.summary: For the two Class 152 pattern sets, we prove that the common number of inversion sequences of length \(n\geq 1\) is \(a_n=1+\sum_{j=1}^{n-1}\binom{2j}{j}\). The Class 152 proof uses first-descent and last-zero decompositions, with weighted Dyck paths evaluating the resulting generating functions. For Class 207, we prove equality of the three total-count series and give their common generating function as an explicit Lambert-series expression after the substitution \(z=q/(1+q)^2\).
arxiv:2611.21657.authors: Haobo Ma, Toufik Mansour, Wenlin Zhang

arxiv:2611.21664.title: Co-edge-regular graphs with two $\lambda$-values and four distinct eigenvalues
arxiv:2611.21664.summary: A connected $k$-regular graph $G$ on $n$ vertices is co-edge-regular if any two distinct non-adjacent vertices have the same number of common neighbors. For adjacent vertices $u$ and $v$, let $\lambda(u,v)=|N(u)\cap N(v)|$. Ge and Koolen asked whether the theorem of Neumaier on strongly regular graphs with fixed smallest eigenvalue extends to co-edge-regular graphs with exactly four distinct eigenvalues in which $\lambda(u,v)$ takes exactly two values over the edges $uv$.

arxiv:2611.21665.title: A Proof of the Achlioptas-Friedgut Convergence Conjecture
arxiv:2611.21665.summary: For every fixed integer $q\ge3$, we show that the $q$-colourability transition in a sparse random graph takes place at a limiting edge density, thus proving the Achlioptas-Friedgut convergence conjecture. The proof adapts the argument we recently introduced to settle the satisfiability conjecture.

arxiv:2611.21670.title: Resistance-regular graphs need not be regular
arxiv:2611.21670.summary: A connected graph is resistance-regular if the sum of the effective resistances from a vertex to all other vertices does not depend on the vertex, or equivalently if the Moore-Penrose inverse of its Laplacian has constant diagonal. Walk-regular graphs have this property, and Zhou, Wang and Bu asked in 2016 whether every resistance-regular graph is regular, a question that also arises in the study of graphs with constant resistance curvature. We answer this question in the negative and examine both what resistance-regularity forces and how far from regular such graphs can be.
arxiv:2611.21670.authors: Murad ul Islam Khan, Ghulam Haidar

arxiv:2611.21673.title: Gallai's path decomposition conjecture for $K_5$-minor-free graphs
arxiv:2611.21673.summary: Gallai conjectured that the edges of every connected graph on $n$ vertices can be partitioned into at most $\ceil{n/2}$ paths. We prove that every connected $K_5$-minor-free graph other than $K_3$ and $K_5-e$ admits such a partition into at most $\floor{n/2}$ paths. The two exceptions require $\ceil{n/2}$ paths.
arxiv:2611.21673.authors: Junhao Zhang, Qinghai Liu, Yanmei Hong

arxiv:2611.21692.title: The injectivity of the Kudla--Millson lift on unitary Shimura varieties
arxiv:2611.21692.summary: We prove the injectivity of the Kudla--Millson lift on unitary Shimura varieties over imaginary quadratic fields under some lattice hypotheses. We express integrals of the lift over special cycles as special values of Dirichlet series and deduce injectivity by separating the Fourier coefficients of the cusp forms. We also establish a converse theorem for Borcherds products on $\mathrm{U}(n,1)$.

arxiv:2611.21699.title: The system of length sets of transfer Krull monoids over $C_3 \oplus C_3 \oplus C_3$
arxiv:2611.21699.summary: Let $H$ be a Krull monoid with class group $G$ and suppose that each class contains a prime divisor. There are precisely nine groups (up to isomorphism) for which the set of distances of $H$ is contained in $\{1, 2\}$. For all these groups, except for $C_3 \oplus C_3 \oplus C_3$, the system of length sets has been written down explicitly.
arxiv:2611.21699.authors: Alfred Geroldinger, Benjamin Hackl, Qinghai Zhong

arxiv:2611.21703.title: Remarks on Fourier--Mukai invariances
arxiv:2611.21703.summary: This note proves that smoothness and Gorensteinness are Fourier--Mukai invariants for proper flat families of Noetherian algebraic spaces. Moreover, a kernel realizing such a partnership is perfect if, and only if, the families are smooth.

arxiv:2611.21796.title: Bounded functions on the character variety for quadratic extensions of $\mathbb{Q}_p$
arxiv:2611.21796.summary: For any finite extension $L$ of $\mathbb{Q}_p$, Schneider--Teitelbaum defined and studied the character variety in $p$-adic Fourier theory. It is a rigid analytic curve over $L$ that parameterizes the set of locally $L$-analytic characters of $o_L$. It is conjectured that all bounded functions on the character variety of Schneider--Teitelbaum come from $p$-adic measures.
arxiv:2611.21796.authors: Laurent Berger, Johannes Sprang, Rustam Steingart

arxiv:2611.21818.title: Hill's Lunar Equation as a Leaf: Riccati Reduction and Frobenius Theory for Second-Order PDEs
arxiv:2611.21818.summary: The equations of Hill and Adams for the lunar perigee and node, Mathieu's equation and Lam\'e's equation arise as leafwise restrictions of one class of linear partial differential equations, the \emph{square-type foliated equations} $L^2u+A\,Lu+B\,u=0$, where $L$ is an analytic vector field and $A,B$ are analytic functions. Such an equation has a regular singularity exactly when the foliation defined by $L$ is analytically linearizable. At rational saddles, where every point of the indicial conic is resonant, we obtain convergent solutions whose exponents are holomorphic functions of a first integral; their variation describes the monodromy along the leaves and decides when classical…

arxiv:2611.21853.title: Translation surfaces with logarithmically growing systole
arxiv:2611.21853.summary: We exhibit a sequence of translation surfaces $T_1, T_2,...$ with $T_g$ of genus $g$ and area $g$, such that the systole grows logarithmically with $g$. They are produced by starting with a fixed translation surface, taking covers with the same topology as those discovered by Brooks, and then adding handles by gluing along slits.

arxiv:2611.21856.title: Optimal Network Design under Node Failures
arxiv:2611.21856.summary: Networks are frequently constructed before it is determined which nodes will persist. We address the design problem in scenarios where nodes fail independently, links are costly and must be established in advance, and the benefits to surviving nodes diminish with distance. Examples include supplier, interbank, and infrastructure networks.
arxiv:2611.21856.authors: Michele Lombardi, Francesco Umutcan, Enjun Liu

arxiv:2611.21866.title: Topology of some smooth real Fano threefolds arising from blow-ups along rational curves
arxiv:2611.21866.summary: We describe the topological blow-up of a fibre of a Seifert fibration. We then apply this result to determine the diffeomorphism types of the real loci of smooth real Fano threefolds obtained by blowing up either $\mathbb{P}^3_{\mathbb{R}}$ or a smooth real quadric threefold along a smooth real rational curve. As an application, we also determine the topology of the real loci of the two real forms of the quintic del Pezzo threefold $V_5$, completing the topological classification of smooth real rational del Pezzo threefolds.

arxiv:2611.21868.title: The Conic Tverberg plus minus
arxiv:2611.21868.summary: We prove a Tverberg type theorems: Given a set $A\subset \mathbb{R}^d$ and an affine subspaces $L_1,...,L_m\subset \mathbb{R}^d$. In some conditions there is a partition $A_1, ..., A_m, B_1, ..., B_m$ of $A$ such that the sets $L_i\cup A_i\cup B_i$ for $i=1,...,m$ have common barycentre with negative masses in $B_i$ and positive masses in $A_i$. The case $B_1=...=B_m=L_1=...=L_m=\varnothing$ is Tverberg's classical theorem.

arxiv:2611.21870.title: A local-local principle for quadratic forms over semiglobal fields
arxiv:2611.21870.summary: Given a quadratic form over a semiglobal field, the set of discrete valuations on the field for which the form is anisotropic over the completion is either empty, or it contains a valuation extending that of the base field with a transcendental residue field extension. In dimension at least $3$, this gives a refinement of the local-global principle for isotropy. In dimension $2$, the result yields a description of the set of elements that are locally squares everywhere.
arxiv:2611.21870.authors: Karim Johannes Becher, David Grimm, Parul Gupta

arxiv:2611.21871.title: Obstructions to Hadamard Deformations of Fourier Matrices
arxiv:2611.21871.summary: We study deformations of the Fourier spin model commuting square in the space of commuting squares, or equivalently deformations of the matrix $\sqrt nF_n$, where $F_n$ denotes the Fourier matrix, by complex Hadamard matrices. If $n$ is neither a prime power nor twice a prime, we show that there exist unit vectors in the enveloping tangent space that cannot be realized as directions of convergence of sequential deformations. Consequently, the derivative of any differentiable Hadamard family through $\sqrt nF_n$ has rank strictly smaller than the dimension of the enveloping tangent space at $\sqrt nF_n$ (i.e., the defect of $F_n$).

arxiv:2611.21875.title: Virtually solvable groups with balanced presentations
arxiv:2611.21875.summary: We show that if $G$ is a virtually solvable group with finite Hirsch length and such that $\beta_2(G;\mathbb{Q})\leq\beta=\beta_1(G;\mathbb{Q})$ then $\beta\leq3$. This sharpens bounds on the Betti numbers of 3-manifolds which embed in $S^4$ with the fundamental groups of each complementary region virtually solvable and of finite Hirsch length.

arxiv:2611.21894.title: Permutation groups, derangements and connections
arxiv:2611.21894.summary: What is the chance that a random shuffling of a deck of cards leaves no card in its original place? More precisely, what is the chance that a random permutation has no fixed points? A permutation with no fixed points is known as a derangement.

arxiv:2611.21913.title: An upper bound on non-overlapping codes
arxiv:2611.21913.summary: Non-overlapping codes (also known as bifix-free codes or strong comma-free codes) have now been studied for over 60 years as part of information theory, with regular new applications appearing and much recent interest. Let $X$ be a binary non-overlapping code of length $n$. The paper contains a self-contained proof that \[ |X|\leq \left(\frac{5}{6e} +O(n^{-1})\right)\frac{2^n}{n} \] as $n\rightarrow\infty$.

arxiv:2611.21961.title: Forbidden Substructures Preserved by the Blob Graph Operation
arxiv:2611.21961.summary: The blob graph $G^\circ$ of a graph $G$ has a vertex for each non-empty connected vertex subset of $G$, with two distinct subsets adjacent whenever they intersect or are joined by an edge of $G$. This construction has been used in reductions from induced subgraph optimisation problems to maximum-weight independent set, where the preservation of forbidden substructures is essential. We completely characterise the graphs $H$ for which excluding $H$ from $G$ guarantees that $G^\circ$ also excludes $H$, under six containment relations.
arxiv:2611.21961.authors: Jakub P\k{a}czka, Agnieszka Prze\'zdziecka, Piotr Tyrakowski

arxiv:2611.21966.title: Supersaturation and reconfiguration diameter of independent transversals
arxiv:2611.21966.summary: Consider the collection of independent transversals of a vertex-partitioned graph of maximum degree $\Delta$. It is a classic result that when all parts have size at least $2\Delta$, the collection is nonempty. Recently, it was found that if the parts have size at least $2\Delta+1$, then every pair of independent transversals is connected, within the collection, by a sequence of one-vertex reconfigurations.
arxiv:2611.21966.authors: Wouter Cames van Batenburg, Penny Haxell, Ross J. Kang, Ronen Wdowinski

arxiv:2611.21967.title: Exotic smooth structures on nonorientable 4-manifolds
arxiv:2611.21967.summary: We construct closed nonorientable aspherical 4-manifolds with an arbitrarily large number of distinct smooth structures. This uses the reflection trick of Davis-Hayden-Huang-Ruberman-Sunukjian. Our examples become mutually diffeomorphic after either type of stabilization: taking a product with the real line, or taking a connected sum with sufficiently many copies of S^2 x S^2.

arxiv:2611.21968.title: Shifted Hankel determinants via Hankel continued fractions
arxiv:2611.21968.summary: The Hankel determinants $H_n(F)$ of a power series $F(x)$, as well as the shifted ones $H_n^{(1)}(F)$ and $H_n^{(2)}(F)$, can be read off from its Jacobi continued fraction, provided that all $H_n(F)$ are nonzero. Without any condition on $F$, the Hankel continued fraction ($H$-fraction) still yields all $H_n(F)$. We show that the $H$-fraction of $F$ also determines the shifted Hankel determinants $H_n^{(1)}(F)$, $H_n^{(2)}(F)$ and the backward shifted ones $H_n^{(-1)}(F)$, and we give explicit formulas for them.

arxiv:2611.21979.title: Laplacian Eigenvectors of Generically Weighted Graphs Have Pairwise Distinct Coordinates
arxiv:2611.21979.summary: Poignard, Pereira and Pade conjectured that, for a generic choice of the nonzero weights of a given graph, the Fiedler vector of the weighted Laplacian has pairwise distinct coordinates. We give a proof that also covers every nonconstant eigenvector. For each connected graph on n vertices we construct a nonzero homogeneous polynomial with integer coefficients in the edge weights, of degree n(n-1)(n^2-n+2)/4, which vanishes at a positive weighting exactly when the Laplacian has a repeated eigenvalue, an eigenvector with a zero coordinate, or a nonconstant eigenvector with two equal coordinates.
arxiv:2611.21979.authors: Santiago Pineda Montoya, Edisson Gallego Gonz\'alez, Jaiberth Porras Barrera, Johan Heriberto R\'ua Mu\~noz

arxiv:2611.21983.title: Large Language Models as Nonlinear Dynamical Systems: The Three Clocks of Depth, Training, and Generation
arxiv:2611.21983.summary: Language models are dynamical systems. A transformer is iterated over its layers, over the steps of its training and over the tokens it generates, and on each of these three clocks it shows behavior that nonlinear dynamics has studied for a century: fixed points, bifurcations, synchronization, chaos and noise-driven escape from potential wells. The two communities rarely meet, so this behavior is often rediscovered under new names.

arxiv:2611.21990.title: Hyperk\"ahler Periods in Families of Parabolic Higgs Bundle Moduli Spaces
arxiv:2611.21990.summary: We consider the period map on families of parabolic Higgs bundle moduli spaces with varying parabolic weights $\alpha$ and Higgs field eigenvalues $\sigma$. We assemble the moduli spaces into a smooth family $\pi:\mathscr M\to\Lambda$ where $\Lambda$ encodes $(\alpha,\sigma)$, and define parallel transport for homology along paths in an open dense subset $\Lambda_0\subset\Lambda$. By generalizing a classical theorem of Duistermaat and Heckman, we prove that the period map is affine linear in $(\alpha,\sigma)$, with slope governed by the curvature class of a principal torus bundle over $\mathscr M$.
arxiv:2611.21990.authors: Panagiotis Dimakis, Laura Fredrickson, Arya Yae

arxiv:2611.22018.title: Structural functional identifiability of unknown differential equation observation maps
arxiv:2611.22018.summary: In many differential equation models of real-world systems, the mechanistic structure of the dynamics is known, but the map from the dynamics to the observations is not. This is potentially problematic, as it can prevent us from e.g. learning model parameter values from data. Examples where this occurs include measuring a fluorescent marker as a proxy for the dynamics of a cellular circuit, and using wastewater measurements to follow the development of an epidemic.
arxiv:2611.22018.authors: Torkel E Loman, Alexander P Browning, Ruth E Baker

arxiv:2611.22021.title: Perfect matching complexes of antiprism graphs and independence complexes of generalized Petersen graphs $GP(n,2)$
arxiv:2611.22021.summary: We show that the perfect matching complexes of antiprism graphs and the independence complexes of the generalized Petersen graphs $GP(n, 2)$ are homotopy equivalent to wedges of spheres, and we determine the number and dimensions of the spheres. For the former we compute the initial values of Adamaszek's recursion for the independence complexes of cubes of cycles.

arxiv:2611.22023.title: Single-Vertex Metropolis on Minor-Free Graphs: A General EPTAS
arxiv:2611.22023.summary: We consider a class of combinatorial optimization problems where the goal is to find a largest induced subgraph with a prescribed property. We assume that the property is preserved by taking induced subgraphs and disjoint unions, holds for all edgeless graphs, and can be tested in polynomial time. We study the single-vertex Metropolis process for this class of problems.

arxiv:2611.22026.title: New necessary conditions on $h$-vectors of simplicial balls
arxiv:2611.22026.summary: Although the $h$-vectors of simplicial balls of dimension at most $4$ have been completely characterized, much less is known in dimensions $5$ and higher. We establish new necessary conditions on the $h$-vectors of simplicial balls in these dimensions. Together with the necessary conditions of Billera and Lee and the sufficient conditions of Kolins, our results yield a complete characterization of the $h$-vectors of $5$- and $6$-dimensional simplicial balls.
arxiv:2611.22026.authors: Luz Elena Grisales G\'omez, Satoshi Murai, Isabella Novik

arxiv:2611.22031.title: An improved bound on the strong chromatic index via local flag algebras
arxiv:2611.22031.summary: A strong edge coloring is an edge coloring where two edges receive different colors if they are incident or joined by a third edge. For a graph $G$, the strong chromatic index of $G$, denoted by $\chi'_s(G)$, is the minimum number of colors needed for a strong edge coloring of $G$. In this paper, using a local flag algebra method, we prove that for every graph $G$ of sufficiently large maximum degree $\Delta$, $\chi'_s(G)\le 1.642\Delta^2$, improving the previous best bound $1.73\Delta^2$ due to Davey, Hurley, de Joannis de Verclos, Kang, and Volec.

arxiv:2611.22032.title: FunSearch and Structured SAT Search for Weak Schur Partitions
arxiv:2611.22032.summary: The weak Schur problem asks how large an interval of consecutive integers can be partitioned into a fixed number of classes with no class containing a monochromatic solution to $a+b=c$ with $a\neq b$. We investigate whether FunSearch, an evolutionary program-search method guided by a large language model, can discover effective construction strategies for this classical combinatorial problem. In our adaptation, FunSearch evolves a priority function used by a fixed greedy solver, while a separate validity check enforces the weakly sum-free condition.
arxiv:2611.22032.authors: Rebecca Vicenzi, Pablo Christofferson, Caleb Hartman, Jingxuan Feng, Suleman Khan, Omar M. Elshinawy, Eric Ramos

arxiv:2611.22034.title: Klarner's sequences have density $0$
arxiv:2611.22034.summary: We prove that the set of non-negative integers $n$ which can be obtained from $0$ by repeated application of affine maps $x\mapsto 2x$, $x\mapsto 3x+2$ and $x\mapsto 6x+3$ has density $0$. Moreover, we reach the same conclusion for five other sequences of similar type introduced by D. Klarner.

arxiv:2611.22037.title: Cubic graphs with circumference ratio 21/22 and cyclic connectivity 5
arxiv:2611.22037.summary: We construct a cyclically $5$-connected cubic graph of order $22m$ and circumference $21m$ for every $m\geq 3$. Consequently, the shortness coefficient of the class of cyclically $5$-connected cubic graphs is at most $21/22$, improving the previously known upper bound of $24/25$. We also demonstrate how I-reductions, which delete an edge and suppress its two end-vertices, can be used to prove cyclic connectivity.

arxiv:2611.22053.title: Exotic cluster structures on $Sp_{2n}$
arxiv:2611.22053.summary: We modify the seeds of Berenstein, Fomin and Zelevinsky attached to reduced words for~$(w_0,w_0)$, for any simply connected simple complex algebraic group and any aperiodic Belavin--Drinfeld pair. In every type, moves of words act on the resulting seeds by mutations. After a change of coordinates introduced by Gekhtman, Shapiro and Vainshtein, the seeds are, for $SL_N$, seeds of the cluster structures of these authors, and for $Sp_{2n}$ they define regular complete cluster structures with the expected properties.

arxiv:2611.22058.title: Positivity in symmetric webs and block permanents
arxiv:2611.22058.summary: We use symmetric webs to prove Marcus's block-permanent inequality for up to four blocks of every size, for five blocks of size at least three, and for any fixed number of blocks above an explicit logarithmic bound on the block size. The proof idea is easy: Bending strands in the Schur relation turns the comparison into a calculation with squared norms.

arxiv:2611.22082.title: Enumerating orbits of finite classical groups on their Lie algebras
arxiv:2611.22082.summary: We enumerate the orbits of a finite classical group in the adjoint action on its Lie algebra, giving exact generating functions and very good upper bounds. We treat the general linear, unitary, symplectic and orthogonal groups, in both odd and even characteristic. In even characteristic, we get very nice formulas for the number of orbits on nilpotent classes both in the finite and algebraically closed case.
arxiv:2611.22082.authors: Jason Fulman, Robert M. Guralnick, Richard Stong

arxiv:2611.22089.title: Toroidal Obstructions with No K_5 Minor
arxiv:2611.22089.summary: Finding the complete set of forbidden minors for the torus remains an open problem. We determine the complete list of toroidal minor obstructions with no $K_5$ minor and prove that there are exactly $74$, each with between $10$ and $14$ vertices. Combined with the known classification of toroidal obstructions with no $K_{3,3}$ minor, this determines every toroidal obstruction that excludes one of the forbidden minors for planarity.

arxiv:2611.22104.title: Directed triangles in oriented graphs without a directed cycle of length $3t$
arxiv:2611.22104.summary: For integers $k,\ell\ge 3$, let $\operatorname{ex}(n,\Cdir_k,\Cdir_\ell)$ denote the maximum number of directed cycles of length $k$ in an $n$-vertex oriented graph containing no directed cycles of length $\ell$. Grzesik, Jaworska, Kielak, Kuc and \'Slusarczyk~\cite{GJ} systematically studied the generalized Tur\'an problem for directed cycles and conjectured that, for every fixed integer $t\ge 2$, $\operatorname{ex}(n,\Cdir_3,\Cdir_{3t})=\frac{t-1}{4}n^2+o(n^2)$. They proved this asymptotic formula for $t=2$.

arxiv:2611.22110.title: Real-Rootedness and Log-Concavity of Zigzag Eulerian Polynomials
arxiv:2611.22110.summary: We prove that the zigzag Eulerian polynomials have only real, negative, simple zeros, and hence strictly log-concave coefficients, settling the first two parts of a conjecture of Petersen and Zhuang. Real-rootedness in combinatorics is usually proved inside a single algebraic framework, such as interlacing or stability. Our proof rests on a different premise: different parts of a zero set become visible in different representations of the same polynomial, and classical tools suffice once each part is viewed in the right one.

arxiv:2611.22145.title: The topology of the mean action spectrum
arxiv:2611.22145.summary: We prove that if an area-preserving diffeomorphism of the closed two-disk is neither a pseudo-rotation nor a periodic map, then the closure of its mean action spectrum contains an interval of positive length. This partially answers a question of Hutchings. We do not require any additional assumptions on the area-preserving map, such as non-degeneracy or specific behavior near the boundary.
arxiv:2611.22145.authors: Habib Alizadeh, Dan Cristofaro-Gardiner, Abror Pirnapasov, Egor Shelukhin

arxiv:2611.22154.title: Cyclic group actions on K3 surfaces and almost complex structures
arxiv:2611.22154.summary: Fintushel, Stern and Sunukjian constructed exotic $\mathbb{Z}_n$-actions on $K3$ for $n=2,3,4$ using twist-rim surgery. We prove that these exotic actions do not preserve any Ricci flat metric or any integrable complex structure. This answers a question of Farb and Looijenga in the negative.

arxiv:2611.22182.title: On Contractibility of Geometric Joins
arxiv:2611.22182.summary: The geometric join of a family of sets in $\mathbb R^d$ is the union of the convex hulls of all colorful sets. For every $d \geq 4$, we construct $\lceil\frac{(d-1)^2}{2}\rceil$ sets in $\mathbb R^d$ whose geometric join is not contractible, disproving the conjecture of B\'ar\'any, Holmsen, and Karasev that the geometric join of at least $d+1$ sets is contractible.

arxiv:2611.22185.title: On Threshold Probabilities for the Stability of the Independence Number of a Random Subgraph
arxiv:2611.22185.summary: For an arbitrary sequence of graphs $G_n$, we consider a random spanning subgraph $G_{n,p}$ in which each edge of the graph $G_n$ survives independently of the others with probability $p$. We obtain a general upper bound for the independence number $\alpha(G_{n,p})$, from which, for an arbitrary probability $p=p(n)$, we derive sufficient conditions for asymptotic stability, i.e., for the equality $\alpha(G_{n,p})=(1+o(1))\alpha(G_n)$ asymptotically almost surely, as well as upper bounds for the independence number of the random subgraph, including unconditional ones; for $p=1/2$ they recover A. M.

arxiv:2611.22204.title: Flocking Time and Graph Volume in Nonlinear Cucker-Smale Models with Dynamic Networks
arxiv:2611.22204.summary: This study proposes a Cucker-Smale model incorporating dynamic networks and the discrete $p$-Laplacian ($p \in (1,2)$) and analyzes the relationship between flocking time constraints and graph connectivity from both theoretical and experimental perspectives. We establish that this model achieves flocking within finite time and derive a quantitative relationship between the lower bound of flocking time and graph volume. Based on these results, we observe that imposing sufficiently small flocking time induces an increase in network volume, and that larger initial velocity variance requires greater volume under the same time constraint.

arxiv:2611.22205.title: More lower bounds for Hales--Jewett and van der Waerden numbers
arxiv:2611.22205.summary: We give explicit colourings improving the comparison lower bounds assembled here for several Hales--Jewett and van der Waerden numbers. The main algebraic tool generalises Rabung's power-residue colouring from arithmetic progressions to arbitrary sets. If every translate of a t-element set S in F_p meets at least two classes of the r-th power character, and the integer weights have both parities, then a period-2p one-weight colouring of [t]^p has no monochromatic combinatorial line.

arxiv:2611.22214.title: The Nygaard graded piece, the Frobenius--Witt cotangent complex and regularity criteria
arxiv:2611.22214.summary: For a $p$-torsionfree $p$-quasisyntomic ring, we construct a fiber sequence relating the $p$-th Nygaard graded piece of absolute prismatic cohomology to the Frobenius--Witt cotangent complex. The latter is an arithmetic analogue of the cotangent complex in which the differential of $p$ need not vanish. We also clarify the relationship between the regularity criterion proved by Mao using the Frobenius--Witt cotangent complex and the regularity criterion established by Bhatt and Mathew using the Nygaard graded piece.

arxiv:2611.22249.title: $H_2$-optimal riblet profiles for turbulence suppression in channel flows
arxiv:2611.22249.summary: The drag-reducing properties of streamwise-elongated surface corrugations, commonly referred to as riblets, have been extensively studied through experiments, simulations, and reduced-order modeling. Notably, the linearized Navier-Stokes framework introduced by Ran, Zare, and Jovanovic (J. Fluid Mech., vol. 906, 2021) employs volume penalization to model riblet-induced boundary conditions and predict drag reduction.

arxiv:2611.22254.title: Between proper and strong edge-colorings of graphs with maximum degree at most four
arxiv:2611.22254.summary: A $(1^j,2^k)$-packing edge-coloring of a graph $G$ is a partition of its edge set $E(G)$ into $j$ matchings and $k$ induced matchings. It can be viewed as intermediate colorings between proper and strong edge-coloring. The study of this topic on subcubic graphs has drawn considerable attention recently, with many conjectures and open problems proposed and resolved.
arxiv:2611.22254.authors: Aistis Atminas, Xujun Liu, Zihui Xu

arxiv:2611.22293.title: Orbifold Morse Handles II. Boundary Regions, Gluing Maps, and Surgery Cobordisms
arxiv:2611.22293.summary: We study four-dimensional quotient handles defined by faithful representations of finite groups in $\mathrm{SO}(4)$ and invariant splittings of indices $1$, $2$, and $3$. We identify their attaching and belt regions as oriented $3$-orbifolds described by labeled singular graphs. We determine the orbifold isotopy class of the boundary gluing map.

arxiv:2611.22337.title: The Zaks--Perles--Wills volume conjecture I: three-dimensional lattice polytopes
arxiv:2611.22337.summary: We prove the three-dimensional Zaks--Perles--Wills volume bound for lattice polytopes with $k\ge3$ interior lattice points: the Euclidean volume of such a lattice polytope is at most $6(k+1)$, with equality if and only if the polytope is affinely unimodularly equivalent to $\operatorname{conv}(0,2e_1,3e_2,6(k+1)e_3)$. The inequality is strict when the minimum lattice width is at least three. Together with the known cases $k=1,2$, this completely resolves the three-dimensional Zaks--Perles--Wills volume conjecture.
arxiv:2611.22337.authors: Feihu Liu, Jinlong Tang, Sihao Tao, Zihao Zhang

arxiv:2611.22340.title: Growth of Sobolev Norms for Linear Schrodinger Equations with Denjoy--Carleman Potentials
arxiv:2611.22340.summary: We consider the linear Schr\"odinger equation on a torus of arbitrary dimension with a real time-dependent potential satisfying a mixed space--time Denjoy--Carleman condition. More precisely, for an increasing concave weight \(\omega(r)\asymp \log^\sigma(e+r)\), \(\sigma> 1\),we assume \[ \sup_{t\in\mathbb R}|\partial_t^q\widehat V(k,t)| \le Ae^{Bq^{p}}e^{-\rho_{0}\omega(|k|)},\qquad p=\frac{\sigma}{\sigma-1}. \] The corresponding spatial class is strictly larger than every Gevrey class, while the moment factor gives the quantitative ultradifferentiable control in time needed by the finite normal form.

arxiv:2611.22344.title: iBraid group symmetries of iquantum groups via star product
arxiv:2611.22344.summary: We establish ibraid group symmetries on universal iquantum groups of symmetrizable Kac-Moody type, proving a conjecture of Wang and Zhang. Building on the star product realization of quantum symmetric pairs $(\widetilde{\mathbf U},\widetilde{\mathbf U}^{\imath})$, we relate these symmetries to Lusztig's braid group symmetries, extending the compatibility previously obtained via iHopf algebras in the quasi-split setting. Via the Letzter map $\psi$ from the iquantum group $\widetilde{\mathbf U}^{\imath}$ to the horospherical algebra $\mathcal A\subset \widetilde{\mathbf U}$, we show that the ibraid group symmetry $\widetilde{\mathbf T}'_{i,-1}$ of $\widetilde{\mathbf U}^{\imath}$ transported…

arxiv:2611.22346.title: Minimum degree thresholds for even cycle residues
arxiv:2611.22346.summary: Dean's conjecture asserts that, for every integer $m\ge3$, every graph of minimum degree at least $m$ has a cycle whose length is divisible by $m$. This degree bound is best possible for odd $m$. For every integer $k\ge2$, we prove that every graph of minimum degree at least $2k-1$ has a cycle whose length is congruent to $r$ modulo $2k$ for every even $r\not\equiv2\pmod{2k}$.
arxiv:2611.22346.authors: Hojin Chu, Masaki Kashima, Shun-ichi Maezawa, Boram Park

arxiv:2611.22364.title: A new premodel for bounded type Siegel disks of some transcendental entire functions
arxiv:2611.22364.summary: In the 1980s, Douady and Sullivan conjectured that the Siegel disks of rational maps with degree at least two are Jordan domains. Based on the study of Blaschke models, this conjecture was settled by Zhang under the condition that the Siegel disks are of bounded type, and by Zakeri for a large number of transcendental entire functions under the same condition. The entire functions studied by Zakeri have exactly one finite asymptotic value, which is the center of the fixed Siegel disk.
arxiv:2611.22364.authors: Fei Yang, Gaofei Zhang, Yanhua Zhang

arxiv:2611.22365.title: Strong Transitivity of Group Cellular Automata: Characterization and Decidability
arxiv:2611.22365.summary: A discrete-time dynamical system is strongly transitive if every point can be reached, in finitely many steps, from every non-empty open set. We study this property for group cellular automata, \ie cellular automata over a finite group alphabet whose global map is a group endomorphism, in every dimension $d\geq1$. We prove that no group cellular automaton over a non-abelian group is strongly transitive, and we develop a decomposition of group cellular automata over abelian groups, via quotients by power subgroups, which preserves strong transitivity.
arxiv:2611.22365.authors: Niccol\`o Castronuovo, Alberto Dennunzio, Luciano Margara

arxiv:2611.22390.title: Waist inequality and a Hurewicz-type theorem for mean dimension
arxiv:2611.22390.summary: We establish a Hurewicz-type inequality relating mean dimension and conditional metric mean dimension. For every equivariant continuous map between dynamical systems, the mean dimension of the domain is bounded above by the sum of the mean dimension of the target and the conditional metric mean dimension of the map. In particular, any equivariant continuous map that decreases mean dimension must have infinite topological conditional entropy.
arxiv:2611.22390.authors: Qiang Huo, Kangbo Ouyang, Ruxi Shi, Masaki Tsukamoto

arxiv:2611.22433.title: Enriched nerves, interleaving distances and the multiplicative magnitude-path spectral sequence
arxiv:2611.22433.summary: By regarding the nerves of categories enriched over a monoidal poset as persistence simplicial sets, we investigate an upper bound of the interleaving distance in the homotopy category between the nerves in the sense of Lanary and Scoccola. In particular, it holds that the distance between the nerves for $r$-homotopy equivalent generalized metric spaces is less than or equal to the half of $r$. Moreover, a product on the cochain complex associated with a persistence simplicial set is introduced and related to the cup product on the magnitude cochain complex in the sense of Hepworth.

arxiv:2611.22451.title: Global phase-plane organization of a toxin-mediated plant-herbivore model
arxiv:2611.22451.summary: Plant-herbivore interactions with chemical plant defence mechanisms can generate complex population dynamics through the nonlinear interplay between resource availability, herbivore pressure, and defence-induced feedbacks. In this work, we investigate the dynamical organization of a plant-herbivore model characterized by a non-monotone functional response accounting for inhibitory effects on grazing activity. In particular, we perform a qualitative and geometric analysis of the associated homogeneous system, characterizing the dynamical regimes supported by the model and the transitions between them.

arxiv:2611.22478.title: On representation-theoretic and homological properties of distance algebras of finite graphs
arxiv:2611.22478.summary: Distance algebras were introduced by Asao and Ivanov to realize magnitude homology and cohomology as bigraded Tor and Ext groups. We study the representation-theoretic and homological properties of the distance algebra $\Sigma_G$ of a finite connected graph $G$. We characterize the graphs for which $\Sigma_G$ is representation-finite, multiserial, biserial, or self-injective by an explicit graph-theoretic classification.

arxiv:2611.22507.title: A sharp minimum degree condition for Hamiltonicity in line graphs of 3-hypergraphs
arxiv:2611.22507.summary: Let $G$ be the line graph of a $3$-hypergraph, and let $n$ be its order. We prove that if $G$ is $3$-connected, $n\ge4936$, and $\delta(G)\ge(n+5)/10$, then $G$ is Hamiltonian if and only if it does not belong to an explicitly described family of exceptional graphs. This extends the sharp minimum degree bound of Lai, Shao, and Zhan for $3$-connected claw-free graphs beyond the claw-free setting, since line graphs of $3$-hypergraphs may contain induced claws.

arxiv:2611.22513.title: Distance algebras of finite distributive lattices are Gorenstein
arxiv:2611.22513.summary: Distance algebras were introduced by Asao and Ivanov to realize magnitude homology and cohomology of quasi-metric spaces as Tor- and Ext-groups respectively. Let $\Sigma_L$ be the distance algebra of the Hasse graph of a finite distributive lattice $L$, where the metric is given by the lengths of shortest paths in the graph. We show that $\Sigma_L$ is Gorenstein over any Gorenstein commutative noetherian ring $R$, and give bound of its self-injective dimension.

arxiv:2611.22528.title: Flip Combinatorial Invariance for flipclasses with small residues
arxiv:2611.22528.summary: We establish (Normal) Flip Combinatorial Invariance for flipclasses with no residues longer than 8. Actually, we show more generally that all flipclasses of finite type with no residues longer than 8 have only one increasing path. For flipclasses of Weyl type, these are precisely the flipclasses having only one increasing path.
arxiv:2611.22528.authors: Francesco Esposito, Mario Marietti, Giovanni Paolini

arxiv:2611.22534.title: $D_n$-quasi-invariant polynomials in characteristic $p$
arxiv:2611.22534.summary: We give explicit descriptions of the $m$-harmonic polynomials for dihedral groups via hypergeometric functions. Using these, we compute the parameters $m$ for which the Hilbert series of the $D_n$-quasi-invariant polynomials in characteristic $p$ differs from the Hilbert series of $D_n$-quasi-invariant polynomials in characteristic $0$. We also give explicit descriptions of the generators of the $D_n$-quasi-invariant polynomials in characteristic $p$ when this is the case.

arxiv:2611.22535.title: Asymptotic enumeration of histories and limit laws in two random graph evolution models
arxiv:2611.22535.summary: We study growth models for random graphs where the growth is established by vertex or edge creations and where there is no dependence between vertices and edges. Creations are logged by time stamps such that the history of the resulting graph can be reconstructed. We investigate two prototypical models, an undirected and a directed one, called undirected independent growth model (UIG-model) and directed independent growth model (DIG-model).
arxiv:2611.22535.authors: Nadja Azzouz, Olivier Bodini, Francis Durand, Bernhard Gittenberger

arxiv:2611.22552.title: On (Pathwidth, Clique)-boundedness
arxiv:2611.22552.summary: We prove that every $(\pw,\omega)$-bounded class of graphs has bounded tree-independence number, answering a question of Be\v{s}ter \v{S}torgel, Dallard, Lozin, Milani\v{c}, and Zamaraev. We deduce this from a bound on the tree-independence number of graphs with neither $\B_\rho$ nor $K_{\sigma,\sigma}$ as an induced minor, where $\B_\rho$ is the complete binary tree of height $\rho$ and the bound depends only on $\rho$ and $\sigma$. We then obtain an asymptotically sharp bound on the path-independence number of $n$-vertex graphs in any $(\pw,\omega)$-bounded class.

arxiv:2611.22555.title: Higher orbifold Euler characteristics of torus representations
arxiv:2611.22555.summary: We compute the $\Gamma$-Euler characteristic of a finite-dimensional representation of the compact torus $\mathbb{T}^k$ where $\Gamma$ is an arbitrary finitely presented group. We additionally compute the $\Gamma$-Euler characteristic of the unit sphere in such a representation as well as the corresponding symplectic quotient at a nonzero level of the moment map. In each case, the $\Gamma$-Euler characteristic is expressed in terms of the weight matrix for the representation as well as a description of the abelianization of $\Gamma$.

arxiv:2611.22622.title: The Cooperstein conjecture and additive alternating $d$-codes
arxiv:2611.22622.summary: Let $\bigwedge^2 V$ be the second exterior power of a vector space $V$ over a finite field. The Cooperstein conjecture asserts a dimension bound for flats external to varieties consisting of points of bounded rank in $\mathrm{PG}(\bigwedge^2 V)$. This geometric problem can be translated into a question about linear spaces of alternating matrices whose nonzero elements have rank at least a prescribed value.

arxiv:2611.22653.title: Almost-Global Coordinates on Matrix Manifolds
arxiv:2611.22653.summary: We study global coordinates on smooth manifolds outside some closed subsets of measure zero. We first give an elementary proof that every compact smooth manifold admits such coordinates, allowing the Euclidean parameter domain to be disconnected. We then study parametrizations of classical matrix groups, Stiefel manifolds, Grassmannians and real flag manifolds.
arxiv:2611.22653.authors: Bingjie Li, Jiaxiang Wang, Zhigang Yao

arxiv:2611.22656.title: Golomb rulers with real marks: the real and integer optima agree up to ten marks
arxiv:2611.22656.summary: A Golomb ruler is a set of integer marks whose pairwise differences are distinct. We let the marks be real numbers and ask that every difference be at least 1 and that any two differences be at least 1 apart. Every integer Golomb ruler satisfies these conditions, so the least length $G_R(n)$ of such a real ruler with $n$ marks is at most the optimal Golomb length $G_Z(n)$.

arxiv:2611.22690.title: The minimum degree of minimally k-extendable graphs for some k
arxiv:2611.22690.summary: A graph on at least 2k+2 vertices is k-extendable if every matching of size k extends to a perfect matching, and it is minimally k-extendable if it is k-extendable but deleting any edge is not. Plummer proved that every k-extendable graph is (k+1)-connected. So its minimum degree is at least k+1.

arxiv:2611.22703.title: The Minimal Background Period for Infinitely Many Spectral Gaps in Anderson-Bernoulli Models
arxiv:2611.22703.summary: We prove that three is the smallest background period for which a one-dimensional discrete Anderson-Bernoulli operator can have infinitely many gaps in its almost-sure spectrum. For an explicit period-three background and coupling, we construct infinitely many bounded gaps accumulating from the right at a spectral energy, for every nondegenerate Bernoulli law. This property persists on an open set of background and coupling parameters.

arxiv:2611.22710.title: Feedback and Resource Competition in Incoherent Feedforward Loops: When Is Cumulative Dose Ordering Preserved?
arxiv:2611.22710.summary: Biochemical coupling can change the expression levels and timing predicted by an incoherent feedforward loop (IFFL) model without changing cumulative dose ordering. We derive ordering conditions using shared-production identities and Metzler comparison bounds, with tail guarantees beyond finite computation. A nonlinear example exhibits delayed slope reversal at a fixed dose, on an $O(1/\eta)$ timescale as pathway mismatch $\eta$ vanishes.
arxiv:2611.22710.authors: Iva Jankovi\'c, Fabiana Calandra, Giansimone Perrino, Velia Siciliano, Filippo Menolascina

arxiv:2611.22720.title: Positivity of Signed Odd-Multiplicity Partitions
arxiv:2611.22720.summary: We establish coefficientwise nonnegativity for the signed partition $q$-series \[ A_k(q)= \sum_{1\le j_1<\cdots<j_k} \prod_{i=1}^k\frac{q^{j_i}}{1+q^{2j_i}} =\sum_{n\ge0}a_k(n)q^n, \qquad k\ge0, \] with $A_0(q)=1$. The coefficient $a_k(n)$ counts, with signs, partitions of $n$ having exactly $k$ distinct part sizes, each occurring with odd multiplicity. A partition with multiplicities $2t_1+1,\ldots,2t_k+1$ is assigned the sign $(-1)^{t_1+\cdots+t_k}$.

arxiv:2611.22754.title: Maximum number of cells in a matroid subdivision of hypersimplex
arxiv:2611.22754.summary: David Speyer proved that the maximum number of cells in a regular matroid subdivision of the hypersimplex $\Delta(m,t)$ is $\binom{t-2}{m-1}$ , using the language of tropical geometry and properties of the Tutte polynomial of a matroid \cite[Theorem 6.1]{Speyer}. In this paper, we prove this result in general, i.e. for arbitrary matroid subdivisions including the non-regular ones. We perform a different combinatorial way using our results in \cite{HHH} and independent of tropical language.

arxiv:2611.22760.title: Sharp lower bounds for weighted bisections of graphs with bounded maximum degree
arxiv:2611.22760.summary: A bisection of a graph is a partition of its vertex set into two parts the sizes of which differ by at most one. We prove that every finite simple graph of maximum degree at most an odd positive integer $k$, with arbitrary nonnegative real edge weights, has a bisection of weight at least $(k+1)/(2k)$ times its total edge weight. The corresponding bound $(k+2)/(2(k+1))$ for even $k$ follows immediately.
arxiv:2611.22760.authors: Stefanie Gerke, Gregory Gutin, Anders Yeo, Yacong Zhou

arxiv:2611.22780.title: Heap-type permutation generation with a prescribed final arrangement
arxiv:2611.22780.summary: Heap's algorithm generates all permutations of an array of n items, obtaining each one from its predecessor by a single swap. We determine the net permutation applied to the array by every complete recursive call: a transposition when the number of items is odd and at least three, and a cycle through all items when it is even. We show that the output of each call is a concatenation of right cosets of the symmetric group on one item fewer, and we prove a general formula: the order in which the items are parked at the last position may be chosen freely, every such order corresponds to exactly one valid schedule, and it determines the net permutation of the call.

arxiv:2611.22824.title: An extremal question of Erd\H{o}s et al. on cycles
arxiv:2611.22824.summary: This paper addresses an extremal problem on long cycles proposed by Erd\H{o}s, Faudree, Schelp and Simonovits in 1989. Let \(2\le k\le d<n\) be positive integers. For an n-vertex simple graph G, let \(\theta_+^G\) count vertices of degree at least d, and \(C_{\ge k+1}\) denote a cycle of length at least \(k+1\).
arxiv:2611.22824.authors: Zhiyong Gan, Zhiliang Tan, Yi Huang

arxiv:2611.22830.title: Independent sets in the 2-token graph of a cycle and kings on the torus
arxiv:2611.22830.summary: The 2-token graph of the cycle $C_n$ and the king graph on the $n\times n$ torus are known to have the same independence number. Answering a question of Reyes, Dalf\'o and Fiol, for every $n\ge4$ we give an explicit bijection between a maximum independent set of the king graph and a maximum independent set of the $2$-token graph: each pair of tokens is represented by a king placed in the row of one of its two tokens and in the column given by their sum. We also show that the $2$-token graph of $C_n$ has exactly one maximum independent set, or exactly $n$ when $n\equiv3\pmod 4$, all of them rotations of each other.

arxiv:2611.22843.title: Quantitative FS-domains over continuous t-norms
arxiv:2611.22843.summary: We introduce quantitative FS-domains over continuous t-norms using a scalar-valued finite-separation degree and an approximate identity. The construction recovers classical FS-domains over the Boolean base. Symmetric quantitative FS-domains are characterized by compactness of their ball topology.

arxiv:2611.22849.title: Tilings of integer sets of prime-power cardinality
arxiv:2611.22849.summary: Let $A$ be a finite integer tile of cardinality $p^k$, where $p$ is prime and $k\geq1$. We first determine all possible fundamental periods of tilings of $A$. A cyclotomic argument gives a common period $PD$, where $P$ is a power of $p$ and $D$ is a greatest common divisor of normalized differences in $A$.
arxiv:2611.22849.authors: Wenchuan Hu, Chao Wang, Erxiao Wang, Fuhai Zhu

arxiv:2611.22863.title: Positivity of minimal volume entropy for some closed manifolds with zero simplicial volume
arxiv:2611.22863.summary: For every integer $m\ge4$, we construct a closed connected oriented smooth $m$-manifold whose simplicial volume is zero and whose minimal volume entropy is positive. This answers negatively the question, attributed to Gromov, whether vanishing simplicial volume implies vanishing minimal volume entropy. Each example has a connected regular five-sheeted covering with zero minimal volume entropy, so vanishing of this invariant does not descend through finite coverings.

arxiv:2611.22881.title: Equivalence of Small and Large Quasi-kernels
arxiv:2611.22881.summary: A quasi-kernel of a digraph $D$ is an independent set which can reach every vertex of $D$ by a directed path of length at most 2. The Small Quasi-kernel Conjecture states that every $n$-vertex source-free digraph $D$ contains a quasi-kernel $Q$ with $|Q|\le n/2$, and the Large Quasi-kernel Conjecture states that every $n$-vertex digraph $D$ contains a quasi-kernel $Q$ with $|N^+[Q]|\ge n/2$. Our main result shows for any $\frac{1}{2}<\beta<1$ an equivalence between the following two statements: \[\textrm{Every }n\textrm{-vertex source-free digraph contains a quasi-kernel with } |Q|\le n-\Omega(n^\beta).\] \[\textrm{Every }n\textrm{-vertex digraph contains a quasi-kernel with } |N^+[Q]|\ge…

arxiv:2611.22909.title: Minimum outdegree forcing directed cycles
arxiv:2611.22909.summary: The Caccetta-H\"aggkvist conjecture, one of the best known open problems on oriented graphs, asserts that every oriented graph on $n$ vertices with minimum outdegree at least $n/\ell$ contains a directed cycle of length at most $\ell$. Motivated by it, Kelly, K\"uhn and Osthus asked for the minimum degree condition that forces a directed cycle of length exactly $\ell$. The semidegree version of this problem was recently solved, but the methods used there rely on bounding the directed diameter, which requires control over the indegrees.
arxiv:2611.22909.authors: Andrzej Grzesik, Justyna Jaworska, Piotr Kuc

arxiv:2611.22918.title: Reconstructing hidden attractors with reservoir computing
arxiv:2611.22918.summary: Hidden attractors are difficult to locate as their basins of attraction do not intersect with any small neighborhood of an equilibrium point. We examine the possibility of reconstructing the hidden chaotic attractor from time series via reservoir computing, where the reservoir is built by a network of driven Kuramoto oscillators. We compare all-to-all coupling, nearest-neighbour ring coupling, and a ring with one modified oscillator equation which ensures that any attractor will be hidden.
arxiv:2611.22918.authors: Mohammad Zaman, Emel Khan, Thomas Geert de Jong

arxiv:2611.22919.title: Tannaka groups of holonomic D-modules on semi-abelian varieties are almost connected
arxiv:2611.22919.summary: In this short note we prove that Tannaka groups arising from convolutions of D-modules on complex semi-abelian varieties are almost connected. This generalizes results known for tori on the one hand and abelian varieties on the other.

arxiv:2611.22920.title: Round hyperspheres uniquely minimize most tangent-point energies
arxiv:2611.22920.summary: We show that round hyperspheres uniquely minimize a broad class of generalized tangent-point energies among all boundaries of bounded Caccioppoli sets sharing the same perimeter or enclosed volume. This includes closed $C^1$-hypersurfaces. Equivalently, we establish sharp lower bounds for the associated scale-invariant ratios of energy to surface measure and energy to volume, respectively, with equality precisely for round spheres.
arxiv:2611.22920.authors: Alexander Dohmen, Heiko von der Mosel

arxiv:2611.22957.title: Sums and Products in Dynamically Central Syndetic Sets
arxiv:2611.22957.summary: Glasscock and Le introduced the notion \textit{dynamically central syndetic sets} in a minimal topological dynamical system under the minimal action of the semigroup $(\mathbb{N}, +).$ In this short note, we introduce these large sets in the semigroup $(\mathbb{N}, \cdot)$ and establish that dynamically central syndetic sets contain the Hindman configuration $\{x,y,x+y,xy\}$. Furthermore, we show that there are dynamically central piecewise syndetic sets that do not contain such configurations.

arxiv:2611.22972.title: Hypersurfaces that are far from ruled
arxiv:2611.22972.summary: We show that a very general complex hypersurface of degree $d$ in $\mathbb P^{n+1}$ is not ruled whenever $n\geq3$ and $d\geq2\lceil(n+2)/3\rceil$. This improves Koll\'ar's original degree bound to the bound subsequently obtained by Totaro for stable irrationality and, in particular, includes very general quartic fourfolds. More precisely, we find new bounds for the minimal degree of a dominant rational map from a very general hypersurface to a ruled variety or a conic bundle, improving on previous bounds of Chen--Stapleton.

arxiv:2611.22992.title: Generators of derived category and toric Frobenius morphism
arxiv:2611.22992.summary: We investigate the action of the toric Frobenius pushforward functor on the derived category of a toric variety. Our main goal is to characterize objects of the derived category which become generators after applying a sufficiently high Frobenius pushforward. In particular, we extend a conjecture of A.Hanlon, J.Hicks, and O.Lazarev, which describes line bundles with this property, to arbitrary equivariant objects, and prove the extended conjecture for all smooth toric varieties.

arxiv:2611.22993.title: Complete characterization of graphs with common maximal abelian cover
arxiv:2611.22993.summary: The maximal abelian cover of a connected graph is the quotient of its universal cover by the commutator subgroup of its fundamental group. We provide a complete classification of finite connected graphs with isomorphic maximal abelian covers. For trees or for connected graphs with at least two cycles, the cover determines the base up to isomorphism; in cycle rank one, it determines the primitive cyclic pattern of rooted trees attached to the unique cycle.
arxiv:2611.22993.authors: Frederico Can\c{c}ado, Gabriel Coutinho, Thom\'as Jung Spier

arxiv:2611.22997.title: On Green's Conjecture for Curves on Anticanonical Surfaces
arxiv:2611.22997.summary: We prove Green's conjecture for smooth curves $C$ on rational surfaces $X$ such that $-K_X|_C$ is effective on $C$. In addition, on birationally ruled surfaces $X$ of irregularity $q \geq 1$ carrying an effective anticanonical divisor, we show that Green's conjecture holds for all smooth curves $C$ on $X$ covering the base curve with degree at least $2$, provided the latter has only finitely many gonal pencils or the gonality of $C$ is special with respect to the ruling.

arxiv:2611.23018.title: An infinite family of bipartite hypotraceable graphs
arxiv:2611.23018.summary: A graph is hypotraceable if it has no Hamiltonian path but every vertex-deleted subgraph does. In 1978, Gr\"otschel asked whether a bipartite hypotraceable graph exists. We resolve this long-standing question in a strong sense by proving that such graphs exist for every sufficiently large even order.

arxiv:2611.23033.title: The orbital architecture of 14 Herculis system as a KAM-stable three-body configuration
arxiv:2611.23033.summary: The 14 Herculis system hosts two massive giant planets on eccentric and mutually inclined orbits, making it a compelling test case for long-term stability in the spatial planetary three-body problem. We develop an analytical description of its dynamics using averaging, symplectic reduction of symmetries and KAM theory. For parameters compatible with the observed architecture, the secular quadrupole Hamiltonian possesses two elliptic relative equilibria that organise the nearby dynamics.
arxiv:2611.23033.authors: Francisco Crespo, Jes\'us F. Palaci\'an, Edward A. Turner, Patricia Yanguas

arxiv:2611.23061.title: The profinite shape equivalence
arxiv:2611.23061.summary: We show that, for every $\infty$-topos $\mathcal{X}$, the profinite shape induces a canonical equivalence between the $\infty$-category of pro-objects in locally constant constructible sheaves of anima in $\mathcal{X}$ and the slice $\infty$-category of profinite anima over the profinite shape $\widehat{\Pi}_{\infty}(\mathcal{X})$. We deduce this profinite shape equivalence from the monodromy classification theorem by establishing a continuous version of the straightening-unstraightening equivalence for profinite anima. In addition, we explain how the monodromy classification theorem recovers its classical counterparts concerning locally constant sheaves of finite sets and of (abelian)…

arxiv:2611.23064.title: Associative Log Rings and their Bimodules
arxiv:2611.23064.summary: We propose a definition of associative log rings. The role of the commutative monoid is replaced by a variant of a crossed module whose source is a monoid, and we use the resulting group action to control the failure of commutativity. This extends the classical notion of a log ring, even in the commutative case.
arxiv:2611.23064.authors: Deik van der Horst, Tommy Lundemo

arxiv:2611.23077.title: Divisible design graphs from a construction of antipodal distance-regular graphs based on Ree groups and Suzuki groups
arxiv:2611.23077.summary: In this paper, we present a new construction of divisible design graphs with new parameters, obtained by plugging a difference set into a known construction of antipodal distance-regular graphs of diameter 3 that is based on Ree groups and Suzuki groups.
arxiv:2611.23077.authors: Bart De Bruyn, Sergey Goryainov, Yilin Xie

arxiv:2611.23097.title: New bounds on simplex-avoiding sets in two dimensions
arxiv:2611.23097.summary: We study extremal densities of measurable subsets of metric spaces avoiding prescribed finite geometric configurations. We prove two new upper bounds for three-point avoidance problems: a measurable subset of $S^2$ containing no orthonormal basis has normalized spherical measure at most $7/11$, and a measurable subset of $\mathbb{R}^2$ containing no unit equilateral triangle has upper Banach density at most $9/16$. The first bound appears to be the first improvement over the trivial averaging bound for this problem, while the second improves the previously best known upper bound.
arxiv:2611.23097.authors: Domonkos Czifra, \'Akos D\'ucz, P\'eter Madarasi, D\'aniel Varga, P\'al Zs\'amboki

arxiv:2611.23103.title: Riemannian geometry and quantum gravity on trees
arxiv:2611.23103.summary: We show that the tree graphs that admit a quantum Riemannian geometry (QRG) with a positive ratio metric are exactly the Dynkin graphs of finite type $A,D,E$ and affine type $\widetilde D,\widetilde E$. A metric in this context is an assignment of a nonzero real value to each arrow and positive ratio requires that the two directions on any edge have the same sign. It turns out that the metric value in one direction can be chosen freely and the other is then determined.

arxiv:2611.23105.title: Holomorphic Vector Bundles on the Quantum Projective Line
arxiv:2611.23105.summary: We study Birkhoff--Grothendieck splitting for holomorphic vector bundles on the quantum projective line in the Dolbeault-module framework. We prove that every polynomial holomorphic bundle admitting a finite filtration by standard line objects is a direct sum of standard lines, with uniquely determined splitting integers. The proof uses a Dolbeault differential graded category and the two-arrow Kronecker quiver.
arxiv:2611.23105.authors: P. Aschieri, M. Khalkhali, G. Landi

arxiv:2611.23109.title: Derandomized Sunflowers and Radical Lower Bounds
arxiv:2611.23109.summary: Robust Sunflower lemmas imply that any large enough monotone DNF of width $w$ contains a sunflower, i.e., a DNF equivalent to the conjunction of a common core with a DNF that is heavily biased towards $1$. While these lemmas are typically proved in the context of the uniform distribution or i.i.d. distributions, they also hold for $O(w^2)$-wise independent distributions by Bazzi's theorem (Bazzi (SICOMP 2009); Tal (CCC 2017)), which states that width-$w$ DNFs cannot distinguish between such distributions and the uniform distribution. We prove a derandomization of robust sunflower lemmas for $O(w)$-wise independent distributions, which recovers the derandomization above with slightly weaker…
