arxiv:2611.23109.authors: Bruno Cavalar, Th\'eo Bor\'em Fabris, Partha Mukhopadhyay, Srikanth Srinivasan, Amir Yehudayoff

arxiv:2611.23117.title: Tropicalization and slow manifolds: A case study of the Michaelis--Menten reaction
arxiv:2611.23117.summary: We present a case study of a recently developed approach to multiple-scale systems based on exponential scaling and tropicalization (Kristiansen and Sarantaris, \emph{On a tropicalization of planar polynomial ODEs}). Parameters and variables are scaled exponentially with respect to a small parameter $\epsilon$, so that orders of magnitude become a genuine non-smooth singular limit $\epsilon\to 0$. Tropical geometry, via subdivisions of the Newton polygon, classifies the asymptotic regimes and locates the candidates for slow manifolds on all scales of the variables simultaneously.

arxiv:2611.23141.title: General curves on smooth quadric hypersurfaces
arxiv:2611.23141.summary: We prove a sharp existence theorem for non-degenerate maps from a general curve to a smooth quadric hypersurface, deforming in a smooth family of expected dimension. Along the way, we prove that if a general curve in projective space lies on a quadric (as dictated by the Maximal Rank Conjecture, now a theorem of E. Larson), then a general such quadric is smooth.

arxiv:2611.23163.title: Calabi--Yau dimensions of monotone Fukaya summands from infinitesimal gradings
arxiv:2611.23163.summary: We develop a theory of infinitesimal gradings for $\mathbb{Z}/2$-graded $A_\infty$-categories and use it to detect Calabi--Yau dimensions of monotone Fukaya summands from quantum cohomology. The dimensions we find agree with predictions from Serre functors of Kuznetsov components, such as $2$ for Gushel--Mukai and Verra fourfolds and the fractional value $\frac{n-2}{n}$ for the symplectic Grassmannian $\operatorname{IG}(2,2n)$. An infinitesimal grading induces endomorphisms on cohomological morphism spaces, and we prove a straightening theorem that realizes its weights as an actual grading compatible with the $A_\infty$-structure.

arxiv:2611.23164.title: Determining Compatible Groups in $\Gamma$-Zonal Labelings
arxiv:2611.23164.summary: Let $G$ be a plane graph with vertex, edge, and region sets $V(G),$ $E(G),$ and $F(G)$ respectively, and let $\Gamma$ be a nontrivial abelian group with identity element $0$. A $\Gamma$-zonal labeling of a plane graph $G$ is a labeling $\ell: V(G)\rightarrow \Gamma\setminus\{0\}$ such that for every region $f\in F(G)$, the sum of labels on the boundary of $f$ is $0$ in $\Gamma$. We say a $\Gamma$-zonal labeling is generative if the labels used generate $\Gamma$, and strong if the additive order of each label matches the degree of the corresponding vertex.

arxiv:2611.23166.title: A bordism perspective on ends of manifolds
arxiv:2611.23166.summary: We refine the classical pro-homotopy type of the end of a manifold by recording the boundaries of a compact exhaustion together with the bordisms between them. We show that this assignment, the bordism-end, is functorial in embeddings, and independent of the choice of exhaustion. Its target is the free sequential colimit completion of the bordism $\infty$-category.

arxiv:2611.23172.title: On the V-toothpick sequence
arxiv:2611.23172.summary: We give a generating function for the V-toothpick sequence and an algorithm that computes any term in time polynomial in the number of binary digits of its index. We determine its quadratic growth and periodic fluctuations, and give convergent series for the constants in its asymptotic bounds.

arxiv:2611.23176.title: Dynamics-preserving graph sparsification
arxiv:2611.23176.summary: Many dynamical systems unfold on networks of nodes coupled by edge interactions. This work is motivated by the following question: can we remove most edges from a networked dynamical system without significantly altering its behavior? For a given network, our goal is to find a sparser network that approximately preserves the dynamics on the nodes.
arxiv:2611.23176.authors: Emmie Fitz-Gibbon, Maximilian Jerdee, Yuanzhao Zhang, Rosemary Braun, Cristopher Moore

arxiv:2611.23195.title: Multifractal analysis of Takagi-type functions built from beta-expansion cylinders
arxiv:2611.23195.summary: We study a family of Takagi functions obtained by placing a normalized tent on each beta-expansion cylinder, with amplitude $\beta^{-\alpha n}$ at order $n$, where $\beta>1$ and $0<\alpha\le1$. We characterize their pointwise H\"older regularity in terms of cylinder lengths and distances from the point under consideration. The characterization holds more generally for nested interval partitions with exponentially decreasing mesh, without requiring interval lengths at a given order to be comparable.

arxiv:2611.23222.title: Sidorenko Inequalities in Oriented Graphs
arxiv:2611.23222.summary: We introduce relative Sidorenko and relative anti-Sidorenko inequalities for oriented graphs, strengthening the corresponding well-studied notions for tournaments by allowing arbitrary host graphs. An orientation $\vec H$ of a graph $H$ is relatively Sidorenko if $\hom(\vec H,\vec G) \ge 2^{-e(H)}\hom(H,G)$ for every oriented graph $\vec G$ with underlying graph $G$, and relatively anti-Sidorenko if the reverse inequality holds. We provide a complete characterisation of the class of connected relatively Sidorenko graphs in terms of weakly norming graphs, and exhibit several families of relatively Sidorenko and relatively anti-Sidorenko oriented graphs.
arxiv:2611.23222.authors: Veronica Bitonti, Emma Hogan, Jonathan A. Noel, Dmitry Tsarev

arxiv:2611.23230.title: On the multiplicity of crossing limit cycles of double diagonalizable piecewise linear vector fields
arxiv:2611.23230.summary: We consider planar piecewise linear vector fields with two zones separated by a straight line and having two diagonalizable components, which we call the \emph{double diagonalizable configuration}. In this configuration, the Poincar\'{e} half-maps correspond to separatrices of saddle points in the foliations of symmetric differential forms $\omega_r(x)-\omega_r(y)$, where $\omega_r$ is a rational $1$-form with exactly three simple poles. Limit cycles correspond to non-diagonal intersections of two such separatrices, and the multiplicity of a limit cycle is precisely the order of contact at the intersection point.

arxiv:2611.23235.title: Hessian--Maslov Geometry of Oja--Brockett Flows
arxiv:2611.23235.summary: This paper is organized in three parts. Part I develops the theoretical foundations of the Maslov index for caustics of the Legendre map, covering its semiclassical origin, geometric formulation as an intersection number in the Lagrangian Grassmannian, Hormander's local formula, and the dynamical viewpoint of bifurcating fixed points of a gradient flow. The theory is illustrated on the two-dimensional vector-valued quartic potential, whose caustic is a cusp and whose minima and saddles exchange stability when the eigenvalue ratio crosses 1.

arxiv:2611.23237.title: Commuting integrals of motion for free bosonic CFTs revisited: certified densities, spectral rigidity, and an exact identification at the c=1 branch point
arxiv:2611.23237.summary: We revisit the commuting local integrals of motion for free bosonic CFTs constructed in hep-th/0404195 as input data for integrable boundary states, using exact-arithmetic operator-product engines. A bootstrap lemma reduces its overdetermined bilinear commutativity systems to a distinguished odd charge D plus linear kernel problems -- conditionally on even-spin vacancy, a machine-verified but finite-range input. For the Z_2 x Z_2 "paperclip" family we publish the spin-7 density P_8, prove [I_3,I_5]=[I_3,I_7]=[I_5,I_7]=0 identically in n, and verify the Lukyanov-Vitchev-Zamolodchikov four-screening characterization at spins 7 and 9 at sampled n.

arxiv:2611.23238.title: Spectral dimension reduction of dynamical systems on graphons
arxiv:2611.23238.summary: Spectral dimension reduction approximates a dynamical system on a large network by a low-dimensional system whose variables are weighted averages of the node states, with weights given by dominant eigenvectors of the network. Its effectiveness is closely related to the low-rank structure of the interaction matrix. We develop a graphon analogue of this reduction for dynamical systems on dense graph limits.

arxiv:2611.23244.title: Goemans's Unsplittable-Flow Conjecture: The Anatomy of AI-Assisted Counterexample Discovery
arxiv:2611.23244.summary: Goemans conjectured that any fractional single-source flow could be converted into an unsplittable flow without increasing total cost and while increasing any arc load by at most the largest demand. Recently, Dmitry Rybin announced a seven-vertex counterexample found through an interaction with ChatGPT, which disproved this long-standing conjecture. However, the interaction did not reveal why this particular topology and its demand, fractional-flow, and cost choices work together, whether the example belongs to a broader family, or which structural features determine where counterexamples can occur.
arxiv:2611.23244.authors: Jingwei Ge, Na Xie, Li Li, Jiayang Li

arxiv:2611.23262.title: A Topologist's Proof of Krasnosel'skii's Bifurcation Theorem
arxiv:2611.23262.summary: This note offers a proof of Krasnosel'skii's bifurcation theorem that bypasses the traditional machinery of nonlinear analysis: neither the Leray-Schauder degree nor the Lyapunov-Schmidt reduction is used. The argument rests only on elementary operator theory and straightforward vector-bundle topology, providing a topologist's perspective on a classical result in nonlinear functional analysis.

arxiv:2611.23269.title: The Bapat-Sunder eigenvalue conjecture fails over the reals
arxiv:2611.23269.summary: In 1986 Bapat and Sunder asked whether $\operatorname{per}(A)$ is the largest eigenvalue of $F_A=[a_{i,j}\operatorname{per}(A(i,j))]$ for every positive semidefinite Hermitian $A$, where $A(i,j)$ deletes row $i$ and column $j$. Drury disproved this over the complex field in 2018 and conjectured that the property holds for real positive semidefinite matrices. We disprove Drury's conjecture with a rank-$4$, $32\times32$ integer Gram matrix and an integer vector whose Rayleigh quotient exceeds $\operatorname{per}(A)$; verification uses integer arithmetic.

arxiv:2611.23270.title: Octahedrally and Icosahedrally Symmetric Solutions of the N-Vortex Problem on the Sphere
arxiv:2611.23270.summary: We investigate the octahedrally and icosahedrally symmetric solutions of the N-vortex problem on the sphere, for N = 24 and N = 60 respectively, in the case of equal vorticities. Exploiting the symmetries arising from rotations and permutations of the vortices, the problem is reduced to the analysis of a one-degree-of-freedom Hamiltonian system on the sphere. The original contributions of this article concern the analysis of this reduced system yielding in particular a classification of the equilibrium and collision configurations with the prescribed symmetries.

arxiv:2611.23272.title: Cohomology Rings of Fiber Products of Lefschetz Fibrations
arxiv:2611.23272.summary: We prove a Lefschetz-type theorem for the cohomology rings of fiber products of two Lefschetz fibrations with disjoint critical loci. As an application, we compute the Hodge numbers of several examples of higher-dimensional Schoen's Calabi-Yau manifolds.

arxiv:2611.23279.title: Existence of SRB measures for some R\"ossler systems
arxiv:2611.23279.summary: We prove that for the R\"ossler system $\dot x=-(y+z)$, $\dot y=x+ay$, $\dot z=b+z(x-c)$ with $a=b=0.2$, the set of parameters $c$ within $6\cdot10^{-5}$ of the classical value $c=5.7$ for which the flow has a H\'enon-like strange attractor supporting a Sinai--Ruelle--Bowen (SRB) measure has positive Lebesgue measure. The key step, proved with computer assistance, is that at a parameter localised in an explicit interval within $5.5\cdot10^{-5}$ of $5.7$ the period-one saddle of the Poincar\'e map has a quadratic homoclinic tangency that unfolds generically; the conclusion then follows from the theorems of Mora--Viana, Benedicks--Young and Benedicks--Viana. The same method gives two further…

arxiv:2611.23280.title: Affine extensions and central compression for product-one-free sequences
arxiv:2611.23280.summary: Let $H_s=H_{27}\times C_3^s$, where $H_{27}$ is the nonabelian group of order $27$ and exponent three. We study the elements which can be adjoined to a product-one-free sequence $L$ of length $2s+5$. Let $Q$ be its central subsequence and let $h$ be the dimension of the subgroup generated by $Q$.

arxiv:2611.23288.title: Digital Twin Models for Malaria Transmission: A Classical and Stieltjes Derivative Approach
arxiv:2611.23288.summary: We propose two mathematical models for malaria transmission grounded in mosquito--human interactions and the digital twin framework. The first model is formulated using classical derivatives, whereas the second employs Stieltjes derivatives to represent abrupt biological events such as egg hatching and adult-emergence pulses in \emph{Anopheles} mosquito populations. The Stieltjes formulation unifies, in a single equation with two derivators, the continuous transmission dynamics, the biological impulses and the data-assimilation corrections of the digital twin; we prove its well-posedness, specify the order of biological and assimilation atoms when they coincide, and give quantitative…
arxiv:2611.23288.authors: Iv\'an Area, Emmanuel Afolabi Bakare, Francisco J. Fern\'andez, Daniel Muyiwa Adefisoye

arxiv:2611.23290.title: Strong Structural Stability of Scalar-Plus-Compact Operators on Banach Spaces
arxiv:2611.23290.summary: We prove that every strongly structurally stable operator of the form \(\lambda I+K\) on a real or complex Banach space, where \(\lambda\) is a scalar and \(K\) is compact, is hyperbolic. Applying this result to the real Banach space constructed by Argyros and Haydon and its complexification, both of which are infinite-dimensional separable Banach spaces with the scalar-plus-compact property, we show that neither space supports a nonhyperbolic and strongly structurally stable operator, thereby giving a negative answer to the part of the open problem of Bernardes and Messaoudi concerning strong structural stability.
arxiv:2611.23290.authors: Xinxing Wu, Mengjuan Wang, Xu Zhang

arxiv:2611.23291.title: Structure-Preserving Universal Differential Equations for Epidemic Dynamics
arxiv:2611.23291.summary: Universal differential equations (UDEs) combine mechanistic epidemic models with learned neural closures, but generic additive corrections may violate essential epidemiological properties. We introduce a class of structure-preserving epidemic UDEs in which learned closures parameterize intercompartmental fluxes and the force of infection factorizes through infected compartments. This architecture guarantees positivity, population boundedness, and invariance of the disease-free set.

arxiv:2611.23292.title: Log-concavity for alternating Eulerian polynomials
arxiv:2611.23292.summary: Alternating Eulerian polynomials enumerate permutations by the alternating descent statistic introduced by Chebikin. We prove that their coefficient sequences are log-concave, verifying a conjecture of Lin, Ma, Wang and Wang. Our proof combines a factorization involving reciprocal quadratic factors, estimates for ordinary Eulerian zeros, and a log-concavity criterion for products of such factors.

arxiv:2611.23295.title: Local connectivity of friends-and-strangers graphs with a star
arxiv:2611.23295.summary: Given two finite simple graphs $X$ and $Y$ with the same number of vertices, the vertex set of the friends-and-strangers graph $\FS(X,Y)$ consists of all bijections from the vertices of $X$ to the vertices of $Y$. Two bijections are adjacent exactly when one is obtained from the other by swapping the images of two adjacent vertices of $X$, while leaving all other images unchanged, and the two swapped images are adjacent in $Y$. For $n\ge2$, let $\Star_n$ be the star on $n$ vertices.

arxiv:2611.23301.title: Longitudinal Subdivision Invariance of Periodic Directed Strips and Its Application to Elongated Octagonal Strips
arxiv:2611.23301.summary: We prove that longitudinal refinements of finite-width periodic directed strips preserve subdivision containment. The refinement lengths may be arbitrary positive integers, without a uniform upper bound, and no matching condition is imposed on the horizontal arcs. We construct subdivision models in both directions that preserve each designated rail as a whole.

arxiv:2611.23333.title: Classification of Forbidden 0-1 Patterns by Their Extremal Function
arxiv:2611.23333.summary: This paper concerns the maximum weight of $n\times n$ 0-1 matrices that avoid some pattern $P$, denoted $\operatorname{ex}(n,P)$. Furedi and Hajnal initiated a research program of classifying all patterns according to their extremal function, but to date, only the weight-4 patterns are completely understood. In this paper we make progress on several fronts of the classification problem.

arxiv:2611.23338.title: An Explicit Construction of Large Families of MSTD Sets
arxiv:2611.23338.summary: A finite set $S\subset\mathbb Z$ is more sums than differences (MSTD) if $|S+S|>|S-S|$. Yufei Zhao's bidirectional-ballot construction gives $\Theta(2^N/N)$ MSTD subsets of $[0,N-1]$, the best previously known size bound for an explicit family, to the author's knowledge. We improve this bound: for every fixed integer $T\geq1$, we construct a family of $\Theta_T(2^N/(\log_2^{\circ T} N)^{2^T})$ MSTD subsets, where $\log_2^{\circ T}$ denotes the $T$-fold iterated logarithm.

arxiv:2611.23377.title: The Holomorphic-Topological Poisson Sigma Model and Quantization of Affine W-algebras
arxiv:2611.23377.summary: We construct explicit deformation quantizations of classical principal affine $W$-algebras for every simple Lie algebra $\mathfrak g$ using the holomorphic-topological Poisson sigma model of A. Khan and K. Zeng.
arxiv:2611.23377.authors: Niklas Garner, Brian R. Williams, Paul-Hermann Balduf

arxiv:2611.23421.title: Non-principality of forbidden subposet problems
arxiv:2611.23421.summary: We show pairs of posets such that the largest families not containing any of them is substantially smaller than the largest families avoiding only one of them.

arxiv:2611.23434.title: Replicating chaotic dynamics from sparse sensors with recurrent latent states
arxiv:2611.23434.summary: Forecasting a high-dimensional nonlinear system from a few point sensors requires an estimate of the current state and a model of its evolution. Reduced-order models usually take the full state as input, so with only sparse sensors they require an auxiliary full-state estimate whose error is inherited by the latent representation. We instead build the latent state from sensor measurements alone, using a shallow recurrent decoder (SHRED) network that encodes a history of point measurements, and train an echo state network to advance that latent state autonomously.
arxiv:2611.23434.authors: Jan P. Williams, J. Nathan Kutz, Krithika Manohar

arxiv:2611.23437.title: Symmetries of symplectic Khovanov-Rozansky homology
arxiv:2611.23437.summary: We study the behavior of Manolescu's construction of symplectic Khovanov-Rozansky homology under symmetries. Specifically, for k<n we construct a localization spectral sequence from the symplectic sl(n) homology of a knot to the direct sum of the symplectic sl(k) and sl(n-k) homologies of the same knot, giving a geometric analog of rank-reducing spectral sequences arising from deformations on the non-symplectic theory. We also prove the existence of a localization spectral sequence relating the symplectic Khovanov--Rozansky homology of a two-periodic link to the symplectic Khovanov-Rozansky homology of the quotient link, in analogy to a theorem of Seidel and Smith for symplectic Khovanov…
arxiv:2611.23437.authors: Akram Alishahi, Kristen Hendricks, Cheuk Yu Mak

arxiv:2611.23451.title: Finite regularity moduli stacks through diffeology
arxiv:2611.23451.summary: Diffeological non-Abelian Hodge theory motivates the study of $C^r$ families of Higgs bundles and flat bundles for finite $r$. In this article, we provide a uniform language for treating moduli stacks parametrizing such objects in terms of diffeology. More specifically, we develop a theory of stacks presentable by diffeological groupoids over the site of $C^r$ manifolds for arbitrary $r$.

arxiv:2611.23460.title: Antidirected paths on five vertices in 5-chromatic digraphs
arxiv:2611.23460.summary: We prove that every 5-chromatic digraph containing no copy of the regular tournament on five vertices contains both antidirected paths on five vertices. This answers a question posed by El Sahili in 2004. The proof uses an edge bound for 5-critical graphs to constrain the out-degrees in a counterexample and obtain a contradiction by constructing a proper 4-colouring.

arxiv:2611.23464.title: Minimal super dominating sets of maximum cardinality
arxiv:2611.23464.summary: Let $G = (V,E)$ be a graph. A subset $S \subseteq V$ of vertices is a super dominating set if every vertex $v \in V - S$ has a neighbour $u \in S$, whose only neighbour in $V - S$ is $v$. A set $S \subseteq V$ is called open irredundant if every vertex $u \in S$ has at least one neighbour $v \in V - S$ whose only neighbour in $S$ is $u$.
arxiv:2611.23464.authors: Diana Avella-Alaminos, Magdalena Lema\'nska, Rita Zuazua

arxiv:2611.23478.title: Unique-maximum colourings of planar graphs with respect to neighbourhoods
arxiv:2611.23478.summary: A colouring of the vertices of a graph by positive integers is a unique-maximum colouring with respect to open (resp. closed) neighbourhoods if the maximum colour appears exactly once in the open (resp. closed) neighbourhood of every vertex. Fabrici, Lu\v{z}ar, Rindo\v{s}ov\'a and Sot\'ak (Discrete Appl. Math. 324 (2023) 80-92) conjectured that four colours suffice for closed neighbourhoods in planar graphs.

arxiv:2611.23485.title: Ramsey Theory for Edge Ideals
arxiv:2611.23485.summary: We initiate the study of Ramsey theory for edge ideals. The edge ideal I_G is generated by the monomials x_ux_v for all edges uv of G. A central invariant measuring structure in algebraic geometry and commutative algebra are the betti number beta_{i,j}(S/I) for some ideal I in a ring S.

arxiv:2611.23488.title: Narrower arithmetic progressions in the primes
arxiv:2611.23488.summary: For each fixed $k\geq 3$ and $\delta > 0$, we prove that every subset of the primes up to $X$ of relative density at least $\delta$ contains a non-trivial $k$-term arithmetic progression with common difference $O_{k,\delta,\varepsilon}((\log X)^{k\cdot 2^{k-3}+\varepsilon})$, for any $\varepsilon>0$. This improves the previous exponent $(k-1)2^{k-2}$. The main ingredient is a relative Szemer\'{e}di theorem for narrow progressions under weaker linear forms conditions.

arxiv:2611.23490.title: Large entropy implies H\"older regularity on large sets
arxiv:2611.23490.summary: Let $F$ be a holomorphic endomorphism of $\mathbb{P}^k(\mathbb C)$ of algebraic degree $d\ge2$, with $k\ge1$. We prove that every ergodic $F$-invariant probability measure $\mu$ of entropy strictly greater than $(k-1)\log d$ admits compact sets of $\mu$-measure arbitrarily close to one on which the restrictions of $\mu$ have H\"older continuous super-potentials. Consequently, $\mu$ gives zero mass to every Borel pluripolar set.

arxiv:2611.23519.title: Protection Group of Colored Links
arxiv:2611.23519.summary: Colored links provide a mathematical framework for studying the topological stability and classification of three-dimensional topological vortex configurations. Earlier classifications in settings of physical interest relied on system-specific invariants. Here, we introduce a universal invariant of colored links, the \textit{protection group}, interpret earlier classification results as computations of this group, and compute it in new examples.

arxiv:2611.23521.title: Twisting and foam inequalities for the upsilon invariant
arxiv:2611.23521.summary: We describe two families of bounds on the Ozsv\'ath-Stipsicz-Szab\'o invariant $\Upsilon_K(t)$, one controlling its behavior under inserting full twists into a knot and one controlling a limited class of foams, or singular cobordisms between knots. By constructing certain explicit foams, we show that these two formal properties of $\Upsilon$ together exactly determine $\Upsilon_K(t)$ for all torus knots. This generalizes previously observed behavior at $t = 0$, Livingston's slice-torus invariants, and at $t=1$, Sato's unoriented analogue.

arxiv:2611.23532.title: Compactifying the $G_2'$-Hitchin component via almost-complex curves
arxiv:2611.23532.summary: By studying limits of induced metrics of equivariant almost-complex curves in the pseudosphere $\mathbb{S}^{2,4}$, we compactify the $G_{2}'$-Hitchin component.
arxiv:2611.23532.authors: Parker Evans, Charles Ouyang, Andrea Tamburelli

arxiv:2611.23536.title: Binomially Weighted Partition Statistics: Generating Functions, Asymptotics, and Dominance
arxiv:2611.23536.summary: For an integer partition $\lambda=(\lambda_1,\lambda_2,\ldots)$, we consider $M_m(\lambda)=\sum_{i\geq1}\binom{i+m}{m+1}\lambda_i$, where $m\geq0$. We prove conjugation and Frobenius-coordinate identities for this family and obtain its ordinary and bivariate generating functions. Differentiating the bivariate product gives exact formulas for the mean and variance under uniform sampling of partitions of $n$.
arxiv:2611.23536.authors: Grant Kopitzke, Alex Phillippi, Derek Scheiderer

arxiv:2611.23542.title: The Gini Index of an Integer Composition
arxiv:2611.23542.summary: We extend the discrete Gini statistic on integer partitions to integer compositions by rearranging the parts in decreasing order. Under the uniform distribution on the $2^{n-1}$ compositions of $n$, the resulting statistic has a rational ordinary generating function for its aggregate values, as well as a rational generating function for its second moments. More generally, the generating function of every fixed raw moment is rational, although the bivariate generating function encoding the entire distribution is not.

arxiv:2611.23559.title: 3-Cube-Free Sets in Cyclic Groups
arxiv:2611.23559.summary: A set is called $3$-cube-free if it contains no configuration of the following form: $\{x,y,z,x+y,x+z,y+z,x+y+z\}$. We study the maximum density of $3$-cube-free sets in finite cyclic groups. As observed by Meng, every $3$-cube-free subset of $\mathbb Z_m$ has size at most $2m/3$, and this bound is sharp whenever $3\mid m$.

arxiv:2611.23579.title: Irreducible $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$-action on projective $k$-lattices and Frobenius numbers
arxiv:2611.23579.summary: The irreducible representation of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ induces an action on the space $X_k(\mathbb{R}^n)$ of projective classes of rank $k$-discrete subgroups in $\mathbb{R}^n$. For every lattice subgroup of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$ and every starting point in $X_k(\mathbb{R}^n)$ and $2\leq k<n$, we prove convergence of the orbit averages over expanding norm balls and give a complete, explicit description of their limits. In an overview, every limit is supported on the subbundle over the unique compact $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb{R})$-orbit in the Grassmannian.
arxiv:2611.23579.authors: Michael Bersudsky, Seongmin Kim, Seonhee Lim

arxiv:2611.23590.title: Perspectives on the hidden subgroup problem over unitriangular groups
arxiv:2611.23590.summary: We investigate the quantum Hidden Subgroup Problem (HSP) over the upper unitriangular group $U_n(\mathbb{F}_p)$. While efficient quantum algorithms were discovered for some families of non abelian groups and nil-2 $p$-groups, no efficient algorithms are known for groups of nilpotency class higher than 2. The only techniques known for such groups scale exponentially in the size of the input.

arxiv:2611.23607.title: Averting `Gravity': Launch Control and the Limits of Collision Avoidance in Low Earth Orbit Operations
arxiv:2611.23607.summary: As large constellations fill low Earth orbit, the risk of a runaway collision cascade has become a central concern of space operations. Debris population models treat collision avoidance as a fixed input, although the capacity to screen potential collisions and plan maneuvers degrades as debris accumulates. Using a stylized multi-layer queueing network model, we show that collision avoidance capabilities that saturate as the in-custody fragment count increases, can make the orbital shell bistable, with a low-debris and a high-debris equilibrium, and hysteretic.

arxiv:2611.23612.title: Extreme value statistics for majorisation partial orders
arxiv:2611.23612.summary: We study extreme-value phenomena for random samples in partially ordered sets through their meets and joins, the order-theoretic analogues of minima and maxima. In this paper we consider the probability simplex equipped with either UT-majorisation or majorisation, with samples drawn uniformly from the corresponding simplex. We analyse these extrema both at fixed dimension and as the dimension grows, identifying almost-sure collapse to the bottom or top elements and critical scalings with nondegenerate limiting laws.
arxiv:2611.23612.authors: Elia Bisi, Fabio Deelan Cunden, Giovanni Gramegna, Marilena Ligab\`o

arxiv:2611.23634.title: Irreducible components of affine Deligne-Lusztig variety in the affine flag variety
arxiv:2611.23634.summary: We establish a bijection between elements of stable Demazure crystals and labeled longest increasing paths in the double Bruhat graph. As an application, we show that the orbits of irreducible components of certain special affine Deligne-Lusztig varieties (ADLVs) in the affine flag variety of a split reductive group are counted by weight multiplicities of the associated Demazure modules for the dual group. By decomposing an arbitrary ADLV into strata that are iterated fibrations over these special ADLVs, we then obtain a formula for the number of orbits of irreducible components for ADLVs in the affine flag variety, generalizing the numerical form of the Chen-Zhu conjecture.

arxiv:2611.23641.title: Almost all vertex-transitive graphs and digraphs are Cayley
arxiv:2611.23641.summary: We prove that almost all vertex-transitive digraphs are Cayley digraphs, and that almost all vertex-transitive graphs are Cayley graphs, as the number of vertices tends to infinity through all positive integers. The proportions of Cayley objects are at least $1-2^{-n/4+o(n)}$ for digraphs and $1-2^{-n/24+o(n)}$ for graphs. This proves the McKay--Praeger conjecture and its digraph analogue.

arxiv:2611.23647.title: Removable forests in $k$-connected and $k$-edge-connected graphs
arxiv:2611.23647.summary: We prove the forest conjecture of Clay and Jord\'an: Let $k\ge1$ be an integer and let $F$ be a forest with $m$ vertices and $e$ edges. If a $k$-connected graph $G$ has minimum degree at least $\max\{k+e,m-1\}$, then it contains a copy of $F$ whose edge deletion preserves $k$-connectivity. We also prove the $k$-edge-connectivity version.

arxiv:2611.23650.title: Convergence of the big J-function of a GKM manifold
arxiv:2611.23650.summary: The genus-$0$ equivariant Gromov--Witten (GW) invariants of a GKM manifold can be computed recursively by a recursion discovered by Brown and studied further by Coates--Corti--Iritani--Tseng. In this paper, we prove a slightly modified version of this result by realizing the J-function as a solution to a fixed-point problem. As an application, we prove that both the equivariant and the non-equivariant quantum cohomologies of a GKM manifold are convergent.

arxiv:2611.23653.title: Faster polynomial-space algorithms for poset problems
arxiv:2611.23653.summary: We give a polynomial-space, deterministic, exact algorithm for counting linear extensions of partial orders over $n$ elements, with running time $O^*((2\sqrt{2})^{n}) \subseteq O(2.829^n)$. This improves upon the long-standing bound of $O^*(4^{n})$ attainable by standard divide and conquer (Savitch 1970, Gurevich and Shelah 1987). Our algorithm uses a similar balanced splitting approach as the classical algorithm, but applies it only to the elements outside a largest antichain.

arxiv:2611.23659.title: From Persistent Cohomology to Maps into Arbitrary Eilenberg-MacLane Spaces
arxiv:2611.23659.summary: In this paper, we address the construction of Eilenberg-MacLane coordinates (functions from datasets to Eilenberg-MacLane spaces $K(G,n)$) that encode nontrivial persistent cohomology classes in arbitrary dimensions $n$ and coefficient group $G$. The construction leverages the connecting homomorphism in the long exact sequence in \v{C}ech cohomology, from the short exact sequence of sheaves of continuous maps with values in $G$, $EG$ and $BG$. Crucially, the derivation is constructive: we give an explicit, recursive formula for preimages under the connecting homomorphism, which yields a constructive version of a classical cohomology vanishing theorem and, in turn, an algorithm for general…
arxiv:2611.23659.authors: Tony Xiaochen Xiao, Jose A. Perea

arxiv:2611.23662.title: Conditional limit theorems in dynamical systems
arxiv:2611.23662.summary: This paper develops a comprehensive theory of conditional limit theorems for open dynamical systems. We study the statistical properties of the dynamics within transient regimes by establishing a suite of limit theorems describing the behavior of trajectories under the condition that they remain outside a ``hole'', or region of no return. Under a spectral gap assumption for the associated open transfer operator, we first establish conditioning and Yaglom limits and identify the corresponding conditionally invariant and conditionally ergodic measures.
arxiv:2611.23662.authors: Jason Atnip, Gary Froyland, Cecilia Gonz\'alez-Tokman, Yushi Nakano, Sandro Vaienti

arxiv:2611.23668.title: Circular decompositions for hyperbolic genus one knots
arxiv:2611.23668.summary: We consider hyperbolic genus one knots having two or more non-isotopic, disjoint, genus one Seifert surfaces, with the property that the complementary regiones are handlebody pairs. We determine whether or not these knots have circular width equal to $(3)$. Moreover we give bounds on their circular widths.
arxiv:2611.23668.authors: Mario Eudae-Mu\~noz, Araceli Guzm\'an-Trist\'an, Fabiola Manjarrez-Guti\'errez, Enrique Ram\'irez-Losada

arxiv:2611.23681.title: Geography of Klein bottle Luttinger surgery
arxiv:2611.23681.summary: We propose and study a modification of Auroux's uniqueness question on Luttinger surgery by replacing Lagrangian tori with Klein bottles. In Kodaira dimension $-\infty$, we introduce two simple graphs whose connected components give bounds and, in several cases, exact counts of Klein bottle Luttinger equivalence classes. In Kodaira dimension zero, we provide examples of numerical invariants supporting infinitely many equivalence classes and prove a homological non-triviality theorem for Lagrangian Klein bottles in all symplectic Calabi--Yau surfaces with positive Euler characteristic.
arxiv:2611.23681.authors: Xinle Dai, Boxi Hao, Shengzhen Ning

arxiv:2611.23686.title: Connectivity of Matroids with Breadth-Critical Tangles
arxiv:2611.23686.summary: We construct an explicit infinite sequence of nonnegative integers $(s_0,s_1,\ldots)$ such that, for every $k\ge2$, every finite matroid with a breadth-critical tangle of order at least $k$ is $(s_0,s_1,\ldots,s_{k-2})$-connected. The constants $s_i$ depend only on $i$. This proves a conjecture of Brettell, Jowett, Oxley, Semple, and Whittle.

arxiv:2611.23692.title: Linear Connectivity of Boundaries of Right-Angled Coxeter Groups
arxiv:2611.23692.summary: To every right-angled Coxeter group one can canonically associate a hyperbolic metric space, called its maximized hyperbolic space. This space is Morse recognizing and is obtained from the Davis complex by coning off its standard product regions. We characterize, purely in terms of the defining graph, when the Gromov boundary of a maximized hyperbolic space is nonempty and linearly connected.

arxiv:2611.23694.title: Superspecial curves of genus two over prime fields: Frobenius types and rational (2,2)-kernels
arxiv:2611.23694.summary: Superspecial curves of genus two over a prime field $\mathbb{F}_p$, and the rational $(2,2)$-isogenies between their Jacobians, are the vertices and edges of the graph on which genus-two isogeny-based cryptography is built. Let $C$ be such a curve, with Jacobian $J$ and Frobenius endomorphism $\pi$. We show that $\pi^2 = p\,\alpha_*$ for a unique automorphism $\alpha$ of $C$ over $\mathbb{F}_p$ whose action on the Weierstrass points is the square of that of Frobenius.

arxiv:2611.23696.title: 2-Walk-regular graphs with $k_2$ at most twice the valency
arxiv:2611.23696.summary: In this paper, we characterize $2$-walk-regular graphs with valency $k$, diameter at least four and $k_2\leq 2k$, generalizing a result of Koolen and Park, and classify the distance-regular graphs satisfying these conditions. We also classify $2$-walk-regular graphs with valency $k$, diameter at least four and at most $4k+4$ vertices.

arxiv:2611.23703.title: Degree-three Euclidean spanning trees within a factor of 1.514 of the minimum
arxiv:2611.23703.summary: For every finite point set $X$ in a Euclidean space of arbitrary dimension, we prove that there is a spanning tree of maximum degree three and total length at most $(757/500)\MST(X)=1.514\MST(X)$, where $\MST(X)$ denotes the unrestricted minimum spanning-tree length. More strongly, for any root and any finite list of other points, there is a Hamiltonian path starting at the root whose length is at most $1.514$ times the sum of the root-to-point distances. The proof follows the rooted-path and variable-block framework used in earlier work, and applies Young's weighted-distance inequality to explicit rational mixtures of paths.
arxiv:2611.23703.authors: William Han, Dan Ismailescu, Ganghun Kim

arxiv:2611.23707.title: Functorial height and Orlov's rationality conjecture
arxiv:2611.23707.summary: An exceptional collection in the derived category of a smooth projective variety may fail to generate the whole category, and this failure cannot be detected by K-theory or by Hochschild homology. Kuznetsov's height detects it through Hochschild cohomology, that is, through natural transformations from the identity functor to its shifts. We replace the identity functor by an arbitrary endofunctor $F$ and define the height of a collection with coefficient $F$.

arxiv:2611.23721.title: Optimal homological stability: bounding secondary terms of Cohen-Lenstra moments and $S_d$-fields over $\mathbb{F}_q[t]$
arxiv:2611.23721.summary: We prove an explicit stability line for the homology $H_i(\mathrm{Hur}_n^c,\mathbb{Q})$ of any Hurwitz space associated to a finite rack $c$ depending only on its homology up to some finite $n$. Moreover, as the range of $n$ increases, the slope of the resulting stability line converges to the optimal slope. Thus, for any Hurwitz space, a finite computation will yield near-optimal bounds on secondary terms for the corresponding arithmetic statistics problem.

arxiv:2611.23730.title: Circuit spectra for binary matroids
arxiv:2611.23730.summary: The circuit spectrum of a matroid is defined to be the set of circuit sizes. The circuit $e$-spectrum of a matroid is the set of circuit sizes of the matroid containing the element $e$. The circuit spectrum problem is an important problem.
arxiv:2611.23730.authors: Bing Wei, Haidong Wu, Shunzhe Zhang

arxiv:2611.23735.title: Gopakumar-Vafa invariants and Mordell-Weil lattices
arxiv:2611.23735.summary: Let $X\to B$ be a Weierstrass fibration with integral fibers from a smooth Calabi--Yau threefold to a del Pezzo surface. For a smooth curve $D\subset B$ with smooth inverse image $Y$, we decompose the moduli fiber of stable sheaves with Euler characteristic one and projected cycle $D$. In fiber degree $k$, its components are indexed by all sections $C$ of $Y\to D$ with $\tfrac12\langle C,C\rangle\leq k$, where $\langle\, ,\,\rangle$ is the Mordell--Weil height pairing.

arxiv:2611.23739.title: Heights and energies of polarized fibrations of varieties
arxiv:2611.23739.summary: We study nef line bundles on polarized fibrations $(X/C,\bar{H})$, with a fixed nef metrized ample polarization satisfying $H^d=1$, where $d=\dim X$. We prove a quantitative arithmetic height inequality under relative metric positivity, allowing singular arithmetic models and relatively nef adelic bundles. The height deficit defines a local energy.

arxiv:2611.23767.title: A Lower Bound for the Chromatic Number of Ball-Packing Graphs
arxiv:2611.23767.summary: For every odd prime power $q$, we construct a finite packing of congruent balls in dimension $d=q^2-q+1$ whose contact graph requires at least $2d$ colors. Consequently, the ball-packing chromatic number satisfies $\chiball(q^2-q+1)\ge2(q^2-q+1)$, and the same lower bound holds for congruent-ball packings. The construction starts from the complements of Hubaut's $C_{20}$ graphs and uses their Taylor extensions.
arxiv:2611.23767.authors: Dan Ismailescu, Sunwoo Lee, Terry Lee

arxiv:2611.23785.title: Partial flags of tropical linear spaces may not complete
arxiv:2611.23785.summary: We construct two valuated matroids of ranks 2 and 4 on eight elements that form a valuated quotient, such that no rank 3 valuated matroid forms a valuated quotient with both simultaneously. In other words, a partial flag of tropical linear spaces need not extend to a complete flag containing every intermediate dimension.

arxiv:2611.23805.title: Hydrodynamic limit of the Toda lattice
arxiv:2611.23805.summary: In this paper we consider the Toda lattice under random, spatially inhomogeneous initial data, meaning that its initial momenta and interparticle spacings are independent and their laws may slowly vary in space. When the density is strictly positive (but sufficiently small), we identify the model's hydrodynamic limit under Euler scaling. More precisely, we prove that spatial averages of each of the model's local conserved quantities converge to moments of a density $m_{\tau}(\lambda,q)$ solving the generalized hydrodynamic equation predicted by Doyon arXiv:1902.07624 and Spohn arXiv:1902.07751.

arxiv:2611.23819.title: Chromatic heights of homotopy fixed points of iterated topological Hochschild homology of connective spectra
arxiv:2611.23819.summary: Let $R$ be an $\mathbb{E}_{\infty}$-ring spectrum of height $m$. The chromatic redshift theorem implies that its $n$-fold iterated algebraic $K$-theory $K^{(n)}(R)$ has height $m+n$. Moreover, there is a natural map $K^{(n)}(R)\to (T^n\otimes R)^{hT^n}$, where $T^n\otimes R$ denotes the $n$-fold iterated topological Hochschild homology.

arxiv:2611.23821.title: Hurwitz equivalence in quandles of order at most four
arxiv:2611.23821.summary: Let $X$ be a quandle and let $m\geq 2$ be an integer. The $m$-braid group acts on the $m$-fold Cartesian power $X^m$ by the Hurwitz action. For an $m$-tuple $\boldsymbol{x}\in X^m$, we introduce two invariants of the Hurwitz action: the product $\Pi(\boldsymbol{x})$ of its entries in the associated group $\operatorname{As}(X)$ and the orbit multiplicities $\mu_w(\boldsymbol{x})$ $(w\in X)$.

arxiv:2611.23831.title: Bernstein-Zelevinsky duality for equivariant vector bundles on Drinfeld spaces
arxiv:2611.23831.summary: We study duality and finiteness of locally analytic representations arising from compactly supported coherent cohomology of Drinfeld spaces. We prove that Grothendieck--Serre duality for equivariant vector bundles realizes Bernstein--Zelevinsky duality of locally analytic representations. We follow the strategy of Fargues for $\ell$-adic sheaves and obtain resolutions of locally analytic representations by compactly induced representations.
arxiv:2611.23831.authors: Zhenghui Li, Benchao Su, Zhixiang Wu

arxiv:2611.23846.title: Defining equations for two-block shallow ReLU pattern varieties
arxiv:2611.23846.summary: We give a complete algebraic characterization of two-block shallow ReLU pattern varieties. We show that the determinantal equations arising from rank constraints imposed by the activation patterns generate the defining ideals, thereby proving a conjecture of Alexandr-Mont\'ufar. The set-theoretic proof uses a characterization of orbit closures of matrix pencils in terms of the Kronecker canonical form.
arxiv:2611.23846.authors: Yulia Alexandr, Moritz Grillo, Thiago Holleben, Guido Mont\'ufar, Teresa Yu

arxiv:2611.23853.title: Graded version of local-global principle for Steinberg and Chevalley groups
arxiv:2611.23853.summary: In this article, an analog of a graded version of Quillen-Suslin's local-global principle was established for Steinberg groups $St(\Phi,-)$ and Chevalley groups $G(\Phi,-)$ over a reduced irreducible root system $\Phi$.

arxiv:2611.23868.title: Generalizing the Gaster--Loustau Theorem via Generalized Discrete Markov Spectra
arxiv:2611.23868.summary: We realize generalized Markov numbers (GM numbers) for arbitrary $k_1,k_2,k_3\in \mathbb Z_{\ge0}$ as $\lambda$-lengths of return arcs on a hyperbolic orbifold constructed from local monodromy matrices. The McShane identity of Tan--Wong--Zhang on this orbifold yields a summation identity with multiplicities for the gaps between the associated Markov--Lagrange constants and their limiting value, together with a summation inequality that counts each distinct value once. These results extend the summation identity and inequality of Gaster and Loustau to generalized Markov numbers.

arxiv:2611.23885.title: Quasi-Bisections of Cubic Graphs with Tree and Circuit Decompositions
arxiv:2611.23885.summary: A $2$-quasi-bisection of a graph is a vertex $2$-coloring in which the color classes differ in size by at most two and every monochromatic component has at most two vertices. Esperet, Mazzuoccolo, and Tarsi in [J. Graph Theory, 86(2017), 149-158] conjectured that every cubic graph admits such a coloring.
arxiv:2611.23885.authors: Xixiong Tang, Rong-Xia Hao, Yilun Luo, Cun-Quan Zhang

arxiv:2611.23899.title: Categorified Koszul duality and deformation theory of higher categories
arxiv:2611.23899.summary: This paper develops a deformation theory for stable $(\infty,n)$-categories for $n > 1$. We introduce the framework of complete $t$-structured stable presentable $(\infty,n)$-categories. Within this setting, we establish a higher categorified Koszul duality among complete $t$-structured presentable $(\infty,n)$-categories.

arxiv:2611.23928.title: Rigidity of randomly perturbed expanding circle maps
arxiv:2611.23928.summary: We extend the classical smooth linearization theory of expanding circle maps to randomly perturbed ones without requiring small perturbations, establishing two equivalent rigidity criteria of absolute continuity of random conjugacy and Lyapunov exponents along random periodic orbits. In the random setting, an essential difficulty is the uniqueness of absolutely continuous random invariant measures. For the first criterion, we overcome this difficulty by refining the memory-loss argument of Ott, Stenlund and Young, which gives the exponential convergence of probability densities, to establish the uniqueness of random invariant measures; for the second criterion, we bypass this difficulty by…
arxiv:2611.23928.authors: Jiangqiong Yu, Sandro Vaienti, Wenmeng Zhang

arxiv:2611.23934.title: What Right-Angle Corners Reveal About an Uncalibrated Camera: Convex Cones, Certified Bounds and Identifiability
arxiv:2611.23934.summary: The corner of a box or a room, where three perpendicular edges meet, appears in an image as three segments meeting at a point. We ask what such junctions reveal about an uncalibrated camera's intrinsic parameters. Each junction is consistent with an explicit convex set of cameras; when only the focal length is unknown, this set is an interval in closed form.

arxiv:2611.24019.title: Covering dense $r$-graphs by perfect matchings
arxiv:2611.24019.summary: For a matching-covered graph $G$, let $\tau(G)$ denote the minimum number of perfect matchings needed to cover all edges of $G$. An $r$-regular graph $G$ is said to be an $r$-graph if $|\partial(X)|\geq r$ for each odd set $X\subseteq V(G)$, where $\partial(X)$ denotes the set of edges with precisely one end in $X$. The generalized Berge conjecture, which was proposed by Mazzuoccolo (J.
arxiv:2611.24019.authors: Jingchao Lai, Danyi Li, Weigen Yan

arxiv:2611.24034.title: Incidence methods for algebraic expanders over arbitrary fields
arxiv:2611.24034.summary: Let $A\subset F$ be finite, $N=|A|$, $p=\operatorname{char}F$ (with $p=\infty$ in characteristic zero), and $L=1+\log(2N)$. In the range $N\le p^{1/2}$, we establish \[ |AA+A|\gg N^{129/85}L^{-72/85}. \] This improves the long-standing $3/2$-exponent bound for $AA+A$ in positive characteristic in the range $N\le p^{1/2}$, without any assumption on the multiplicative doubling of $A$.

arxiv:2611.24036.title: A Geometric Characteristic Long Exact Sequence for Codimension-Two Spin and Pin-plus/minus Bordism
arxiv:2611.24036.summary: Following Botvinnik--Rosenberg \cite{BotvinnikRosenberg2023}, we define fibered-boundary bordism, introduce sphere-bundle bordism, and prove an exact sequence relating them to ordinary bordism. The sequence also holds when all sphere fibers are required to be non-$D^r$-bounding. Following Debray--Ye--Yu \cite{DebrayYeYu2026}, we define characteristic cycles with a chosen complement structure trivializing a characteristic class.

arxiv:2611.24040.title: Stability analysis of stochastic differential equations with the Koopman operator
arxiv:2611.24040.summary: This paper investigates the stability of stochastic systems through the lens of the Koopman operator framework. In particular, we establish the connection between the convergence properties of the Koopman semigroup and specific stability properties of the underlying stochastic system. Moreover, we demonstrate that specific Koopman eigenfunctions capture stochastic attractivity properties and we illustrate these results with two numerical examples.
arxiv:2611.24040.authors: Fran\c{c}ois-Gr\'egoire Bierwart, Ga\"etan Louvet, Alexandre Mauroy

arxiv:2611.24048.title: Tur\'{a}n number of the odd-ballooning of odd prisms
arxiv:2611.24048.summary: The Tur\'{a}n problem for odd-balloonings has been studied for various classes of skeleton graphs, including stars, paths, cycles, trees, bipartite graphs, and certain 3-chromatic graphs. The Tur\'{a}n numbers and extremal graphs for odd prisms have also been determined. Motivated by these developments, we investigate the Tur\'{a}n problem for prescribed odd-balloonings of odd prisms.
arxiv:2611.24048.authors: Wenwen Chen, Longfei Fang, Yuke Zhang

arxiv:2611.24066.title: The Borel Ruziewicz problem
arxiv:2611.24066.summary: We prove that for $n\ge2$ the normalized surface measure is the only rotation-invariant finitely additive probability measure on the Borel subsets of $\mathbb S^n$, and that for $d\ge3$ Lebesgue measure is the only finitely additive measure on the bounded Borel subsets of $\mathbb{R}^d$ which is invariant under orientation-preserving isometries and normalized on the unit cube. This answers the Borel version of the Ruziewicz problem. On $\mathbb S^n$ it suffices to assume invariance under a finite set of rotations with a spectral gap, and on $\mathbb{R}^d$ under two such sets of rotations about two distinct centres.

arxiv:2611.24087.title: Unboundedness of regular del Pezzo surfaces over imperfect fields
arxiv:2611.24087.summary: Over an F-finite field, regular del Pezzo surfaces are bounded. Over a non-F-finite field of characteristic two or three, regular del Pezzo surfaces are unbounded.

arxiv:2611.24131.title: Non-bipartite spectral extremal graphs forbidding a three-chromatic color-critical graph
arxiv:2611.24131.summary: A graph is color-critical if it contains at least one color-critical edge. For every fixed three-chromatic color-critical graph $H$, we determine the maximum spectral radius of an $n$-vertex non-bipartite $H$-free graph and characterize the unique extremal graph for all sufficiently large $n$. The extremal graph belongs to one of three graph families: $J_n(s,t)$, $\mathrm{ST}_2(n-1)$ or $L_n(s,t)$.
arxiv:2611.24131.authors: Bo Dong, Cunxiang Duan, Attila Sali, Ligong Wang

arxiv:2611.24139.title: Canonical weight-two algebras and strongly generated vertex operator superalgebras
arxiv:2611.24139.summary: This paper studies vertex operator superalgebras strongly generated by their weight-1, weight-$\frac{3}{2}$ and weight-2 homogeneous subspaces. The presence of a nontrivial weight-1 subspace introduces derivative and quadratic current terms in weight-2. To address this, we use low-weight quasi-primary projections to identify two canonical commutative associative algebras, $\mathcal{A}$ and $A$, within the weight-2 subspace.

arxiv:2611.24183.title: On the slope stability of vector bundles on Sasakian manifolds
arxiv:2611.24183.summary: We study the variation problem of slope stability of $T$-linearized sheaves on a compact Sasakian manifold, or more generally, on an affine variety with a good $T$-action. In particular, we establish the wall-and-chamber structure for the slope stability of $T$-linearized torsion-free sheaves.

arxiv:2611.24186.title: Note on parallel transport of IHS manifolds of Kummer type
arxiv:2611.24186.summary: We give a characterization of parallel transport operators for irreducible holomorphic symplectic manifolds of Kummer type.

arxiv:2611.24199.title: Critical spectral weights on triangulated disk
arxiv:2611.24199.summary: We solve the common-positive-weight support problem at the local spectral threshold 1/2 for relative triangulated disks with interior degrees at most five and an empty or connected degree-five core. We characterize feasibility by a finite decomposition into three elementary pieces and a condition on the original boundary marking. The proof passes from spectral equality to a positive conjugate rectangle, then uses geometric reductions to obtain a serial presentation.

arxiv:2611.24237.title: A semialgebraic description of matrices of positive semidefinite rank at most 2
arxiv:2611.24237.summary: The main result of this paper is a semialgebraic description of the set of matrices of rank at most 3 and psd rank at most 2. Such a semialgebraic description allows one to check whether a matrix has rank at most 3 and psd rank at most 2. This description builds on the geometric characterization of matrices of rank 3 and psd rank 2 using the existence of an ellipse nested between two polygons.
arxiv:2611.24237.authors: Kaie Kubjas, Lilja Mets\"alampi, Milo Orlich

arxiv:2611.24238.title: Counting shorter even cycles in graphs forbidding an even cycle
arxiv:2611.24238.summary: For graphs $H$ and $F$, the generalized Tur\'an number $\operatorname{ex}(n,H,F)$ is the maximum number of copies of $H$ in an $n$-vertex $F$-free graph. Let $C_m$ be a cycle on $m$ vertices. Liu and Wu (2026) proved that, for fixed integers $k>\ell\ge 2$, $\operatorname{ex}(n,C_{2\ell},C_{2k})=\left(\frac{(k-1)_\ell}{2\ell}+o(1)\right)n^\ell$, where $(k-1)_\ell=(k-1)\cdots(k-\ell)$.

arxiv:2611.24250.title: Grade Restriction Rule For D-Brane Transport In Non-Abelian Gauged Linear Sigma Models
arxiv:2611.24250.summary: We study the low energy behaviour of B-type D-branes in non-Abelian gauged linear sigma models. The main problem is to determine the grade restriction rule for D-brane transport from one phase to another along paths. We analyze the convergence condition of the integral for the hemisphere partition function.
arxiv:2611.24250.authors: Richard Eager, Kentaro Hori, Johanna Knapp, Mauricio Romo

arxiv:2611.24286.title: A characterization of uniformly discrete crystalline measures with unit weights
arxiv:2611.24286.summary: We prove that every uniformly discrete set $\emptyset\ne\Lambda\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ admitting a Fourier summation formula with a discrete set of frequencies $S(\Lambda)\subset\mathbb{R}^d$ arises from the Alon--Kummer--Kurasov--Vinzant construction using a Lee--Yang variety. In particular, every crystalline measure with uniformly discrete support and unit weights is a Fourier quasicrystal coming from the above construction. It also implies that every set $\Lambda\subset\mathbb{R}^d\subset\mathbb{C}^d$ as above is the common zero set in $\mathbb{C}^d$ of finitely many trigonometric polynomials, extending the one-dimensional theorem of Olevskii and Ulanovskii.

arxiv:2611.24292.title: Smooth minimal fourfolds not connected by smooth elementary flops
arxiv:2611.24292.summary: We first construct two smooth projective toric fourfolds of Picard number eight that are connected by elementary flops, but cannot be connected by elementary flops through smooth complete toric varieties. This answers a question raised by the first author in 2004. Then, by taking suitable double covers, we construct two smooth projective minimal fourfolds of general type with Picard number nine that are connected by elementary flops, but cannot be connected by elementary flops through smooth projective varieties.

arxiv:2611.24295.title: A Well-Separated Pair Decomposition of Linear Size for Unit-Disk Graphs
arxiv:2611.24295.summary: We prove that every connected Euclidean-weighted unit-disk graph on $n$ vertices has a $(1/\varepsilon)$-well-separated pair decomposition of size $O(n\varepsilon^{-2}\log(1/\varepsilon))$. This resolves an open problem posed by Gao and Zhang in 2003. We also show that this bound is tight: there are connected unit-disk graphs for which any $(1/\varepsilon)$-well-separated pair decomposition has size $\Omega(n\varepsilon^{-2}\log (1/\varepsilon))$.
arxiv:2611.24295.authors: Mark de Berg, Joachim Gudmundsson, Sampson Wong

arxiv:2611.24297.title: Two results on rich-neighbour $5$-colouring of subcubic graphs
arxiv:2611.24297.summary: A rich-neighbour edge-colouring is a proper edge-colouring in which every non-isolated edge has an adjacent edge whose neighbours have pairwise distinct colours. Petru\v{s}evski and \v{S}krekovski conjectured that every connected subcubic loopless multigraph distinct from $K_4$ admits such a colouring with five colours. We prove the conjecture for two classes: claw-free subcubic loopless multigraphs and $2$-connected subcubic outerplanar loopless multigraphs.
arxiv:2611.24297.authors: Masaki Kashima, Mirko Petru\v{s}evski, Jelena Sedlar, Riste \v{S}krekovski

arxiv:2611.24299.title: Boundaries of groups with compact-by-amenable decomposition
arxiv:2611.24299.summary: We look at the Liouville property (triviality of harmonic functions) of topological groups G relative to a compact subgroup K. We show that Gelfand pairs have this property. Furthermore, we show that this property holds if and only if G admits a product decomposition G = K S for an amenable subgroup S.

arxiv:2611.24322.title: Power projections, Gram structures, and finite-field lifting of Butson Hadamard matrices
arxiv:2611.24322.summary: In this paper we investigate the algebraic properties of Hadamard powers of Butson Hadamard matrices $H\in \mathrm{BH}(n,3p)$, and show that for certain parameter values the cube root projection matrix $H^{\circ p}$ has the same structure as the adjacency matrix of a strongly regular graph. Then, by using a simple eigenvalue analysis we show, among other results, the nonexistence of $\mathrm{BH}(17,15)$ matrices. For other parameter values, a more in-depth study and in particular, a complete classification of all possible projection matrices is necessary.
arxiv:2611.24322.authors: Wojciech Bruzda, Domonkos Czifra, Ilona Nagy, Ferenc Sz\"oll\H{o}si

arxiv:2611.24343.title: Intersections of Odd Polygons Revisited
arxiv:2611.24343.summary: It is shown that the maximum number of intersection points between the boundaries of a simple $m$-gon and a simple $n$-gon is $mn-(m+n)+3$ for any odd integers $m,n \ge 3$. The previous best upper bound was $mn-(m+n)+C$, for some huge constant $C$.

arxiv:2611.24349.title: Topological aspects of generalized Sklyanin algebras
arxiv:2611.24349.summary: We are concerned with the topology of Casimir foliations of Sklyanin algebras and their certain generalizations. In particular, we give a complete description of the topological types and bifurcations of Casimir leaves of the original Sklyanin algebras, which improves and extends analogous results from the original papers of E. Sklyanin.

arxiv:2611.24361.title: Generic vanishing and singularities of theta divisors
arxiv:2611.24361.summary: We study the connection between the generic vanishing conjecture for subvarieties of principally polarized abelian varieties and various predictions about the singularities of theta divisors. We deduce new cases of a conjecture on the multiplicities of points on irreducible theta divisors, as well as Beauville's conjecture characterizing Jacobians by the size of their theta singularity loci.

arxiv:2611.24365.title: Lelong Numbers Above an Arbitrary Bound and Plane Curves
arxiv:2611.24365.summary: Let $T$ be a positive closed current of bidimension $(1,1)$ with unit mass on $\mathbb P^2$ and $E^+_{\alpha}(T)$ be the upper level sets of Lelong numbers $\nu(T,x)$ of $T$. For any $\alpha\geq \frac{3}{d+5}$, $d\in \mathbb Z^+$ we show that $|E^+_{\alpha}(T)\setminus C|\leq 2$ for a curve $C$ of degree $d$. As a corollary of this result, we obtain a quantative lower bound for the integrability exponent at any point away from the curve $C$ and a two point set $P$.

arxiv:2611.24389.title: Phase factors and optimal seminorms for polynomial averages of commuting transformations
arxiv:2611.24389.summary: For invertible commuting measure-preserving transformations $T_1, \ldots, T_\ell$ on a standard probability space, we study polynomial averages along both integers and primes. We provide a rank-based criterion ensuring that, even when the polynomials are linearly dependent, finite-order phase factors are characteristic factors. For polynomials with integer coefficients and zero constant terms, it suffices that the dimension of the space spanned (over $\mathbb{Q}$) by any nonempty subfamily of $k$ polynomials exceeds $k/2$.

arxiv:2611.24432.title: Induced matching treewidth in classes with a forbidden structure
arxiv:2611.24432.summary: Induced matching treewidth is a tree-decomposition based parameter where we bound the size of an induced matching whose every edge intersects a single bag of the decomposition. It is known that many computational problems can be solved efficiently in graphs of bounded induced matching treewidth. In this paper we are interested in understanding what classes of graphs have bounded induced matching treewidth.
arxiv:2611.24432.authors: Valia Mitsou, Pawe{\l} Rz\k{a}\.zewski, Giannos Stamoulis

arxiv:2611.24441.title: An additive-square-free word over an alphabet of size 6
arxiv:2611.24441.summary: An additive square over $\mathbb{N}$ is two consecutive nonempty blocks of the same length and same sum. For example, 1423 is an additive square, since 14 and 23 both have length 2 and sum 5. Solving a problem that has been open for more than 50 years, we give an example of an infinite word over a 6-letter subset of N that avoids additive squares.

arxiv:2611.24442.title: Asymptotics of linear normal lambda terms: WKB structure, Airy turning point and a positive recurrence
arxiv:2611.24442.summary: Let a n be the number of closed linear $\lambda$-terms in $\beta$-normal form with n variable occurrences. We prove is the large-order constant of the Riccati-Airy sequence K m attached to the turning point of the WKB expansion. We show that the K m are exactly rescaled coefficients of the formal logarithmic derivative of the Airy asymptotic series, and deduce $\kappa$ $\infty$ = 1/(2$\pi$) from the explicit Airy coefficients.

arxiv:2611.24447.title: Finite-dimensional Hopf algebras generated by the coradical
arxiv:2611.24447.summary: Let $H$ be a finite-dimensional Hopf algebra over a field $k$. The paper is concerned with the question of when $H$ is generated by the coradical $H_0$. We give several characterizations of this property, involving the largest Hopf ideal contained in the Jacobson radical $J(H^*)$ and the coefficient coalgebra of the injective hull of the trivial comodule.

arxiv:2611.24452.title: An Explicit Uniform Connectivity Bound for Generalized Markoff Graphs
arxiv:2611.24452.summary: Let $X_D$ be the surface $x^2+y^2+z^2-xyz=D$ over $\mathbb F_p$. For every prime $p>10^{320}$ and every $D\in\mathbb F_p\setminus\{4\}$, we prove that the three Vieta involutions act transitively on the trace triples of generating pairs of $\mathrm{SL}_2(\mathbb F_p)$. The proof combines an explicit primitive-fiber argument, Chen's orbit-size lower bound, and a weighted maximal-divisor estimate.

arxiv:2611.24456.title: Tropical Geometry of $G_2$
arxiv:2611.24456.summary: We tropicalize the Grassmannian and the flag variety of the algebraic group of type $G_2$. The two tropical varieties are strictly contained in the associated Dressians. Their points are trees in the $G_2$-forest and decorated trees in the $G_2$-orchard.
arxiv:2611.24456.authors: Michael Joswig, Kevin Kuehn, Bernd Sturmfels, Mathieu Vall\'ee

arxiv:2611.24471.title: Semi-exact functors and the conjecture of Coulembier and Flake
arxiv:2611.24471.summary: We introduce the notion of semi-exact functors between abelian categories, which are characterised by either preserving or breaking exactness of sequences. We prove semi-exact functors are always exact with respect to a canonically determined exact structure. For a symmetric tensor category $\Cs$, we define a support theory by considering all $\Bbbk$-linear symmetric monoidal, semi-exact functors $\mathscr{C}\to\operatorname{Ver}_{p^\infty}$ up to equivalence, and conjecture that it agrees with the Balmer spectrum of the stable category when $\mathscr{C}$ is finite.

arxiv:2611.24477.title: The isolation number of uniform hypertrees
arxiv:2611.24477.summary: An isolating set of a hypergraph $H$ is a vertex set whose closed neighbourhood intersects every edge of $H$. The isolation number $\iota(H)$ is the minimum cardinality of such a set. Let $r\ge3$, and let $T$ be an $r$-uniform hypergraph whose incidence graph is a tree.
arxiv:2611.24477.authors: Minhui Li, Shumin Zhang, Junhao Qu

arxiv:2611.24480.title: A Cohen--Macaulay Analogue of the Brodmann--Rotthaus Theorem
arxiv:2611.24480.summary: We prove a Cohen--Macaulay analogue of the theorem of Brodmann and Rotthaus on the lifting of quasi-excellence. More precisely, let $A$ be a Noetherian ring and let $I$ be an ideal contained in the Jacobson radical of $A$. We show that if $A/I$ is $\mathsf{CM}$-Q0 and $A$ is a $\mathsf{CM}$\textnormal{-G-}ring, then $A$ is $\mathsf{CM}$-quasi-excellent.

arxiv:2611.24504.title: A combinatorial proof of a symmetric joint distribution on strict binary trees
arxiv:2611.24504.summary: Nonplanar strict binary trees on $2n+1$ vertices are enumerated by the reduced tangent numbers $T_{2n+1}/2^n$, whose entries are refined by Poupard's triangle. Poupard defined the end of the minimal chain ($\mathrm{eoc}$) and the parent of the maximum leaf ($\mathrm{pom}$) on these trees, proving that $\mathrm{eoc}$ and $\mathrm{pom}+1$ share this triangular distribution. Foata and Han subsequently showed via tree calculus and partial difference equations that the joint distribution of $(\mathrm{eoc}, 2n+1-\mathrm{pom})$ is symmetric.

arxiv:2611.24505.title: Katona's Shadow Equality Persists under Bounded VC-Dimension
arxiv:2611.24505.summary: Katona's intersecting-shadow theorem states that every $t$-intersecting $r$-uniform family has size at most that of its $(r-t)$-shadow, with equality precisely for complete $r$-uniform families on $2r-t$ points. We prove that both the shadow inequality and its equality classification remain valid under the substantially weaker assumption that the VC-dimension is at most $r-t$. By contrast, bounded VC-dimension and $t$-intersection do not, in general, yield the same extremal bounds in the corresponding cardinality problem.

arxiv:2611.24516.title: Nine-Colored Partition Components Modulo 19
arxiv:2611.24516.summary: Let $p_{m}(n)$ be the number of partitions of $n$ into parts of $m$ colors, and let $y=q^{19}$. Starting from Winquist's identity, as Hirschhorn did for the modulus $11$, we express each of the nineteen components of $(q;q)_{\infty}^{10}$ modulo $19$ as a sum of two quartic products of the theta functions $(y^{a};y^{19})_{\infty}(y^{19-a};y^{19})_{\infty}$, and deduce all nineteen generating functions $\sum_{n} p_{9}(19n+r)y^{n}$ modulo $19$ in closed form. The vanishing class $p_{9}(19n+17)$ is the one known previously.

arxiv:2611.24532.title: Cosmetic crossings and the knot complement problem
arxiv:2611.24532.summary: We prove the cosmetic crossing conjecture, Problem 1.58 in Kirby's list, and the generalized cosmetic crossing conjecture for every knot whose branched double cover is an L-space; in particular, both hold for all alternating and all quasi-alternating knots. We also prove the oriented knot complement conjecture, Problem 1.81(D), for all closed 3-manifolds with finite fundamental group, in particular for all lens spaces: in such a manifold, every knot whose exterior is irreducible and not a solid torus is determined by its complement. Both results rest on a monotonicity theorem for Heegaard Floer correction terms: if a knot in a rational homology sphere has an isotropic, nonzero homology…

arxiv:2611.24539.title: Torsion order and the next-to-top term of knot Floer homology
arxiv:2611.24539.summary: Sivek conjectured that, for every nontrivial knot $K\subset S^3$, the dimension of the next-to-top term of $\widehat{\mathrm{HFK}}(K)$ is at least that of the top term. We show that this inequality holds for knots with $U$-torsion order one in either the minus theory $\mathrm{HFK}^-$ or the unoriented theory $\mathrm{HFK}'$. Combined with Eftekhary's work, this implies that knots with rational unknotting number one satisfy the conjecture.

arxiv:2611.24544.title: Treewidth 3 in the Product Structure Theorem for Bounded Degree Graphs in Minor-Closed Classes
arxiv:2611.24544.summary: We show that, for all positive integers $t$ and $\Delta$, there exists an integer $c$ such that, for every $K_t$-minor-free graph $G$ with maximum degree at most $\Delta$, there exists a graph $H$ of treewidth at most $3$ and a path $P$ such that $G$ is isomorphic to a subgraph of the strong product $H\boxtimes P\boxtimes K_c$. This improves on a previous result of Dujumovi\'c, Esperet, Micek, Walczak, and Wood (2022) by bounding the treewidth of $H$ independently of $t$ and $\Delta$. As an immediate consequence we obtain a bound of $O(r^4)$ on the $r$-weak colouring number of bounded-degree graphs from any proper minor-closed graph class.
arxiv:2611.24544.authors: Vida Dujmovi\'c, Robert Hickingbotham, Pat Morin, David R. Wood

arxiv:2611.24563.title: Positivity and uniform log-concavity for rank-two Chern coefficients
arxiv:2611.24563.summary: We study the binomial-basis coefficients in the Schur expansion of the Chern classes of symmetric powers of a rank-two bundle. B\'erczi and Feh\'er conjectured that these coefficients are nonnegative and log-concave in the Newton index. An inverse-series formula yields an integral gamma-positive refinement with exact support and a positive expression for the derivatives of the shifted Chern quotient.

arxiv:2611.24564.title: Asymptotic probabilities in random Latin squares
arxiv:2611.24564.summary: We introduce some new general techniques for studying asymptotic probabilities in random Latin squares. Using these techniques, we obtain an asymptotic formula for the probability that a given 'small' partial Latin square $H$ is present in a uniformly random $n\times n$ Latin square (as conjectured by Divoux-Kelly-Kennedy-Sidhu). As applications, we determine which configurations are likely to appear in random Latin squares (resolving a conjecture of Allsop-Morris), we determine the asymptotic distribution of the number of $3\times 3$ Latin subsquares in a uniformly random $n\times n$ Latin square (resolving conjectures of McKay-Wanless and Kwan-Sah-Sawhney), and we show that the first two…
arxiv:2611.24564.authors: Lenka Kopfov\'a, Matthew Kwan, Richard Montgomery, Kalina Petrova

arxiv:2611.24570.title: Cox rings of Jacobian elliptic surfaces of Kodaira dimension one
arxiv:2611.24570.summary: We study Cox rings of relatively minimal semistable Jacobian elliptic surfaces over $\mathbb P^1$ with $\chi=\chi(\mathcal O_X)\ge3$ and finite Mordell--Weil group. When the Mori cone is generated by the zero section and the reducible-fiber components, we give a finite criterion for Cox-ring generation: a numerically determined set of nef classes must admit sections nonvanishing along the zero section. The criterion supplies a minimal homogeneous generating set without assuming finite generation in advance.

arxiv:2611.24574.title: The number of cycles in a random 2-factor of a random regular graph
arxiv:2611.24574.summary: We study the number of cycles $X$ in a uniformly random 2-factor $F$ of a random $d$-regular graph on $n$ vertices (in the pairing model) for any fixed $d\ge 3$. When the pairing $P$ and the 2-factor $F\subseteq P$ are chosen uniformly at random together, the probability generating function of $X$ is $\Gamma(n+\tfrac u2)\Gamma(\tfrac12)/\bigl(\Gamma(n+\tfrac12)\Gamma(\tfrac u2)\bigr)$, which does not depend on $d$. Consequently, $X$ has mean $\tfrac12\log n+O(1)$ and variance $\tfrac12\log n+O(1)$, satisfies a central limit theorem, and equals $1$ (so that $F$ is a Hamilton cycle) with probability $\Theta(n^{-1/2})$.

arxiv:2611.24587.title: A limit theorem for deviation of ergodic integrals on a class of flows on the two-torus
arxiv:2611.24587.summary: We study the fluctuations of ergodic integrals for locally Hamiltonian flows on the two-torus with a single non-degenerate saddle (Arnol'd flows). We sample a flow from a suitably random family, together with a base point $p$ chosen uniformly at random on that flow's domain. For a smooth observable $f$, we show that the centered Birkhoff integral $\int_{0}^t f(\phi_s p)\,ds-t\bar f$, where $\bar f$ is the spatial mean of $f$, normalized by $(\log t)^2$, converges in distribution to the product of two independent random variables.

arxiv:2611.24589.title: Quasimonomial Monge--Amp\`ere equations for big classes
arxiv:2611.24589.summary: Let X be a normal projective variety over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero. We describe an alternative approach to a differentiability result of volumes of norms defined by finitely many quasimonomial valuations. As a consequence, we prove the non-Archimedean Calabi--Yau theorem for quasimonomial measures on $X$ with respect to big classes, in the trivially valued case.

arxiv:2611.24593.title: The number of $k$-factors of a random regular graph
arxiv:2611.24593.summary: Let $Z_k(G)$ be the number of $k$-factors ($k$-regular spanning subgraphs) of a uniformly random simple $d$-regular graph $G\sim G(n,d)$, where $d\ge 3$ and $1\le k\le d-1$ are fixed integers such that $dn$ and $kn$ are even. We determine the asymptotic second moment of $Z_k(G)$ and show that $Z_k(G)/\mathbb{E} Z_k(G)$ converges in distribution to an explicit random variable $W$ that depends on the short-cycle counts of $G$ but not on $k$. Moreover, for any $1\le k,\ell\le d-1$, the normalised counts on the same graph satisfy $Z_k(G)/\mathbb{E} Z_k(G) - Z_\ell(G)/\mathbb{E} Z_\ell(G) \to 0$ in probability, and, since $W>0$ almost surely, their ratio converges to $1$ in probability.

arxiv:2611.24595.title: Asymptotics for generalized integer partitions
arxiv:2611.24595.summary: We study the asymptotic behavior of weighted partition functions $p_f(n)$, defined by the generating function $\prod_{n \geq 1} (1 - q^{n})^{-f(n)}$ with non-negative real weights $f(n)$. We assume that the associated Dirichlet series $D(s) = \sum_{n \geq 1} f(n) n^{-s}$ admits a meromorphic continuation to a half-plane $\Re(s) \geq -\varepsilon$, with finitely many real poles of arbitrary orders, the largest of which is a positive pole $\alpha$ of order $k$, and a possibly infinite collection of complex poles lying strictly to the left of $\alpha$, with some additional conditions. We extend the saddle-point method of Debruyne and Tenenbaum, and show that the pole $\alpha$ dominates the…

arxiv:2611.24606.title: Combinatorial Properties of The Giant Under Supercritical Percolation
arxiv:2611.24606.summary: We study combinatorial properties, such as diameter and long paths and cycles, of the giant component of percolated graphs. Such combinatorial properties are well studied for classical graphs such as pseudo-random graphs and the hypercube. We aim to obtain similar results for extensive families of $d$-regular $n$-vertex graphs.
arxiv:2611.24606.authors: Sahar Diskin, Mihyun Kang, Michael Krivelevich, Itay Markbreit

arxiv:2611.24613.title: Dessins d'Enfants as a Topological Lens on Temporal Hypergraphs
arxiv:2611.24613.summary: Hypergraphs are the natural language for group interactions, and topological data analysis has given us several ways to look at them: simplicial and cell complexes, persistent homology, and sheaves. All of these treat a hyperedge as an unordered set. In this paper, we introduce a different and, to our knowledge, new viewpoint that comes from Grothendieck's theory of dessins d'enfants and, unlike these approaches, takes into account the order in which vertices appear in each hyperedge and hyperedges appear around each vertex.

arxiv:2611.24652.title: Infinite-dimensional invariant tori for the perturbed modified KdV equation
arxiv:2611.24652.summary: In this paper, we consider the perturbed modified KdV equation $u_t=-u_{xxx}+6u^2u_x+\partial_x(u^5)$ on the circle, without external parameters. We prove that it admits plenty of almost periodic solutions.

arxiv:2611.24665.title: Uniformly positive entropy and mixing in minimal systems
arxiv:2611.24665.summary: Every minimal system with uniformly positive entropy of order two is topologically mixing. In a minimal system, mixing along an infinite set $A\subset\N_0$ is equivalent to $\dist(T^nU,T^nV)\to0$ along $A$ for all nonempty open $U,V$, and to unbounded complexity of each standard binary open cover along every infinite subset of $A$. For $A=\N_0$ it is also equivalent to $\Delta^*$-transitivity.

arxiv:2611.24670.title: Real Fr{\o}yshov invariants and lattice homology
arxiv:2611.24670.summary: For a class of almost rational plumbing 4-manifolds equipped with smooth involutions, we give a description of the Real Fr{\o}yshov invariants of their boundaries in terms of lattice homology. Our approach uses the $S^1$-stable equivalence between Seiberg-Witten Floer spectra and lattice spectra constructed by Dai-Sasahira-Stoffregen, and the $\operatorname{O}(2)$-equivariant versions of these spectra developed by Kang-Park-Taniguchi. As applications, we derive a formula for these invariants for every $\operatorname{spin}^c$ structure on the double branched covers of even torus knots $T_{2p,q}$, and determine the smooth nonorientable $4$-genus of an infinite family of torus knots $T_{4,q}$.
