arxiv:2611.24679.title: Unbounded traces, Connes' index theorem for measured foliations, and the Godbillon-Vey invariant in KK-theory
arxiv:2611.24679.summary: We prove that unbounded positive traces define KK-elements with real coefficients. Such traces naturally arise from invariant transverse measures on foliations (Connes, 1979) and, more generally, on Lie groupoids (Crainic--Mestre, 2019). As an application, we build a canonical KK-element with real coefficients whose associated map of K-groups is the Godbillon-Vey invariant as constructed by Connes.
arxiv:2611.24679.authors: Paolo Antonini, Sara Azzali, Georges Skandalis

arxiv:2611.24680.title: A stratified version of geometric realizations
arxiv:2611.24680.summary: Given a simplicial set $X$, let $\operatorname{B}({X})$ denote its poset of nondegenerate simplices. We define a natural stratification $\left\vert{X}\right\vert\rightarrow\operatorname{B}({X})$. When $X$ is locally finite, we prove that this stratification is conical.

arxiv:2611.24690.title: An $\infty$-category approach to $A_\infty$-algebras and $A_\infty$-categories
arxiv:2611.24690.summary: $A_\infty$-algebras over a commutative ring $R$ are generalizations of $R$-algebras in which multiplication is only associative up to higher homotopies. Similarly, $A_\infty$-categories over $R$ are generalizations of $R$-linear categories in which composition of morphisms is only associative up to higher homotopies. They are important in the definition of Fukaya categories in Symplectic Geometry, and in other areas of mathematics.

arxiv:2611.24692.title: Combinatorial Bloch-Gieseker inequalities on toric surfaces
arxiv:2611.24692.summary: We give a combinatorial proof of the Bloch-Gieseker inequalities in the special case of ample toric vector bundles on toric surfaces via a new rearrangement inequality for planar curves. Using this we establish the Hodge package for combinatorial analogues of cohomology rings of ample projective bundles over toric surfaces which don't appear to arise from matroidal constructions.

arxiv:2611.24695.title: Singularities of ideals with minimal tangent space dimension in the Hilbert scheme of points on a threefold
arxiv:2611.24695.summary: We classify all singular monomial ideals in the Hilbert scheme of $d$ points on $\mathbb{A}^3$ whose tangent spaces have the minimal dimension $3d+6$. There are two families called the opera houses and rotating staircases, and we give their combinatorial and algebraic descriptions. All the opera houses are in one linkage class, and their singularities are smoothly equivalent to the vertex of a cone over the Grassmannian $\mathrm{Gr}(2,6) \hookrightarrow \mathbb{P}^{14}$ in its Pl\"ucker embedding.

arxiv:2611.24703.title: A simplicial model for manifold calculus through the configuration category
arxiv:2611.24703.summary: Let $M$ be a closed $d$-dimensional smooth manifold and $X:\Delta^{op}\rightarrow\operatorname{Fin}$ a finite simplicial set whose geometric realization is homeomorphic to $M$. Given the $\infty$-category $\mathcal{D}\mathrm{isk}_{/M}$ of disks embedded in $M$ and the path components functor $\pi_0:\mathcal{D}\mathrm{isk}_{/M}\rightarrow\operatorname{Fin}$, we construct a cofinal functor $\Gamma_X:\Delta^{op}\rightarrow\mathcal{D}\mathrm{isk}_{/M}$ such that $X=\pi_0\circ\Gamma_X$. This result provides an alternative construction of a simplicial model developed by Boavida de Brito, Lambrechts, Pryor and Songhafouo Tsopm\'en\'e to compute the space-valued presheaf…

arxiv:2611.24704.title: Efficient orders for reciprocal matrices with block structure
arxiv:2611.24704.summary: We consider block partitioned reciprocal matrices. For these matrices, we characterize the efficient vectors whose subvectors, corresponding to principal blocks, are positive multiples of given efficient vectors for those blocks. This generalizes a prior, scalar oriented, extension theorem.

arxiv:2611.24709.title: The computational complexity of Undirected Vertex Geography with maximum height 3
arxiv:2611.24709.summary: The impartial game Undirected Vertex Geography is known to be polynomial time solvable. The variant in which vertices are assigned heights with maximum value m that reduce by 1 whenever the token is moved from that vertex, denoted UIRm, is known to be polynomial time solvable when m=2 and PSPACE-complete when m=4. We solve the open question of the computational complexity of UIR3 by a reduction from Directed vertex geography, and show that the complexity holds when the underlying graph is planar and (a) has degree at most 3, (b) is bipartite with maximum degree 4, or (c) is bipartite with maximum degree 5 and only has heights of 1 and 3.

arxiv:2611.24716.title: The Lyapunov and uniform spectra
arxiv:2611.24716.summary: The \textit{Lyapunov spectrum} of a linear cocycle (or vector bundle) is the set of Lyapunov vectors with respect to all ergodic probability measures for the base topological dynamical system. This spectrum disregards trajectories that are atypical from the measure-theoretic viewpoint, and so it is in general insufficient to determine important properties of the cocycle, such as existence of dominated splittings. We resolve this deficiency by introducing a larger set which we call the \textit{uniform spectrum} of the cocycle.

arxiv:2611.24717.title: On automorphisms of symplectic varieties acting trivially on the second cohomology group
arxiv:2611.24717.summary: We prove that the group of automorphisms acting trivially on the torsion-free part of the integral second cohomology on a primitive symplectic variety is a locally trivial deformation invariant. We exhibit some examples of this invariant.

arxiv:2611.24720.title: Balanced Simplicial Complexes for the $\gamma$-Vectors of Zig-Zag Eulerian Polynomials
arxiv:2611.24720.summary: In this paper, we construct a simplicial complex whose $f$-vector equals the $\gamma$-vector of the descent polynomial of an arbitrary canonically labeled rank-one poset. As an application, we prove Petersen and Zhuang's conjecture that the $\gamma$-vector of the normalized zig-zag Eulerian polynomial is the $f$-vector of a balanced simplicial complex.

arxiv:2611.24724.title: On a Secretary Problem with Two Equal-Sized Pools of Candidates
arxiv:2611.24724.summary: This paper presents the solution of a secretary type problem where the decision maker observes a sequence of offers of two types. There are N objects of both types and these objects appear to the decision maker in random order. Objects can only be compared when they are of the same type.
arxiv:2611.24724.authors: David M. Ramsey, Ma\l gorzata Kuchta, Micha{\l} Morayne, Ma\l gorzata Sulkowska

arxiv:2611.24725.title: An Atiyah--Hirzebruch to Adams map and the hastened Adams spectral sequence for supercohomology
arxiv:2611.24725.summary: We construct a map of filtered spectra inducing a map from the Atiyah--Hirzebruch spectral sequence (AHSS) to the Baker--Lazarev Adams spectral sequence of a $\mathit{ko}$-module $M$. Using this and a theorem of Bruner--Rognes, we construct a hastened Adams spectral sequence (HASS) for the Postnikov truncations of $\mathit{ko}$ and the connective Adams summand. Then, motivated by questions in quantum field theory, topological phases of matter, and tensor category theory, we apply the HASS to supercohomology, the cohomology theory $I_{\mathbb{C}^\times}(\tau_{\le 2}\mathit{ko})$, and observe that in examples of interest it is easier to calculate with than either the AHSS or the usual Adams…
arxiv:2611.24725.authors: Arun Debray, Weicheng Ye, Matthew Yu

arxiv:2611.24732.title: Slope stability for normal varieties
arxiv:2611.24732.summary: In this expository paper, we review the theory of slope stability of torsion-free sheaves with respect to nef curve classes and extend it to normal varieties.
arxiv:2611.24732.authors: Eric Jovinelly, Brian Lehmann, Eric Riedl

arxiv:2611.24735.title: A disproof of the El-Zahar--Erd\H{o}s conjecture
arxiv:2611.24735.summary: El-Zahar and Erd\H{o}s asked whether every graph of bounded clique number and sufficiently large chromatic number contains two vertex-disjoint induced subgraphs, each of large chromatic number, with no edge between them. We give a negative answer even for triangle-free graphs. For every integer $g \ge 4$, we show by a probabilistic argument that there exist graphs of girth at least $g$ and arbitrarily large chromatic number in which any two vertex-disjoint induced subgraphs that each require at least seven colors are joined by an edge.

arxiv:2611.24740.title: An Upper Bound on the Proportional Choice Number of a Graph
arxiv:2611.24740.summary: Proportional choosability is a list analogue of equitable coloring introduced in 2019 that imposes both upper and lower bounds on color class sizes based on the availability of each color. The proportional choice number of a graph $G$, denoted by $\chi_{pc}(G)$, is the smallest positive integer $k$ such that $G$ is proportionally $k$-choosable. A recently proposed conjecture states that for any graph $G$ with at least one edge, $\chi_{pc}(G) \leq \Delta(G) + \text{col}(G) - 1$, where $\Delta(G)$ is the maximum degree of $G$ and $\text{col}(G)$ is its coloring number.

arxiv:2611.24751.title: On the asymmetry polynomial of Schubert varieties
arxiv:2611.24751.summary: Let $W$ be a finite Weyl group with length function $\ell$ and longest element $w_0$. For $w\in W$, let $P_w(q)$ be the Poincar\'e polynomial of the Schubert variety $X_w$. We introduce its asymmetry polynomial $D_w(q):=q^{\ell(w)}P_w(q^{-1})-P_w(q)$.
arxiv:2611.24751.authors: Gaston Burrull, Zhitong Alex Li, Shixuan Zeng, Xinyuan Zhang

arxiv:2611.24752.title: Learning the Anyon Atlas
arxiv:2611.24752.summary: We extend our previous search for the modular data of topological quantum field theories in 2+1 dimensions from 22 to 42 anyons, identifying 150,679 new modular data. We do so by adding to our algorithm three rejection gates, two of them based on logistic regression, that discard representations of $SL(2,\mathbb{Z})$ unlikely to yield modular data. We estimate that roughly 80% of the modular data between ranks 23 and 42 has been identified after closing under known constructions.
arxiv:2611.24752.authors: Jonah Berean-Dutcher, Clay Cordova, Julio Parra-Martinez, Richard Tuddenham, Zekai Zhu

arxiv:2611.24753.title: Computing $F$-Symbols from Modular Data
arxiv:2611.24753.summary: We present a strategy for computing the $F$-symbols of unitary modular categories with a self-dual simple generator, starting from their modular data, which almost entirely avoids the non-linear solution of the pentagon equations. The algorithm climbs a ladder of braid group representations on successively more strands of the generator until enough $F$-symbols have been determined to propagate them to a complete solution. The strategy presented is successful in difficult cases through ranks 11 and 12, including $\operatorname{Z}(\mathrm{Haagerup}_3)$, and does not require the category to be multiplicity-free.
arxiv:2611.24753.authors: Jonah Berean-Dutcher, Clay Cordova, Julio Parra-Martinez, Richard Tuddenham

arxiv:2611.24773.title: On the Beauville Dimension of Finite Abelian Groups
arxiv:2611.24773.summary: Unmixed Beauville manifolds of general type are rigid quotients of products of compact complex curves of higher genus by free diagonal actions of finite groups. Their biholomorphism classes are encoded by equivalence classes of group-theoretic data. For a finite abelian group $G$, we characterize when these data exist and determine the unmixed Beauville dimension $\mathrm{d}_{\mathcal{U}}(G)$, the minimum dimension of such a manifold arising from a diagonal action of $G$.

arxiv:2611.24775.title: A disproof of the van Emde Boas--Kruyswijk conjecture on the Davenport constant
arxiv:2611.24775.summary: The Davenport constant $D(G)$ of a finite abelian group $G$ is the smallest positive integer $\ell$ such that every sequence $S$ with terms from $G$ and with length $|S| \ge \ell$ has a nontrivial zero-sum subsequence. A long-standing conjecture, first proposed by van Emde Boas and Kruyswijk in 1969, states that $D(C_n^r)=r(n-1)+1$ for all positive integers $n$ and $r$. In this paper, we disprove this conjecture by showing that $D(C_6^r)>5r+1$ for every $r\ge23$.
arxiv:2611.24775.authors: Weidong Gao, Alfred Geroldinger, Guoqing Wang, Xiangneng Zeng

arxiv:2611.24787.title: A Poisson boundary solution to Connes' bicentralizer conjecture and Kadison's problem on MASA
arxiv:2611.24787.summary: We prove that, for every inclusion $M\subset P$ of countably decomposable von Neumann algebras with a normal faithful conditional expectation, $M\subset c(P)$ has the weak Dixmier property, where $c(P)$ is the continuous core of $P$. By Haagerup's characterization, we have a completely new proof of Connes' bicentralizer conjecture, independent of the recent proof of Houdayer--Marrakchi. By Marrakchi's characterization, we also prove his relative bicentralizer conjecture.

arxiv:2611.24813.title: The commutator subgroup of the Torelli group of a genus-three surface has finitely generated abelianization
arxiv:2611.24813.summary: We prove that the commutator subgroup of the Torelli group of a genus-three surface with at most one boundary component has finitely generated abelianization. The proof combines Gaifullin's finite-generation sufficient condition with the explicit generating set for the Torelli commutator subgroup due to Brendle, Margalit, and Putman.

arxiv:2611.24814.title: Smooth structures on polyhedral products of disks and spheres
arxiv:2611.24814.summary: We prove that every polyhedral product of disks and their boundary spheres that is a topological manifold admits a stably parallelizable smooth structure. We also show that if a moment-angle complex or a real moment-angle complex admits a smooth structure for which the coordinate action is smooth, then the link of every face of the underlying simplicial complex is a simplicial sphere, and every such smooth structure is stably parallelizable.

arxiv:2611.24824.title: Systole and kissing number of closed hyperbolic surfaces
arxiv:2611.24824.summary: In this article, we prove that if the genus of a closed hyperbolic surface $S$ is sufficiently large, then\[ \operatorname{sys}(S)\leq\frac{4}{3}\log(\operatorname{area}(S)). \] This proves a conjecture by Schmutz for large genus. The proof is based on quantitative counting estimates for closed geodesics derived from the Selberg trace formula.

arxiv:2611.24826.title: Whitehead doubles and the failure of the AJ conjecture
arxiv:2611.24826.summary: For marked Whitehead doubles of torus knots with coprime parameters $2\le r<s$, the AJ conjecture fails for both clasp signs, both companion chiralities, and every integer twist. The zero-framed signed unreduced colored Jones sequence has a nonzero rationally saturated annihilator. Every nonzero primitive representative specializes nontrivially at $t=-1$ with the meridian variable $M$ independent.
arxiv:2611.24826.authors: Jinzheng Li, Yuqi Li, Hao-Yu Sun

arxiv:2611.24832.title: List packing for graphs with small arboricity
arxiv:2611.24832.summary: We prove that every graph $G$ whose edge set is the union of $r$ forests has list packing number at most $2^r$. This means that for all $k\ge 2^r$ and every list-assignment $L$ with lists of size $k$, the graph $G$ admits $k$ disjoint proper $L$-colourings. While for large $r$ this bound is far from optimal, for $r\in\{1,2\}$ it is sharp.
arxiv:2611.24832.authors: Stijn Cambie, Wouter Cames van Batenburg, Xuding Zhu

arxiv:2611.24835.title: On the Vertex Growth Rate of Integer Partition Polytopes and Their Non-Vertex Structure
arxiv:2611.24835.summary: The Hardy-Ramanujan formula states that the asymptotic growth of the number of integer partitions of $n$ is $\exp(\Theta(\sqrt{n}\,))$. We prove that the number of vertices of the integer partition polytope is bounded by $\exp\left(\mathcal{O}(\ln^2 n)\right)$. This implies that all partitions of $n$ can be generated from a negligible subset of vertex partitions using convex combinations.

arxiv:2611.24860.title: Divisibility of Character Values of Wreath Products of Symmetric Groups
arxiv:2611.24860.summary: Let $G$ be a finite group whose character table is integer-valued, and let $K$ be any fixed positive integer. We prove that almost every entry of the character table of the wreath product $G\wr S_N$ is divisible by $K$ as $N\to\infty$.

arxiv:2611.24865.title: The limits of inertia bounds on graph powers
arxiv:2611.24865.summary: We investigate the tightness of inertia and inertia-type bounds related to graph powers. This class of graphs appears in several contexts, such as the theory of distance-regular graphs, quantum information theory and coding theory. They are a priori not covered by previous separation constructions involving locally sparse graphs, see Kwan and Wigderson (2024), or Alon's pseudorandom graphs, see Elphick, Tang and Zhang (2025).
arxiv:2611.24865.authors: Aida Abiad, Nils Van de Berg, Sam Mattheus

arxiv:2611.24868.title: The Ceresa Cycle on $X_0^+(p)$
arxiv:2611.24868.summary: We consider the curve $X_0^+(p)$ with prime $p$, which is the quotient of the modular curve $X_0(p)$ by the Fricke involution. We describe how one can explicitly calculate the shadow of a Hecke operator on $X_0^+(p)$, which is a rational divisor on $X_0^+(p)$ whose nonvanishing is an obstruction to the Ceresa cycle of $X_0^+(p)$ being torsion in the Chow group of the Jacobian of $X_0^+(p)$. We also provide an implementation of this procedure in PARI/GP and SageMath and use this on all primes below 5000.

arxiv:2611.24871.title: Pair Siegel-Veech constants for branched covers of tori and Veech surfaces
arxiv:2611.24871.summary: For a locus $\mathcal{E}$ of branched covers of tori satisfying a monodromy assumption, we show there exists an explicit constant $c_A(\mathcal{E})$ so that the number of pairs of saddle connections on surfaces in $\mathcal{E}$ of length at most $R$ and cross product at most $A$ grows like $c_A(\mathcal{E})R^2$ for every Diophantine surface in $\mathcal{E}$; this constant is moreover piecewise linear in $A$. In particular, this covers the case of billiards on rectangles with a barrier. Similar pointwise results are shown for Veech surfaces.

arxiv:2611.24879.title: Gauss--Bonnet theorem for o-minimal surfaces with isolated singularities
arxiv:2611.24879.summary: We study the relationship between topology and curvature of surfaces definable in an o-minimal structure. Our main result is a Gauss--Bonnet-type formula for closed (not necessarily compact) definable surfaces with finitely many singular points, expressing the Euler characteristic in terms of the total Gaussian curvature, the local densities at the singular points, and the density at infinity. As consequences, we obtain an inequality for definable minimal surfaces with isolated singularities and, for complex algebraic curves, a formula and an inequality relating the Euler characteristic, the total curvature, the multiplicities at the singular points and the degree.
arxiv:2611.24879.authors: Lucas Holanda Pinheiro, Jos\'e Edson Sampaio, Euripedes Carvalho da Silva

arxiv:2611.24907.title: Shadowing Property for Linear Operators on Banach Spaces
arxiv:2611.24907.summary: This note is dedicated to the study of the shadowing property for (bounded linear) operators on Banach spaces. We combine the spectral characterization of the shadowing property, recently established by Dragi\v{c}evi\'c and Pituk, with tools from local spectral theory, to obtain new results and simpler proofs of known results on shadowing for operators. We also prove that the shadowing property always implies the average shadowing property and the asymptotic average shadowing property for invertible operators on Banach spaces.
arxiv:2611.24907.authors: Nilson C. Bernardes Jr., Antonio Bonilla

arxiv:2611.24930.title: A Weinstein manifold without any spherical Fukaya category
arxiv:2611.24930.summary: We show that, after attaching a subcritical handle to $T^*\bP^2$ to obtain a manifold $M$, the integral wrapped Floer endomorphism algebra of a cotangent fibre admits no spherical refinement for any choice of brane structure; this obstructs the existence of any wrapped Fukaya category for $M$ over the sphere spectrum. We further discuss some features of the resulting Weinstein eight-manifold $M$, which is homotopy equivalent to $S^4$.

arxiv:2611.24958.title: Thirteen Improved Binary Constant-Weight Codes with Explicit Cyclic Orbit Certificates
arxiv:2611.24958.summary: We exhibit thirteen explicit binary constant-weight codes improving lower bounds recorded in Brouwer's table, including $A(29,6,5)\geq 333$, $A(55,4,5)\geq 66144$, and $A(62,4,5)\geq 107360$. Their 408,729 codewords are specified by 11,386 orbit representatives under explicitly given cyclic coordinate permutations, together with a standalone reconstruction and distance verifier. All thirteen orbit expansions were checked to agree exactly with the full codeword lists.

arxiv:2611.24966.title: Lattice-ordered Spectral Systems for Morse Representations
arxiv:2611.24966.summary: We show that Morse representations can be algebraically described by spectral systems, a notion introduced by B. Matschke for poset-filtered chain complexes. This provides an algebraic alternative to connection matrices and yields algebraic invariants via R-modules over an arbitrary ring R.

arxiv:2611.24973.title: Star decomposition of complete multipartite graphs
arxiv:2611.24973.summary: We study minimum degree-sum conditions for decompositions into stars of sizes $k$ and $k+1$, where $k\ge3$. Write $\sigma(G)=\min_{uv\in E(G)}(d(u)+d(v))$, and let $c_k$ be the least integer threshold guaranteeing a $\{K_{1,k},K_{1,k+1}\}$-decomposition for every finite simple graph. Using Tarsi's sufficient condition, we prove that $K_n$ admits such a decomposition whenever $n\ge2k$.

arxiv:2611.24974.title: The chromatic-AT choosability of Pseudo-Halin graphs
arxiv:2611.24974.summary: The \emph{Alon-Tarsi number} $AT(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the smallest integer $k$ such that $G$ admits an orientation $D$ with maximum outdegree at most $k-1$ in which the number of even Eulerian subdigraphs differs from the number of odd Eulerian subdigraphs. A 2-connected planar graph $G$ with minimum degree at least 3 is called a \emph{pseudo-Halin graph} if deleting the edges on the boundary of a single face $f_0$ yields a tree. Let $\mathcal{A}$ denote the class of pseudo-Halin graphs in which no two interior vertices are adjacent and every interior vertex has odd degree (equivalently, graphs obtained by iterated Haj\'{o}s sums of wheels with an odd number of exterior vertices).
arxiv:2611.24974.authors: Zhiguo Li, Cuicui Ma, Zeling Shao

arxiv:2611.24982.title: Orbits of $p$-adic flows: balls, time-one maps and minimal group actions
arxiv:2611.24982.summary: Let $f$ be a vector field on $\mathbb{Z}_p^d$ given by polynomials, or by power series converging on $\mathbb{Z}_p^d$, whose coefficients are divisible by $p^c$, where $c \ge 1$ ($c \ge 2$ when $p = 2$). Its flow exists for every $p$-adic time. I show that $t \mapsto \varphi_t(x)$ multiplies distances by exactly $\|f(x)\|_p$, in every dimension.

arxiv:2611.24997.title: There is no binary linear $[65,9,29]$ code
arxiv:2611.24997.summary: We prove that no binary linear $[65,9,\geqslant29]$ code exists, equivalently, that no even binary linear $[66,9,\geqslant30]$ code exists. Together with known constructions, this determines $d_2(65,9)=28$, $n_2(9,29)=66$, and $n_2(9,30)=67$. A residual-code bound and a known construction also give $d_2(122,10)=56$.

arxiv:2611.25006.title: Mateability of Fuchsian lattices with polynomials, and failure of algebraicity
arxiv:2611.25006.summary: We prove that all Fuchsian lattices, with the possible exceptions of those associated with compact orbifolds of type (0,3) and (1,1), can be mated with complex polynomials, providing the first examples of such combinations beyond genus-zero orbifolds. We also present the first construction of matings between simply degenerate Kleinian groups and polynomial maps. These matings are realized as holomorphic, though not necessarily algebraic, correspondences, demonstrating that Fatou's vision of unifying Kleinian group actions and polynomial dynamics can be fulfilled in the wider setting of transcendental correspondences.
arxiv:2611.25006.authors: Yusheng Luo, Mahan Mj, Sabyasachi Mukherjee

arxiv:2611.25011.title: Near-Quadratic Sample Compression for All VC Classes
arxiv:2611.25011.summary: The sample compression conjecture is a longstanding open problem in learning theory, originating in the work of Littlestone and Warmuth in the 1980s. At its heart is a connection between simplification and generalization: if a predictor consistent with a training sample is defined using only a small part of that sample, then it is likely to generalize. Sample compression schemes formalize this idea, and many natural learning algorithms can be analyzed this way.
arxiv:2611.25011.authors: Yang Cai, Vineet Gupta, Yanchen Jiang, Christopher Liaw, Aranyak Mehta, Shay Moran, Grigoris Velegkas, Di Wang, Manfred K. Warmuth

arxiv:2611.25017.title: Quiver-Invariant Triality between Brane Brick Models
arxiv:2611.25017.summary: We study quiver-invariant triality between 2d (0,2) supersymmetric gauge theories described by brane brick models associated with toric Calabi-Yau 4-folds. The dual theories share the same gauge groups, field content and E-terms but have distinct J-terms. We present an explicit pair of such brane brick models and identify the sequence of triality mutations relating them.
arxiv:2611.25017.authors: Dongwook Ghim, Juno Kwon, Rak-Kyeong Seong

arxiv:2611.25025.title: The Clifford Hierarchy from Clifford Stabilizers in 2D
arxiv:2611.25025.summary: The Bravyi-K\"onig theorem limits the constant-depth logical gates of 2D topological Pauli stabilizer codes to be in the Clifford group. Known qubit codes with Clifford stabilizers exceed it by only one level of the Clifford hierarchy, and this was conjectured to hold generally. We show that this bound can be completely bypassed, and that topological codes with Clifford stabilizers in 2D can realize transversal logical gates at any level of the Clifford hierarchy.

arxiv:2611.25042.title: A census of alternating tangles
arxiv:2611.25042.summary: We give a census of the roughly 10 billion prime, connected, alternating tangles with at most 14 crossings. Along the way, we prove analogs of the Tait conjectures for alternating tangles and observe that aspects of the geometry of alternating tangles are reflected in their diagrams, as is the case with links.

arxiv:2611.25050.title: On the Erd\H{o}s--Ginzburg--Ziv problem for $\mathbb Z_n^3$
arxiv:2611.25050.summary: The Erd\H{o}s--Ginzburg--Ziv constant $\mathsf s(\mathbb Z_n^r)$ is the least positive integer $t$ such that every sequence of $t$ elements of $\mathbb Z_n^r$ contains $n$ terms whose sum is zero. In this paper, we prove that $$\mathsf s(\mathbb Z_n^3)=9n+o(n)$$ for odd $n$. For every fixed $r\ge 4$, we also show that $\mathsf s(\mathbb Z_n^r)\le\bigl(\binom{2r-1}{r}+1\bigr)n+o_r(n).$ Our approach combines Alon--Dubiner-type spectral expansion, Zakharov's convex-geometric framework, and restricted-sum ideas developed by Han and Ren.

arxiv:2611.25057.title: Monomial singularities of maps in low codimension and their deformations
arxiv:2611.25057.summary: We study complex analytic map germs whose coordinate functions are monomials up to a change of coordinates. Motivated by recent normal form results of Rodrigues Hernandes and Ruas for $\mathcal{A}$-finite monomial maps in the range $p\ge 2n$, we address the remaining gap $p<2n$, solving an open problem posed in their work in the range $n<p<2n$. Our main results show that a monomial map germ $f:(\mathbb{C}^n,0)\to(\mathbb{C}^p,0)$ with $p < 2n$ and $(n,p) \neq (1,1)$ is $\mathcal{A}$-finite if and only if it is $\mathcal{A}$-equivalent to an $\mathcal{A}$-stable germ.
arxiv:2611.25057.authors: R. Gim\'enez Conejero, M. E. Rodrigues Hernandes

arxiv:2611.25068.title: Globally $F$-regular varieties are rationally chain connected
arxiv:2611.25068.summary: We prove that projective globally $F$-regular varieties are rationally chain connected. We deduce this from a study of the positivity of their tangent bundles and their purely inseparable covers. Although some globally $F$-regular varieties admit non-vanishing pluridifferential forms, we show that each admits a unique purely inseparable crepant cover that does not have this pathology.
arxiv:2611.25068.authors: Eric Jovinelly, Brian Lehmann, Eric Riedl

arxiv:2611.25072.title: The Partial Trace Functor on Soergel Bimodules in Type $\mathbb{B}$
arxiv:2611.25072.summary: We write down some observations about the partial trace functor between the categories of Soergel bimodules of type $\mathbb{B}_{n+1}$ and $\mathbb{B}_n$ for future reference. In particular, we observe that, like in type $\mathbb{A}$, the partial trace sends Soergel bimodules to a semi-infinite $q$-graded sum of Soergel bimodules.

arxiv:2611.25081.title: The Markov Property on Decorated Metric Planar Maps
arxiv:2611.25081.summary: We introduce decorated metric planar maps: planar maps whose edges $e$ are replaced by segments $[0,w_e]$, together with a continuous function on the resulting metric space, the decoration. We consider laws under which, conditionally on the metric map, the decoration follows a statistical physics model such as the Ising model or the Gaussian free field: the values at the vertices interact through a quadratic Hamiltonian and, given these values, the decoration along each edge is a Brownian bridge. Working with 4-regular maps with a boundary (the duals of quadrangulations with a boundary), we define a Markov property that allows explorations to stop in the middle of an edge.
arxiv:2611.25081.authors: Pablo Araya, Luis Fredes, Avelio Sep\'ulveda

arxiv:2611.25099.title: Flatness and Tightness in Hypertopes
arxiv:2611.25099.summary: A hypertope is a thin, residually connected incidence geometry. For each pair of types $\{i,j\}$, the residues of that type must be polygons, and if all residues of that type are the same type of polygon, then we can record this information in a diagram $D$. Given such a diagram, we prove a lower bound on the number of chambers of a hypertope with that diagram.
arxiv:2611.25099.authors: Gabe Cunningham, Claudio Alexandre Piedade, Philippe Tranchida

arxiv:2611.25115.title: A Density Bound for Mu\~niz's List Reversal
arxiv:2611.25115.summary: Mu\~niz described the problem of reversing a list of positive integers under the following rules: given a list of distinct positive integers, at each step, one can combine two adjacent entries into their sum or break an entry into two entries with the same sum, under the constraints that after each step the list must contain distinct entries no larger than the original largest entry. The question of what lists are and are not reversible under these rules is studied and an asymptotic upper bound on the density of an irreversible list is established.

arxiv:2611.25118.title: Rank and Rel in Strata of Abelian Differentials
arxiv:2611.25118.summary: We prove that every invariant subvariety M in a genus g stratum H(k_1,...,k_n) of Abelian differentials satisfies rank(M) <= rel(M) + 1 + sum_i (k_i - 1). In particular, every invariant subvariety with rel zero in a principal stratum is a Teichm\"uller curve. Combined with work of Eskin, Filip and Wright, this implies that each principal stratum contains only finitely many nonarithmetic Teichm\"uller curves.

arxiv:2611.25122.title: Algebraically elliptic resolutions in a family of determinantal quartic threefolds
arxiv:2611.25122.summary: We construct a family of determinantal irrational quartic threefolds in $\mathbf{P}^4$ for which the blow-up of the sixteen nodes and two distinguished small projective resolutions are algebraically elliptic in the sense of Gromov.
arxiv:2611.25122.authors: Alexander Dvorsky, Shulim Kaliman, Mikhail Zaidenberg

arxiv:2611.25137.title: Labeled Chip-Firing on Ordered Directed Graphs
arxiv:2611.25137.summary: We study labeled chip-firing on rooted directed graphs where for each vertex $v$, the children of $v$ are linearly ordered. When a vertex fires, the selected chips are sent to its children in increasing order. We show that homomorphisms preserving these child choices transport legal firing sequences.
arxiv:2611.25137.authors: Ryota Inagaki, Tanya Khovanova, Austin Luo

arxiv:2611.25143.title: New lower bounds for six small hypergraph Ramsey numbers
arxiv:2611.25143.summary: Let $R(k,l;t)$ denote the least $n$ such that every colouring of the $t$-subsets of an $n$-set with two colours has $k$ points all of whose $t$-subsets have the first colour, or $l$ points all of whose $t$-subsets have the second. We give explicit colourings proving $R(4,5;3)\ge 38$, $R(4,6;3)\ge 71$, $R(5,5;3)\ge 99$, $R(5,6;4)\ge 201$, $R(6,6;4)\ge 601$ and $R(6,6;5)\ge 84$. The first three improve the bounds 35, 63 and 88 listed in Radziszowski's dynamic survey.

arxiv:2611.25148.title: A refinement of Szemer\'edi's distinct-distance bound for points in general position
arxiv:2611.25148.summary: We prove that every collinear triple free set of $n\ge4$ points in the Euclidean plane determines at least $\lfloor n/3\rfloor+1$ distinct distances. This refines the classical bound $\lceil(n-1)/3\rceil$ of Szemer\'edi that is based on counting isosceles triangles. The refinement is based on treating the diameters separately: they only appear on the convex hull, so for them, we can use the planar diameter theorem and Altman's theorem on distances in convex polygons.

arxiv:2611.25153.title: \textsc{Max-Cut} on Token Graphs
arxiv:2611.25153.summary: Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, with a positive weight assigned to each edge. A cut of $G$ is a partition of its vertices into two sets $X$ and $Y$; the weight of $(X,Y)$ is the sum of the weight of the edges of $G$ with one endpoint in $X$ and the other endpoint in $Y$. The Max-Cut problem asks for the maximum weight, $m(G)$, of a cut of $G$.
arxiv:2611.25153.authors: Jos\'e Angel Alejandro-Soto, Paulo T. Araujo, Ruy Fabila-Monroy, Sergio Gerardo G\'omez-Galicia, Mohamed Hibat-Allah, Md Moshiur Rahman Raj, Mahmud Ashraf Shamim, Ana Laura Trujillo-Negrete

arxiv:2611.25162.title: On the ring of bounded functions on the character variety
arxiv:2611.25162.summary: Let $\mathfrak{X}$ denote the character variety associated to the group $(o_L, +)$, where $o_L$ is the ring of integers in a finite extension $L/\mathbb{Q}_p$. $\mathfrak{X}$ is a rigid analytic variety parametrizing locally $L$-analytic characters. Let $\Lambda_L\left(\mathfrak{X}\right)$ denote the global sections bounded by $1$.

arxiv:2611.25164.title: Convexity is overrated: Shortest paths on 4-polytopes are hard to compute
arxiv:2611.25164.summary: We prove that computing geodesic distance on the boundary of a rational convex $4$-polytope is NP-hard. We then construct rational $4$-polytopes with two rational points joined by exponentially many shortest paths of equal rational length, disproving several conjectures along the way. For the same problem, we also prove SQRTSUM-hardness under deterministic polynomial-time Turing reductions.

arxiv:2611.25175.title: An Explicit Three-Dimensional Dispersing Billiard with Finite Horizon
arxiv:2611.25175.summary: We construct an explicit three-dimensional periodic Lorentz gas whose quotient by the period lattice \(2\Z^3\) has 38 spherical scatterers with rational centers and four rational radii. The scatterers are strictly separated, so the associated dispersing billiard has no corners or cusps. We prove finite horizon by establishing a common blocking margin for every rational direction.

arxiv:2611.25182.title: Iterative constructions of semifields 2-dimensional over a nucleus
arxiv:2611.25182.summary: The construction of finite semifields dates back to Dickson's work in 1906. To the best of our knowledge, only two iterative constructions were previously known: those of Hiramine, Matsumoto and Oyama in 1987, and of Kantor and Williams in 2004. The latter yields, for suitable even orders, superpolynomially many pairwise non-isotopic semifields.
arxiv:2611.25182.authors: Lukas K\"olsch, Paolo Santonastaso, Yue Zhou

arxiv:2611.25183.title: The rational points of the non-split Cartan modular curve of level 121
arxiv:2611.25183.summary: We prove that the modular curve $X_{\mathrm{ns}}^{+}(121)$ of the normalizer of a non-split Cartan subgroup of level 121, of genus 511, has exactly seven rational points, all of them CM. This is the level 121 case of a conjecture of Rouse, Sutherland and Zureick-Brown, and with their theorem it determines the 11-adic images of Galois of non-CM elliptic curves over $\mathbb{Q}$. The Jacobian has rank equal to the genus.

arxiv:2611.25187.title: A Hopf algebra action on the cohomology of moduli of abelian varieties
arxiv:2611.25187.summary: We show that the rational compactly supported cohomology of the moduli space $\mathcal{A} = \bigsqcup_{g \geq 0} \mathcal{A}_g$ of principally polarized abelian varieties is free as a bigraded module over the Hopf algebra formed by its weight-zero subspace. The action arises from a symplectic analog of the Waldhausen $S$-construction. This structure yields new lower bounds for Betti numbers and the dimensions of the graded pieces of the weight filtration on the cohomology of $\mathcal{A}_g$.

arxiv:2611.25190.title: Comodule algebras and the cohomology of symplectic groups
arxiv:2611.25190.summary: We prove that the homology of symplectic groups with Steinberg module coefficients forms a comodule algebra over the homology of general linear groups with Steinberg module coefficients. We prove a freeness-type result for comodule algebras. We deduce new lower bounds for the high-dimensional cohomology of symplectic groups of number rings and their congruence subgroups.
arxiv:2611.25190.authors: Jeremy Miller, Urshita Pal, Peter Patzt

arxiv:2611.25244.title: A note on Tur\'an densities of daisies and hypergraph products
arxiv:2611.25244.summary: The Tur\'an density of an $r$-uniform hypergraph $\mathcal H$ is defined as ${\pi}(\mathcal{H})=\lim_{n\rightarrow\infty} \operatorname{ex}(n,\mathcal{H})/\binom{n}{r}$, where $\operatorname{ex}(n,\mathcal H)$ denotes the largest number of edges in an $\mathcal H$-free $r$-uniform hypergraph on $n$ vertices. For integers $r\geq s\geq2$ and $t\geq s$, an $(r,s,t)$-daisy $\mathcal D_r(s,t)$ is the $r$-uniform hypergraph consisting of all unions of a fixed $(r-s)$-set with the $s$-subsets of a disjoint $t$-set. We show that for every fixed $s\geq3$, \[ \lim_{r\rightarrow\infty}{\pi}(\mathcal D_r(s,t))=1-O_s(t^{-(s-1)}) \] as $t\rightarrow\infty$.

arxiv:2611.25266.title: Nilpotent skew-symmetric tridiagonal Bohemian matrices: a proof of Corless's conjecture
arxiv:2611.25266.summary: Corless studied the skew-symmetric tridiagonal matrices $T_m(u)$ with superdiagonal $u \in \{1, i\}^{m-1}$. He showed that $T_m(u)$ can be nilpotent only if $m = 2^K - 1$ and that the $2^{K-1}$ vectors $u$ obtained from the empty vector by repeated application of $u \mapsto (u, 1, i, \rev u)$ and $u \mapsto (u, i, 1, \rev u)$ give nilpotent matrices, and he conjectured that there are no others. We prove this conjecture.

arxiv:2611.25268.title: Integer Programming Strategies for the Snake-in-the-Box Problem
arxiv:2611.25268.summary: We present a selection of Integer Programming (IP) strategies for the Snake-in-the-Box problem, which asks for the longest induced path in the $d$-dimensional hypercube. Current records are based on sophisticated, exhaustive searches, with optimality proven only for instances up to dimension 8, motivating our study of IP formulations. We address symmetries and potential strengthenings.
arxiv:2611.25268.authors: Tim Kunt, Thorsten Koch, Hyejun Park

arxiv:2611.25275.title: Moduli of continuity preserved by the Hilbert Transform
arxiv:2611.25275.summary: It has long been known that the Hilbert transform preserves certain moduli of continuity such as H\"older continuity. In~\cite{GS01}, M. Goldstein and W.

arxiv:2611.25277.title: Preservation of big diagonal for automorphisms of Hilbert schemes
arxiv:2611.25277.summary: If $X$ is a smooth projective surface that is not K3 or abelian surface, we show that any automorphism of the Hilbert scheme of points $X^{[n]}$ preserves the big diagonal. This generalizes several previous works, and gives a complete description of automorphisms of $X^{[n]}$ when $X$ is not K3 or abelian surface. We also obtain a Torelli-type theorem: a smooth projective surface $X$ can be recovered from $X^{[n]}$ unless $X$ is a K3 surface.

arxiv:2611.25295.title: Kernel Regression using Persistence Diagrams
arxiv:2611.25295.summary: Persistence diagrams are widely used in topological data analysis to summarize topological and geometric structure in data. We study nonparametric regression where inputs are persistence diagrams and outputs are real-valued. Using kernel-based local averaging estimators defined directly over diagram space with Wasserstein distance, we establish consistency and derive bounds on the rate of convergence under suitable assumptions in the $L^2$-theory.
arxiv:2611.25295.authors: Saksham Aggarwal, James Nichols, Katharine Turner

arxiv:2611.25313.title: Variational integrators for time-dependent Lagrangian systems on Lie groups
arxiv:2611.25313.summary: We develop fixed-step variational integrators for time-dependent Lagrangian systems on Lie groups, derive their reduced dynamics, and analyze their long-time behavior by backward error analysis. We derive the continuous Euler-Lagrange equations, energy balance, and Noether conservation laws, and construct time-indexed discrete Lagrangians using retractions, with the midpoint-Cayley scheme treated explicitly. On their regularity domains, the resulting phase-space maps are symplectic.
arxiv:2611.25313.authors: Leonardo Colombo, Mar\'ia Emma Eyrea Iraz\'u, David Mart\'in de Diego, Mar\'ia Daniela S\'anchez, Marcela Zuccalli

arxiv:2611.25318.title: Kakutani equivalence of higher rank unipotent abelian actions I
arxiv:2611.25318.summary: We study Kakutani equivalence of higher-rank abelian unipotent actions. We construct a Kakutani invariant for general $\mathbb{R}^n$-actions and establish a quantitative vanishing criterion. By this criterion, we prove that ergodic abelian horocyclic actions on finite-volume quotients of connected semisimple Lie groups are loosely Kronecker.
arxiv:2611.25318.authors: Adam Kanigowski, Philipp Kunde, Kurt Vinhage, Daren Wei

arxiv:2611.25330.title: Counting Elements and Conjugacy Classes of Fixed Genus in Hyperbolic Groups
arxiv:2611.25330.summary: Let $G$ be a non-elementary hyperbolic group equipped with a word metric. A group element in $G$ has orientable genus $n$ if it can be written as the product of $n$ commutators and no fewer. Similarly, a group element in $G$ has non-orientable genus $m$ if it can be written as the product of $m$ squares and no fewer.
arxiv:2611.25330.authors: Ritwik Chakraborty, Inhyeok Choi, Biswajit Nag

arxiv:2611.25331.title: The Semi--Fibonacci Partition Tree
arxiv:2611.25331.summary: In this work, we introduce a binary tree in which every semi-Fibonacci partition appears exactly once. The left--right address of a vertex gives an explicit formula for the parts of the corresponding partition and encodes statistics such as the largest $2$-adic valuation among its parts. We construct a sign-reversing involution that refines Andrews's parity theorem by determining the difference between the numbers of partitions of a given integer at even and odd depths.
arxiv:2611.25331.authors: Andr\'es R. Moreno, Jos\'e L. Ram\'irez

arxiv:2611.25346.title: A complete intersection theorem for sets of bounded size
arxiv:2611.25346.summary: Let \(1\le t\le k\le n\) and \(2k<n+t\). We prove that a largest \(t\)-intersecting family of subsets of \([n]\) of size at most \(k\) is obtained by taking all such subsets that contain at least \(t+r\) points of a fixed \((t+2r)\)-element set, for some \(0\le r\le\left\lfloor\frac{n-t}{2}\right\rfloor\). This settles a conjecture of Ahlswede, Bey, Engel and Khachatrian from 2002.

arxiv:2611.25362.title: Rigidity and Non-Rigidity of Disk Pseudo-Rotations below $C^2$
arxiv:2611.25362.summary: For every $0<\beta\le1$, we prove $C^0$-rigidity of area-preserving $C^{1,\beta}$ disk pseudo-rotations with non-Brjuno rotation number. At the $C^1$ endpoint, every non-Brjuno rotation number of zero exponential type admits non-rigid examples. We also obtain a different rigidity result when the rotation number has positive exponential type: the boundary restriction of every $C^1$ pseudo-rotation is rigid and topologically conjugate to a rotation.

arxiv:2611.25381.title: Strong chromatic index of graphs with Ore-degree at most nine
arxiv:2611.25381.summary: The strong chromatic index $\chi_s^{\prime}(G)$ of a graph $G$ is the minimum number of colors in an edgecoloring in which distinct edges at distance at most two in the line graph receive different colors. Let $\theta(G)=\max _{x y \in E(G)}\left(d_G(x)+d_G(y)\right)$ denote the maximum edge weight, also called the Ore-degree, of $G$. We prove that every finite loopless multigraph $G$ with $\theta(G) \leq 9$ satisfies $\chi_s^{\prime}(G) \leq 28$.
arxiv:2611.25381.authors: Xiaoxue Hu, Jiangxu Kong, Yu Xue

arxiv:2611.25399.title: Rational Elliptic Period Relations Across Realizations: Complex Lattices, Local p-adic Periods, and Drinfeld Modules
arxiv:2611.25399.summary: We determine the algebraic relations among full de Rham comparison periods of elliptic curves over finite extensions of $\mathbb Q_p$. The connected local monodromy group gives the transcendence degree and an explicit affine linear relation ideal for the full matrix in Fontaine's field $B_{\mathrm{dR}}$. After normalizing the holomorphic row and reducing to $\mathbb C_p$, the transcendence degree drops by one and the normalized determinant supplies the additional relation.

arxiv:2611.25421.title: Formality of finite abelian covers and Jordan blocks of the monodromy
arxiv:2611.25421.summary: Let $X$ be a connected finite-type CW-complex with a map to the circle that is surjective on fundamental groups. If $X$ is formal, the algebraic monodromy of the associated infinite cyclic cover has no Jordan block of size greater than one at the eigenvalue 1, over the rationals; if the $d$-fold cyclic cover of $X$ along the map is formal, the same holds at every $d$-th root of unity. We study how formality of finite abelian covers and Jordan blocks of the monodromy constrain each other.

arxiv:2611.25447.title: Note on the random triadic process II
arxiv:2611.25447.summary: For a fixed integer $r\geqslant 3$, the random $r$-generalized triadic process starts from a minimum weakly $K_r$-saturated graph, namely the complete $(r-1)$-partite graph $K_{1^{r-2},n-r+2}$ with $r-2$ singleton parts and one part of size $n-r+2$. At each step of the process a new edge $\boldsymbol{e}$ is added with probability $p$, provided there exists a copy of $B_{r-2}$ in $K_n$ for which $\boldsymbol{e}$ is its spine and the only edge that has not yet been added to the current graph, where $B_{r-2}$ denotes a triangular book graph consisting of $r-2$ triangles sharing a single common edge known as the spine of the book. When $r=3$, this is the random triadic process.

arxiv:2611.25465.title: DeoPC: Data-Enabled Output-Feedback Predictive Control for State Regulation
arxiv:2611.25465.summary: Constrained regulation of the internal state of an unknown linear system is challenging when only input-output measurements are available online. In this work, we develop a data-enabled output-feedback predictive control (DeoPC) framework for constrained state regulation using input-output data. Specifically, a data-driven state estimate is constructed from past input-output data via a subspace-based singular value decomposition.
arxiv:2611.25465.authors: Jingyuan Li, Dawei Shi, Ling Shi

arxiv:2611.25467.title: On the Type E case of the Brown Wemyss realization conjecture
arxiv:2611.25467.summary: We consider the remaining Type E case of the Brown-Wemyss numerical realization conjecture. The noncommutative splitting lemma and the Type A and D classifications of Brown and Wemyss leave two-generator cyclic potentials with cubic part $x^3$. For these remaining potentials, we construct geometric realizations under the hypothesis of radical growth dimension at most one.

arxiv:2611.25482.title: Twisted enveloping algebras for permutation orbifolds
arxiv:2611.25482.summary: We formulate a topological formal calculus for continuous distributions with values in linearly topologized spaces. We apply it here to construct permutation-twisted fields directly from products and branch specializations. For a vertex operator algebra $V$, the key structural observation is that modes of tensors with at most one non-vacuum factor topologically generate the permutation-twisted enveloping algebra.

arxiv:2611.25501.title: Stein degree on birational log Calabi-Yau fibrations
arxiv:2611.25501.summary: We prove uniform bounds for the Stein degrees of boundary divisors on generalised log Calabi-Yau fibrations of Fano type over arbitrary fields of characteristic zero. The main ingredient is the birational case for which we provide two approaches.

arxiv:2611.25505.title: Fixed-opening-set positivity for perfect matchings
arxiv:2611.25505.summary: For a perfect matching $M$ on $[2n]$, let $P_M$ be the interval order on its edges and let $\operatorname{Open}(M)$ be the set of smaller endpoints of its edges. For an opening set $O$ that occurs for some matching, put $S_O=\sum_{\operatorname{Open}(M)=O}X_{\operatorname{Inc}(P_M)}$ and $H_O=\omega S_O$. We give explicit Schur and power-sum expansions of $H_O$ with nonnegative integer coefficients, and prove that $H_O$ is $h$-positive (equivalently, $S_O$ is $e$-positive).

arxiv:2611.25516.title: Rational Designs and Prouhet--Tarry--Escott Problems
arxiv:2611.25516.summary: For every strength, we prove the existence of rational designs on spheres, orthogonal and unitary groups, real and complex Grassmannians, and ellipsoids that are defined by positive-definite quadratic forms with rational coefficients and have a rational point. This answers Bannai's Problem for these spaces, solves the problem of Cui--Xia--Xiang on rational spherical $4$-designs on the unit circle, and proves Xiang's conjecture in the stronger form of existence in every dimension. To this end, we introduce the $(G,\mathcal{S})$-Prouhet--Tarry--Escott problem for an abelian group $G$ and a finite set of characters $\mathcal{S}$ and develop its existence and minimality theory.

arxiv:2611.25544.title: Distance-hereditary split graphs whose second largest eigenvalue does not exceed 1
arxiv:2611.25544.summary: The gem is obtained by joining a vertex to every vertex of a path on four vertices. A distance-hereditary split graph is a split graph containing no induced gem. In this paper, we characterize all connected distance-hereditary split graphs whose second largest eigenvalue does not exceed 1 and determine the multiplicity of the eigenvalue 1.
arxiv:2611.25544.authors: Zihao Geng, Qian-Qian Chen, Ji-Ming Guo

arxiv:2611.25559.title: k-trees with second largest eigenvalue at most one
arxiv:2611.25559.summary: The problem of characterizing graphs whose second largest adjacency eigenvalue is at most $1$ was posed by Hoffman and first studied by Cvetkovi\'c in 1982. In this paper, all $k$-trees with second largest eigenvalue at most $1$ are characterized. We determine all equality cases and the multiplicity of the eigenvalue $1$.
arxiv:2611.25559.authors: Zihao Geng, Ji-Ming Guo, Jongyook Park

arxiv:2611.25600.title: Criteria for memory-induced blow-up in distributed delay differential equations
arxiv:2611.25600.summary: This paper investigates the conditions under which solutions to distributed delay differential equations describing memory accumulation and forgetting blow up in finite time. It provides criteria for memory-induced blow-up, which means finite-time blow-up of the delayed equation while the corresponding non-delayed equation, obtained in a certain limit, has global solutions. In the author's previous work, memory-induced blow-up was shown for specific nonlinearities by means of Poincar\'e-type compactification, but a general theory was not established.

arxiv:2611.25615.title: Finitely supported mapping classes on infinite-type surfaces
arxiv:2611.25615.summary: We study the topological closure of the group of mapping classes group with finite-type support on an infinite-type surface. Since every such mapping class fixes each end which is not a puncture, we have that the closure is contained in the pointwise stabilizer of infinite-type ends. A natural question is therefore when this inclusion is an equality, and if it is not, what must be added to obtain the full stabilizer.

arxiv:2611.25630.title: Linear dependence and tameness for homogeneous nilpotent-Jacobian maps in dimension four
arxiv:2611.25630.summary: Let $K$ be a field of characteristic zero, and let $H\in K[x_1,x_2,x_3,x_4]^4$ be homogeneous of positive degree. We prove that the components of $H$ are linearly dependent over $K$ whenever $JH$ is nilpotent, extending the known quadratic and cubic results to every positive homogeneous degree. This fills the gap regarding homogeneous linear dependence in four dimensions.

arxiv:2611.25662.title: Positive semidefiniteness of random submatrices
arxiv:2611.25662.summary: Given a symmetric matrix $A \in [-1,1]^{n \times n}$, we estimate the probability that a random principal submatrix, obtained by taking each index independently with probability $p$, is positive semidefinite. As a corollary, we show that $O(\varepsilon^{-1})$ indices chosen uniformly at random suffice for testing positive semidefiniteness with squared Frobenius distance threshold $\varepsilon n^2$, thus nearly matching the lower bound of Bakshi, Chepurko, and Jayaram (``Testing Positive Semi-Definiteness via Random Submatrices'', FOCS 2020). The key ingredient is a dense model lemma for positive semidefinite matrices, proved using the hyperplane separation theorem and a contraction…

arxiv:2611.25676.title: On quasi-triangular Hopf algebras of square-free dimensions
arxiv:2611.25676.summary: Let $H$ be a quasi-triangular Hopf algebra of sqaure-free dimension over $\mathbb{C}$. In this note, we show that $H$ is semisimple and cocommutative. Equivalently, a braided finite tensor category $\mathcal{C}$ of square-free Frobenius--Perron dimension with a fiber functor is tensor equivalent to the representation category of a finite group.
arxiv:2611.25676.authors: Jiacheng Bao, Zhiqiang Yu, Ying Zheng

arxiv:2611.25684.title: A sharp bounded bijection for tight cylindric partitions
arxiv:2611.25684.summary: Fix a cyclic profile of coprime rank $r$ and level $\ell$, both at least three, and an entry bound $n\ge1$. Let $d$ be the deficit from the maximum volume of a tight cylindric partition. For $d\le n\min(r,\ell)$, the one-row combinatorial $R$ matches the tight cylinders whose last slice lies inside the maximizer's last slice with the partitions of $d$ in which each part occurs fewer than $r$ times.

arxiv:2611.25685.title: Extremal spectral results of outerplanar graphs without starlike trees
arxiv:2611.25685.summary: A graph $G$ is $F$-free if it does not contain $F$ as a subgraph. Let $\operatorname{SPEX}_{\mathcal{OP}}(n,F)$ denote the set of $n$-vertex $F$-free outerplanar graphs with maximum spectral radius. Define $S(l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t)$ as the starlike tree obtained from $t$ vertex-disjoint paths of lengths $l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t$ by identifying one endpoint of each path, and $C_{l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t}$ as the graph obtained from $t$ vertex-disjoint cycles of lengths $l_1,l_2,\ldots,l_t$ by identifying one vertex from each cycle.
arxiv:2611.25685.authors: Fulong Ye, Bofeng Huo, Yuxiang Liu, Ligong Wang

arxiv:2611.25690.title: Determinant Massey products
arxiv:2611.25690.summary: We introduce the determinant Massey product, a secondary operation on the cohomology of commutative dg algebras which is reminiscent of the classical Massey product. We prove some of the elementary properties of this product, compute several examples, and relate them to classical and matric Massey products. When 2 is invertible, a determinant Massey product is a matric Massey product, but over $\mathbb F_2$, it is not.
arxiv:2611.25690.authors: Ois\'in Flynn-Connolly, Jos\'e M. Moreno-Fern\'andez, Fernando Muro

arxiv:2611.25693.title: Constructible properties of minimal models
arxiv:2611.25693.summary: We prove that, given a projective minimal model and a projective family of good minimal models, the subset of the base parametrizing fibers isomorphic (or birationally equivalent) to the given minimal model is constructible in the Zariski topology. Together with recent boundedness results for polarized log Calabi--Yau fibrations, this constructibility theorem provides new finiteness results predicted by the relative Kawamata--Morrison--Totaro cone conjecture.

arxiv:2611.25715.title: Real Principal-Minor Detectors: Normal Forms and Regular Parity Lifts
arxiv:2611.25715.summary: Let $A$ be a symmetric matrix over $\mathbb{F}_2$ on a finite index set, and let $t$ be the column of diagonal entries of $A$, viewed over $\mathbb{R}$. A real detector of $A$ is a real matrix whose principal minors equal the integer $0/1$ representatives of the corresponding principal minors of $A$. We prove that $A$ has a real detector if and only if it has one of the form $K+tt^T$, with $K$ skew-symmetric and $\{0,\pm1\}$-valued.

arxiv:2611.25727.title: Fourier bases for square-order Paley graphs
arxiv:2611.25727.summary: Let $q$ be an odd prime power and consider the Paley graph $P(q^2)$ on the finite field $\mathbb{F}_{q^2}$. A well-known optimal eigenfunction of this graph is supported on the norm-one subgroup, where it takes the values $1$ and $-1$ on the two cosets of its subgroup of index two. Its support has the minimum possible size $q+1$.
arxiv:2611.25727.authors: Bart De Bruyn, Sergey Goryainov, Yilin Xie, Weihao Yan, Ferdinando Zullo

arxiv:2611.25741.title: Beyond geometric lattices: pseudo-atoms and redundant join representations in the face lattice of the permutohedron
arxiv:2611.25741.summary: We study the lattice obtained from the poset of ordered set partitions (the Fubini poset), ordered by merging adjacent blocks, by adjoining a bottom element of rank -1. It is the face lattice of the permutohedron. We look at it from the point of view of geometric lattices: it is graded, atomic and coatomic in the strong sense that every element is a meet of coatoms, but it is not semimodular.

arxiv:2611.25758.title: Global-in-Time Nonrelativistic Limit and KAM Tori for the Complex Klein-Gordon Equation on the Circle
arxiv:2611.25758.summary: This paper establishes a global-in-time nonrelativistic limit for families of small-amplitude quasi-periodic solutions of the cubic complex Klein-Gordon equation on the circle. Firstly, we construct by a KAM block scheme, small-amplitude two-frequency invariant tori and show that their linear stability depends on whether the two excited Fourier indices coincide or are distinct: coincident indices yield linearly stable tori, whereas distinct indices yield partially hyperbolic tori. Moreover, controlling the dependence of the KAM scheme on the speed of light, we construct quasi-periodic solutions whose frequencies, after a gauge transformation, coincide exactly with those of quasi-periodic…

arxiv:2611.25767.title: Plane curves attaining the Dimca-Sernesi bound and Jacobian syzygies of pencil-type curves
arxiv:2611.25767.summary: For a reduced plane curve $C:f=0$ of degree $d$ with only weighted homogeneous singularities, Dimca and Sernesi proved that the minimal degree of a Jacobian relation satisfies $\mathrm{mdr}(f)\geq \alpha_C\, d-2$, where $\alpha_C$ is the minimal Arnold exponent of the singularities of $C$. We call $C$ DS-extremal (Dimca-Sernesi extremal) when equality holds. We show that curves of pencil type $f=\Phi(g,h)$, in particular curves of $(p,q)$-torus type $g^p+h^q$, are DS-extremal, the minimal syzygy being $\nabla g\times\nabla h$.

arxiv:2611.25783.title: Symmetry of pole order spectra and freeness of plane curves
arxiv:2611.25783.summary: Let $C:f=0$ be a reduced plane curve of degree $d$ having only weighted homogeneous singularities, and let $\mathrm{Sp}_P^0(f)$ be the pole order spectrum of the top cohomology of its Milnor fiber. Writing $\mathrm{Sp}^0_P(f)=\sum_q m_q\,t^{q/d}$, we show that $m_q-m_{2d-q}=n(f)_{q-3}-n(f)_{q+d-3}$ for every integer $q$, where $n(f)_k$ is the Hilbert function of the Jacobian module $N(f)$. Consequently, $\mathrm{Sp}^0_P(f)$ is symmetric with respect to $\alpha\mapsto 2-\alpha$ if and only if $C$ is free.

arxiv:2611.25785.title: Coxeter Group Symmetries of Frieze Patterns
arxiv:2611.25785.summary: Coxeter group symmetries of frieze patterns are investigated through their relation to $2\times n$ matrices and the associated Pl\"ucker coordinates. For odd order $n$, the symmetric group acts on the set of friezes, while for even $n$, the dihedral subgroup acts. We further show that a larger group acts when $n = 6$.

arxiv:2611.25850.title: Weak Degeneracy with Availability for Planar Graphs
arxiv:2611.25850.summary: Every planar graph admits exponentially many proper colorings for any assignment of lists of five allowed colors to its vertices. In this paper, we show that very little beyond degeneracy is needed to prove that this statement holds. In particular, given a planar graph G (but not the list assignment), our argument provides an algorithm consisting entirely of instructions of the following form: ``Color the vertex v using any color c from its list, and remove c from the lists of neighbors of v.'' and ``For the edge uv, choose any k colors from the list of u, then color v by any color c from its list that does not appear among these k colors, and remove c from the lists of neighbors of v.''…

arxiv:2611.25863.title: A note on the learning coefficient of exceptional singularities
arxiv:2611.25863.summary: We compute the learning coefficient of a polynomial neural network at a point of its neurovariety all of whose real parameters are good, and show that it equals $d/2$, with multiplicity one, where $d$ is the difference between the dimension of the parameter space and the dimension of the group of symmetries of the architecture. This is the value attained at a generic point of the neurovariety; consequently, exceptional singularities are invisible to the pair $(\lambda,\theta)$ whenever all real parameters in their fibre are good. By contrast, at a full parameter in the interior of the parameter domain whose differential has non-maximal rank we show that $\lambda<d/2$.

arxiv:2611.25890.title: An A $\infty$ -algebra structure for enriched Morse complexes
arxiv:2611.25890.summary: We construct a homotopy coherent product structure extending the Chas-Sullivan product on chains of the free loop space of a manifold. Our construction uses the framework of Morse homology with DG coefficients and perturbed Morse gradient trees. We define an operad given by moduli spaces of Morse gradient trees with a twisted differential.

arxiv:2611.25893.title: A very robust Ramsey theorem for hypergraph matchings
arxiv:2611.25893.summary: A fundamental result in Ramsey theory due to Alon, Frankl and Lov\'asz gives an exact formula for the $q$-colour Ramsey numbers of matchings in $r$-uniform hypergraphs: if $n\ge\mathsf{AFL}_r(\mathbf{t})=(r-1)\|\mathbf{t}\|_\infty+1+\sum_{j=1}^q(t_j-1)$ then in any $q$-edge-colouring of $K^r_n$ there is some colour $j$ with a matching of size $t_j$. We show that a very weak quasirandomness assumption suffices for this Ramsey property: we can replace $K^r_n$ by any $r$-graph $H$ on at least $\mathsf{AFL}_r(\mathbf{t})+o(n)$ vertices that is a sublinear connector, meaning that it has no balanced $r$-partite holes of linear size. This generalises the result for $r=2$ (ordinary graphs) that we…

arxiv:2611.25956.title: Schubert Calculus in the Eye of the Storm
arxiv:2611.25956.summary: We introduce new combinatorial objects, called storm diagrams, to study the torus-equivariant quantum $K$-theory of complete flag varieties $GL_n(\mathbb{C})/B$. We consider the quantum product of an arbitrary Schubert class with a modified Hirzebruch $\lambda_y$-class of a tautological subbundle. We show that its Schubert expansion coefficients are given by the total weights of storm diagrams.
arxiv:2611.25956.authors: Neil J. Y. Fan, Peter L. Guo, Changzheng Li, Rui Xiong

arxiv:2611.25973.title: Proof of Stanley's Conjecture on the Leading Ehrhart Coefficients of the Birkhoff Polytope
arxiv:2611.25973.summary: Let $c(n,k)$ denote the coefficient of $r^{(n-1)^2-k}$ in the Ehrhart polynomial of the $n\times n$ Birkhoff polytope. For every fixed nonnegative integer $k$, we prove that $c(n,k)/c(n,0)\sim n^{3k}/(2^k k!)$ as $n\to\infty$, confirming a conjecture of Stanley.

arxiv:2611.25974.title: Uniform Bounds of $F$-Signature and Effective Ideal Containments
arxiv:2611.25974.summary: We establish inequalities between numerical invariants and ideal containments in local rings containing a field. We prove the positivity of $F$-signature for klt-type algebras essentially of finite type over $\mathbb{C}$ under prime characteristic reduction and resolve the Uniform Symbolic Topology Problem effectively for both $F$-finite strongly $F$-regular rings of prime characteristic and klt type algebras over $\mathbb{C}$. Consequently, letting $s(R)$ denote the $F$-signature and $d$ the Krull dimension, if $d\geq 2$ then $I^{\left(\left\lceil\frac{d-1}{s(R)}\right\rceil n\right)} \subseteq \overline{I^{n}}$ and $I^{\left(d\left\lceil\frac{d-1}{s(R)}\right\rceil n\right)} \subseteq…

arxiv:2611.25996.title: Rational maps with at most three critical values have no Herman rings
arxiv:2611.25996.summary: We prove that any rational map with at most three critical values has no Herman rings. This generalizes previous results of Shishikura and Milnor on bi-critical rational maps.
arxiv:2611.25996.authors: Yuming Fu, Weiwei Su, Fei Yang

arxiv:2611.25997.title: Minimal primes and radicality of join-meet ideals of modular lattices with one diamond
arxiv:2611.25997.summary: Let $L$ be a finite modular lattice with exactly one diamond, that is, exactly one interval of length two with at least three atoms. We describe the minimal primes of the join-meet ideal $I_L$ in terms of maximal closed distributive sublattices of $L$, and we show that $I_L$ has height $|L|-\mathrm{rank}(L)$. Moreover, we characterize the radicality of $I_L$, over any field, in terms of the complements of the atoms of the diamond in their fibres.

arxiv:2611.26001.title: Moduli spaces of $(3,6)$-$K3$ surfaces and cubic surfaces
arxiv:2611.26001.summary: We compare the ball quotient for marked nodal cubic surfaces with the arithmetic quotient of a domain of type IV associated with $K3$ surfaces arising from configurations of six lines in $\mathbb{P}^2$. Using the Coble map and the period mapping associated with the hypergeometric system of type $(3,6)$, we identify a common open subset of the GIT quotient of six ordered points in $\mathbb{P}^2$ and the ball quotient. This identification gives an analog in dimension four of the Janus-like phenomenon for the Segre cubic and the Igusa quartic, making precise a comparison suggested by Allcock, Carlson, and Toledo.

arxiv:2611.26028.title: On the dimension of $V$-variable fractals
arxiv:2611.26028.summary: Random recursive sets have been used to model a wide range of fractal phenomena, but they can be slow and difficult to generate. $V$-variability address this problem by allowing these sets at most $V$ distinct shapes at each level of magnification. The formulae for the almost sure Hausdorff dimension of both classes is known, and it has been conjectured that (under mild assumptions) the $V$-variable dimension converges to the random recursive dimension as $V\to\infty$.

arxiv:2611.26034.title: Stars and paths in oriented graphs
arxiv:2611.26034.summary: Let $\overrightarrow{F}$ be a fixed oriented graph. Its oriented Tur\'{a}n number, written $\exo(n,\overrightarrow{F})$, is the largest size of an $n$-vertex oriented graph with no copy of $\overrightarrow{F}$. This parameter extends the classical notion of Tur\'{a}n number to oriented graphs.
arxiv:2611.26034.authors: Xuanrui Hu, Hanyi Wang, Yuefang Sun, Bo Deng

arxiv:2611.26037.title: An improved Moore bound for girths seven and eleven
arxiv:2611.26037.summary: Let $n(d,k)$ be the minimum number of vertices of a graph of minimum degree $d$ and girth at least $g=2k+1$. A simple counting argument gives the classical lower bound $n(d,k)\ge m(d,k)=1+d\sum_{i=0}^{k-1}(d-1)^i$, known as the Moore bound and dating back at least to 1960. Apart from complete graphs and odd cycles, graphs attaining this lower bound can exist only for girth $5$ and degrees $3,7$ and $57$ (Hoffman and Singleton 1960; Bannai and Ito 1973; Damerell 1973).

arxiv:2611.26092.title: Control of Complex Social Systems via Committed Minorities and Opinion Broadcast
arxiv:2611.26092.summary: Complex social systems are often characterized by a deep interconnection between individuals' opinion formation and their decision-making processes. In this chapter, we show how these two dynamics can be incorporated within a unifying game-theoretic coevolutionary model for actions and opinions. We present the main theoretical results concerning the convergence of the coevolutionary model, and its recent extensions to incorporate further features of real-world social systems.
arxiv:2611.26092.authors: Roberta Raineri, Mengbin Ye, Lorenzo Zino

arxiv:2611.26093.title: Post-Hopf structures on $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$ and post-Lie bialgebras
arxiv:2611.26093.summary: We classify post-Hopf structures on the Drinfeld-Jimbo quantum group $U_q(\mathfrak{sl}_2)$, for $q\in\mathbb{C}^\times$ not a root of unity, proving that there are exactly three isomorphism classes. We then investigate the semiclassical limits of post-Hopf quantized universal enveloping algebras and derive a compatibility condition between the induced post-Lie product and Lie cobracket. This leads to the notion of a post-Lie bialgebra.

arxiv:2611.26110.title: Hilbert functions over the exterior algebra and f-vectors in higher rank III: Lattice points of the Kozlov polytope
arxiv:2611.26110.summary: Let $E$ be the exterior algebra on $n$ generators and $F=\bigoplus_{i=1}^r Eg_i$ a graded free $E$-module with $\deg g_i=d_i$. Part I of this series identified the convex hull of the Hilbert functions of the quotients $F/M$, $M$ a proper monomial submodule, as the Kozlov polytope $\mathrm{Koz}(n;\mathbf{d})$, a Minkowski sum of shifted Kozlov simplices, and described its vertices at rank two, conjecturing its facets there; Part II counted the Hilbert functions. Here we study the lattice points of the polytope.

arxiv:2611.26115.title: Rational multisections and unirationality of supersingular K3 surfaces
arxiv:2611.26115.summary: We prove that every supersingular K3 surface of Artin invariant at most nine is unirational, confirming the question of Artin, Rudakov, Shafarevich and Shioda outside the generic case of Artin invariant ten. In odd characteristic, we reduce the question to Artin invariant nine and sweep out the K3 surface by Abel--Jacobi images of rational multisections of its Artin--Tate twists which vary along the supersingular twistor line.

arxiv:2611.26130.title: Maximum signless Laplacian spectral radius of graphs with given minimum degree and edge connectivity
arxiv:2611.26130.summary: Let $G$ be a simple connected graph of order $n$ with minimum degree $\delta$ and edge connectivity $k$. Recently, in [Linear Algebra Appl. 751 (2026) 318-330], Zhao, Ye, and Fan characterized the extremal graph with maximum signless Laplacian spectral radius among all graphs of order $n$ with minimum degree $\delta$ and edge connectivity $k$ when $n \geq \delta^2+4\delta+3$ and $k \in \{0,1,2\}$, and proposed the corresponding problem for $3 \leq k \leq \delta-1$. In this paper, we solve the problem for the entire range $0 \leq k \leq \delta-1$ and completely remove the order restriction.

arxiv:2611.26151.title: Power topologies and uniformities on bistochastic operators
arxiv:2611.26151.summary: We prove that the set of invertible Koopman operators attached to the usual interval probability space is dense (and hence dense $G_{\delta}$) in the space of bistochastic operators in the polynomial weak topology. This extends the non-polynomial analogue (due to Brown/Vershik/Ryzhikov/Eisner). We also show that the plain and polynomial weak topologies are distinct on bistochastic operators, confirming the distinction between the two results.

arxiv:2611.26152.title: Orbifold Chern slopes of surfaces with negative second Segre number and big cotangent bundle
arxiv:2611.26152.summary: In this paper, we construct smooth minimal projective surfaces of general type with negative second Segre number and big cotangent bundle, and prove that every rational number in $(1,3]$ is realized as the orbifold Chern slope of a Du Val contraction of such a surface. The upper endpoint is attained by a canonical model with eighteen $A_8$ singularities and three $A_2$ singularities, which is a compact complex two-ball quotient by the equality case of the orbifold Miyaoka-Yau inequality. We also construct an explicit sequence of canonical-model orbifold Chern slopes converging to three from below.

arxiv:2611.26155.title: The $RO(C_{p^n})$-graded Tambara functor of perfectoid THH
arxiv:2611.26155.summary: Let $R$ be a perfect $\mathbb F_p$-algebra or a nonzero $p$-torsionfree perfectoid ring and $p$ be an arbitrary prime number. We compute the $RO(C_{p^n})$-graded Tambara functor of $\operatorname{THH}(R;\mathbb Z_p)$ for every $n\ge0$, including all homotopy groups, products, restrictions, transfers, Weyl actions and norms. We also compute genuine cyclotomic restriction.

arxiv:2611.26163.title: Uniform Positivity of the $F$-Signature and Pure Descent of klt Singularities
arxiv:2611.26163.summary: In this paper, we affirmatively answer the question of Carvajal-Rojas, Schwede, and Tucker on the uniform positivity of the $F$-signature, and prove a converse. Namely, given a klt type singularity, we establish uniform lower bounds on the $F$-signatures of its reductions mod $p$ for $p$ sufficiently large. Conversely, if the $F$-signatures of the reductions of a normal singularity are uniformly bounded below by a positive constant on large primes, we prove that the singularity is of klt type.

arxiv:2611.26184.title: Invariant real curves arising from semiconjugacies of rational maps
arxiv:2611.26184.summary: In this paper, we study real analytic invariant curves arising from semiconjugacies of real rational maps. Such semiconjugacies arise naturally in Eremenko's work on invariant Jordan analytic curves. While invariant generalized circles are easy to obtain from real rational maps, we are interested in curves not contained in any generalized circle.

arxiv:2611.26185.title: Euler up-down numbers and quiver representations
arxiv:2611.26185.summary: We show that Euler up-down numbers enumerate isoclasses of representations arising from quiver Grassmannians which provide an explicit realization of PBW degenerate flag varieties. Using this geometric realization, we derive several formulas connecting Euler up-down numbers, median Genocchi numbers, and Motzkin numbers. We also define a new $q$-analogue of Euler up-down numbers and derive several formulas for these polynomials.
arxiv:2611.26185.authors: Giovanni Cerulli Irelli, Evgeny Feigin, Markus Reineke

arxiv:2611.26189.title: Optimal Radius Ratio of Compact Nonuniform Packings
arxiv:2611.26189.summary: We study the ratio of the smallest to the largest radius in a nonuniform disk packing whose tangency graph triangulates the plane. We give a computer-assisted proof that the largest possible ratio is $s=0.651050185882609\ldots$, attained uniquely up to similarity by packing~53 of Fernique, Hashemi, and Sizova. In fact, every nonuniform packing with radius ratio at least $0.65105$ is similar to this packing.

arxiv:2611.26205.title: Convergence of the Most Probable Transition Paths in Multiscale Systems
arxiv:2611.26205.summary: This paper is devoted to study the convergence behavior of the most probable transition paths in a class of multiscale stochastic dynamical systems. First, based on Euler-Lagrange equations, we establish proximity and convergence results in the space of continuous functions endowed with the supremum norm. These results compare the most probable paths of the multiscale system with those of averaged system derived from the averaging principle.
arxiv:2611.26205.authors: Qiqi Lian, Shanqi Liu, Jinqiao Duan

arxiv:2611.26207.title: Surface sheaves on the quintic I. Expanded degenerations and virtual gluing
arxiv:2611.26207.summary: We study the specialization of Donaldson-Thomas virtual cycles for surface sheaves on a Calabi Yau threefold degenerating to a simple normal crossing threefold, composed of two quasi Fano threefolds glued along a common (double) divisor. The compactification of the two relative sheaf moduli spaces involves construction of suitable moduli space of sheaves on expanded degenerations of each quasi Fano variety. On a fixed expanded fiber the matching datum is an equivalence of the derived restrictions of the component sheaves.

arxiv:2611.26217.title: Surface sheaves on the quintic II. Donaldson-Thomas invariants and the M5-brane modified elliptic genus in string theory
arxiv:2611.26217.summary: We compute Donaldson-Thomas invariants of pure two-dimensional sheaves in the hyperplane class of a smooth quintic threefold. We take advantage of two degenerating families to relate the DT geometry of Quintic threefold to geometry of pure two dimensional shaves on a quartic threefold and correction terms induced by invariants of relative Hilbert schemes of points. For this we use degeneration technique and virtual gluing formula in the prequel Part I.

arxiv:2611.26226.title: The existence of generalized Steiner systems
arxiv:2611.26226.summary: A generalized Steiner system $GS(t,w,n,q)$ is a $q$-ary constant-weight code of length $n$ and weight $w$ that has minimum distance at least $2(w-t)+1$ and attains the Johnson-type upper bound $(q-1)^t\binom nt/\binom wt$. For strengths $t=1$ and $t=2$, such systems were known to exist for all sufficiently large lengths satisfying the necessary divisibility conditions. For general fixed parameters, Liu and Shangguan (J.
arxiv:2611.26226.authors: Xuan Wang, Shitao Li, Minjia Shi

arxiv:2611.26229.title: Sharp topological overlap in every dimension
arxiv:2611.26229.summary: For a positive integer $d$ let $c_d^{\mathrm{top}}$ (resp. $c_d^{\mathrm{aff}}$) be the maximum $c$ such that, for every continuous (resp. affine) map from the $n$-dimensional simplex $\Delta^n$ to $\mathbb{R}^d$, some point of $\mathbb{R}^d$ lies in the images of at least $(c-o(1))\binom{n+1}{d+1}$ of the $d$-dimensional faces, as $n\to\infty$.
